# API: the public Java API

<!-- generated by build_api.py from the original's class files and the analyst's notes -->

Part 2 of `SPEC.md`. Other plugins compile against these types and call them at run time, so every declaration below is contract, exactly: package, type name, kind, modifiers, type parameters and their bounds, supertypes, and every public or protected member with its parameter types, return type, generics, varargs, `throws` clause, constant value and annotation default. The hidden tests compare the replacement's class files with them.

**How to read it.**
- One `## Package` section per package, one `###` section per type. A member type follows its enclosing type and is named `Outer.Inner`.
- Each type starts with its declaration in Java. Then one table row per public or protected member it declares itself, in Java syntax without parameter names (choose your own). Members it inherits are not repeated; its supertypes give them.
- Type names are fully qualified, except those of `java.lang`. The names of type variables (`T`, `K`) are free; keep them for readability.
- `NAME (enum constant)` is a constant of an enum, in declaration order. A field with `= value` is a compile-time constant with exactly that value.
- A type that is a public API class may still be created only by the plugin; the meaning says so where it matters.
- The meanings describe how the original behaves as seen by a caller: what a method returns, what it changes, when it fails, what `null` means, and for interfaces who implements them (the plugin, or other plugins) and when the plugin calls them. Behaviour that needs more than a sentence is in `claims.jsonl`.
- Members not described differently follow the usual Java conventions: `equals` and `hashCode` compare by value, `toString` is for debugging only and its text is not contract.

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api`

Entry points into the plugin's public API: a single aggregate of all public service components, and a helper exposing permission checks, Jira services, web-resource inclusion and issue search used across the plugin.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.StructureComponents`

```java
public interface StructureComponents
```

One-stop access to every public service component of the plugin. The plugin provides the single implementation and exposes it as a component that other plugins obtain by injection (OSGi import); each getter returns the same long-lived singleton service that could also be injected directly. Never returns null; the object holds no state of its own and is safe to share between threads.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.StructurePluginHelper`

```java
public interface StructurePluginHelper
```

A grab-bag helper used throughout the plugin: permission checks for the plugin's application permissions and for Jira permissions, access to commonly used Jira services, web-resource inclusion for pages, issue search through the Jira index, localisation helpers and issue lookup. Marked as internal API (not guaranteed stable for other plugins). The plugin provides the single implementation as a component obtainable by injection; it is stateless apart from configuration read at start-up and is thread-safe. Methods without a user argument act for the current user as seen by `StructureAuth` (for the `getIssueError` and `isStructureAvailable...` defaults) or by Jira's authentication context (for `getUser()`-based defaults such as `isAdmin()`).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError getIssueError(Long, boolean, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Checks whether the issue with the given numeric ID (first argument) is usable by the given user (third argument, null meaning anonymous). Returns null if the issue exists and the user may browse it and, when the second argument is true, also edit it. Returns the plugin's 'item does not exist or is not accessible' error for a null ID, a missing issue or no browse permission, and the 'item edit denied' error when editing is required but not allowed. Returns a Jira data-access error if reading the issue fails. When security is overridden in `StructureAuth` no permission checks are made. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError getIssueError(Long, boolean)` | Same as the three-argument `Long` variant, for the current user from `StructureAuth`. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError getIssueError(com.atlassian.jira.issue.Issue, boolean, boolean, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Checks an issue object (first argument) for the given user (fourth argument, null meaning anonymous). Returns null when it is accessible. Returns a non-null error when: the issue is null or the user lacks the Browse Projects permission ('item does not exist or not accessible'); the third argument is true and the issue's project is not enabled for the plugin in the configuration ('project not enabled'); the second argument is true and Jira reports the issue as not editable by the user ('item edit denied'). Checks are made in that order and the first failure is returned. When security is overridden in `StructureAuth`, only the null check applies. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.agile`

Minimal read-only view of agile (Jira Software) data that the plugin exposes through other API types, such as the sprint of a planning task.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.agile.Sprint`

```java
public interface Sprint
```

A sprint of an agile board, as seen by the plugin. Instances are created by the plugin (immutable value objects read from the agile sprint custom field) and returned by other API calls, for example a planning task's sprint; callers may also pass them back, for example when setting a planning task's sprint.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long getId()` | The sprint's numeric ID as assigned by Jira Software. |
| `public abstract String getSprintName()` | The sprint's name as shown to users. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute`

Attributes: named, parameterised values that the plugin computes for rows of a forest or for items (field values, totals, formulas and so on). Contains the attribute identity (`AttributeSpec`, `ValueFormat`), the value wrappers returned by loading (`AttributeValue`, `LoadedValue`, `RowValues`), well-known attribute specs, and the service that loads values.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeErrorInfo`

```java
public class AttributeErrorInfo
```

Describes one problem that happened while loading an attribute: which attribute, optionally for which row or item, and the cause. Immutable; created by the plugin and returned in `ValuesMeta.getLoadingErrors()` and `AttributeSubscription.drainAttributeErrors()`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public AttributeErrorInfo(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>, Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, Throwable)` | Creates an error record for the attribute (first argument, not null), the row ID (second, null if not row-specific), the item (third, null if not item-specific) and the cause (fourth, may be null). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?> getAttributeSpec()` | The attribute that failed. |
| `public Long getRowId()` | The row the problem relates to, or null. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity getItemId()` | The item the problem relates to, or null. |
| `public Throwable getCause()` | The exception that caused the problem, or null. |
| `public String toString()` | A one-line description: `problem:` followed by the spec, then `:row=` and `:item=` parts when present, then `:` and the cause's message when there is a cause. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec`

```java
public final class AttributeSpec<T>
```

The identity of an attribute: a string ID, a `ValueFormat` that fixes the Java type of the values, and an optional map of parameters. Two specs are equal when ID, format and parameters are all equal, so a spec can be used as a map key. Instances are immutable value objects created by anyone, directly or through `AttributeSpecBuilder`. Parameters must be JSON-like: string keys, and values that are `String`, `Integer`, `Long`, `Double`, `Boolean`, `List` or `Map` of such values (JSON library arrays and objects are converted). Parameters are normalised on creation: entries whose value is null, false, an empty list or map, a `Long` zero or an `Integer` equal to the parameter's default (normally 0; -1 for `depth` and `level` of the `aggregation-parent` attribute; 1 for `fromdepth` and `fromLevel` of `aggregation-join` and `aggregation-array`) are dropped, also inside nested attribute objects (maps holding only `id`, `params` and optionally `format`), so specs that differ only by default values are equal.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public AttributeSpec(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValueFormat<T>)` | Creates a spec with the given ID (first argument) and format (second argument) and no parameters. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the ID is null, blank, longer than 190 characters or contains a colon, or if the format is null. |
| `public AttributeSpec(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValueFormat<T>, java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Creates a spec with the given ID, format and parameters (third argument, null meaning none). The parameter map is deep-copied into an unmodifiable map, validated and normalised (see the type description). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an invalid ID or null format (as the two-argument constructor) and for invalid parameters: a null or non-string key, a null value, or a value of an unsupported type, at any depth. |
| `public String getId()` | The attribute ID, never null or blank. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValueFormat<T> getFormat()` | The value format, never null. |
| `public java.util.Map<String, Object> getParamsMap()` | The normalised parameters, never null (empty when there are none). Treat it as read-only. It is unmodifiable when the spec was created through a public constructor without needing normalisation; in other cases (built by `AttributeSpecBuilder`, `replaceParams`, or changed by normalisation) the plugin does not protect it, but it must not be modified. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.SpecParams getParams()` | The parameters wrapped in a `SpecParams` helper for typed access. Created on first use and then reused. |
| `public boolean is(String)` | True if this spec's ID equals the argument. |
| `public boolean is(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValueFormat<?>)` | True if this spec's format equals the argument (formats are equal when their format IDs are equal). |
| `public boolean is(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValueFormat<?>)` | True if both the ID (first argument) and the format (second argument) match. |
| `public <V> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<V> as(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValueFormat<V>)` | This spec with the given format: the same object (typed accordingly) if the format already matches, otherwise a new spec with the same ID and parameters and the given format. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T> withParam(String, Object)` | A new spec equal to this one with the named parameter (first argument) set to the given value (second argument), replacing an old value. A null value leaves the parameters unchanged; an `AttributeSpec` value is stored as a nested attribute object (`id`, `format`, `params`). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an invalid value. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T> replaceParams(java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | A new spec with the same ID and format and the given parameter map instead of the current one. The map is used as is (only normalised), without copying or validation, so the caller must pass a valid map and must not change it afterwards. Null means no parameters. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T> noParams()` | A new spec with the same ID and format and no parameters. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True if the other object is an `AttributeSpec` with an equal format, ID and parameter map. |
| `public int hashCode()` | A hash code consistent with `equals`, computed from the ID, format and parameters; cached after first use. |
| `public String toString()` | The ID, then, if there are parameters, a colon and the parameters as JSON, then a colon and the format ID; for example `sum:{"distinct":true}:duration`. Cached after first use. |

A null spec gives an empty builder. |

Nested parameter objects that ended up empty are left out, and the parameters are normalised as for `AttributeSpec`. If the key already holds a nested object builder, that builder is returned; otherwise a new empty nested object replaces any value under that key. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a null key. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpecBuilder<T>.ParamsBuilder<P> set(String, Object)` | Sets the parameter with the given key (first argument) to the value (second argument) and returns this builder. Entries are added to any nested object already under that key. Returns this builder. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpecNormalization`

```java
public class AttributeSpecNormalization
```

Static helper that normalises attribute parameters the way `AttributeSpec` does on creation. Marked internal. Not meant to be instantiated.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public AttributeSpecNormalization()` | Public default constructor (the class has only static members). |
| `public static java.util.Map<String, Object> normalizeParams(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Returns the normalised form of the parameters (second argument) of the attribute with the given ID (first argument): entries with default-like values (null, false, empty list or map, `Long` zero, an `Integer` equal to the parameter's default) are removed, recursively inside lists and nested attribute objects. When something is removed, nested attribute objects are rebuilt with their keys in the order `id`, `format`, `params` (empty `params` and missing `format` are left out); when nothing needs to change, their original key order is kept. Nested maps that are not attribute objects are never normalised. Returns the same map object when nothing needs to change, otherwise a new mutable map. Does not validate or copy values. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue`

```java
public abstract class AttributeValue<T>
```

An immutable wrapper of a single attribute value. It is either defined (holds a non-null value) or undefined; an undefined value may be marked as an error, as absent (no value was produced) or as inaccessible (hidden from the user). Any value may also carry opaque loader data that a loader attaches for its own later use; loader data takes part in equality. Created through the static factories; the undefined variants without loader data are shared singletons. Equality: two defined values are equal if their values are equal; two undefined values if they have the same kind.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> of(T)` | A defined value holding the given non-null object. Passing null is a programming error (checked only by a Java assertion; with assertions off it yields an undefined value). |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> ofNullable(T)` | A defined value holding the given object, or `undefined()` if it is null. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> undefined()` | The shared plain undefined value: the attribute has no value for this row or item. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> error()` | The shared undefined value that marks a failure to compute the value (`isError()` is true). |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> absent()` | The shared undefined value that marks that no value has been produced at all (`isAbsent()` is true), as opposed to a computed empty value; consumers skip absent values. Marked internal. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> inaccessible()` | The shared undefined value that marks a row or item the user is not allowed to see (`isInaccessible()` is true). Marked internal. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> withData(Object)` | A value of the same kind and content carrying the given loader data instead of any existing one. Null removes the loader data (and returns this object if there is none). |
| `public abstract T getValue()` | The held value, or null if undefined (of any kind). |
| `public final T getDefinedValue()` | The held value; throws `StructureRuntimeException` if this value is undefined. Use after checking `isDefined()`. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> ifPresent(java.util.function.Consumer<? super T>)` | Calls the consumer with the held value if defined; does nothing otherwise. Returns this object. |
| `public abstract boolean isDefined()` | True if a non-null value is held. |
| `public abstract boolean isError()` | True only for the error kind of undefined value. |
| `public abstract boolean isAbsent()` | True only for the absent kind of undefined value. |
| `public abstract boolean isInaccessible()` | True only for the inaccessible kind of undefined value. |
| `public <D> D getLoaderData(Class<D>)` | The attached loader data if it is an instance of the given class, otherwise null (also null when there is none). |
| `public <X> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<X> cast(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<X>)` | Returns this object typed for the given spec's format, provided the held value is null or an instance of the format's value class. A mismatch is a programming error: a Java assertion fails, or with assertions off null is returned. Marked internal. |


Callback that receives attribute values as they are loaded by `StructureAttributeService.loadAttributeValues`. Implemented by the caller. The plugin calls it on the loading thread (the caller's thread), possibly several times per attribute; values may arrive in parts and, for the `loadAttributeValues` methods, outdated values may be delivered first.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract <T> void receiveValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValueColumn<Long, T>)` | Called with an attribute (first argument) and a column of its values for the requested rows (second argument). The column is valid only during the call. For an attribute that cannot be loaded at all (unknown, or its loader failed to build), a column in which every row has the error value is delivered. |
| `public default boolean isCancelled()` | Polled by the plugin during loading; returning true stops the loading early (silently, without an exception). Default false. |
| `public default void valuesReady(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | Called when all values of the given attribute for the requested rows have been delivered. Default does nothing. |
| `public default void receiveMeta(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValuesMeta)` | Called once at the end of a successful loading with information about the loading: data versions and errors. Default does nothing. |
| `public default void receiveInaccessibleRows(com.almworks.integers.LongSet)` | Called before values are delivered with the set of requested rows that the current user may not see; no values are delivered for them. Not called when all rows are visible or security is overridden. Default does nothing. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.StructureAttributeService`

```java
public interface StructureAttributeService
```

The service that computes attribute values for rows of a forest or for items. The plugin provides the single implementation as a component (also available from `StructureComponents.getAttributeService()`); thread-safe. Values are computed for the current `StructureAuth` user: unless security is overridden, rows whose items the user may not see are left out (reported to receivers as inaccessible) and values depend on the user's permissions, locale and time zone where relevant. Values are cached and shared between requests where possible. In all methods a null forest, row list or attribute collection means there is nothing to load (an empty result or no callbacks), not an error. Requested rows that are not in the forest get no values. If loading has to be restarted too many times because of concurrent changes, a `StructureRuntimeException` is thrown.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void loadAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, boolean, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValuesReceiver)` | Loads values of the attributes (fourth argument) for the rows (third argument) of the forest described by the spec (first argument), delivering them to the receiver (fifth argument) as they become available, on the calling thread; returns when done or when the receiver reports cancellation. Values may be outdated (see `LoadedValue.isOutdated`). If the second argument (strict) is false, the plugin may use an equivalent but cheaper forest to share cached values: a trailing single-item filter transformation is ignored, and an untransformed secured spec is replaced by its unsecured form; visibility of rows is still enforced. If true, the spec is used exactly. If the forest cannot be obtained, forest-dependent attributes get no values. |
| `public default void loadAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValuesReceiver)` | Same as the five-argument variant with strict set to false. |
| `public abstract void loadAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValuesReceiver)` | Like the `ForestSpec` variant but for an arbitrary forest given together with its items (first argument), which need not be stored anywhere; rows may be temporary. Forest-dependent values are not cached between calls. |
| `public abstract void loadAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValuesReceiver)` | Like the `ItemForest` variant, for a forest of existing rows; the items of the rows are looked up through the row manager. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues getAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, boolean, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>, java.util.function.Consumer<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValuesMeta>)` | Loads values as `loadAttributeValues(ForestSpec, boolean, ...)` does and returns them collected in a `RowValues` (only up-to-date values, no outdated ones). The fifth argument, if not null, receives the loading's `ValuesMeta`. Never null; `RowValues.EMPTY` when the spec, rows or attributes are null. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues getAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>)` | Same as the five-argument `getAttributeValues` with strict false and no meta consumer. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues getAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>)` | Collects into `RowValues` the values that the `Forest` variant of `loadAttributeValues` would deliver. Never null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues getAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>)` | Collects into `RowValues` the values that the `ItemForest` variant of `loadAttributeValues` would deliver. Never null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ConsistentRowValues getConsistentAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, boolean, java.util.function.Function<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, com.almworks.integers.LongList>, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Loads the latest forest for the spec (first argument; strict flag as in `loadAttributeValues`), chooses rows by applying the function (third argument) to that forest (null means all rows), and loads the attributes (fourth argument), repeating until the forest and the item data did not change during loading. Returns the values together with the forest and versions they match. Tries at most the number of times set by the dark feature `structure.attribute.maxConsistentLoadAttempts` (default 5) and then throws `StructureException` (a 'consistent operation failed' error). Returns `ConsistentRowValues.EMPTY` if the spec or attributes are null, if the forest cannot be obtained (the problem is logged, not thrown) or if loading is cancelled. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ConsistentRowValues getConsistentAttributeValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, java.util.function.Function<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, com.almworks.integers.LongList>, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Same as the four-argument variant with strict false. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ItemValues getItemValues(java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>)` | Loads the attributes (second argument) for the given items (first argument), independently of any forest: each distinct item is treated as a top-level row of a temporary flat forest. Returns values indexed by item identity; never null, `ItemValues.EMPTY` if either collection is null or empty. Forest-dependent attributes give values as computed for that flat forest. |
| `public abstract boolean isItemAttribute(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | True if the attribute's value depends only on the item (not on the row's position in a forest), so it is cached per item. False for null, for attributes that cannot be loaded, and for forest-dependent attributes. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValuesWithUpdateChecker getAttributeValuesWithUpdateChecker(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec)` | Collects values as `getAttributeValues(ItemForest, ...)` does and also returns a checker that tells later whether they changed. The fourth argument, if not null, is the spec of a stored forest the item forest is based on, used to share cached data. Returns empty values and a checker that always answers false when the forest, rows or attributes are null. Marked internal. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValuesWithUpdateChecker getAttributeValuesWithUpdateChecker(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>)` | Collects values as `getAttributeValues(ForestSpec, rows, attributes)` does and also returns a checker that tells later whether they changed. Empty values and an always-false checker when an argument is null. Marked internal. |
| `public abstract boolean hasUpdate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValuesMeta)` | True if values of the attributes (third argument) for the rows (second argument) loaded with the given meta (fourth argument) may have changed since; the first argument is the forest spec they were loaded for, or null for values not tied to a stored forest. Returns false if rows or attributes are null and true when in doubt. Marked internal. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader`

The extension point for computing attribute values. Other plugins (and the plugin itself) supply `AttributeLoaderProvider` components that turn an `AttributeSpec` into an `AttributeLoader`; the loader kinds here (item, derived, single-row, aggregate, propagate, scanning) differ in what data a value may depend on, and the context interfaces are what the plugin hands to loaders while it calculates. It also holds the trail model (`TrailItemSet`) used for cache invalidation.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AggregateAttributeContext`

```java
public interface AggregateAttributeContext extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.RowAttributeContext
```

Context passed to an `AggregateAttributeLoader` while it computes the value for one row; in addition to the row it exposes the row's direct children. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow> getChildren()` | The direct children of the current row in the forest being calculated, in forest order. The list has the same size and order as the list of child values passed to `AggregateAttributeLoader.loadValue`. Empty for a leaf row; never null. Read-only. If the loader is not allowed to access items, the rows returned refuse to resolve their items. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AggregateAttributeLoader`

```java
public interface AggregateAttributeLoader<T> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.MultiRowAttributeLoader<T>
```

Extension-point loader kind for values that depend on the row's subtree (totals, counts and the like). The plugin calculates children before parents and calls the loader once per row with the already computed values of the row's direct children. Implemented by plugins and returned from an `AttributeLoaderProvider`. As a multi-row loader its default caching strategy is `SHOULD`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> loadValue(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AggregateAttributeContext)` | Computes the value for the row given by `context.getRow()`. Argument 1: the values already computed for the row's direct children, one entry per child in the same order as `context.getChildren()` (entries are never null; missing values are undefined values). Argument 2: the aggregate context. Returns the value; returning null is treated by the plugin as an undefined value (inside a composite loader null means 'not handled, try the next loader'). A runtime exception thrown here is logged and turned into an error value for that row. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeCachingStrategy`

```java
public enum AttributeCachingStrategy
```

Tells the plugin whether the values produced by a loader may be kept in its value cache between requests. Returned by `AttributeLoader.getCachingStrategy()`. A dependency's `MUST_NOT` is inherited by every attribute that depends on it.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `SHOULD (enum constant)` | Values are expensive to compute and should be cached. Default for multi-row loaders (aggregate, propagate, scanning). |
| `MAY (enum constant)` | Values may be cached; computing them again is also acceptable. Default for loaders whose spec uses one of the standard value formats. |
| `SHOULD_NOT (enum constant)` | Values should not be stored in the value cache (each request recomputes them), though the plugin still keeps invalidation tracking for them. Default for non-standard value formats. |
| `MUST_NOT (enum constant)` | Values must never be cached, and nothing derived from them may be cached either: every attribute that depends on such an attribute is also treated as `MUST_NOT`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeCachingStrategy[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeCachingStrategy valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeCachingStrategy guessCachingStrategy(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | Default strategy for a spec when a loader does not state one: `MAY` if the spec's value format is one of the standard formats known to `ValueFormat` (looked up by format id), otherwise `SHOULD_NOT`. The argument must not be null (NullPointerException). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContext`

```java
public interface AttributeContext
```

Base context available to loaders and providers during attribute calculation: who the values are computed for, locale and time zone, the time of the request, the base structure, and a per-request scratch map for sharing objects between loaders. Implemented only by the plugin. When called by a loader, several getters verify that the loader declared the matching `AttributeContextDependency`; calling them without it throws IllegalStateException (if the dependency is only inherited from an attribute dependency, a warning is logged instead). When called from an `AttributeLoaderProvider` while the loader is being created, the same getters instead mark the provider's loader as not reusable and record the dependency as implied. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser getUser()` | The user on whose behalf values are calculated, or null for an anonymous user. Requires the `USER` context dependency. |
| `public abstract com.atlassian.jira.util.I18nHelper getI18nHelper()` | Jira's `I18nHelper` for the calculating user's locale. Requires `USER_LOCALE` (or `USER`). Never null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.i18n.I18n getI18n()` | The plugin's `I18n` text helper for the calculating user's locale, backed by the same Jira helper. Never null. Note: unlike `getI18nHelper()`, the plugin does not check context dependencies here. |
| `public abstract java.util.Locale getLocale()` | The calculating user's locale (as reported by the user's `I18nHelper`). Requires `USER_LOCALE` (or `USER`). Never null. |
| `public abstract java.util.TimeZone getTimeZone()` | The calculating user's time zone as configured in Jira. Requires `USER_TIMEZONE` (or `USER`). Never null. |
| `public abstract long getBaseStructureId()` | Id of the structure on whose forest the values are being calculated, or 0 when the calculation is not tied to a structure. Requires the `STRUCTURE` context dependency. |
| `public abstract long getLoadTimeMillis()` | Wall-clock time (milliseconds since the epoch) captured when the loading request began; the same for every value computed in that request, so use it instead of the system clock. Requires `CURRENT_TIME`. |
| `public abstract long getLoadTimeNanos()` | Value of the JVM's monotonic nanosecond timer captured when the loading request began; only meaningful for measuring intervals within this JVM. Requires `CURRENT_TIME`. |
| `public abstract String getBaseUrl()` | Jira's configured base URL without a trailing slash, or an empty string if none is configured. Never null. |
| `public abstract void putObject(Object, Object)` | Stores an object under a key in a scratch map that lives as long as the loading request and is shared by all loaders called in it (useful for request-level caches). Argument 1: the key (not null). Argument 2: the value; null removes the key. Throws IllegalArgumentException for keys that are reserved by the export framework (the keys defined in `ExportContextKeys`), which are read-only to loaders. |
| `public abstract <T> T getObject(Object)` | Returns the object stored under the key in the request's scratch map (by `putObject` or by the plugin, e.g. export keys from `ExportContextKeys`), cast to the caller's expected type; null if absent. The cast is unchecked, so a wrong expected type fails at the caller. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency`

```java
public enum AttributeContextDependency
```

Kinds of context information (besides attribute dependencies and the item/row itself) a loader's values may depend on. A loader declares them through `AttributeLoader.getContextDependencies()`; the plugin keys cached values by the declared dimensions (for example, per user) and refuses context getters for undeclared ones. Declaring `USER` implies `USER_LOCALE` and `USER_TIMEZONE`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `USER (enum constant)` | Values depend on the calculating user (permissions, user-specific data). Cached values are kept per user. Implies locale and time zone. |
| `USER_LOCALE (enum constant)` | Values depend on the calculating user's locale (e.g. localised text) but not otherwise on the user. |
| `USER_TIMEZONE (enum constant)` | Values depend on the calculating user's time zone (e.g. date formatting or day boundaries). |
| `STRUCTURE (enum constant)` | Values depend on which structure is being calculated (see `AttributeContext.getBaseStructureId()`); cached values are kept per structure. |
| `CURRENT_TIME (enum constant)` | Values depend on the current time. Required to call the load-time getters and `AttributeLoaderContext.valueExpires`; such values expire and are periodically recalculated. |
| `TRAIL (enum constant)` | The loader reports trails (`AttributeLoaderContext.addTrail`): its values depend on items other than the row's own item, and change to those items must invalidate them. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |
| `public static java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency> guessContextDependencies(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | Default context dependencies for a spec when a loader does not state them: a set containing only `USER` if the spec's format is the HTML format (`ValueFormat.HTML`), otherwise null (no context dependencies). The argument must not be null. |
| `public static java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency> union(java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency...)` | Returns a new, mutable set holding all elements of the given set plus the additional dependencies. Argument 1 may be null (treated as empty); the varargs array and its null elements are ignored. Never returns null; the arguments are not modified. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader`

```java
public interface AttributeLoader<T>
```

Base interface of all attribute loaders: an object that computes values of exactly one attribute spec. Loaders are created by `AttributeLoaderProvider` implementations (usually from the builders in `AttributeLoaders`) and then used by the plugin, possibly from several threads and for many requests, so implementations should be stateless or thread-safe. A loader must implement exactly one of the concrete kinds (`ItemAttributeLoader`, `DerivedAttributeLoader`, `SingleRowAttributeLoader`, `AggregateAttributeLoader`, `PropagateAttributeLoader`, `ScanningAttributeLoader`); the getters here describe what the values depend on and are read once, when the plugin assembles the loader.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T> getAttributeSpec()` | The attribute spec this loader computes values for. Never null. It should equal the spec the provider was asked for (a spec with a subset of its parameters and a convertible format is also accepted and adapted by the plugin); otherwise the plugin discards the loader with a warning. |
| `public default java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>> getAttributeDependencies()` | Specs of other attributes whose values this loader reads through `AttributeLoaderContext.getDependencyAttributeValue`. The plugin loads them first and rejects reading any spec not listed here. Null or empty means no dependencies (default: null). Circular dependencies make the attribute unavailable. |
| `public default java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency> getContextDependencies()` | Context information the values depend on (see `AttributeContextDependency`). Null means 'not declared' and is treated like an empty set; the default returns `AttributeContextDependency.guessContextDependencies(getAttributeSpec())`. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeCachingStrategy getCachingStrategy()` | How the plugin may cache the loader's values; null means no preference. Default: `AttributeCachingStrategy.guessCachingStrategy(getAttributeSpec())`. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet getGlobalTrail()` | Items whose change must invalidate every cached value of this attribute, regardless of row (for example a configuration object the attribute reads). Null (the default) means none. A non-null global trail also disables the plugin's shortcut of re-validating cached values without recomputation. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoaderContext`

```java
public interface AttributeLoaderContext extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContext
```

Context for loaders that compute values: adds access to the values of declared attribute dependencies and lets the loader report trails and expiration for the value being computed. Implemented only by the plugin. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract <V> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<V> getDependencyAttributeValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<V>)` | Returns the already computed value of a dependency attribute for the current item or row. The spec must be one of the loader's declared `getAttributeDependencies()`, otherwise IllegalArgumentException. Never returns null: a missing value is an undefined value; if the current row is hidden from the user and the loader is a sensitive multi-row loader, the result is an inaccessible value. If an item-level loader asks for a dependency that needs the forest (a row-based attribute), IllegalArgumentException is thrown. Reading a dependency also makes the current value expire no later than the dependency's value. |
| `public default <V> V getDependencyValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<V>)` | Shortcut for the plain value of `getDependencyAttributeValue(dependency)`; null when that value is undefined, an error or otherwise has no value. Same exceptions. |
| `public abstract void addTrail(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet)` | Records that the value being computed also depends on the given items, so that a change to any of them invalidates this value. Calls accumulate (union) for the current value. Null or an empty set is ignored. Requires the `TRAIL` context dependency (IllegalStateException otherwise). |
| `public default void addTrail(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Same as `addTrail(TrailItemSet.of(item))`: records a single item the value depends on. Null is ignored. Reporting the current item itself is pointless (the plugin logs a warning). |
| `public abstract void valueExpires(long, java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit)` | Declares that the value being computed becomes stale after the given time, measured from the start of the request. Argument 1: the time to live, must be positive (IllegalArgumentException otherwise). Argument 2: its unit. Several calls (and dependencies' own expirations) keep the earliest expiry. Requires the `CURRENT_TIME` context dependency (IllegalStateException otherwise). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoaderProvider`

```java
public interface AttributeLoaderProvider
```

Extension point through which plugins contribute attributes: given a requested attribute spec, a provider returns a loader for it or null if it does not serve that spec. Implementations are registered as plugin modules/components; the plugin asks every registered provider each time it needs a loader for a spec it has not assembled yet, and combines all loaders returned for the same spec into one composite loader (see `CompositeAttributeLoader`). Assembled loaders are cached and reused for later requests unless the provider called `AttributeProviderContext.mustNotCacheLoader()` or used user-dependent context while creating the loader.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<?> createAttributeLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeProviderContext) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureProviderException` | Returns a loader for the spec (argument 1), or null if this provider does not support it. Argument 2 gives the request context (user, locale and so on); using it makes the created loader request-specific. The returned loader's spec should equal the requested spec (a more general spec with fewer parameters and a convertible format is also accepted). Throwing `StructureProviderException` signals that the spec is recognised but cannot be served; the plugin logs it and continues with other providers, as it also does for runtime exceptions. |

Use `valueFunction`/`valueFunctionAV` on it; because the item class is preset, the identity-based value functions (`valueFunctionII`, `valueFunctionIIAV`) make `build()` fail with IllegalArgumentException. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeProviderContext`

```java
public interface AttributeProviderContext extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContext
```

Context passed to `AttributeLoaderProvider.createAttributeLoader`. Besides the general context it lets the provider influence whether the created loader may be reused, and query the kind of other attributes. Implemented only by the plugin. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

The plugin does this automatically when the provider reads user, locale, time zone, structure or time information from the context. |
| `public abstract boolean isItemAttribute(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | True if the given attribute's values depend only on the item (not on the row's position in a forest), i.e. it is computed by item loaders or by derived loaders over such attributes. False for null and for row-based attributes. Throws IllegalArgumentException if the check recurses into the attribute currently being checked. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.PropagateAttributeLoader`

```java
public interface PropagateAttributeLoader<T> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.MultiRowAttributeLoader<T>
```

Extension-point loader kind for values that flow from parent to children (inherited values, paths, depths). The plugin processes the forest top-down: for each parent it calls `loadChildren` once with the parent's computed value and then applies the returned function to each child in order. Default caching strategy `SHOULD`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract java.util.function.BiFunction<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.PropagateAttributeContext, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>> loadChildren(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.PropagateAttributeContext.Parent)` | Prepares the computation of a parent's children. Argument 1: the parent's value (undefined for root rows unless the loader computes a super-root value). Argument 2: the parent context. Returns a function taking a child row and its context and returning the child's value (a null result means undefined). Returning null from this method makes all these children undefined; a runtime exception makes them error values. The returned function is used only for this parent's children within the current request. |
| `public default boolean isLoadingSuperRoot()` | Whether the loader also computes a value for the synthetic super-root above the roots; if so, the plugin first calls `loadChildren` with an undefined parent value and a null parent, applies the function to the super-root row, and passes that value as the parent value of the root rows. Default false. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet`

```java
public abstract class TrailItemSet
```

An immutable set of items, used as a trail: the items a value depends on, whose change must invalidate it. To stay small it may be stored imprecisely: up to a limit of 50 individual items it keeps the exact items; beyond that it keeps only their item types (matching every item of those types); beyond 10 types it becomes the set of all items. So `contains` may answer true for items that were never added, but never false for ones that were. The limits are read once from the plugin's dark-feature settings `structure.trail.itemLimit` and `structure.trail.typeLimit`. Instances come from the static factories and the `NONE`/`ALL_ITEMS` constants; the concrete subclasses are public only so that visitors can distinguish them. Immutable and thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean contains(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | True if a change to the given item is covered by this set (exactly, or by its item type, or because the set covers all items). False for null. |
| `public boolean containsAny(java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | True if `contains` is true for at least one item of the collection. False for a null or empty collection. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet expand(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Returns a set that also covers the given item (this set itself if already covered or if the item is null). May widen to item-type level or all items when limits are exceeded. Never null; this set is unchanged. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet union(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet)` | Returns a set covering everything in this set and in the argument; the argument may be null (returns this set). The result may be less precise (type level or all items) when the combined size exceeds the limits. Never null. |
| `public abstract void accept(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet.Visitor)` | Calls exactly one method of the visitor according to the set's form: `visitNone` for the empty set, `visit(OneItem)`, `visit(SpecificItems)`, `visit(OneType)`, `visit(SpecificTypes)`, or `visitAll`. |
| `public final boolean isEmpty()` | True only for the empty set (`None`). |
| `public final boolean equals(Object)` | Two trail sets are equal when they have the same form and cover the same items, types, or all items. |
| `public final int hashCode()` | Hash code consistent with `equals`, computed from the content (cached after the first call; never 0). |
| `public String toString()` | Debug text listing the content in braces, for example `{ALL}` or `{}`; the exact format is not a contract. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet of(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity...)` | Creates a set of the given items; null elements are ignored. Empty input gives `None.NONE`; one distinct item gives a one-item set; up to the item limit an exact item set; more items are reduced to their item types (and, past the type limit, to `ALL_ITEMS`). A null array throws NullPointerException. Known defect: when the input contains nulls and exactly one distinct non-null item, the original returns a one-item set built from the first element of the input, which may be null (a set that then contains nothing). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet of(java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Same as the varargs form for a collection; a null collection gives `None.NONE`. The same defect with a leading null element applies. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet ofTypes(java.util.Collection<String>)` | Creates a set covering all items of the given item types. Null elements are ignored; null or empty input gives `None.NONE`; one type gives a one-type set; past the type limit (10) the result is `ALL_ITEMS`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet.Collector`

```java
public static class TrailItemSet.Collector implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet.ReadVisitor
```

A read visitor that gathers the content of a trail set into plain Java sets; used for comparisons, hashing and printing. Obtain one with `collect`. The collector is mutable and not thread-safe; the sets it returns are its own mutable sets.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet.Collector collect(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet)` | Creates a collector, lets the given set visit it, and returns it filled. The argument must not be null. |
| `public java.util.Set<String> getTypes()` | The item types collected from a type-level set, or null if the visited set had no types (empty, item-level, or all-items). |
| `public java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity> getItems()` | The items collected from an item-level set, or null if the visited set had no individual items (empty, type-level, or all-items). |
| `public boolean isAll()` | True if the visited set covers all items. |
| `public void visitItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Adds the item to the collected items. If the collector was prepared for a type-level set, an assertion fails when assertions are enabled; otherwise the item is still recorded. |
| `public void visitType(String)` | Adds the item type to the collected types, with the same assertion behaviour as `visitItem` for a mismatching set. |
| `public void visitAll()` | Marks that all items are covered. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | Equal to another collector with the same items, types and all-items flag. |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash code consistent with `equals`. |
| `public String toString()` | Debug text: `{ALL}` for all items, otherwise the types and items joined by commas inside braces (the original always prints a separating comma, even when one side is empty). Not a contract. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic`

Ready-made abstract base classes and a few concrete loaders (sums, inherited values, simple derivations) that make writing attribute loaders easier, plus a minimal `AttributeLoaderProvider` implementation that serves a fixed set of loaders.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.AbstractAggregateLoader`

```java
public abstract class AbstractAggregateLoader<T> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.AbstractAttributeLoader<T> implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AggregateAttributeLoader<T>
```

Convenience base class for `AggregateAttributeLoader` implementations: holds the spec and offers a helper for error propagation. Subclasses implement `loadValue`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected AbstractAggregateLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>)` | Creates the loader for the given spec. Throws IllegalArgumentException if the spec is null. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> firstChildError(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>)` | Returns the first element of the list that is an error value (null elements are skipped), or null if none is. Useful for making an aggregate an error when any child is. The list must not be null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.AbstractNaiveDistinctAggregateLoader`

```java
public abstract class AbstractNaiveDistinctAggregateLoader<T> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.AbstractAggregateLoader<T>
```

Base class for aggregates that count every item once even if it occurs in several rows of the subtree (distinct totals). Each row's result carries, as loader data, an unmodifiable map from item identity to that item's own value for all items in the subtree; the parent merges the children's maps, adds its own item, and combines the map's values. 'Naive' because each row keeps a map of its whole subtree, so memory grows with subtree size.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public AbstractNaiveDistinctAggregateLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>)` | Creates the loader for the given spec. Throws IllegalArgumentException if the spec is null. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> loadValue(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AggregateAttributeContext)` | Merges the item-to-value maps carried by the defined children's values (undefined children contribute nothing), adds the current row's item with the value from `getRowValue` unless the item is already present or that value is null, and returns `combine` of all collected values with the map attached as loader data. `combine` must not return null (the result is created as a defined value). |
| `protected abstract T getRowValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.RowAttributeContext)` | Subclass hook: the current row's own contribution, or null if it has none. |
| `protected abstract T combine(java.util.Collection<T>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AggregateAttributeContext)` | Subclass hook: combines the per-item values of the whole subtree (each distinct item once, in no particular order) into the row's total. Must not return null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.AbstractScanningLoader`

```java
public abstract class AbstractScanningLoader<T> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.AbstractAttributeLoader<T> implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.ScanningAttributeLoader<T>
```

Base class for scanning loaders that accumulate a running value over rows and support two optional spec parameters: `baseLevel` (integer, default 0; negative treated as 0) - rows shallower than this depth get an undefined value and do not contribute; `levels` (list of 1-based level numbers) - only rows at those levels contribute, other rows are skipped and carry the running value through. Level numbers below the base level are dropped. Subclasses implement `loadValueForPassingRow`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected AbstractScanningLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>)` | Creates the loader and reads `baseLevel` and `levels` from the spec's parameters. Throws IllegalArgumentException if the spec is null. |
| `protected boolean isLevelSkipped(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.ScanningAttributeContext)` | True if a `levels` parameter was given and the current row's depth is not one of the listed levels. |
| `protected boolean isAboveBaseLevel(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.ScanningAttributeContext)` | True if the base level is above 0 and the current row's depth is smaller than it. |
| `protected Integer getBaseLevel()` | The effective base level (0-based depth, at least 0). Declared nullable but always returns a number. |
| `protected com.almworks.integers.IntList getLevelsSorted()` | The contributing depths from the `levels` parameter converted to 0-based depths, sorted ascending without duplicates and without depths below the base level; null if the parameter is absent. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> loadValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.ScanningAttributeContext)` | Rows above the base level get an undefined value. Skipped rows (wrong level, or `isRowSkipped` true) carry the running value: see `carryPrecedingValueForSkippedRow`. For other rows the running value is taken from the preceding row (its value, or the value it carries as loader data if it was skipped) and `loadValueForPassingRow` gives the new value; if it equals the running value and the preceding value was defined, the preceding value object is returned, otherwise the new value (undefined if null). |
| `protected abstract T loadValueForPassingRow(T, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.ScanningAttributeContext)` | Subclass hook: computes the new running value for a contributing row from the running value so far (argument 1, null at the start or when nothing has accumulated) and the context. Null means undefined. |
| `protected boolean isRowSkipped(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.ScanningAttributeContext)` | Subclass hook to exclude more rows; a skipped row carries the running value through. Arguments: the preceding row's value and the context. Default false. |
| `protected com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> carryPrecedingValueForSkippedRow(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>)` | Produces the value of a skipped row: if the preceding value is defined, an undefined value that carries the preceding value as loader data (so the row shows nothing but the running value continues); otherwise the preceding value itself. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.NumberAccumulator`

```java
public class NumberAccumulator
```

Mutable helper for summing numbers of mixed types precisely: stays with exact `long` arithmetic while all inputs are integral, switches to compensated (Kahan) `double` summation once a fractional value is added, and switches to `BigDecimal` (64-bit decimal precision) once a `BigDecimal` or `BigInteger` is added. Null inputs are ignored. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public NumberAccumulator()` | Creates an empty accumulator (no value yet). |
| `public void add(Number)` | Adds the number. Null is ignored. |
| `public void remove(Number)` | Subtracts the number. Null is ignored. The accumulator becomes defined even if the result is zero. |
| `public void removeMultiply(Number, int)` | Subtracts the number multiplied by the count (argument 2). Null is ignored. |
| `public void addMultiply(Number, int)` | Adds the number multiplied by the count (argument 2, may be negative). Null is ignored; any non-null number marks the accumulator as defined. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<Number> toValue()` | The current total as an attribute value; undefined if nothing was ever added. |
| `public Number toNumber()` | The current total, or null if no non-null number was ever added. The type is `Long` while all inputs were integral, `Double` once a fractional value was added, or a `BigDecimal` with trailing zeros stripped once big numbers were involved. |
| `public String toString()` | Debug text showing the total, marked with `L` (long) or `D` (double), or as a plain decimal. |

| `public Number merge(java.util.function.Supplier<Number>, java.util.function.Supplier<Number>)` | Sum of the row's own value (argument 1) and the already reduced children value (argument 2); null if both are null. |
| `public Number merge(java.util.function.Supplier<Number>, java.util.List<Number>)` | Sum of the row's own value (argument 1) and all non-null values in the list; null if all are null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.SimpleAttributeProvider`

```java
public abstract class SimpleAttributeProvider implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoaderProvider
```

Minimal `AttributeLoaderProvider` serving a fixed set of loaders registered up front (marked internal). Loaders are grouped by attribute id; a request is answered with the most specific registered loader whose spec parameters all appear, with equal values, in the requested spec. Lookup is synchronized.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public SimpleAttributeProvider()` | Creates a provider with no loaders; subclasses register loaders, typically in their constructor. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.SimpleAttributeProvider create(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<?>...)` | Returns a provider that serves exactly the given loaders (none may be null). |
| `protected final void registerLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<?>)` | Adds a loader, filed under its spec's attribute id. Several loaders may be registered for one id. Not synchronized: register before the provider is used. |
| `protected final <T> void registerCompositeLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<T>...)` | Combines the given loaders for one spec into a composite loader (see `CompositeAttributeLoader.create`) and registers it. Throws IllegalArgumentException if no loaders are given. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<?> createAttributeLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeProviderContext) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureProviderException` | Among the loaders registered for the requested spec's id, picks those whose spec parameters are a subset of the requested spec's parameters; prefers the one with the most parameters, then one whose format equals the requested format. Returns null if none matches. The returned loader may have a more general spec than requested; the plugin adapts it. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.SimpleDerivedAttributeLoader`

```java
public abstract class SimpleDerivedAttributeLoader<T, D> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.AbstractDerivedAttributeLoader<T>
```

Base class for derived loaders computed from exactly one dependency. Handles missing dependency values: with 'yield' on (the default), a missing input or a null result makes the loader return null so that another loader of the same attribute may supply the value; with 'yield' off, a missing input is passed through as the result (keeping its undefined or error state) and a null result becomes an undefined value.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<? extends D> myDependency` | The single dependency spec, available to subclasses. |
| `protected SimpleDerivedAttributeLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<? extends D>)` | Argument 1: the spec computed (not null). Argument 2: the dependency. Yield is on. |
| `protected SimpleDerivedAttributeLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<? extends D>, boolean)` | Argument 1: the spec computed (not null). Argument 2: the dependency. Argument 3: the yield flag described on the class. |
| `public final java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>> getAttributeDependencies()` | A singleton set holding the dependency. Final. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> loadValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.DerivedAttributeContext)` | Reads the dependency's value; if it has no value applies the yield rule, otherwise returns the result of `getValue` wrapped as an attribute value (null result handled by the yield rule). |
| `protected abstract T getValue(D, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.DerivedAttributeContext)` | Subclass hook: computes the value from the dependency's non-null value (argument 1) and the context. May return null. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<T> idLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>)` | Returns a loader for spec (argument 1) that simply copies the value of spec (argument 2), or null if the two specs' formats are not the same instance (two equal but separately created formats count as different). Used to serve a spec by reusing an equivalent one. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.builder`

Fluent builders that create attribute loaders from lambdas (item, derived, single-row), and the loader classes those builders produce. Normally reached through the static factory methods of `AttributeLoaders` / `SharedAttributeLoaders`.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.builder.ArbitraryDependenciesAttributeLoaderBuilder`

```java
public abstract class ArbitraryDependenciesAttributeLoaderBuilder<T, S extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.builder.ArbitraryDependenciesAttributeLoaderBuilder<T, S>> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.builder.AttributeLoaderBuilder<T, S>
```

Abstract builder base adding a freely chosen set of attribute dependencies to the common builder settings. Builders are mutable, not thread-safe, and return themselves from every setter for chaining.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ArbitraryDependenciesAttributeLoaderBuilder()` | Creates a builder with no dependencies declared. |
| `public S dependencies(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>...)` | Adds each given spec as a dependency (see `dependency`). A null array or null elements are ignored. |
| `public S dependency(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | Adds one attribute dependency; null is ignored. Order of first addition is kept; duplicates collapse. |
| `protected java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>> buildDependencies()` | For subclasses: the dependencies declared so far as an unmodifiable copy, or null if `dependency`/`dependencies` never added anything. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.builder.AttributeLoaderBuilder`

```java
public abstract class AttributeLoaderBuilder<T, S extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.builder.AttributeLoaderBuilder<T, S>>
```

Abstract base of all loader builders, holding the settings shared by every loader kind: spec, context dependencies, caching strategy and global trail. Settings left unset make the built loader fall back to the `AttributeLoader` defaults (guessed from the spec's format). Builders are mutable, not thread-safe, and return themselves from every setter for chaining.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T> myAttributeSpec` | The spec set by `spec`, or null; for subclasses. |
| `protected com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeCachingStrategy myCachingStrategy` | The strategy set by `cachingStrategy`, or null for the default; for subclasses. |
| `protected com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet myGlobalTrail` | The global trail accumulated by `globalTrail`, or null; for subclasses. |
| `public AttributeLoaderBuilder()` | Creates a builder with nothing set. |
| `public S spec(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>)` | Sets the spec of the loader to build (replacing any earlier one). Required before `build()`. |
| `public S contextDependencies(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency...)` | Adds each given context dependency (see `contextDependency`). A null array or null elements are ignored. |
| `public S contextDependency(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency)` | Adds one context dependency; null is ignored. Once any is added, the built loader declares exactly the added set instead of the default. Defect: after `noContextDependencies()` this throws UnsupportedOperationException (the explicit empty set cannot be extended); this also affects the trail setters of subclasses, which add `TRAIL`. |
| `public S noContextDependencies()` | Declares explicitly that the loader has no context dependencies (overriding the format-based default, e.g. `USER` for HTML), discarding any added earlier. |
| `public S cachingStrategy(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeCachingStrategy)` | Sets the caching strategy; null restores the default. |
| `public S globalTrail(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet)` | Adds the given items to the loader's global trail (union with what was set before). Null leaves it unchanged. |
| `public S globalTrail(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Adds a single item to the global trail. A null item still sets the global trail to the empty set if none was set before, which marks the loader as having a global trail. |
| `protected S self()` | Returns this builder typed as the concrete builder class. |
| `protected java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency> buildContextDependencies()` | For subclasses: null if no context dependencies were set; an empty unmodifiable set after `noContextDependencies()`; otherwise an unmodifiable copy of the added set. |
| `protected static <R> R notNull(R, String)` | For subclasses: returns the value (argument 1) or throws IllegalArgumentException naming the parameter (argument 2) if it is null. |
| `protected static <R extends java.util.Collection> R nullableCollectionOfNonNulls(R, String)` | For subclasses: returns the collection (argument 1) unchanged, which may be null; throws IllegalArgumentException naming the parameter (argument 2) and the index if any element is null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.builder.ItemAttributeLoaderBuilder`

```java

```

Builder for item loaders. Choose one value function form (the last call wins): forms named `...II...` receive the item identity; the others receive the item resolved to the class set with `itemClass` (an item that cannot be resolved to that class gets an undefined value). Forms ending in `AV` return attribute values as they are; the others return plain values, which are wrapped (null becomes undefined, or yields with `yieldOnNull`). Some optional settings only work with some forms; an incompatible combination makes `build()` throw IllegalArgumentException. Obtained from `AttributeLoaders.itemLoader` or `issueLoader`. Builders are mutable, not thread-safe, and return themselves from every setter for chaining.

Incompatible with `itemClass`, `yieldOnNull`, `valueTrail`, `itemTrail` and `trailItemSet`. A null function throws IllegalArgumentException immediately. |
