## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.composition`

Support for combining several loaders that serve the same attribute into one composite loader, including adapting a simpler loader kind to a more general one, and the `LoaderType` classification of loader kinds.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.composition.AttributeLoaderAdapter`

```java
public abstract class AttributeLoaderAdapter<T, L extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<T>> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.delegate.DelegatingAttributeLoader<T, L>
```

Converts a loader of a simpler kind into an equivalent loader of a more general kind so that loaders of different kinds can be combined. Supported conversions: derived to any other kind; item to single-row, aggregate, propagate or scanning; single-row to aggregate, propagate or scanning. The adapted loader reports the same spec, dependencies, context dependencies, caching strategy and global trail as the original; an adapted item loader returns null for rows whose item type it does not support and preloads only items of supported types.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static <T, C extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<T>> C adapt(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<T>, Class<C>)` | Returns the loader (argument 1) as an instance of the loader interface given by argument 2 (one of the six kind interfaces), wrapping it if its kind differs. If the loader already has that kind it is returned unchanged. Throws IllegalArgumentException if the conversion is not supported or if either argument is not of a recognised loader kind. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.composition.CompositeAttributeLoader`

```java
public abstract class CompositeAttributeLoader<T, L extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<T>> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.AbstractAttributeLoader<T>
```

A loader made of several loaders for the same attribute, as the plugin builds when several providers (or one provider) supply loaders for one spec. The composite has the most general kind among its parts (see `LoaderType` weights); parts of simpler kinds are adapted (see `AttributeLoaderAdapter`) and parts that cannot be adapted are dropped with a warning. A value is taken from the first part, in the given order, that returns a non-null value; if all return null the result is undefined. Immutable; the parts' collection is unmodifiable.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected CompositeAttributeLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>, java.util.Collection<L>)` | For subclasses: creates the composite for the spec (argument 1, not null) from the parts (argument 2, not null, already of the composite's kind) and computes the combined properties described by the getters. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<T> create(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<T>>)` | Builds a composite of the right kind for the spec (argument 1) from the loaders (argument 2, in priority order). Throws IllegalArgumentException if the list is null or empty, or a loader is not of a recognised kind. Item composites ask only the parts that support an item's type; aggregate, propagate, scanning and single-row composites call `preload` on every part and are whole-forest dependent if any part is; a propagate composite uses the first non-null child function and loads the super-root if any part does. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeCachingStrategy getCachingStrategy()` | The strictest strategy among the parts: `MUST_NOT` if any part has it, else `SHOULD_NOT`, else `SHOULD`, else `MAY` (parts returning null are ignored). |
| `public java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>> getAttributeDependencies()` | The union of all parts' attribute dependencies, unmodifiable, never null. |
| `public java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency> getContextDependencies()` | The union of all parts' context dependencies, unmodifiable, never null. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet getGlobalTrail()` | The union of the parts' global trails, or null if no part has one. |
| `public static <L extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<?>> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeCachingStrategy getCompositeCachingStrategy(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>, java.util.Collection<L>)` | Computes the combined caching strategy of the given loaders as described for `getCachingStrategy` (argument 1 is only used for a warning logged when both `MUST_NOT` and `SHOULD` occur). Returns `MAY` for an empty collection. |
| `public static <L extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<?>> java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>> getCompositeDependencies(java.util.Collection<L>)` | The union of the given loaders' attribute dependencies (nulls ignored), as an unmodifiable set. |
| `public static <L extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<?>> java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContextDependency> getCompositeContextDependencies(java.util.Collection<L>)` | The union of the given loaders' context dependencies (nulls ignored), as an unmodifiable set. |
| `public static <L extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeLoader<?>> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.TrailItemSet getCompositeGlobalTrail(java.util.Collection<L>)` | The union of the given loaders' non-null global trails, or null if none has one. |

The six loader kinds, each with the kind interface it corresponds to and a weight expressing generality (higher is more general; a loader of lower weight can be adapted to a higher one). Every loader must implement exactly one kind interface.

| `SINGLE_ROW (enum constant)` | `SingleRowAttributeLoader`, weight 3. |
| `ITEM (enum constant)` | `ItemAttributeLoader`, weight 2. |
| `DERIVED (enum constant)` | `DerivedAttributeLoader`, weight 1. |

Throws IllegalArgumentException if it implements none of the kind interfaces; NullPointerException for null. |

Throws IllegalArgumentException if none matches. With assertions enabled, a class implementing more than one kind also fails. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce`

Aggregate loaders that compute a row's value by reducing the values of its subtree, with pluggable reduction strategies (whole subtree, children only, leaves only, strict subtree) selected by the attribute spec's `type` parameter.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReducingAggregateLoader`

```java
public abstract class ReducingAggregateLoader<T> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.basic.AbstractAggregateLoader<T> implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ValueReducer<T>
```

Base class for aggregates defined by a `ValueReducer` (which this class implements) and a per-row self value. The reduction strategy comes from the spec's `type` parameter (see `ReductionStrategy.forAttributeSpec`); an unknown type makes the constructor throw. Children that are automation rows (generators and effectors, see `CoreIdentities.isAutomation`) are ignored. If any remaining child value is an error, that error is the result.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ReducingAggregateLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>)` | Creates the loader and selects the reduction strategy from the spec's `type` parameter (default `subtree`). Throws IllegalArgumentException for a null spec or an unknown type. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> loadValue(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AggregateAttributeContext)` | Drops values of automation children, returns the first child error if there is one, otherwise applies the reduction strategy to the row's self value (obtained lazily from `getSelfValue`), the remaining child values and this reducer. |
| `protected abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> getSelfValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AggregateAttributeContext)` | Subclass hook: the current row's own value to be combined with its children's. Must not return null (an undefined value means no contribution). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy`

```java
public interface ReductionStrategy<T>
```

One way of combining a row's own value with its children's values into an aggregate. Strategies are stateless singletons obtained from the static methods. The value of each row may carry extra loader data that later rows of the same attribute read, so a strategy must be used consistently for all rows of an attribute. Four exist, named by the spec parameter `type`: `subtree` (default), `children`, `leaves` and `strict`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> apply(java.util.function.Supplier<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ValueReducer<T>)` | Computes the row's aggregate. Argument 1: supplies the row's own value (called lazily, at most as needed). Argument 2: the children's values as computed by the same strategy (not null; may be empty). Argument 3: the reducer. Never returns null. If the self value is read and is an error, the error is returned (for `strict` and `children`, it is carried as loader data instead); `leaves` does not read the self value of a row that has children. |
| `public static String getStrategyType(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | The value of the spec's `type` parameter as a string, or `subtree` if absent. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy<T> forAttributeSpec(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | The strategy named by the spec's `type` parameter (see `forStrategyType`). |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy<T> forStrategyType(String)` | Returns the strategy for `children`, `leaves`, `strict` or `subtree`. Throws IllegalArgumentException for any other name (case-sensitive). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy.AbstractReductionStrategy`

```java
public abstract static class ReductionStrategy.AbstractReductionStrategy<T> implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy<T>
```

Package-level base of the four strategies with shared helpers; it is not meant to be extended outside the API (its helpers are not public).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public AbstractReductionStrategy()` | Creates a strategy; only used by the built-in strategies. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy.ChildrenReductionStrategy`

```java
public static class ReductionStrategy.ChildrenReductionStrategy<T> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy.AbstractReductionStrategy<T>
```

Strategy `children`: a row's value is the reduction of its direct children's own values (not their subtrees); the row's own value is not included in its result but is attached as loader data for use by its parent.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ChildrenReductionStrategy()` | Not for public use; obtain the shared instance with `ReductionStrategy.forStrategyType("children")`. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> apply(java.util.function.Supplier<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ValueReducer<T>)` | Reduces the own values carried by the children (an error carried by a child becomes the result; a reducer ClassCastException is logged and gives an error value) and attaches the row's own value as loader data. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy.LeavesReductionStrategy`

```java
public static class ReductionStrategy.LeavesReductionStrategy<T> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy.AbstractReductionStrategy<T>
```

Strategy `leaves`: a leaf row's value is its own (converted) value; a parent's value is the reduction of its children's values, ignoring the parent's own value. Thus only leaves contribute.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public LeavesReductionStrategy()` | Not for public use; obtain the shared instance with `ReductionStrategy.forStrategyType("leaves")`. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> apply(java.util.function.Supplier<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ValueReducer<T>)` | With no children: the reducer's `convert` of the own value (an own error is returned as is). Otherwise: the reducer's `reduce` of the children's plain values (null entries for children without value). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy.StrictReductionStrategy`

```java
public static class ReductionStrategy.StrictReductionStrategy<T> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy.AbstractReductionStrategy<T>
```

Strategy `strict`: a row's value is the reduction over its descendants only, excluding the row's own value. Each row also carries, as loader data, its full subtree value including itself, which its parent reduces. Leaves have an undefined value.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public StrictReductionStrategy()` | Not for public use; obtain the shared instance with `ReductionStrategy.forStrategyType("strict")`. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T> apply(java.util.function.Supplier<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeValue<T>>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ValueReducer<T>)` | With no children: an undefined value carrying the converted own value. Otherwise: the reduction of the children's carried subtree values (an error carried by a child becomes the result), carrying as loader data the merge of the own value with that reduction. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ReductionStrategy.SubtreeReductionStrategy`


| member | meaning |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.reduce.ValueReducer`

```java
public interface ValueReducer<T>
```

Defines how a list of values is combined into one (sum, min, max, ...); used by the reduction strategies. Implemented by `ReducingAggregateLoader` subclasses or as a lambda; only `reduce` is required. Values passed in may be null (rows without a value).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract T reduce(java.util.List<T>)` | Combines the values (elements may be null) into one; returns null if there is no result. |
| `public default T convert(java.util.function.Supplier<T>)` | Turns a leaf's own value (from the supplier) into an aggregate value. Default: the own value unchanged. |
| `public default T merge(java.util.function.Supplier<T>, java.util.function.Supplier<T>)` | Combines the row's own value (argument 1) with the already reduced children value (argument 2). Default: `reduce` of a two-element list of both (either may be null). |
| `public default T merge(java.util.function.Supplier<T>, java.util.List<T>)` | Combines the row's own value (argument 1) with the children's values (argument 2). Default: `merge(self, () -> reduce(list))`. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription`

Long-lived, incremental attribute loading: a client subscribes to a set of attributes for a set of rows of a forest, asks for loading in the background, and then polls for the values that changed since a given version.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscription`

```java
public interface AttributeSubscription extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.VersionedDataSource<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscriptionUpdate>
```

A long-lived request for values of a set of attributes (the subscription's attributes) for a set of rows (its rows) of one forest (its forest spec), together called its window. The client changes the window with `changeSubscription`, starts background loading with `loadValues`, and reads values with `getUpdate`: either all values or only those changed since a version it already has. Created by `AttributeSubscriptionService`; implemented by the plugin; thread-safe. Values are computed as the subscription's owner. After it is dropped or expires the subscription is deactivated: changes are ignored, loading does nothing and updates are empty.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long getSubscriptionId()` | The subscription's ID, used with `AttributeSubscriptionService`. |
| `public abstract void changeSubscription(java.util.function.Consumer<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscriptionPatch>)` | Changes the window: calls the consumer with a patch pre-filled with the current window, then applies the result atomically. The consumer may be called more than once if another thread changes the subscription at the same time, so it must have no other side effects. Values for rows and attributes no longer in the window are discarded; if the forest changes in a way that changes rows' meaning (another structure, version, query, clipboard session, user, or switching to a secured forest), all values are discarded. Loading tasks that are no longer needed are cancelled. Does nothing (logs a warning) on a deactivated subscription. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec getForest()` | The forest spec of the current window; an empty text query forest if none was set. |
| `public abstract java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>> getAttributes()` | The attributes of the current window, as an unmodifiable list in the order they were added. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongList getRows()` | The rows of the current window, sorted ascending without duplicates. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscriptionUpdate getUpdate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion)` | The values known now, relative to the given version (a version returned earlier by this subscription; null or `DataVersion.ZERO` asks for everything). If the version is from another subscription instance or too old (more than the last 1000 changes, dark feature `structure.attribute.subscription.maxHistory`, minimum 10), a full update with all current values in the window is returned. If nothing changed, an empty incremental update is returned. Otherwise an incremental update contains the current values of the cells that changed. The update's version is the one to pass next time. Does not start loading. Deactivated subscriptions return an empty non-full update with version zero. |
| `public abstract java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion> loadValues()` | Starts loading values for the current window in the background (on the plugin's job pool, as the owner) unless the same attributes are already being loaded, and returns a future completed with the subscription's data version when loading finishes (also when it fails; failures are logged, not reported through the future). The future is cancelled if the loading is cancelled by a window change or deactivation. Returns an already completed future if there are no attributes or the subscription is deactivated, and a failed future if the job cannot be scheduled. |
| `public abstract boolean isLoadingValues()` | True while a background loading started by `loadValues` is running. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues getFullUpdate(long, java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit) throws InterruptedException, java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException` | Starts loading (as `loadValues`), waits up to the given timeout (first argument, in the given unit) for it to finish, and returns all values currently in the window. Throws `InterruptedException` if interrupted, `TimeoutException` if loading does not finish in time, and `CancellationException` if the loading is cancelled. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues getFullUpdate()` | Like the timed variant with a timeout of one day, but reports interruption (after restoring the thread's interrupt flag), timeout and cancellation as `StructureRuntimeException`. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongSet getInaccessibleRows()` | The rows in the window that the owner may not see, as reported by the latest loading; their values are inaccessible. Empty after the window changes until the next loading. |
| `public abstract java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeErrorInfo> drainAttributeErrors()` | Returns and forgets the loading errors collected since the previous call. Only the first error ever seen for each attribute is reported, once per subscription lifetime. Never null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscriptionPatch`

```java
public interface AttributeSubscriptionPatch
```

A mutable description of a subscription's window, given to the consumer passed to `AttributeSubscription.changeSubscription`. It starts with the current window; each method changes it and returns the same patch for chaining. Valid only during that call. Row lists are de-duplicated and sorted when the patch is applied.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscriptionPatch setForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec)` | Sets the forest spec; null means an empty text query forest. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscriptionPatch setAttributes(java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>)` | Replaces the attributes with a copy of the given collection (not null). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscriptionService`

```java
public interface AttributeSubscriptionService
```

Creates and finds attribute subscriptions. The plugin provides the single implementation as a component (also available from `StructureComponents.getAttributeSubscriptionService()`); thread-safe. Subscriptions live in memory on one node only, belong to the user who created them (the current `StructureAuth` user at creation), and expire after one hour without access; at most 10000 exist at a time (dark feature `structure.attribute.maxSubscriptionCount`); beyond that, older subscriptions are evicted. An evicted or expired subscription is deactivated.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscription createSubscription()` | Creates a new empty subscription owned by the current user, with a new ID unique on this node since start-up (1, 2, 3, ...). Throws `StructureRuntimeException` if it cannot be created. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.subscription.AttributeSubscription getSubscription(Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | The subscription with the given ID. Throws `StructureException` with the 'subscription does not exist or is not accessible' error if the ID is null, unknown, expired, or the subscription belongs to another user than the current one (anonymous counts as a user). |
| `public abstract void dropSubscription(Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Deletes the subscription with the given ID and stops its loading; afterwards it behaves as deactivated. Throws `StructureException` as `getSubscription` does. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.auth`

Control over the identity under which the plugin's code runs: who the current user is for the plugin, whether permission checks are bypassed, and running code as another user or with security overridden.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.auth.AuthContext`

```java
public interface AuthContext
```

An immutable snapshot of an authentication context: a user (possibly anonymous) and a flag saying whether permission checks are bypassed, plus a way to run code under that context. Obtain the current one with `StructureAuth.currentContext()`, create one with `AuthContext.Custom`, or use the live `CURRENT` constant. Implementations are thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.auth.AuthContext CURRENT` | A shared instance that always reflects the calling thread's context at the moment of the call: its `getUser()` and `isSecurityOverridden()` delegate to `StructureAuth`, and its `sudo` simply runs the callable in the caller's current context without changing anything. |
| `public abstract com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser getUser()` | The user of this context, or null for anonymous. |
| `public abstract boolean isSecurityOverridden()` | True if code running in this context should skip permission checks. |
| `public abstract <R, E extends Exception> R sudo(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.CallableE<R, E>) throws E` | Runs the callable with this context's user and security-override flag in effect on the current thread (as `StructureAuth.sudo(user, flag, f)` does), restores the previous context afterwards even on failure, and returns the callable's result. Exceptions thrown by the callable propagate unchanged. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.auth.AuthContext.Custom`

```java
public static class AuthContext.Custom implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.auth.AuthContext
```

A fixed `AuthContext` holding the user and override flag given at construction. Immutable and thread-safe; its methods are final.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public Custom(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, boolean)` | Creates a context for the given user (first argument, null meaning anonymous) with the given security-override flag (second argument). |
| `public final com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser getUser()` | The user given at construction, or null for anonymous. |
| `public final boolean isSecurityOverridden()` | The override flag given at construction. |
| `public final <R, E extends Exception> R sudo(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.CallableE<R, E>) throws E` | Runs the callable through `StructureAuth.sudo` with this context's user and override flag, returning its result and propagating its exception. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.auth.StructureAuth`

```java
public class StructureAuth
```

Static utility that defines the identity the plugin acts for on the current thread. By default it is the user logged in to Jira's authentication context, with security not overridden; `sudo` temporarily replaces both for the duration of a call. All plugin services that check permissions consult this class, so code running inside `sudo` with the override flag set sees all data regardless of permissions. The state is per thread and is not inherited by other threads. Not meant to be instantiated.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public StructureAuth()` | Public default constructor (the class has only static members; creating an instance is pointless). |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser getUser()` | The user the plugin acts for on this thread: the user set by the innermost active `sudo` (null for anonymous), or, outside any `sudo`, the user logged in to Jira's authentication context. If Jira's authentication context cannot be obtained, returns null (anonymous) and logs an error once. |
| `public static String getUserKey()` | The Jira user key of `getUser()`, or null when that is anonymous. |
| `public static boolean isSecurityOverridden()` | True only inside a `sudo` call that turned the override on. When true, plugin services skip permission checks for the current user. |
| `public static <R, E extends Exception> R sudo(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, boolean, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.CallableE<R, E>) throws E` | Runs the callable (third argument) as the given user (first argument, null meaning anonymous) with security override set to the second argument, and returns its result; exceptions from the callable propagate unchanged. If both the user and the override flag already equal the current ones, the callable simply runs. Otherwise, for the duration of the call both this class and Jira's authentication context report the given user, and the logging context shows the change of user; afterwards the previous state of both is restored, even on failure. Calls may be nested. Requires Jira's authentication context to be available. |
| `public static <R, E extends Exception> R sudo(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.CallableE<R, E>) throws E` | Runs the callable as the current user (`getUser()`) with security override turned on, so that permission checks are skipped; returns its result and propagates its exception. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.auth.AuthContext currentContext()` | A new immutable `AuthContext` capturing the current thread's user and override flag at the time of the call (outside `sudo`: the Jira logged-in user and no override). It can be passed to other threads and used there with `sudo` to run code in the same context. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup`

Backing up and restoring all of the plugin's data as an XML document (optionally zipped), and an extension point through which other plugins add their own data to the same backup and get it back on restore or migration.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation`

```java
public interface BackupOperation
```

A configurable, single-use backup job created by `StructureBackupManager.backup()`. The setters return the same object for chaining; then `backup()` writes to the configured file or `backupToStream` writes to a stream. Not thread-safe; use from one thread. By default everything is included (all structures and views, application configuration, perspectives, favourites, saved columns, generic item history, data of all extension providers) except structure history. The backup is an XML document with root element `structure-backup` (format version `5.0`) that records the time and the user key of the current `StructureAuth` user (or `system`). Data is read with security overridden, so the backup contains all data regardless of the caller's permissions.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setFile(java.io.File)` | Sets the target file for `backup()`. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the file is null or not an absolute path. If the file name has no dot, `.zip` or `.xml` (depending on `setUseZip` at the time of `backup()`) is appended when writing. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setUseZip(boolean)` | True to write a zip archive containing a single XML entry, false (default) to write plain XML. In a file backup the entry is named after the file with `.xml` replacing a `.zip` suffix (or appended); in a stream backup it is `backup.xml`. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setBackupStructureIds(com.almworks.integers.LongIterable)` | Limits the backup to the structures with the given IDs: their definitions, forests, synchronizers, properties, view associations, notes and so on. Null (default) means all structures. The IDs are copied. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setBackupViewIds(com.almworks.integers.LongIterable)` | Limits the backed-up views to those with the given IDs. Null (default) means all views. The IDs are copied. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setBackupAppConfiguration(boolean)` | Whether to include the plugin's global settings: stored properties, configuration (enabled projects, permissions and so on), attribute sensitivity settings and dark features set as application properties. Default true. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setBackupPerspectives(boolean)` | Whether to include perspectives (saved, shareable view states). Default true. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setBackupFavorites(boolean)` | Whether to include users' favourite structures. Default true. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setBackupSavedColumns(boolean)` | Whether to include saved columns. Default true. When false, references to saved columns are also removed from the column definitions of backed-up views. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setBackupHistory(boolean)` | Whether to include the change history of the backed-up structures. Default false. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setBackupGenericItemHistory(boolean)` | Whether to include the change history of generic items (such as folders) that appear in the backed-up structures. Default true. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation setBackupExtensions(java.util.Set<String>)` | Limits which extension providers (`StructureBackupProvider`) contribute data, by the plugin key of the plugin that declares them. Null (default) means all installed providers; an empty set means none. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation backup() throws Exception` | Writes the backup to the configured file and returns this operation. Missing parent directories are created. On success `getFinalFile()` returns the written file. On failure the partial file is deleted and an exception is thrown: `IllegalStateException` if no file was set, `IOException` for file-system or XML-writing problems or a target directory that cannot be created, `StructureException` or a database exception for data access problems, and an unchecked exception wrapping the original cause if an extension provider fails. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation backupToStream(java.io.OutputStream) throws Exception` | Writes the backup to the given stream (null throws `IllegalArgumentException` with the message `output stream cannot be null`) instead of a file, zipped if `setUseZip(true)`, and returns this operation. The stream is not closed. Clears any previously configured file, so a later `getFinalFile()` fails. Exceptions as for `backup()`; the stream may contain partial data on failure. |
| `public abstract java.io.File getFinalFile()` | The file the backup was written to after a successful `backup()`; before that, the file that would be written (the configured file with the default extension appended if needed). Throws `IllegalStateException` if no file is set. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupReader`

```java
public interface BackupReader
```

Streaming XML reader given to a `StructureBackupProvider` during restore or migration. It reads the provider's own section of the backup document; the current position is a start element (initially the provider's `extension` element). Implemented by the plugin; marked internal; valid only during the provider call. XML errors propagate as exceptions.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void readSection(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupReader.ElementReader)` | Reads the content of the current element up to its end tag, calling the callback once for each start element found inside it, in document order. When called, the reader is positioned on that element, so the callback may use `getAttributeValue`, `getElementText`, `skipSection` or a nested `readSection` to consume it; nested elements that the callback does not consume are reported to the callback as well. Throws `IllegalStateException` if the reader is not on a start element. |
| `public abstract void skipSection()` | Skips the current element and everything inside it. Throws `IllegalStateException` if the reader is not on a start element. |
| `public abstract String getElementText()` | Reads and returns the text content of the current element, which must contain only text, and moves to its end tag. |
| `public abstract String getAttributeValue(String)` | The value of the current element's attribute with the given local name, or null if absent. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupReader.ElementReader`

```java
public interface BackupReader.ElementReader
```

Callback for `BackupReader.readSection`, called for each element in a section. Implemented by the backup provider, typically as a lambda.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void readElement(String)` | Called with the local name of the element the reader is now positioned on. The implementation may read attributes, text or the element's subtree through the `BackupReader`. |

```java
public interface BackupWriter
```

Streaming XML writer given to a `StructureBackupProvider` during backup. Writes go directly into the backup document inside the provider's `extension` element. Implemented by the plugin; marked internal; valid only during the `backup` call. XML streaming errors propagate as exceptions.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void writeStartElement(String)` | Opens a new element with the given local name (no namespace). |
| `public abstract void writeEndElement()` | Closes the most recently opened element. Throws `IllegalStateException` if no element opened through this writer is still open. |
| `public abstract void writeElement(String, String)` | Writes a complete element with the given name (first argument) and text content (second argument); null text gives an empty element. |
| `public abstract void writeAttribute(String, String)` | Adds an attribute with the given name and value to the element just opened; must be called right after `writeStartElement`, before any content. |
| `public abstract void writeCharacters(String)` | Writes text content (escaped as needed) into the currently open element. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.ErrorsContainer`

```java
public interface ErrorsContainer
```

Problems collected while restoring or migrating a backup, grouped by kind. Obtained from `RestoreOperation.getErrorsContainer()`. The returned collections are the live, mutable internal collections of the operation; read them after the operation has finished. Keys that are structure IDs refer to the IDs in the backup.

| member | meaning |

| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<String> getInvalidIssueMessages()` | Issues referenced by the backup that do not exist on this instance: map from issue ID to a human-readable message (with the issue key and summary when the backup recorded them). |
| `public abstract java.util.Map<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, String> getInvalidItemMessages()` | Non-issue items (projects, components, versions and other item types) referenced by the backup that could not be resolved: map from item identity to a human-readable message. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet> getInvalidStructureItems()` | For each structure, the set of items in its forest or manual adjustments that could not be resolved. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet> getInvalidHistoryItems()` | For each structure, the set of items mentioned in its history that could not be resolved. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<String> getInvalidSynchronizerMessages()` | Synchronizers that could not be restored: map from synchronizer ID to an error message. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<? extends com.almworks.integers.LongList> getInvalidStructureSynchronizers()` | For each structure, the IDs of its synchronizers that could not be restored. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<java.util.List<String>> getStructureOtherProblems()` | For each structure, a list of other problem messages. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<java.util.Set<String>> getStructureFieldResolutionProblems()` | For each structure, the distinct messages about fields (for example custom fields used in its configuration) that could not be resolved, in the order first found. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<String> getOtherProblems()` | Problem messages not tied to a structure, including messages reported by extension providers through `ErrorsReporter` and failures of extension providers. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongSortedSet getInvalidStructures()` | The sorted set of IDs of all structures that have at least one problem in any of the per-structure maps above. Computed anew on each call. |

Mapping from identities in a backup to identities on the target instance, given to `StructureBackupProvider.migrate` when backed-up data is merged into an instance that already has data (migration) rather than replacing it. Created by the plugin; marked internal. The maps are read-only.

| member | meaning |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.RestoreOperation`

```java
public interface RestoreOperation
```

A single-use restore job created by `StructureBackupManager.restore()`. Restoring replaces all of the plugin's data on the instance with the contents of a backup file. `setFile` must be called first; calling other methods before it fails with `NullPointerException`. Not thread-safe. Progress can be watched (and the operation cancelled) from another thread through `getProgressGauge()`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.RestoreOperation setFile(java.io.File)` | Sets the backup file to read (plain XML or zip) and prepares the operation to restore everything, including history. Returns this operation. Nothing is read yet. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.RestoreOperation restore() throws java.io.IOException` | Performs the restore and returns this operation. While it runs the plugin's storage is locked (see `StructurePluginHelper.isStructureLocked()`). The whole file is first validated; then all existing plugin data is deleted and replaced with the backup's contents, caches are cleared on all cluster nodes, and extension providers receive their sections through `StructureBackupProvider.restore`. Items that cannot be found on this instance and other non-fatal problems are recorded in `getErrorsContainer()` rather than failing the restore. Throws `IOException` if the file cannot be read or is not a valid backup (in which case existing data is untouched if the problem is found during validation). If cancelled through the progress gauge, returns normally with the restore incomplete. Performs no permission check. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.RestoreOperation checkBackupFile() throws java.io.IOException` | Checks, without changing any data, that the file can be opened (a file named `.zip` must be a non-empty valid zip; other files are read as zip if possible, otherwise as plain XML) and that its root element is a backup of a supported format version (3.0, 3.3 or 5.0). Returns this operation; throws `IOException` describing the problem otherwise. It does not validate the rest of the document. |
| `public abstract java.util.Map<Long, String> getStructureNames()` | Map from structure ID (as in the backup) to structure name, for structures with a non-empty name read so far. Filled while `restore()` reads the file; empty before. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.ErrorsContainer getErrorsContainer()` | The collection of problems found while reading and restoring the backup. Filled during `restore()`; inspect it afterwards. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProgressGauge getProgressGauge()` | The progress indicator of this restore; it can also be used to request cancellation. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.RestoreOperation setRestoreHistory(boolean)` | Whether to restore structure history contained in the backup (default true after `setFile`). Must be called after `setFile`. Returns this operation. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.StructureBackupManager`

```java
public interface StructureBackupManager
```

Factory of backup and restore operations. The plugin provides the single implementation as a component (also available from `StructureComponents.getBackupManager()`). It performs no permission checks itself: any code that can call it can export or replace all of the plugin's data, so callers must check that the user is a Jira administrator.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupOperation backup()` | Creates a new, unconfigured `BackupOperation`. Each call returns a fresh object that must be configured and run once. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.RestoreOperation restore()` | Creates a new, unconfigured `RestoreOperation`. Each call returns a fresh object. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.StructureBackupProvider`

```java
public interface StructureBackupProvider
```

Extension point that lets another plugin store its own data in the plugin's backups. A plugin declares an implementation as a `structure-backup-provider` module; providers are identified by the key of the declaring plugin (one per plugin). During backup the plugin opens an `extension` element (with the plugin key and version) and calls `backup`; during restore it calls `restore` for each extension section whose provider is installed; during migration it calls `migrate`. Marked internal.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final String PARAM_INCLUDE_DASHBOARD_GADGETS = "includeDashboardGadgets"` | Name of the parameter (value `includeDashboardGadgets`, a `Boolean`) in the map passed to the three-argument `backup`: true when the backup also includes dashboard gadget data, so the provider should include its gadget-related data too. |
| `public abstract void backup(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupWriter, com.almworks.integers.LongSet)` | Writes the provider's data through the writer (first argument). The second argument is the set of structure IDs being backed up, or null for all structures; data tied to other structures should be left out. Any exception aborts the whole backup. Elements left open are closed by the plugin (with a warning). |
| `public default void backup(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupWriter, com.almworks.integers.LongSet, java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Same as the two-argument `backup` with extra parameters (third argument, see `PARAM_INCLUDE_DASHBOARD_GADGETS`). This is the variant the plugin calls; by default it ignores the parameters and calls the two-argument variant. |
| `public abstract void restore(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupReader, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.ErrorsReporter)` | Restores the provider's data from its section of a backup being restored over all existing data. The reader (first argument) is positioned on the provider's `extension` start element. Non-fatal problems go to the reporter (second argument). If the method throws, the plugin records the failure as a problem, skips the rest of the section and continues the restore. |
| `public abstract void migrate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupReader, java.util.Map<Long, Long>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.ErrorsReporter)` | Deprecated. Like `restore`, but the data is merged into an instance with existing data; the map (second argument) translates structure IDs in the backup to IDs on this instance. Must be implemented; the plugin reaches it only through the default `MigrationMapping` variant. |
| `public default void migrate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.BackupReader, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.MigrationMapping, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.backup.ErrorsReporter)` | Merges the provider's backed-up data into this instance, translating structure IDs and item identities through the mapping (second argument). This is the variant the plugin calls during migration; by default it calls the deprecated variant with the structure ID map only. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.cache`

Control over the plugin's in-memory caches, including clearing them across all nodes of a Jira cluster.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.cache.StructureCacheHelper`

```java
public interface StructureCacheHelper
```

Clears the plugin's in-memory caches, locally or on every node of a Jira Data Center cluster. Marked internal. The plugin provides the single implementation as a component (also returned by `StructurePluginHelper.getCacheHelper()`); thread-safe. Clearing affects only cached, recomputable data, never stored data; failures of individual caches are logged and ignored.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void clearAllStructureCaches()` | Clears all of the plugin's caches on this node, for all users. |
| `public abstract void clearAllStructureCachesOnAllNodes()` | Clears all of the plugin's caches on this node and sends a cluster message so every other node does the same. |
| `public default void clearUserStructureCachesOnAllNodes(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Same as `clearUserStructureCachesOnAllNodes(String)` with the user's key. The user must not be null. |
| `public abstract void clearUserStructureCachesOnAllNodes(String)` | Clears the caches that hold data specific to the user with the given user key, on this node and, through a cluster message, on all other nodes. On each node, nothing happens if no user has that key. |
| `public abstract void clearCurrentUserStructureCaches()` | Clears the user-specific caches of the current `StructureAuth` user on this node. For an anonymous user nothing is cleared (an information message is logged). |
| `public abstract void clearUserStructureCaches(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Clears the caches that hold data specific to the given user (not null) on this node only. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.cache.access`

Cached checks of which rows, items and issues a user cannot see. Used to hide inaccessible content of forests.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.cache.access.ForestAccessCache`

```java
public interface ForestAccessCache
```

A cache that answers which rows, items or issues a user is not allowed to see, used to hide inaccessible content of forests. Marked internal. The plugin provides the single implementation as a component; thread-safe. Results are cached per user and invalidated when items change; the whole cache is also dropped automatically every five minutes. Anything that cannot be checked (missing rows, unknown item types, errors in visibility checks, search failures) is reported as invisible, so the check fails closed.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void clear()` | Drops all cached visibility data for all users. |
| `public default void clear(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Drops cached visibility data for the given user (not null; null fails with `NullPointerException`). |
| `public abstract void clear(String)` | Drops cached visibility data for the user with the given user key. Does nothing for null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongSet getInvisibleRows(com.almworks.integers.LongIterable, String) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.cache.access.ForestAccessCache.UserLookupException` | Like the `ApplicationUser` variant, for the user with the given user key (second argument); null means anonymous. Throws `ForestAccessCache.UserLookupException` if the key is not null and no such user exists. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongSet getInvisibleRows(com.almworks.integers.LongIterable, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | The subset of the given row IDs (first argument) whose items the user (second argument, null meaning anonymous) cannot see, never null. Rows that do not exist are included. Duplicates are ignored, and negative (temporary) row IDs must not be passed: they are ignored. A loop-marker row is judged by the item of the row it points to. Security override is not applied: the user's real permissions are checked. Returns an empty set for null or empty input. |
| `public abstract void collectInvisibleRows(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, String, com.almworks.integers.LongCollector) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.cache.access.ForestAccessCache.UserLookupException` | Like the `ApplicationUser` variant, for the user with the given user key (second argument); null means anonymous. Throws `ForestAccessCache.UserLookupException` if the key is not null and no such user exists. |
| `public abstract void collectInvisibleRows(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, com.almworks.integers.LongCollector)` | Adds to the collector (third argument) the IDs of all rows of the forest (first argument) whose items the user (second argument, null meaning anonymous) cannot see, in forest order. Uses the items carried by the forest itself rather than looking rows up, so it also works for temporary rows. Security override is not applied. |
| `public abstract void collectInvisibleIssues(com.almworks.integers.LongIterable, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, boolean, com.almworks.integers.LongCollector)` | Adds to the collector (fourth argument) the IDs among the given issue IDs (first argument) that the user (second argument, null meaning anonymous) cannot see or that do not exist, checked through the Jira index. If the third argument is true, only existence is checked (security override). Duplicates are reported once, in ascending order. If the search fails, all checked issues are reported as invisible. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet getInvisibleItems(java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | The subset of the given item identities that do not exist or that the user (second argument, null meaning anonymous) may not see, judged by each item's type. Items of unknown or unavailable types, and items whose type fails during the check, are counted as invisible. Never null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.cache.access.ForestAccessCache.UserLookupException`

```java
public static class ForestAccessCache.UserLookupException extends Exception
```

Checked exception thrown by the user-key variants of `ForestAccessCache` methods when a non-null user key does not belong to any existing user. Carries no message.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public UserLookupException()` | Creates the exception with no message or cause. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.calendar`

Extension point for work calendars. A calendar measures how much working time lies between two moments; formulas and time-in-status columns use calendars to compute durations. Other plugins can contribute calendars through a plugin module.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.calendar.Calendar`

```java
public interface Calendar
```

A work calendar that measures working time between two instants. Implemented by plugins that provide calendars (and by the plugin itself for its built-in calendars); instances are obtained from a `CalendarProvider`. The plugin calls it when computing time-in-status values and calendar-aware durations in formulas. Implementations must be thread-safe and fast, since they may be called for many rows.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean isTimeZoneDependant()` | True if the result of `getDuration` depends on the viewing user's time zone; the plugin then treats values computed with this calendar as depending on the user's time zone and does not share them between users of different zones. The built-in calendars return false. |
| `public abstract long getDuration(long, long)` | The amount of working time, in milliseconds, between the start instant (first argument) and the finish instant (second argument), both in milliseconds since the epoch. The plugin always passes start not later than finish (it swaps and negates itself when needed); the built-in calendars throw `java.security.InvalidParameterException` when finish is before start. The plain built-in calendar returns the elapsed time; the built-in work calendar counts only 09:00 to 17:00 on Monday to Friday in Jira's default time zone. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.calendar.CalendarInfo`

```java
public interface CalendarInfo
```

Descriptive information about one calendar offered by a `CalendarProvider`: its ID within the provider, name and description. Implemented by calendar providers; the plugin lists them in its calendar picker and resolves calendar names in formulas from them.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long getId()` | The calendar's ID, unique within its provider. Together with the provider's module key it forms the calendar's full ID, written as `<module key>/<id>`. The built-in plain calendar has ID 0 and the built-in work calendar ID 1. |
| `public abstract String getName()` | The calendar's display name, possibly localised for the current user. Formulas may refer to a calendar by this name (matched case- and space-insensitively as the formula language normalises names). Never null. |
| `public abstract String getDescription()` | A human-readable description of the calendar, or null if there is none. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.calendar.CalendarProvider`

```java
public interface CalendarProvider
```

Extension point: a source of calendars. Other plugins declare an implementation as a `structure-calendar-provider` module in their plugin descriptor; the plugin also ships a built-in provider with a plain (elapsed time) calendar and a work-hours calendar. A calendar is addressed by the provider's module key and the calendar's ID. The plugin calls the provider when listing calendars and when resolving a calendar referenced by a column, attribute or formula. Implementations must be thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.calendar.CalendarInfo> getCalendarInfos()` | Descriptions of all calendars this provider offers, in the order they should be listed. Never null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.calendar.Calendar getCalendar(long)` | The calendar with the given ID (as reported by `CalendarInfo.getId()`), or null if this provider has no such calendar. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.darkfeature`

Access to hidden tuning switches ("dark features"): named settings read from Jira application properties or JVM system properties, used to change the plugin's behaviour without a user interface.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.darkfeature.DarkFeatures`

```java
public class DarkFeatures
```

Static utility for reading dark features: named settings that tune the plugin. Each lookup first reads the Jira application property (string) with that name; if it is missing or empty, the JVM system property with the same name is used; if that is missing too, the given default. Values are read on every call (callers often cache them at start-up). Failures to reach Jira's application properties are logged and treated as "not set". Not meant to be instantiated.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public DarkFeatures()` | Public default constructor (the class has only static members; creating an instance is pointless). |
| `public static long getLong(String, long)` | The named setting (first argument) as a long. If the application property is set but is not a valid number, the default (second argument) is returned without consulting the system property; if only the system property is set and it is not a valid number, the default is returned. An application property is read as a plain decimal number; a system property is decoded the way `Long.getLong` does, so `0x10` and `#10` are 16 and `010` is 8. |
| `public static int getInteger(String, int)` | The named setting as an int, with the same fallback rules and number formats as `getLong` (a system property decoded the way `Integer.getInteger` does). |
| `public static boolean getBoolean(String)` | The named setting as a boolean, defaulting to false. Same as `getBoolean(name, false)`. |
| `public static boolean getBoolean(String, boolean)` | The named setting as a boolean: a non-empty application property is true only if it equals `true` ignoring case; otherwise the system property is read the same way; if neither is set, the default (second argument) is returned. |
| `public static String getProperty(String)` | The named setting as a string, or null if neither the application property nor the system property is set (an empty application property counts as not set). |
| `public static String getProperty(String, String)` | The named setting as a string, or the default (second argument) if neither property is set. A system property set to the empty string counts as set and is returned as `""`. Never null when the default is not null. |
| `public static String getApplicationProperty(String)` | Only the Jira application property with the given name, or null if it is not set or Jira's application properties are not available (problems are logged at most occasionally, never thrown). Marked internal. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect`

Effects: serializable descriptions of a single change to Jira or to a structure (`StoredEffect`), the extension point that turns them into executable changes (`EffectProvider`, `Effect`, `EffectResponse`), and ready-made factory methods for common issue changes (`CoreEffects`). Effects are produced by effectors and applied later by the plugin's effector process engine.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.CoreEffects`

```java
public final class CoreEffects
```

Static factory methods that build `StoredEffect` values understood by the effect providers bundled with the plugin. It cannot be instantiated. Each method only builds an immutable description; nothing is changed until an effector process applies the effect, at which point the change is made on behalf of the process owner with Jira's normal issue update rules and permissions. Every result names a bundled provider module by its complete key (the plugin key followed by `:` and the module name given per method below) and carries the issue as parameter `issue` (the issue id, a `Long`). A null `issue` (or a null collection or custom field) causes a `NullPointerException`. The notification flag parameter is not set by these helpers. Methods that take a `CustomField` first check its type and throw `IllegalArgumentException` if the field's type is not the expected Jira custom field type (or, for version and group pickers, if its single/multiple setting does not match).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect emitWarning(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Builds a warning pseudo-effect. It is shown in the process preview but never applied and never produces an effect record; a preview that contains only warnings finishes without applying anything. Arguments: the localizable warning text (not null) and the identities of the items it concerns (not null, may be empty). Stored as module `warning-effect-provider` with parameters `i18nKey` (the text's key), `arguments` (the text's arguments converted with `String.valueOf`) and `affectedItems` (the item identities as strings). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect assignIssue(com.atlassian.jira.issue.Issue, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Builds an effect that sets the assignee of the given issue. Arguments: the issue (not null) and the new value; null means unassign. Stored as provider module `assignee-effect-provider` with parameter `assignee` holding the user key (omitted when null). Applying it is a no-op when the issue already has that value; the undo effect restores the previous value. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect setIssueReporter(com.atlassian.jira.issue.Issue, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Builds an effect that sets the reporter of the given issue. Arguments: the issue (not null) and the new value; null clears the reporter. Stored as provider module `reporter-effect-provider` with parameter `reporter` holding the user key (omitted when null). Applying it is a no-op when the issue already has that value; the undo effect restores the previous value. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect setIssuePriority(com.atlassian.jira.issue.Issue, com.atlassian.jira.issue.priority.Priority)` | Builds an effect that sets the priority of the given issue. Arguments: the issue (not null) and the new value; null clears the priority. Stored as provider module `priority-effect-provider` with parameter `priority` holding the priority id (omitted when null). Applying it is a no-op when the issue already has that value; the undo effect restores the previous value. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect setIssueDescription(com.atlassian.jira.issue.Issue, String)` | Builds an effect that sets the description of the given issue. Arguments: the issue (not null) and the new value; null clears it. Stored as provider module `description-effect-provider` with parameter `description` holding the text (omitted when null). Applying it is a no-op when the issue already has that value; the undo effect restores the previous value. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect setIssueEnvironment(com.atlassian.jira.issue.Issue, String)` | Builds an effect that sets the environment field of the given issue. Arguments: the issue (not null) and the new value; null clears it. Stored as provider module `environment-effect-provider` with parameter `environment` holding the text (omitted when null). Applying it is a no-op when the issue already has that value; the undo effect restores the previous value. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect setIssueResolution(com.atlassian.jira.issue.Issue, com.atlassian.jira.issue.resolution.Resolution)` | Builds an effect that sets the resolution of the given issue. Stored as provider module `resolution-effect-provider` with parameter `resolution` holding the resolution id (omitted when null). Applying it is a no-op when the issue already has that value; the undo effect restores the previous value. |

Arguments: the issue (not null) and the new value; a null status is stored as an absent parameter, which the bundled provider rejects (the effect turns into a warning in the preview). Stored as provider module `status-effect-provider` with parameter `status` holding the status id (omitted when null). Arguments: the issue (not null) and the new value; null clears it. Stored as provider module `remaining-estimate-effect-provider` with parameter `remainingEstimate` holding the duration in milliseconds (not seconds as Jira stores it; the bundled provider converts, and treats a zero estimate on the issue as no value) (omitted when null). ### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.Effect`

```java
public interface Effect
```

A ready-to-run change, returned inside a valid `EffectResponse` by an `EffectProvider`. Implemented by effect providers (usually as a lambda). The plugin calls it at most once, while applying an effector process, on a background thread with the process owner as the current user.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect apply() throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Performs the change and returns a `StoredEffect` that would undo it (the plugin saves it in the effect record and uses it for undo processes). Must not return null. Throw `StructureException` to report a failure: the plugin records an error record using the exception's localized text and continues with the next effect. Other runtime exceptions are also caught and recorded as a generic apply failure. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.EffectProvider`

```java
public interface EffectProvider
```

Extension point that knows how to validate, describe and execute one kind of `StoredEffect`. Other plugins register implementations as effect-provider modules in their plugin descriptor; a stored effect selects its provider by the module's complete key (`StoredEffect.getModuleKey()`). The plugin calls the provider while computing an effector preview (`optimize`, then `resolve` for validation) and again when applying (`resolve`, then `Effect.apply()`).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.EffectResponse resolve(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect)` | Checks the stored effect against the current state of Jira and the current user's permissions and returns an `EffectResponse`: valid (with the executable `Effect`, a success message, a description and the affected items), error (with the reason), or empty (nothing to do, e.g. the value is already set). Must not return null and should not change anything itself. It may be called more than once for the same effect (once during preview, once just before applying). During preview an error response turns the effect into a warning and an empty response drops the effect (unless it carries a `conflicts` parameter); during apply an empty response produces no record and an error response produces an error record. |
| `public default java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect> optimize(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect>)` | Given all effects of one preview that belong to this provider, in production order, returns the list to keep. Lets a provider merge or drop redundant effects (for example, several updates of the same field of the same issue). The default returns the input unchanged. The bundled providers keep the last value per issue and field and attach the overridden values to it as a `conflicts` parameter. Must not return null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.EffectResponse`

```java
public class EffectResponse
```

The outcome of `EffectProvider.resolve(StoredEffect)`: one of three immutable variants, `Valid`, `Error` or `Empty`, all of which carry a human-readable description of the effect and the list of affected items. Create instances with the static factories `valid`, `error` and `empty` (or the public constructors of `Error` and `Empty`); the base class itself cannot be instantiated or subclassed outside the API.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.Effect getEffect()` | The executable effect. Null in the base class and in `Error` and `Empty`; only `Valid` returns a non-null value. |
| `public java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity> getAffectedItems()` | Identities of the items (typically issues) the effect touches; never null, possibly empty. The list is returned as given to the factory (not copied). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText getDescription()` | Localizable text describing what the effect would do, used in previews. Never null. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText getSuccessMessage()` | Localizable text to record after the effect was applied successfully. Null except in `Valid`. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText getError()` | Localizable text explaining why the effect cannot be applied. Null except in `Error`. |
| `public boolean isError()` | True only for the `Error` variant. |
| `public boolean isEmpty()` | True only for the `Empty` variant, meaning there is nothing to change. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.EffectResponse valid(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.Effect, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Creates a `Valid` response. Arguments in order: the executable effect, the success message, the description and the affected items. None should be null (not checked). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.EffectResponse error(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Creates an `Error` response. Arguments in order: the error text, the description and the affected items. None should be null (not checked). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.EffectResponse empty(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Creates an `Empty` response meaning the effect would change nothing. Arguments: the description and the affected items. None should be null (not checked). |
