### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect`

```java
public final class StoredEffect
```

An immutable, JSON-serializable description of one change: the complete module key of the `EffectProvider` that understands it, plus a map of parameters. Effectors produce these, previews and effect records store them, and undo uses them. Create with `builder(String)`, `CoreEffects`, or the constructor (also used for JSON deserialization with properties `moduleKey` and `parameters`). Instances are value objects: equality and hash code use the module key and parameters.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public StoredEffect(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Creates a stored effect. Arguments: the provider's complete module key (expected non-null, not checked) and the parameters. The parameters are deep-copied into an unmodifiable map, keeping insertion order; null or empty means no parameters. Every key must be a `String` and every value must be non-null and one of `String`, `Integer`, `Long`, `Double`, `Boolean`, a list of such values or a map with string keys of such values (nested to any depth); otherwise `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown. |
| `public String getModuleKey()` | The complete module key (plugin key, `:`, module key) of the effect provider that must handle this effect. Never null. |
| `public java.util.Map<String, Object> getParameters()` | The effect's parameters as an unmodifiable map (nested lists and maps are also unmodifiable). Never null; empty if there are none. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect.Builder builder(String)` | Returns a new mutable `Builder` with the given module key and no parameters. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True if the other object is a `StoredEffect` with an equal module key and equal parameters. |
| `public String toString()` | Debug text containing the module key and parameters; the format is not a contract. |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash code consistent with `equals`, computed from the module key and parameters. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect.Builder`

```java
public static final class StoredEffect.Builder
```

Mutable, non-thread-safe builder for `StoredEffect`. Can be reused: each `build()` makes an independent immutable copy.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public Builder(String)` | Starts a builder with the given module key and no parameters. |
| `public Builder(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect)` | Starts a builder pre-filled with the module key and all parameters of an existing stored effect, to derive a modified copy. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect.Builder setModuleKey(String)` | Replaces the module key. Returns this builder. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect.Builder setParameter(String, Object)` | Sets the parameter with the given key to the value; a null value removes the parameter instead. Values are validated only at `build()`. Returns this builder. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect build()` | Creates the immutable `StoredEffect` from the current module key and parameters. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if a parameter value is not of an allowed type (see the `StoredEffect` constructor). |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch`

Internal bookkeeping for undo and redo of forest actions performed through generators. Types here are marked internal; they are public only so that the plugin's modules can share them, and third parties should not rely on them.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectBatch`

```java
public class EffectBatch
```

Internal record of the effects of one user action performed on a generated forest (for example moving rows that makes generators change issues), kept so that the action can be undone and redone. Created by the plugin's forest engine and stored in `EffectService`. Fields are public and partly mutable; instances are synchronized on by the plugin while undoing or redoing. Not intended for third-party use.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec spec` | The forest specification the action was performed on. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion version` | The forest version right after the action; undo/redo re-applies row replacements only if the forest's version signature still matches. |
| `public final com.almworks.integers.LongIterable movedRows` | Ids of the rows the user moved in the action. |
| `public final java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectPair> effects` | The generator effects performed, in order, each with its inverse. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.RowsToReplace redoReplace` | Rows to substitute in the forest when the batch is redone; null if not applicable. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.RowsToReplace undoReplace` | Rows to substitute in the forest when the batch is undone; null if not applicable. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectState state` | Whether the batch is currently applied or undone; starts as `APPLIED` and is updated by undo/redo. |
| `public long timestamp` | Time of creation or last undo/redo, from `System.nanoTime()` (only meaningful for comparisons within one JVM). Used to expire batches. |
| `public final String userKey` | Key of the user who performed the action (the current user at construction; may be null for anonymous). |
| `public EffectBatch(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion, com.almworks.integers.LongIterable, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.RowsToReplace, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.RowsToReplace, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectPair>)` | Creates a batch from, in order: the forest spec, the forest version, the moved rows, the redo replacement, the undo replacement and the effect pairs. Sets state to `APPLIED`, the timestamp to now and the user key to the current user. |
| `public long getTimestamp()` | Same as the `timestamp` field. |
| `public String getUserKey()` | Same as the `userKey` field. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectPair`

```java
public class EffectPair
```

Internal: one generator effect performed as part of an `EffectBatch`, with the effect that reverses it. Immutable.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public final long generatorRowId` | Row id of the generator that produced the effect; used to report problems against that row. |
| `public final boolean external` | True if the effect changes data outside the forest (for example a Jira issue field) rather than only the forest itself. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionEffect effect` | The effect as performed (re-run on redo). |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionEffect inverse` | The effect that reverses it (run on undo); null if it cannot be undone. |
| `public EffectPair(long, boolean, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionEffect, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionEffect)` | Creates a pair from, in order: generator row id, external flag, effect, inverse (nullable). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectService`

```java
public interface EffectService
```

Internal store of recent `EffectBatch` objects for undo/redo of forest actions. The plugin's implementation keeps them in memory only (lost on restart), and expires batches about 71 seconds after they were stored (configurable); loading a batch does not extend this. Expired batches are removed by a cleanup that runs about every 35 seconds, so a batch can stay loadable for up to about 106 seconds. Not intended for third-party use.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long recordBatch(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectBatch)` | Stores the batch and returns a new id for it. Ids are unique within the running node; the high 32 bits identify the node's runtime instance. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectBatch loadBatch(long)` | Returns the batch with the given id, or null if it does not exist, has expired, was recorded by another runtime instance, or belongs to a different user than the current one (unless security checks are overridden). |


Internal: whether an `EffectBatch` is currently in effect or reverted.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `APPLIED (enum constant)` | The batch's effects are in effect (initial state, and after redo). |
| `UNDONE (enum constant)` | The batch's effects have been reversed by undo. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectState[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.EffectState valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectbatch.RowsToReplace`

```java
public class RowsToReplace implements com.almworks.integers.func.LongToLong
```

Internal undo/redo helper describing which forest fragments must be re-inserted and how old row ids map to new ones when generated rows are replaced. Also acts as a row-to-generator function (`LongToLong`). Fields are public and mutable; the plugin updates them during undo/redo.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest> forests` | Forest fragments to insert, keyed by the id of the parent row they belong under (0 for the top level). |
| `public com.almworks.integers.wrappers.LongLongHppcOpenHashMap replacements` | Mapping from old row ids to the row ids that replace them. |
| `public long replacingGenerator` | The generator row id to report for every row when `replacingGenerators` is null. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.wrappers.LongLongHppcOpenHashMap replacingGenerators` | Per-row mapping from row id to the generator row id responsible for it; null means use `replacingGenerator` for all rows. |
| `public RowsToReplace(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, long, com.almworks.integers.wrappers.LongLongHppcOpenHashMap, long, com.almworks.integers.wrappers.LongLongHppcOpenHashMap)` | Creates the object for a single fragment. Arguments in order: the fragment, the parent row id it goes under, the row id replacements, the single replacing generator id, and the per-row generator map (nullable). |
| `public RowsToReplace(com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest>, com.almworks.integers.wrappers.LongLongHppcOpenHashMap, long, com.almworks.integers.wrappers.LongLongHppcOpenHashMap)` | Creates the object from, in order: fragments keyed by parent row id, the row id replacements, the single replacing generator id and the per-row generator map (nullable). Arguments are stored as given. |
| `public long invoke(long)` | Returns the generator row id responsible for the given row: `replacingGenerator` if there is no per-row map, otherwise the mapped value (0 when the row is not in the map). |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector`

Effectors: an extension point for automation that walks a forest and proposes changes (effects) for the items in it. Contains the `Effector` module interface, the function it returns, the collector and context it receives, its response type and its well-known parameter names.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.CoreEffectorParameters`

```java
public class CoreEffectorParameters
```

Names of parameters shared by the effectors bundled with the plugin and by its effector configuration UI. Constants only; instantiating the class is possible but useless.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final String FIELD_ID = "fieldId"` | Parameter `fieldId`: the target Jira field id (system field id or `customfield_NNNNN`). |
| `public static final String ATTRIBUTE_JSON = "attributeJson"` | Parameter `attributeJson`: the source attribute specification, serialized as JSON. |
| `public static final String JQL = "jql"` | Parameter `jql`: a JQL query restricting which issues the effector acts on. |
| `public static final String NAME_PARAM = "effectorName"` | Parameter `effectorName`: the user-given display name of an effector instance. When set and not blank, the plugin shows it instead of the generated summary; the plugin's edit form stores it in the instance parameters. |
| `public static final String SEND_NOTIFICATIONS = "sendNotifications"` | Parameter `sendNotifications`: boolean, whether Jira should send notifications for the issue updates the effects make. |
| `public static final String COLLECTION_OPERATION = "collectionOperation"` | Parameter `collectionOperation`: for multi-value fields, which operation to perform, one of `set`, `add` or `remove` (the bundled forms default to `set`). |
| `public CoreEffectorParameters()` | Default constructor; the class has no instance state. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.EffectCollector`

```java
public interface EffectCollector
```

Sink that receives the effects an `EffectorFunction` produces. Implemented by the plugin and passed to `EffectorFunction.produceEffects`; not thread-safe, so call it only from the thread that invoked the function.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void addEffect(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect)` | Appends an effect to the process preview, after any previously added effects. The order of addition is the preview order (before providers' `optimize` regroups effects by provider module key, keeping the first-seen order of keys). Use `CoreEffects.emitWarning` to add a warning instead of a change. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.Effector`

```java
public interface Effector
```

Extension point for an automation that inspects a forest and proposes changes. Other plugins register implementations as effector modules in their plugin descriptor; the module's complete key identifies the effector in effector instances and processes. The plugin calls `getEffectorFunction` when an effector process starts calculating; the form and summary methods are called by the plugin's configuration UI; `isAvailable` decides whether the effector is offered to users.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.EffectorFunctionResponse getEffectorFunction(java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.EffectorContext)` | Validates the saved parameters and prepares the function that will produce effects. Arguments: the instance or one-off parameters (never null, possibly empty) and the context, through which the effector must request any attribute values it needs (requests made after this method returns are ignored). Return `EffectorFunctionResponse.valid` with the function, or an errors response; error texts are turned into warnings in the preview and the effector produces no effects. Called on a background thread with the process owner as the current user; must not return null. |
| `public default boolean isAvailable()` | Whether the effector may be offered and configured on this system. Unavailable effectors are hidden from the list of effectors in the UI. Default: true. |
| `public abstract void addDefaultFormParameters(java.util.Map<String, Object>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.EffectorUnavailableException` | Fills the template variables for the configuration form of a new effector instance. The argument is the mutable map of form variables. Throw `EffectorUnavailableException` if the effector cannot be configured now; its localized message is shown to the user. |
| `public abstract void addParametersToForm(java.util.Map<String, Object>, java.util.Map<String, Object>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.EffectorUnavailableException` | Fills the configuration form for editing an existing instance. Arguments: the saved instance parameters (read-only) and the mutable map of form variables to fill. Throw `EffectorUnavailableException` if the effector cannot be configured now. |
| `public abstract java.util.Map<String, Object> buildParametersFromForm(java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.atlassian.jira.util.ErrorCollection) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.EffectorUnavailableException` | Converts submitted form values into instance parameters. Arguments: the submitted form (keys are field names, values usually arrays of strings as delivered by the web layer) and an error collection to which validation errors are added (field errors appear next to the fields; any error makes the plugin show the form again instead of saving). Returns the parameters to save; must not return null and values must be JSON-compatible. The plugin adds `effectorName` itself. Throw `EffectorUnavailableException` if the effector cannot be configured now. |
| `public default void addParametersForSummary(java.util.Map<String, Object>, java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Adds values used to render the short human-readable summary of an instance. Arguments: the saved instance parameters and the mutable map of summary template values to fill. Default does nothing. Not called when the instance has a non-blank `effectorName`. |
| `public default void addPlaceholdersForSummaryTemplate(java.util.Map<String, String>)` | Adds placeholder strings for each summary template value so the UI can render a generic summary template, for example mapping `applyDelay` to `{applyDelay}`. The argument is the mutable map to fill. Default does nothing. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.EffectorContext`

```java
public interface EffectorContext
```

Context passed to `Effector.getEffectorFunction`. Implemented by the plugin, one per process; not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void requireAttribute(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | Declares that the effector function needs the given attribute. The plugin loads all declared attributes for all rows of the forest in one consistent snapshot and passes them as `RowValues` to `EffectorFunction.produceEffects`. Calling it more than once with the same spec has no extra effect. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec getForestSpec()` | The forest the process runs on: for effector instances, the structure that owns the instances; for one-off runs, the forest spec given to `EffectorProcessManager.startProcess`. Never null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.EffectorFunction`

```java
public interface EffectorFunction
```

The working part of an effector, returned by `Effector.getEffectorFunction` inside a valid `EffectorFunctionResponse`. Implemented by effector authors. Called once per process (per instance) on a background thread with the process owner as the current user.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void produceEffects(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.EffectCollector, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProgressSink)` | Inspects the forest and adds proposed effects to the collector. Arguments: the forest with its items (for an effector instance, the sub-forest under the parent of the instance's row, or the whole forest if the row is at top level; for a one-off run, the whole forest), the values of the attributes requested via `EffectorContext.requireAttribute` (for all rows of the full forest), the collector, and a progress sink to report progress and to check for cancellation. Should stop early when the sink reports cancellation. Must not modify anything itself. An exception thrown here fails the calculation (status `CALCULATION_FAILED`) with the exception's message. |

Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the list is empty. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.instance`

Persistent effector instances: an effector module key plus saved parameters, optionally attached to a structure (they appear as effector rows in that structure). Provides the read model and a manager for creating, reading, updating and deleting them.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.instance.EffectorInstance`

```java
public interface EffectorInstance
```

A saved effector configuration: effector module key, parameters and the owning structure. Instances are created by the plugin (returned by `EffectorInstanceManager.getEffectorInstance`) and are immutable value objects; equality covers all four properties. In a forest an effector instance appears as an item of the effector item type with the same id.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long getId()` | The instance id, a positive number assigned at creation; also the id of the corresponding effector item. |
| `public abstract String getModuleKey()` | Complete module key of the `Effector` this instance runs. Never null. |
| `public abstract java.util.Map<String, Object> getParameters()` | The saved parameters as an unmodifiable map (empty if none were saved). Never null. |
| `public abstract Long getOwningStructure()` | Id of the structure the instance belongs to, or null if it is not attached to any structure. Only instances with an owning structure can be run. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.instance.EffectorInstanceManager`

```java
public interface EffectorInstanceManager
```

Service for persisting effector instances. Implemented by the plugin and obtained as an OSGi component (injection). Data is stored in the plugin's database tables and cached. Changes are recorded as item changes so that forests showing the instances refresh. Note: the implementation performs no permission checks; callers must check that the current user may configure effectors in the owning structure.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long createEffectorInstance(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>, Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Creates and saves a new instance and returns its id. Arguments: the effector's complete module key (not checked against installed effectors), the parameters (null or empty stores none; must be serializable to JSON) and the owning structure id (nullable). The plugin's implementation never throws `StructureException` here; it fails with an unchecked exception if the plugin is stopped or storage fails. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.instance.EffectorInstance getEffectorInstance(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Returns the instance with the given id. If loading fails it throws an unchecked `StructureRuntimeException`, not the declared `StructureException`. Although declared not-null, the plugin's implementation returns null when no instance has that id; callers should handle null. |
| `public abstract void updateEffectorInstance(long, String, java.util.Map<String, Object>, Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Replaces the module key, parameters and owning structure of an existing instance. Arguments in order: instance id, new module key, new parameters (null or empty clears them), new owning structure id (null detaches). Throws `StructureException` with `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` if the id does not exist. |
| `public abstract void deleteEffectorInstance(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Deletes the instance with the given id. Deleting a missing id silently does nothing. Does not remove rows referring to it from forests. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process`

Effector processes: the asynchronous, persistent jobs that first compute a preview of effects and then apply them, with per-effect records and undo. Provides the process read model, its status lifecycle, the records and the manager service used to start, confirm, cancel, undo and query processes.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectRecord`

```java
public interface EffectRecord
```

The persisted result of applying one preview effect in an effector process: success message or error, the undo effect and the affected items. Created by the plugin while applying and read through `EffectorProcessManager.getEffectRecords`. Immutable value object.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long getProcessId()` | Id of the effector process the record belongs to. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText getEffectMessage()` | On success, the provider's success message; on failure, the error message. Never null. |
| `public abstract boolean isError()` | True if the effect could not be applied (no provider, provider returned an error, or applying threw). |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect getUndoEffect()` | The effect that reverses this change, as returned by `Effect.apply()`; null for error records. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity> getAffectedItems()` | Identities of the items the effect touched, as reported by the provider; never null (empty if unknown, e.g. when no provider was found). |
| `public abstract long getTimestamp()` | When the effect was applied, in epoch milliseconds. |
| `public abstract int getPreviewIndex()` | Zero-based index of the effect in the process preview list (`EffectorPreview.getPreviewEffects()`); used to resume interrupted processes and to select records for undo. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorPreview`

```java
public interface EffectorPreview
```

The calculated outcome of the calculation phase of an effector process: the list of effects that will be applied, or the errors that stopped the calculation. Immutable as returned by the plugin.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText> getErrors()` | Errors that made the calculation fail (status `CALCULATION_FAILED`). Never null; empty when calculation succeeded. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.StoredEffect> getPreviewEffects()` | The effects to apply, in application order, after provider optimization and validation; may include warning pseudo-effects, which are shown but not applied. Never null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcess`

```java
public interface EffectorProcess
```

A snapshot of an effector process: a persistent background job that first calculates a preview of effects and then applies them. Returned by `EffectorProcessManager`; immutable, so re-read it to see progress. Progress percentages and cancellation are tracked by a separate process handle.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long getId()` | The process id (positive). |
| `public abstract long getProcessHandleId()` | Id of the plugin's generic process handle that tracks this process's progress and cancellation in the UI. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorPreview getEffectorPreview()` | The preview, if one is stored: set when calculation finishes or fails, and cleared (null) again when the process completes or is stopped. Null while pending or calculating. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcess.Status getStatus()` | The current status (see `EffectorProcess.Status`). Never null. |
| `public abstract String getUserKey()` | Key of the user who started the process; effects are applied on that user's behalf. Never null. |
| `public abstract Long getStartTime()` | Epoch milliseconds when calculation started, overwritten with the time applying started; null if the process has not started yet. |
| `public abstract Long getFinishTime()` | Epoch milliseconds when the last phase ended (calculation finished, failed or stopped; applying completed or stopped). Reset to null while applying is in progress; null before the first phase ends. |
| `public abstract Long getRevertedProcessId()` | For an undo process, the id of the process it reverts; null for normal processes. |
| `public abstract boolean isAcknowledged()` | True once the owner has dismissed the finished process (see `EffectorProcessManager.acknowledgeFinished`). Unacknowledged processes are those listed by `getRunningProcessesForUser`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcess.Status`

```java
public enum EffectorProcess.Status
```

Lifecycle status of an effector process. Normal flow: `PENDING` -> `CALCULATING` -> `CALCULATED` (only when confirmation is required) -> `QUEUED` -> `IN_PROGRESS` -> `COMPLETED` or `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`. A process whose preview is empty or contains only warnings goes straight to `COMPLETED`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `PENDING (enum constant)` | Created and waiting for its calculation to start. |
| `CALCULATING (enum constant)` | The effectors are running and the preview is being computed. |
| `CALCULATED (enum constant)` | The preview is ready and waits for the user to confirm (`confirm`) or discard (`deleteCalculated`). |
| `CALCULATION_FAILED (enum constant)` | Calculation failed; the errors are in the preview's `getErrors()`. |
| `CALCULATION_STOPPED (enum constant)` | Calculation was cancelled by the user, or abandoned because the node restarted while calculating. |
| `QUEUED (enum constant)` | Waiting in the apply queue; processes are applied one at a time, oldest queued first. |
| `IN_PROGRESS (enum constant)` | Effects are being applied. |
| `COMPLETED (enum constant)` | Applying finished with no error records (also used for previews with nothing to apply). |
| `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS (enum constant)` | Applying finished but at least one effect produced an error record, or applying aborted with an unexpected error. |
| `APPLY_INTERRUPTED (enum constant)` | Applying (or waiting in the queue) was cut short by a node shutdown or failover; can be continued with `resumeInterrupted`. |
| `APPLY_STOPPED (enum constant)` | Applying was cancelled by the user; the effects already applied stay applied. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcess.Status[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcess.Status valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcessManager`

```java
public interface EffectorProcessManager
```

Service to start, observe and control effector processes. Implemented by the plugin and obtained as an OSGi component (injection). All methods act as the current user. Processes are stored in the database and run on background jobs: calculation runs right after start; applying is done by a periodic job (about every 2 seconds) that takes one queued process at a time, cluster-wide on a single node. Methods that take a process id throw `StructureException` with the plugin's own error 6017 `ENTITY_NOT_EXISTS_OR_INACCESSIBLE` (category `NOT_FOUND`; see SPEC.md, the plugin's own error codes) unless the current user started the process, is a Jira administrator, or security checks are overridden.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void validateStartProcess(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.instance.EffectorInstance>, long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Checks, without starting anything, that the current user may run the given effector instances from the given structure. Same checks and exceptions as `startProcess(List, long, boolean)`. |
| `public abstract void validateStartProcess(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Checks, without starting anything, that the current user may run a one-off effector. Same checks and exceptions as `startProcess(String, Map, ForestSpec, boolean)`; the parameters are not validated. |
| `public abstract long startProcess(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.instance.EffectorInstance>, long, boolean) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Starts a process that runs the given saved effector instances and returns its id. Arguments: the instances (not empty), the id of the structure the user runs them from, and whether the preview must be confirmed before applying (if false, a non-empty preview is queued for applying automatically). Instances are evaluated in forest order by depth, then position; each sees the sub-forest under its row's parent. Throws `StructureException` with `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED` if the user lacks the global permission to execute effectors, or if an instance belongs to a structure other than the given one and the user lacks the permission to run effectors on queries; with `INVALID_PARAMETER` if the list is empty, an instance's module is not installed or an instance has no owning structure; with `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` if the user cannot view an owning structure. Problems found later (instance row missing or duplicated in the forest) make the process fail with `CALCULATION_FAILED`. |
| `public abstract long startProcess(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec, boolean) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Starts a one-off process that runs an effector with the given parameters over the given forest, without a saved instance, and returns its id. Arguments: the effector's complete module key, its parameters, the forest spec and the confirmation flag (as above). Throws `StructureException` with `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED` if the user lacks the global permission to execute effectors or the permission to run effectors on queries; `INVALID_PARAMETER` if no such effector is installed; `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` if the forest spec refers to a structure the user cannot view. |
| `public abstract long startUndoProcess(long, java.util.Collection<Integer>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Starts a process that reverts the applied effects of a finished process and returns the new process id. Arguments: the process to revert and the preview indexes of the records to revert (null means all successful records). The undo effects of the selected successful records are queued for applying immediately, without confirmation, in record order. Throws `StructureException`: `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED` without the global execute permission; not-found if the process is not accessible; `INVALID_PARAMETER` if the process status is not `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`, `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` or `APPLY_STOPPED`, or if no successful record matches. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcess getProcess(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Returns the current snapshot of the process. Throws `StructureException` if it does not exist or the current user may not see it. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectRecord> getEffectRecords(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Returns the records of all effects applied so far by the process (successes and errors). Order: Not determined (database order, in practice usually application order); use `getPreviewIndex()` to sort. Same access check as `getProcess`. |
| `public abstract void confirm(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Confirms a calculated preview so that it is queued for applying. Throws `StructureException` with `INVALID_PARAMETER` if the status is not `CALCULATED`, the preview is missing or it has no effects; with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the status changed concurrently. If the preview contains only warnings, the process is completed instead and nothing is queued. |
| `public abstract void confirm(long, java.util.Collection<Integer>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Deprecated. Like `confirm(long)`, but when the second argument is not null only the preview effects at those zero-based indexes are kept (out-of-range indexes are ignored; `INVALID_PARAMETER` if none remain) and the stored preview is replaced by that subset before queuing. Null applies all effects. |
| `public abstract void cancel(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Requests cancellation of a calculating or applying process. Asynchronous: the job notices the request at its next check and the status becomes `CALCULATION_STOPPED` or `APPLY_STOPPED`. Effects already applied are not reverted. A queued process that was cancelled stops as soon as applying begins (`APPLY_STOPPED`). Not determined: the effect on a process waiting for confirmation (`CALCULATED`). Throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the process handle cannot be found. |
| `public abstract void acknowledgeFinished(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Marks a finished process (status `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`, `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` or `APPLY_STOPPED`) as acknowledged, removing it from `getRunningProcessesForUser`. Throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the process is in another status. |
| `public abstract void deleteCalculated(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Deletes a process whose status is `CALCULATED`, `CALCULATION_STOPPED` or `CALCULATION_FAILED`, together with its process handle (used to discard a preview). Throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the process is in another status. |
| `public abstract void resumeInterrupted(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Puts an `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` process back into the apply queue (status `QUEUED`, acknowledged flag cleared); applying continues with the preview effects that have no record yet. Throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the process is in another status. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcess> findProcesses(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcess.Status, Long)` | Returns processes matching all given filters, newest first: started by the given user (null = any user), in the given status (null = any) and for the given structure id (null = any; matches the structure of instance runs or the structure in a one-off run's forest spec). Never null. Note: performs no permission check, so any caller can list other users' processes. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.process.EffectorProcess> getRunningProcessesForUser(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Returns all processes of the given user that are not yet acknowledged (running, waiting or finished but not dismissed), newest first. Never null. Performs no permission check. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error`

Error reporting for the whole API: the checked `StructureException` with its builder, the `StructureError` code interface with categories, the built-in catalogue of error codes `StructureErrors`, and two auxiliary exception classes.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError`

```java
public interface StructureError
```

An error code: a numeric code plus a category. The built-in codes are the `StructureErrors` enum; other plugins may implement this interface (typically with an enum) for their own codes, annotated with `CodeRange` to declare the range they use. Default methods offer shortcuts for building a `StructureException` with this code, e.g. `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER.forStructure(id).withMessage(...)`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract int getCode()` | The numeric error code. Codes are meant to be unique across all error enums; the built-in ones lie in 0..6999. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureErrorCategory getCategory()` | The broad category of the error, used to choose a reaction (for example an HTTP status). Should not be null. |
| `public default String name()` | A symbolic name for logs and messages. Default: `error#` followed by the code; enum implementations return the constant name instead. |
| `public default boolean is(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureErrorCategory)` | True if this error's category is the given one. |
| `public default boolean isOneOf(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureErrorCategory...)` | True if this error's category equals any of the given categories; false for an empty argument list. |
| `public default boolean isOneOf(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError...)` | True if this error equals (by `equals`) any of the given errors; false for an empty argument list. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException.Builder builder()` | Returns a new `StructureException.Builder` for this error. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException withLocalizedMessage(String, Object...)` | Shortcut: builds an exception with this error and a localizable message from an i18n key and arguments. Returns the exception; does not throw it. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException withMessage(String)` | Shortcut: builds an exception with this error and a plain, non-localized message (nullable). Returns the exception. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException withoutMessage()` | Shortcut: builds an exception with this error and no message. Returns the exception. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException.Builder forStructure(Long)` | Starts a builder for this error that refers to the given structure id (nullable). |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException.Builder forView(Long)` | Starts a builder for this error that refers to the given view id (nullable). |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException.Builder forRow(Long)` | Starts a builder for this error that refers to the given row id (nullable). |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException.Builder forItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Starts a builder for this error that refers to the given item (nullable). |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException.Builder forIssue(long)` | Starts a builder for this error that refers to the issue item with the given id. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException.Builder causedBy(Throwable)` | Starts a builder for this error with the given cause (nullable). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError.CodeRange`

```java
public @interface StructureError.CodeRange
```

Annotation for a `StructureError` implementation type that declares the inclusive range of codes it uses, so that ranges of different code sets do not overlap. Retained at runtime; applies to types only.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract int from()` | Lowest code in the range (inclusive). |
| `public abstract int to()` | Highest code in the range (inclusive). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureErrorCategory`

```java
public enum StructureErrorCategory
```

Broad classes of errors, used to decide how to react (for example which HTTP status to send).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `GENERAL (enum constant)` | Any problem not covered by the other categories, usually a failed operation. |
| `INVALID_INPUT (enum constant)` | The caller supplied a bad argument or an operation that is not valid in the current state. |
| `NO_PERMISSION (enum constant)` | The current user is not allowed to perform the operation. |
| `NOT_FOUND (enum constant)` | The requested object does not exist or the user may not see it (the two cases are deliberately not distinguished). |
| `INTERNAL (enum constant)` | An internal failure, such as failing to obtain a lock. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureErrorCategory[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureErrors`

```java
public enum StructureErrors implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError
```

The built-in error codes, in range 0..6999 (`CodeRange`). Each constant has a fixed numeric code and category; codes and categories are part of the contract (clients and the REST layer see them). `name()` returns the constant name.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `GENERIC_ERROR (enum constant)` | Unspecified failure; also used when a `StructureException` is created with a null error. |
| `LICENSE_PROBLEM (enum constant)` | The plugin's license is missing or invalid, so modifying operations are refused. |
| `LOCK_FAILED (enum constant)` | A required lock could not be acquired (for example a timeout while locking data for an update). |
| `INVALID_PARAMETER (enum constant)` | An argument or request parameter is invalid, or the object is in a state that does not allow the operation. |
| `DECISION_REQUIRED (enum constant)` | The operation needs an explicit choice from the user before it can continue. Not used by the plugin code examined. |
| `FOREST_SOURCE_ACTION_FAILED (enum constant)` | An action on a forest (move, add, remove rows) could not be performed by the forest source, for example because a generator refused it. |
| `UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED (enum constant)` | Changing an item (for example a Jira issue) failed. |
| `CREATE_ITEM_FAILED (enum constant)` | Creating a new item failed. |
| `FOREST_CHANGE_PROHIBITED_BY_PARENT_PERMISSIONS (enum constant)` | The forest change is not allowed because of the permissions that apply to the parent part of the forest (for example a sub-structure or an automation-managed region). |
| `PROJECT_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_STRUCTURE (enum constant)` | The issue's project is not enabled for use with the plugin. |
| `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE (enum constant)` | The structure does not exist or the user may not view it. |
| `NOT_ALLOWED_TO_CREATE_STRUCTURE (enum constant)` | The user may not create structures. |
| `STRUCTURE_ADMIN_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user lacks the administer (control) permission level on the structure. |
| `STRUCTURE_EDIT_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user lacks edit permission on the structure. |
| `JIRA_ADMIN_DENIED (enum constant)` | The operation requires Jira administrator rights. |
| `STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user is not allowed to use the plugin at all. |
| `ARCHIVED_STRUCTURE_EDIT_DENIED (enum constant)` | The structure is archived and therefore cannot be changed. |
| `STRUCTURE_OWNER_EDIT_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user may not change the structure's owner to the requested user. |
| `STRUCTURE_AUTOMATION_EDIT_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user may not change the automation (generators or effectors) of the structure. |
| `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE (enum constant)` | The view does not exist or the user may not see it. |
| `VIEW_ADMIN_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user lacks control permission on the view. |
| `VIEW_EDIT_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user lacks edit permission on the view. |
| `VIEW_CREATION_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user may not create views. |
| `PERSPECTIVE_CREATION_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user may not create perspectives (saved, shareable display states). |
| `ITEM_EDIT_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user may not edit the item. |
| `AUTOMATION_ACCESS_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user may not use or configure the automation involved (for example a generator in the forest). |
| `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user may not run effectors (globally, or on queries and sub-structures). |
| `JOB_NOT_EXISTS (enum constant)` | The background job with the given id does not exist. |
| `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE (enum constant)` | The item does not exist or the user may not see it. |
| `SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE (enum constant)` | The data subscription does not exist or belongs to someone else. |
| `INVALID_FOREST_OPERATION (enum constant)` | The forest change is inconsistent, for example it refers to a row that is not in the forest or not under the given parent. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_FOREST_SOURCE_OPERATION (enum constant)` | The forest source does not support the requested kind of change. |
| `UNAVAILABLE_MODULE (enum constant)` | A required extension module (for example a generator) is not installed or could not be loaded. |
| `MODULE_ERROR (enum constant)` | An extension module failed while being called. |
| `SIGNATURE_MISMATCH (enum constant)` | The client's forest version signature does not match the current one (the forest was rebuilt), so the change based on it is rejected and the client must reload. |
| `AUTOMATION_FAILED (enum constant)` | The forest's automation is in a failed or stopped state, so its content cannot be produced. |
| `CONSISTENT_OPERATION_FAILED (enum constant)` | An operation that needs a consistent snapshot of data could not obtain one (after retries) because the data kept changing. |
| `SAVED_COLUMN_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE (enum constant)` | The saved column does not exist or the user may not see it. |
| `SAVED_COLUMN_MANAGEMENT_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user may not create, change or delete saved columns. |
| `NOTE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE (enum constant)` | The note item does not exist or the user may not see it. |
| `NOTE_EDIT_DENIED (enum constant)` | The user may not edit the note. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureErrors[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |

| `public int getCode()` | The numeric code of the constant, as listed in its declaration. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureErrorCategory getCategory()` | The category of the constant, as listed in its declaration; never null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException`

```java
public class StructureException extends Exception
```

The checked exception used throughout the API. It carries a `StructureError` code and optionally the structure, view, row and item it refers to, a plain message or an i18n key with arguments, and a cause. Usually created through `StructureError` shortcuts or `StructureException.Builder`. `getMessage()` is an English text of the form `<details> - structure <error name> (code:<code> structure:<id> view:<id> row:<id> item:<item>)`, where details is the plain message or the message key rendered in English, and ids are included only when positive (item only when set). When the item lookup feature is enabled (a system property; on by default only in development mode), a description of the row's or item's object is appended in parentheses.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public StructureException(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError)` | Creates an exception with the error (null means `GENERIC_ERROR`) and nothing else. |
| `public StructureException(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError, String)` | Creates an exception with the error and a plain message. |
| `public StructureException(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError, Long)` | Creates an exception with the error and a structure id (nullable). |
| `public StructureException(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError, Long, Long)` | Creates an exception with the error, structure id and row id (both nullable). |
| `public StructureException(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError, Long, Long, String)` | Creates an exception with the error, structure id, row id and plain message. |
| `public StructureException(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError, Long, Long, String, Throwable)` | Creates an exception with the error, structure id, row id, plain message and cause. |
| `public StructureException(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError, Long, Long, Long)` | Creates an exception with the error, structure id, row id and view id (note the order: structure, row, view). |
| `public StructureException(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError, Long, Long, Long, String)` | Creates an exception with the error, structure id, row id, view id and plain message. |
| `protected StructureException(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError, Throwable, Long, Long, Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, String, String, Object...)` | Protected full constructor used by the builder and subclasses. Arguments in order: error (null means `GENERIC_ERROR`), cause, structure id, view id, row id, item, plain message, i18n message key, key arguments; all nullable. If a key is given it marks the exception as localized; if the plain message is null, the key rendered in English is used as the problem details. |
| `public String toString()` | The class name, followed by `: ` and `getMessage()` when the message is not null. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureError getError()` | The error code; never null (`GENERIC_ERROR` if none was given). |
| `public String getProblemDetails()` | The non-localized problem text: the plain message, or the English rendering of the message key, or if both are empty `error ` followed by the error's `toString()`. Never null. |
| `public long getStructure()` | The structure id the error refers to, or 0 if none. |
| `public long getView()` | The view id the error refers to, or 0 if none. |
| `public long getRow()` | The row id the error refers to, or 0 if none. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity getItem()` | The item the error refers to, or null. |
| `public boolean isLocalized()` | True if the exception was created with an i18n message key. |
| `public String getLocalizedMessage()` | The message for the current user: the message key rendered in the current user's locale if localized, otherwise `getProblemDetails()`. Never null. |
| `public String getLocalizedMessage(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Like `getLocalizedMessage()` but rendered in the given user's locale (null user means the default locale). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText asI18nText()` | The message as an `I18nText`: the key and arguments if localized, otherwise a text holding `getProblemDetails()`. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event`

Change notifications about Jira issues and links as seen by the plugin (`IssueEventBridge`, `IssueListener`, `JiraChangeEvent` and subclasses, `JiraChangeType`), plus two plain event objects the plugin publishes on the Jira event publisher (`StructureDeletedEvent`, `StructureItemConvertedEvent`).

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.IssueChangeEvent`

```java
public class IssueChangeEvent extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.JiraChangeEvent
```

A change notification about one issue. Created by the plugin from Jira issue events and other sources and delivered to `IssueListener`s; other code may create and report its own via `IssueEventBridge.reportEvent`. Immutable.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public IssueChangeEvent(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.JiraChangeType, long, com.atlassian.jira.event.issue.IssueEvent)` | Creates the event. Arguments: the change type (not null, else `NullPointerException`), the issue id and the original Jira event (nullable). |
| `public IssueChangeEvent(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.JiraChangeType, long)` | Creates the event for the issue id without an original Jira event. |
| `public IssueChangeEvent(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.JiraChangeType, com.atlassian.jira.event.issue.IssueEvent)` | Creates the event from a Jira issue event, taking the issue id from the event's issue. If the event, its issue or the id is missing, the id is 0 (an assertion error is raised instead when JVM assertions are enabled). |
| `public long getIssueId()` | The id of the changed issue (0 if unknown). |
| `public com.atlassian.jira.event.issue.IssueEvent getJiraEvent()` | The Jira event that caused this notification, or null if it came from another source. |
| `public String toString()` | The change type followed by the issue id in parentheses, e.g. `ISSUE_UPDATED(10001)`. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongList getAffectedIssuesSorted()` | A one-element list containing the issue id. |
| `public static long getIssueId(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.JiraChangeEvent)` | Returns the issue id if the given event is an `IssueChangeEvent`, otherwise 0 (also for null). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.IssueEventBridge`

```java
public interface IssueEventBridge
```

Service that fans out issue and link change notifications to registered `IssueListener`s. Implemented by the plugin and obtained as an OSGi component (injection). The plugin feeds it from the Jira event publisher (issue events, field value changes, issue links, remote links, issue properties) and from its own agile integrations. Listeners are called synchronously on the thread that reports the change; notifications are suppressed while Jira has notifications disabled for an import.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void addListener(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.IssueListener)` | Registers a listener; null is ignored. Adding the same listener twice makes it receive each event twice. Listeners are held strongly, so remove them when done. |
| `public abstract void removeListener(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.IssueListener)` | Unregisters a listener (one registration); unknown or null listeners are ignored. |
| `public abstract void reportChanges(com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.JiraChangeType)` | Reports that each issue in the list changed with the given change type: one `IssueChangeEvent` per id, in list order, delivered immediately to all listeners. A null list is ignored. The change type should not be null (an `IssueChangeEvent` cannot be created without one). |
| `public abstract void reportEvent(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.JiraChangeEvent)` | Delivers the given event immediately to all listeners; null is ignored. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.IssueListener`

```java
public interface IssueListener
```

Callback for issue and link change notifications, registered with `IssueEventBridge.addListener`. Implemented by clients.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void onIssueChanged(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.JiraChangeEvent)` | Called for every reported change, synchronously on the reporting thread (often a Jira request or event thread), so it should return quickly. The argument is never null; check its type for `IssueChangeEvent` or `LinkChangeEvent` details. Exceptions thrown here are logged and do not affect other listeners; an `Error` is not caught, stops delivery to the later listeners and reaches the reporting code. |

| `public com.almworks.integers.LongList getAffectedIssuesSorted()` | Ids of the issues affected, in ascending order. Empty in the base class. |
| `public String toString()` | The change type's name. |

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `ISSUE_CREATED (enum constant)` | An issue was created. |
| `ISSUE_UPDATED (enum constant)` | An issue was edited (also used for field value change events and issue property changes). |
| `ISSUE_DELETED (enum constant)` | An issue was deleted. |

| `GH_RANK_UPDATED (enum constant)` | The agile (board) rank of issues changed. |
| `GH_SPRINT_UPDATED (enum constant)` | An issue's agile sprint changed (also reported for sub-tasks of a moved parent). |
| `GH_EPIC_UPDATED (enum constant)` | An issue's epic link changed. |
| `UNKNOWN_CHANGE (enum constant)` | A change of unknown nature was detected (for example a request that may have modified issues). |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export`

Extension points and data types for exporting a structure view to a file: a provider picks a renderer for each column of the view, and the renderer fills header and data cells through format-neutral cell and column interfaces. The plugin drives the export; other plugins contribute renderers.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportCell`

```java
public interface ExportCell
```

One cell of an export (a header cell or a data cell) as seen by an export renderer. The plugin implements it for each format; renderers call exactly one of the setters to give the cell its value, and the format decides how the value is shown. The same cell object is reused for every row of a column, so a renderer must not keep it after the call returns. Not thread-safe; used only on the exporting thread.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void setText(String)` | Sets plain text as the cell value. Null clears the cell (blank in Excel, empty in printable). Printable escapes the text for HTML. Excel truncates text longer than 32767 characters to that length. |
| `public abstract void setNumber(Number)` | Sets a numeric value. Null clears the cell. Excel stores it as a number (as a double) and applies the column's rounding format if `ExportColumn.setRounding` was called; printable formats it with the user's locale, without grouping separators, and with the column's fixed number of decimals when rounding was set. |
| `public abstract void setPercentage(Double)` | Sets a percentage given as a fraction (1.0 means 100 %). Null clears the cell. Excel stores the fraction; without a column rounding it is rounded to 4 decimal places of the fraction, with rounding it gets a percent format with that many decimals. Printable shows either a progress bar (value clamped to 0..1) with the percent text, or only the percent text, depending on `PrintableColumn.setPercentageStyle`. |
| `public abstract void setDate(java.util.Date)` | Sets a calendar date (no time of day). Null clears the cell. The instant is converted to a date in the exporting user's time zone. Excel stores a date value (the renderer should also set `ExcelStyle.DATE` to get date formatting); printable shows the date in the user's date format. |
| `public abstract void setDatetime(java.util.Date)` | Sets a date with time of day. Null clears the cell. Converted in the exporting user's time zone. Excel stores a date-time value (pair with `ExcelStyle.DATETIME`); printable shows it in the user's complete date-time format. |
| `public abstract void setDuration(Long)` | Sets a duration in seconds. Null clears the cell. Excel stores it as a fraction of days (seconds / 86400), suitable for the `ExcelStyle.DURATION` hours:minutes format; printable shows it as Jira-style duration text (see `PrintableColumn.setDurationAsCalendarTime`). Durations under one minute in absolute value are shown as zero in printable. |
| `public abstract void setHyperlink(String, String)` | Sets a link. Arguments: the link text, then the URL. A null URL clears the cell; a null text uses the URL as text. If the URL is not a well-formed absolute URL the cell gets only the text, without a link. Excel creates a URL hyperlink (pair with `ExcelStyle.HYPERLINK` for link look); printable writes an HTML anchor with both parts escaped. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportColumn`

```java
public interface ExportColumn<C extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportCell>
```

One column of an export as seen by a renderer while it configures the column. The plugin implements it per format (see `ExcelColumn` and `PrintableColumn`); the renderer receives it in `ExportRenderer.configureColumn`. Settings apply to all data cells of the column. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract C getHeaderCell()` | Returns the header cell of this column, never null. The renderer normally sets the column title into it with `setText`. In Excel the header cell starts with the left-aligned header style. |
| `public abstract void setRounding(int)` | Fixes the number of decimal places used for numbers and percentages in this column. The argument is the count of decimals, 0 or more; a negative value throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Printable rounds half-up; Excel applies a number format with that many decimals. Without a call, numbers are shown as given. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportContextKeys`

```java
public final class ExportContextKeys
```

Holder of the well-known keys that the plugin puts into the export context (an `AttributeContext`), so renderers can read export state with `getObject(key)`. The class itself has no behaviour; its nested enums are the keys. These keys are read-only: `putObject` with any of them throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ExportContextKeys()` | Public no-argument constructor with no effect; the class is only a namespace for the nested key enums and is never meant to be instantiated. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportContextKeys.Excel`

```java
public enum ExportContextKeys.Excel
```

Context keys available only during an Excel export. Each constant is a key for `AttributeContext.getObject`; the value is the current Apache POI object of the workbook being written. They let a renderer do Excel work the API does not cover directly. Values change as the exporter moves through the sheet.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `POI_WORKBOOK (enum constant)` | Key for the Apache POI `Workbook` being written (XSSF for .xlsx or HSSF for .xls). Set once when the workbook is created. |
| `POI_HELPER (enum constant)` | Key for the workbook's Apache POI `CreationHelper` (for creating rich text, hyperlinks, data formats). |
| `POI_SHEET (enum constant)` | Key for the Apache POI `Sheet` into which the structure is exported (there is one sheet). |
| `POI_ROWNUM (enum constant)` | Key for an `Integer`: the zero-based sheet row index of the row currently being written (the header row while columns are configured, then each data row). |
| `POI_ROW (enum constant)` | Key for the Apache POI `Row` currently being written (header row during column configuration, then each data row). |
| `POI_COLUMN (enum constant)` | Key for an `Integer`: the zero-based sheet column index of the column currently being configured or rendered. |
| `POI_CELL (enum constant)` | Key for the Apache POI `Cell` currently being configured (header cell) or rendered (data cell). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportContextKeys.Excel[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportContextKeys.Excel valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |

Context keys available in every export format. Each constant is a key for `AttributeContext.getObject`.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRenderContext`

```java
public interface ExportRenderContext extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContext
```

The context given to a renderer while it configures its column and renders cells. It is an `AttributeContext` (user, locale, time zone, base URL, context objects) that also gives access to the attribute values the exporter loaded. Implemented by the plugin; valid only during the export.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues getValues()` | Returns the attribute values loaded for the exported rows, never null (empty when nothing was loaded). Only attributes requested with `ExportRequestContext.requireAttribute` during `prepare` are present. If a column is configured to use the unfiltered forest, the values come from the forest without trailing filter and sort transformations. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRenderer`

```java
public interface ExportRenderer<C extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportCell, M extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportColumn<C>>
```

Extension point: renders one column of a view into export cells. Instances come from an `ExportRendererProvider` and are used for a single export. The plugin calls `prepare` once when the export is set up, then `configureColumn` when the header is built, then `renderCell` for each exported row in forest order. If any call throws (including a linkage error), the plugin logs it and ignores this renderer for the rest of the export; other columns are unaffected.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void prepare(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRequestContext)` | Called once, before the forest and values are loaded. The renderer declares here which attributes it needs (with `requireAttribute`) and may read the forest spec and context objects. If it throws, the renderer is dropped from the export. |
| `public abstract void configureColumn(M, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRenderContext)` | Called to set up the column: arguments are the column (header cell and column settings) and the render context. The renderer typically sets the header text and format options. Excel calls it once; printable calls it each time the header row is produced, and resets the multiline flag and header cell before each call. |
| `public abstract void renderCell(C, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRow, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRenderContext)` | Called for each exported row: arguments are the cell to fill (reused across rows and cleared before each call), the row being exported, and the render context. The renderer sets the cell value, usually from `row.get(attribute)`. For rows the user may not see, `row.get` returns null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRendererProvider`

```java
public interface ExportRendererProvider<C extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportCell, M extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportColumn<C>>
```

Extension point declared by other plugins (and by the plugin itself) as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` module, optionally restricted to an export format and to a column key. For each exported column the plugin asks the providers in this order: those registered for the column's key and the format, then for the key and any format, then for any key and the format, then for any key and any format; the first non-null renderer wins.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRenderer<C, M> getColumnRenderer(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportFormat, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSpecification.Column, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRequestContext) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureProviderException` | Returns a renderer for the given column in the given format, or null if this provider does not handle it (the next provider is then asked). Arguments: the export format, the view column (key and parameters), and the request context. Throwing `StructureProviderException` makes the plugin skip the whole column; any other exception makes the plugin ignore this provider for the rest of the export. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRequestContext`

```java
public interface ExportRequestContext extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.loader.AttributeContext
```

The context given to renderer providers and to `ExportRenderer.prepare`. It is an `AttributeContext` that also lets a renderer request attribute values to be loaded and tells which forest is exported. Implemented by the plugin.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void requireAttribute(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>)` | Asks the exporter to load the given attribute for all exported rows, so it is available later through `ExportRenderContext.getValues` and `ExportRow.get`. Null is ignored. Must be called during `prepare` (or `getColumnRenderer`); later requests have no effect on loaded values. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec getForestSpec()` | Returns the spec of the forest being exported, never null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportRow`

```java
public interface ExportRow
```

One row being exported, passed to `ExportRenderer.renderCell`. Implemented by the plugin. Rows come in forest order; the printable format skips the subtrees of collapsed rows, Excel exports all rows. Rows the user may not see are still listed but give no attribute values.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow getRow()` | Returns the full row (item identity, semantics) for this row ID, never null. May throw the row manager's missing-row error if the row no longer exists. |
| `public abstract long getRowId()` | Returns the row ID. |
| `public abstract int getDepth()` | Returns the depth of the row in the exported forest: 0 for a top-level row, 1 for its children, and so on. |
| `public abstract boolean isExpanded()` | True if the row was expanded in the client's view at export time; true for every row when the request carried no expand state. |
| `public abstract boolean isLeaf()` | True if the row has no children in the exported forest (it is the last row or the next row is not deeper). |
| `public abstract <T> T get(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T>)` | Returns the loaded value of the given attribute for this row, or null if it was not loaded, has no value, or the user is not allowed to see the row. The attribute must have been requested with `requireAttribute`. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.excel`

Excel-specific refinements of the export cell and column interfaces, used when the export format is `ExportFormat.MS_EXCEL`. Renderers that know they write to a spreadsheet can cast to these to set styles, indentation and rich text.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.excel.ExcelCell`

```java
public interface ExcelCell extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportCell
```

A cell in an Excel export. Extends `ExportCell` with Excel-only settings. Implemented by the plugin; renderers get it by casting the cell when the format is `MS_EXCEL`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void setRichTextFromHtml(String)` | Sets the value from an HTML fragment, converting basic markup to Excel rich text: bold, italic, underline (ins), strike-through (del), subscript, superscript, font colour and monospace runs; a background colour on a panel block becomes the cell background. If the HTML has no visible text but contains an image, the first image that can be loaded is placed in the cell. If the HTML cannot be converted, the raw string is stored as text. Text is truncated to 32767 characters. |
| `public abstract void setStyle(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.excel.ExcelStyle)` | Applies one of the predefined cell styles to this cell, replacing its current style. Null means `DEFAULT`. |
| `public abstract void setIndention(int)` | Sets the indentation level of the cell text, clamped to 0..15. It is reset to 0 before each data cell is rendered and applied after the renderer returns. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.excel.ExcelColumn`

```java
public interface ExcelColumn extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportColumn<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.excel.ExcelCell>
```

A column in an Excel export. Extends `ExportColumn` with the default cell style of the column. Implemented by the plugin.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void setDefaultStyle(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.excel.ExcelStyle)` | Sets the default style of the whole sheet column. Null means `DEFAULT`. The plugin sets `DEFAULT` before calling `configureColumn`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.excel.ExcelStyle`

```java
public enum ExcelStyle
```

Predefined Excel cell styles that renderers can apply with `ExcelCell.setStyle` or `ExcelColumn.setDefaultStyle`. Every style aligns content to the top of the cell, except that the header styles align to the bottom.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `DEFAULT (enum constant)` | The plain default style. |
| `HEADER_LEFT_ALIGNED (enum constant)` | Header style: bold, left-aligned, bottom-aligned, thin bottom border. Header cells start with it. |
| `HEADER_RIGHT_ALIGNED (enum constant)` | Same as `HEADER_LEFT_ALIGNED` but right-aligned, for numeric columns. |
| `DATE (enum constant)` | Date format, month/day/two-digit-year (`m/d/yy`). |

```java
public interface PrintableCell extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.ExportCell
```

A cell in a printable (HTML) export. Extends `ExportCell` with raw HTML and CSS classes. Implemented by the plugin; renderers get it by casting the cell when the format is `PRINTABLE`.

| `public abstract void addClasses(String...)` | Adds CSS class names to the cell's element (`th` or `td`). Each name is HTML-escaped; null or empty names are ignored; duplicates are kept once, in first-added order. Classes are cleared before each new row. |


| member | meaning |
