| `public abstract void setMultiline(boolean)` | When true, data cells may wrap onto several lines; when false (the default, reset before each `configureColumn`), cell content is kept on one line. |
| `public abstract void setPercentageStyle(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.printable.PercentageStyle)` | Chooses how percentages are shown in this column. Null (the default) behaves as `PROGRESS_BAR`. |
| `public abstract void setDurationAsCalendarTime(boolean)` | When true, durations are shown as calendar time (24-hour days, 7-day weeks); when false (default) they use Jira's time-tracking format for the current user, which follows the configured working hours per day and days per week. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension`

Internal extension points through which companion apps plug into the core plugin: contributing widget configuration and REST data, describing their licence for support reports, and declaring which structures they are integrated with. Not meant for general third-party use.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.StructureCoreExtension`

```java
public interface StructureCoreExtension
```

Internal extension point for companion apps, declared as a `structure-core-extension` module. The plugin keys each extension by its complete module key. It is asked for extra widget configuration, for extra data to attach to some REST responses, and for its licence information. Every method may return null to contribute nothing.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract java.util.Map<String, Object> getConfigurationForWidget()` | Returns extra configuration for the structure widget in the browser, or null. A non-empty map is included in the widget configuration under the extension's complete module key; null or empty adds nothing. |
| `public abstract Object getRestResponseData(Object)` | Returns extra data to attach to forest, item, poll and effect REST responses, or null for none. The argument is the request data the client sent for this extension (looked up by the extension's complete module key), or null if none was sent. Exceptions are logged and treated as null. A non-null result is added to the response under the module key. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.AppSupportInfo getAppSupportInfo()` | Returns licence and version information of the companion app for licence listings and the about popup, or null if the app does not report one. The original also used it for its periodic licence reports to the vendor; the replacement sends nothing (SPEC 1.8). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.StructureIntegrationDetails`

```java
public interface StructureIntegrationDetails
```

Internal extension point, declared as a `structure-integration-details-provider` module, through which a companion app says which structures it is integrated with, so the structure management pages can show its icon next to them. The plugin labels each provider with its plugin's name.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract String getProductIconUrl()` | Returns the URL of the app's icon to show in the structure management pages. If it returns null the provider is skipped when marking structures. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongSet selectIntegratedStructures(com.almworks.integers.LongSet)` | Given a set of structure IDs, returns the subset that this app is integrated with (for example, has its own data on), or null or an empty set for none. Called when listing structures for management; the argument is never null. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license`

The licence data model shared by the plugin and its companion apps: licence details, licence types, hosting kinds, sources and error codes. Under the replacement's no-Marketplace ruling (SPEC 1.1) every licence the plugin reports is treated as licensed, valid and not expiring.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.AppSupportInfo`

```java
public interface AppSupportInfo
```

Internal: describes a companion app for licence displays (and, in the original, for licence reports). Returned by `StructureCoreExtension.getAppSupportInfo`; implemented by companion apps.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.LicenseData getLicense()` | Returns the app's current licence, never null (`LicenseData.DISABLED` when it has none). Under the replacement's ruling the plugin treats every reported licence as licensed, valid and not expiring. |
| `public abstract Integer getUserCount()` | Returns the number of users the app counts for licensing, or null if unknown. |
| `public abstract String getProductVersion()` | Returns the app's version string, or null if unknown. |
| `public abstract String getProductKey()` | Returns the app's plugin key, never null; used as the key of the app's entry in licence listings. |


Internal component (`app-support-store`, published as an OSGi service) that tells whether a licence serial has been blocked. In the original, serials were blocked as a result of reports to the vendor's server, and a blocked serial made the licence report `REVOKED_LICENSE`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean isLicenseBlocked(String)` | Returns true if the given licence serial is in the blocked list; false for null or an unknown serial. In the replacement nothing is ever reported, so no serial is ever blocked and this always returns false (SPEC 1.8). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.LicenseData`

```java
public interface LicenseData
```

The data model of a licence of the plugin or a companion app: who holds it, its type, limits, dates and validity. Implemented by the licence management code; the constant `DISABLED` stands for no licence. Instances are read-only. Under the replacement's no-Marketplace ruling (SPEC 1.1), the licence the plugin reports for itself and for recognised extensions behaves as licensed, valid and not expiring.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.LicenseData DISABLED` | Shared instance of `LicenseData.Disabled` with error `NO_ERROR`, meaning 'no licence'. |
| `public abstract String getLicensee()` | Returns the name of the licence holder (organisation). `--` when there is no licence. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.StructureLicenseType getLicenseType()` | Returns the licence type; `DISABLED` when there is no licence. Under the replacement ruling, the effective licence is never `DISABLED`; Not determined: which non-disabled type the replacement reports (the spec only fixes the observable 'licensed' outcome). |
| `public abstract String getSerial()` | Returns the licence serial as text (for Marketplace licences, the support entitlement number), or null when there is none. |
| `public abstract long getSerialNumber()` | Returns the numeric serial of a vendor-issued licence, or 0 when there is none (always 0 for Marketplace licences). |
| `public abstract long getExpirationTimestamp()` | Returns when the licence expires, as milliseconds since the epoch, or 0 if it does not expire. Under the replacement ruling: 0 (no expiry). |
| `public abstract long getMaintenanceExpirationDate()` | Returns when maintenance (updates and support) ends, as milliseconds since the epoch, or 0 if not set. Under the replacement ruling: 0. |
| `public abstract java.util.Collection<String> getLicensedServers()` | Returns the server IDs the licence is locked to, or null if it is not server-locked. |
| `public abstract boolean isServerLocked()` | True if the licence is valid only on specific servers (`getLicensedServers` is non-null). |
| `public abstract int getMaximumNumberOfUsers()` | Returns the user tier of the licence; 0 or less when the licence has no user limit or is absent. |
| `public abstract boolean isUnlimitedNumberOfUsers()` | True if the licence has no user limit. Under the replacement ruling: true. |
| `public abstract void extraChecks() throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.LicenseException` | Performs licence-kind-specific validity checks and throws `LicenseException` with the reason if one fails (for example a revoked or wrong-product licence). Does nothing when all checks pass. Under the replacement ruling it never throws. |
| `public abstract boolean hasExpiration()` | True if the licence has an expiry date. Under the replacement ruling: false. |
| `public abstract boolean hasMaintenanceExpiration()` | True if the licence has a maintenance end date. Under the replacement ruling: false. |
| `public abstract boolean isMarketplaceLicense()` | True if the licence comes from the Atlassian Marketplace rather than from the vendor directly. Under the replacement ruling: false (there is no Marketplace licensing). |
| `public abstract boolean isValid()` | True if the licence is present and passes all checks. Under the replacement ruling: true. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.StructureLicenseError getLicenseError()` | Returns why the licence is not valid, or `NO_ERROR`; never null. Under the replacement ruling: `NO_ERROR`. |
| `public default boolean isDataCenterCompatible()` | True unless the licence hosting is `SERVER`; i.e. legacy and Data Center licences may be used on a Data Center installation. Default implementation derives it from `getLicenseHosting`. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.StructureLicenseHosting getLicenseHosting()` | Returns which deployment kind the licence was issued for, never null. The default implementation returns `LEGACY`. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.LicenseSource getLicenseSource()` | Returns where the licence came from, never null. The default implementation returns `MARKETPLACE` when `isMarketplaceLicense` is true and `VENDOR` otherwise. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.StructureLicenseError`

```java
public enum StructureLicenseError
```

Reasons why a licence is not valid, each with a stable numeric code. Under the replacement ruling the plugin always reports `NO_ERROR` for its own and recognised licences.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `NO_ERROR (enum constant)` | The licence is fine. Numeric code 0. |
| `NO_LICENSE (enum constant)` | No licence is installed. Numeric code 1000. |
| `LICENSE_CERTIFICATE_ERROR (enum constant)` | The licence certificate cannot be read or verified. Numeric code 1001. |
| `VENDOR_CERTIFICATE_ERROR (enum constant)` | The certificate of the issuer that signed the licence is not trusted or cannot be read. Numeric code 1003. |
| `NOT_SIGNED (enum constant)` | The licence is not signed. Numeric code 1004. |
| `NO_METADATA (enum constant)` | The licence lacks the required details. Numeric code 1005. |
| `INVALID_DATE (enum constant)` | A date in the licence is malformed. Numeric code 1006. |
| `INVALID_NUMBER (enum constant)` | A number in the licence is malformed. Numeric code 1007. |
| `BAD_PRODUCT_ID (enum constant)` | The licence names a different product ID. Numeric code 1008. |
| `EXPIRED (enum constant)` | The licence has expired. Numeric code 1009. |
| `NO_RELEASE_DATE (enum constant)` | The installed app version has no known release date, so maintenance coverage cannot be checked. Numeric code 1010. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION (enum constant)` | The installed app version was released after the licence's maintenance ended. Numeric code 1011. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_SERVER (enum constant)` | The licence is locked to other servers than this one. Numeric code 1012. |
| `JIRA_LICENSE_MISMATCH_USERS (enum constant)` | The licence's user tier is smaller than the Jira licence's user tier (or Jira is unlimited and the app licence is not). Numeric code 1013. |
| `INVALID_PRODUCT (enum constant)` | The licence is for a different product. Numeric code 1014. |
| `FREE_LICENSE_EXPECTED (enum constant)` | A free licence was expected for this installation but another type was found. Numeric code 1015. |
| `BAD_CUSTOMER_ID (enum constant)` | The customer ID in the licence does not match. Numeric code 1016. |
| `REVOKED_LICENSE (enum constant)` | The licence serial has been blocked (revoked). Numeric code 1017. |
| `TYPE_MISMATCH (enum constant)` | The licence type does not fit the installation. Numeric code 1018. |
| `UNKNOWN_ERROR (enum constant)` | An unexpected error occurred while checking the licence. Numeric code 1019. |
| `JIRA_EVAL_LICENSE_MISMATCH (enum constant)` | Jira runs on an unlimited evaluation licence while the app licence has a user limit. Numeric code 1020. |
| `NO_DATACENTER_SUPPORT (enum constant)` | The installation is Data Center but the licence is for Server hosting only. Numeric code 1021. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.StructureLicenseError[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extension.license.StructureLicenseError valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |
| `public long getCode()` | Returns the numeric code of the error: 0 for `NO_ERROR`, otherwise a value from 1000 to 1021 (1002 is unused). Codes are stable and appear in messages and REST output. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.folder`

Folders: named, storable items that can be placed in a structure to group rows. The package holds the immutable folder value and the manager component that stores folders.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.folder.Folder`

```java
public final class Folder
```

An immutable description of a folder: its name and, optionally, the structure that owns it. Created through `Folder.named` or `Folder.copy` and a builder; stored and loaded through `FolderManager`. Thread-safe. It does not override `equals` or `hashCode` (identity semantics).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public String getName()` | Returns the folder name, never null or blank, with leading and trailing whitespace removed and at most 190 characters long. |
| `public Long getOwningStructure()` | Returns the ID of the structure the folder belongs to, or null when the folder is not tied to a structure. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.folder.Folder.Builder named(String)` | Starts a builder for a folder with the given name. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the name is null, empty or only whitespace. A name longer than 190 characters is shortened to 190 characters ending with `...`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.folder.Folder.Builder copy(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.folder.Folder)` | Starts a builder initialised with the name and owning structure of the given folder. A null argument throws `NullPointerException`. |

```java
public interface FolderManager
```

Component (OSGi service; also via `StructureComponents.getFolderManager`) that stores folders in the database. Folder IDs are positive integers within the 32-bit range. The manager performs no permission checks; it is the caller's job to check access. Changes are recorded with the item tracker so rows showing the folder refresh. Results are cached. All methods throw `StructureStoppedException` (unchecked) while the plugin is stopped.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|

Throws `StructureException` with `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` if no such folder exists. |
| `public abstract void deleteFolder(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Deletes the folder with the given ID. Does nothing (and does not throw) if it does not exist. Rows that show the folder are not removed from structures. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest`

Access to forests (ordered trees of row IDs) and their changes. A `ForestSpec` names which forest is wanted (a structure, a historical version, a query result, the clipboard, optionally transformed and secured for a user); `ForestService` turns a spec into a `ForestSource`, which gives versioned snapshots, incremental updates and accepts actions.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestChange`

```java
public abstract class ForestChange
```

An immutable description of one change to a forest: add a sub-forest, move rows, remove rows, or reorder children. Incremental forest updates (`VersionedForestUpdate.Incremental`) are lists of these. Instances are created with the static factories or the subclass constructors; `ForestChange` itself cannot be subclassed outside the API, but its nested change classes are not final and have public constructors. Positions use row IDs: `under` 0 means the top level and `after` 0 means first position under the parent.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestChange add(long, long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Creates an `Add` change. Arguments: the parent row (0 for top level), the preceding sibling row (0 for first position), and the forest to insert. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the forest is null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestChange move(long, long, com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Creates a `Move` change. Arguments: the new parent row (0 for top level), the row after which to place the moved rows (0 for first position), and the rows to move, in their new order. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the list is null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestChange remove(com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Creates a `Remove` change for the given rows (each removed with its subtree). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the list is null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestChange reorder(long, com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Creates a `Reorder` change. Arguments: the parent row (0 for top level) and its children in the new order. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the list is null. |
| `public abstract void apply(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest)` | Applies the change to the given mutable forest in place. Invalid positions are tolerated as described for each subclass; the forest must not be null. An immutable forest is not tolerated: changing it throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestService`

```java
public interface ForestService
```

Component (OSGi service; also via `StructureComponents.getForestService`) that resolves a `ForestSpec` into a `ForestSource`. Sources are cached, so the same spec usually returns the same source. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSource getForestSource(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Returns the forest source for the spec, never null. A secured spec is checked first: the user named by the spec must exist and, if the spec names a structure, must have at least view permission on it. Throws `StructureException`: `INVALID_PARAMETER` for a null spec or an unsupported query type; `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` if the structure is missing or not viewable; the plugin's own error 6008 `ACTING_USER_NOT_FOUND` (category `NO_PERMISSION`) if the spec's user key is unknown. A text query with an empty query is treated as a JQL query with an empty query (recent items). Unsecured specs are not permission-checked. |
| `public abstract String getDisplayName(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec)` | Returns a human-readable name for the spec in the current user's language, never null: the structure name for a structure spec (requires view permission), a generic 'query' or 'clipboard' label for those kinds, and for a transformed spec the name of the untransformed one with ` (+)` appended. For null or when the name cannot be obtained, returns the generic 'structure' label; errors are logged, not thrown. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSource`

```java
public interface ForestSource extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.VersionedDataSource<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.VersionedForestUpdate>
```

A live, versioned source of one forest, obtained from `ForestService.getForestSource`. It extends `VersionedDataSource`, so callers can also get its current version and an update since an older version (full or incremental). Some sources accept actions that change the forest. Implementations are thread-safe. Secured sources check the user's permissions on actions; unsecured sources do not.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.VersionedForest getLatest()` | Returns the current forest with its version, never null. The forest is immutable. May compute the forest first (running generators), which can take time. |
| `public abstract boolean hasUpdate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion)` | Returns true if the source's current version differs from the given version, i.e. there is something new since then. The argument must not be null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.action.ActionResult apply(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.action.ForestAction, java.util.Map<String, Object>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Performs the action on the forest and returns its result, never null. The map holds action parameters (see `ActionParameters`; besides those, `dryRun` set to true validates without changing anything). Before acting, the source checks that rows named by the action exist and positions are consistent and throws `StructureException` with `INVALID_FOREST_OPERATION` otherwise. Throws `StructureInteractionException` when a decision from the caller is needed (repeat with the answers added to the parameters), and `StructureException` with `UNSUPPORTED_FOREST_SOURCE_OPERATION` from read-only sources. Secured sources also throw when the user lacks permission. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.action.ActionResult apply(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.action.ForestAction) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Same as `apply(action, parameters)` with an empty parameter map. |
| `public default boolean isActionable()` | True if the source accepts actions. Read-only sources (for example a historical version or a skeleton built from a query) return false. Default: true. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSourceHealthStatus getHealth()` | Returns the health of the last forest computation, never null. Default: `ForestSourceHealthStatus.HEALTHY`. |


Diagnostics of the last forest computation of a source: whether generation was stopped early, how long each generator took, which generators hit a result limit, and which seem to update without end. Used for warnings in the UI and REST output. All maps are keyed by generator ID.

| `public default com.almworks.integers.LongSet getInfiniteUpdateGenerators()` | Returns the IDs of generators detected as causing endless re-generation (their own effects keep triggering updates). Never null. Default: empty set. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec`

```java
public final class ForestSpec
```

A value meant to be immutable and thread-safe (but see `Builder.build()`) that names a forest: either a structure (optionally a historical version), a structure query (`SQuery`), or a clipboard session; optionally with a list of transformations (generators applied on top, last one outermost), a 'title' flag (the structure itself shown as a root row), a 'skeleton' flag (only the stored rows, generators not run), and security (the forest as seen by a given user). Exactly one of structure, query or clipboard is meant to be set; this is checked only by Java assertions, so an inconsistent spec can be built with assertions off and fails later. Specs are used as cache keys and compare by all their fields. A non-secured, non-transformed structure spec never carries a user key.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec.Builder builder()` | Returns a new empty builder. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec.Builder builder(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec)` | Returns a builder initialised from the given spec, or an empty builder if the argument is null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec structure(long)` | Spec of the structure with this ID, secured for the current user (anonymous when no user is logged in). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec structure(long, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Spec of the structure with this ID, secured for the given user; null means anonymous. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec unsecuredStructure(long)` | Spec of the structure with this ID with no security: the full forest, no permission checks on reading or acting. Intended for trusted code. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec skeleton(long)` | Spec of the stored rows of the structure (generators not run), unsecured. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec version(long, int)` | Spec of a historical version of the structure: arguments are the structure ID and the version number. Unsecured. Its source is read-only. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec sQuery(String, String)` | Spec of a structure-query result: arguments are the query type (see `SQuery` constants) and the query text. Secured for the current user. Null arguments throw `IllegalArgumentException`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec clipboard(String)` | Spec of the clipboard of the given HTTP session ID. Unsecured. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec secure(String)` | Returns a copy of this spec secured for the user with the given key (null for anonymous). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec transform(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Returns a copy with one more transformation appended: arguments are the generator module key and its parameters (may be null). The copy carries the current user's key and is not a skeleton. Not meant for skeleton specs (only asserted). |
| `public boolean isTransformed()` | True if the spec has at least one transformation. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec getLastTransformedSpec()` | Returns the spec with the last transformation removed (and not a skeleton), or null if the spec is not transformed. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec.Transformation getLastTransformation()` | Returns the last (outermost) transformation, or null if not transformed. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec getUntransformedSpec()` | Returns the spec with all transformations removed, or this spec if it has none. |
| `public Long getStructureId()` | Returns the structure ID, or null if the spec is not about a structure. |
| `public Integer getVersion()` | Returns the historical version number, or null for the current forest. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec.SQuery getSQuery()` | Returns the structure query, or null if the spec is not a query. |
| `public String getClipboardSessionId()` | Returns the HTTP session ID of the clipboard, or null if the spec is not a clipboard. |
| `public String getUserKey()` | Returns the key of the user the spec is for (used for security and for running transformations), or null for anonymous or not user-specific. |
| `public java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec.Transformation> getTransformations()` | Returns the transformations in order of application, never null; an empty, unmodifiable list when there are none. |
| `public boolean isSecured()` | True if the forest is filtered by and acted on with the permissions of the spec's user. |
| `public boolean isSkeleton()` | True if the spec asks for the stored rows only, without running generators. |
| `public boolean hasTitle()` | True if the structure itself is shown as a root row above its forest. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec getUnsecured()` | Returns the same spec without security, or this spec if it is not secured. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec withoutTitle()` | Returns the same spec with the title flag cleared, or this spec if not set. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec withTitle()` | Returns the same spec with the title flag set, or this spec if already set. |
| `public <T> T accept(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec.Visitor<T>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Calls one visitor method and returns its result. The first match wins in this order: secured, then transformed, then structure, then query, then clipboard. Throws `UnsupportedOperationException` if none applies (an empty spec); propagates the visitor's `StructureException`. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True if the other object is a `ForestSpec` with equal structure ID, version, query, clipboard session, user key, transformations and flags. |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash over all fields, consistent with `equals`; computed once and never 0. |

The result is secured with the current user's key, except a clipboard spec (type `clipboard`), which is unsecured and takes its session ID from the current HTTP request. Never a skeleton. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the argument is null, if not exactly one of structure ID, query and clipboard is given, if a version is given without a structure ID, or if the title flag is set without a structure ID. Throws `IllegalStateException` for a clipboard spec when no HTTP request or session is available. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.RestForestSpec toRest()` | Returns the REST form of the spec: structure ID, version, query (type and text), type `clipboard` for a clipboard spec, the transformations (module and parameters), and `title` true when set. Security, user key, skeleton flag and the clipboard session ID are not included. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.SQuerySkeletonFactory`

```java
public interface SQuerySkeletonFactory
```

Experimental extension point, declared by other plugins as a `structure-query-skeleton-factory` module, that supports additional structure query types. The plugin handles `jql`, `text` and `cql` itself; for any other type it looks for a factory whose complete module key equals the query type, and fails with `INVALID_PARAMETER` if there is none. The factory builds the fixed rows (usually generators) whose generated result is the query result.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void createSkeleton(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilder) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Called when a forest source is created for a query of this factory's type. ## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.action`

Actions that a client asks a forest source to perform (add, copy, move, remove rows), their results (applied effects, problems, row ID replacements) and the interaction mechanism by which the plugin asks the caller for a decision before it can complete an action.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.action.ActionParameters`

```java
public class ActionParameters
```

Internal: names of the well-known action parameters that callers pass in the map of `ForestSource.apply`, plus ready-made single-entry maps. Values are generally booleans or numbers; the plugin accepts a single value or a one-element list. Not instantiable.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final String PRIMARY_GENERATOR = "0:PrimaryGenerator"` | Parameter `0:PrimaryGenerator`: the row ID of the generator that should handle the action when several could. The plugin asks for it through a `StructureInteractionException` whose parameter has this ID and whose values are the candidate generator row IDs. |
| `public static final String CONFIRM = "0:Confirm"` | Parameter `0:Confirm`: true confirms an action that would change two or more items. Without it the plugin asks for confirmation through a `StructureInteractionException` with this parameter ID. |
| `public static final String STATIC_CAN_COMPETE = "0:StaticCanCompete"` | Parameter `0:StaticCanCompete`: when true, manually placed (stored) rows may handle an action alongside a generator that inserts items; by default the generator wins and the stored rows are not changed. |
| `public static final String ACT = ":Act"` | Suffix `:Act`: the parameter `<generator row ID>:Act` set to true makes that generator apply an optional effect it would otherwise not apply. |
| `public static final String PASS = ":Pass"` | Suffix `:Pass`: the parameter `<generator row ID>:Pass` set to true makes that generator skip the effect it would otherwise apply. |
| `public static final String IGNORE_REMOVED_ROW_MISSING = "updateSanityCheck.ignoreRemoveRowMissing"` | Parameter `updateSanityCheck.ignoreRemoveRowMissing`: when true, a remove action does not fail if some of its rows are no longer in the forest. |
| `public static final String IGNORE_MOVED_ROW_MISSING = "updateSanityCheck.ignoreMovedRowMissing"` | Parameter `updateSanityCheck.ignoreMovedRowMissing`: when true, a move action does not fail if some of the moved rows are no longer in the forest (the target position is still checked). |
| `public static final String IGNORE_ADD_AFTER_ROW_PROBLEMS = "updateSanityCheck.ignoreAddAfterRowProblems"` | Parameter `updateSanityCheck.ignoreAddAfterRowProblems`: when true, an add action does not fail if its `after` row is missing or not under the given parent. |
| `public static final java.util.Map<String, Object> IGNORE_REMOVED_ROW_MISSING_MAP` | Unmodifiable map with only `IGNORE_REMOVED_ROW_MISSING` set to true. |
| `public static final java.util.Map<String, Object> IGNORE_MOVED_ROW_MISSING_MAP` | Unmodifiable map with only `IGNORE_MOVED_ROW_MISSING` set to true. |
| `public static final java.util.Map<String, Object> IGNORE_ADD_AFTER_ROW_PROBLEMS_MAP` | Unmodifiable map with only `IGNORE_ADD_AFTER_ROW_PROBLEMS` set to true. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.action.ForestAction`

```java
public abstract class ForestAction
```

An immutable request to change a forest, passed to `ForestSource.apply`: `Add`, `Copy`, `Move` or `Remove`. Positions are row IDs: `under` 0 means the top level; `after` 0 and `before` 0 mean no anchor. When `after` is 0 and `before` is not, the new rows go just before `before`; when both are 0 they go first under the parent. In a generated forest, generators decide how to carry out the action (for example by changing issue fields). Cannot be subclassed outside the API.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void accept(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.action.ForestAction.Visitor) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Calls the visitor method matching the concrete action type and passes on its `StructureException`. |

| `public Add(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, long, long, long, long)` | Creates an action that adds a single item. Arguments: the item, the row semantics value (0 for none), then the parent, after and before rows. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item`

Forests whose rows carry item data. An item forest pairs a raw `Forest` (row ids and depths) with a way to look up the `StructureRow` for each row id. The package also holds the builder interfaces that generators use to emit rows, and a ready builder implementation.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ImmutableItemForest`

```java
public final class ImmutableItemForest implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest
```

An `ItemForest` that holds its own copy of every `StructureRow` it contains, so it does not depend on any row service. Instances are created only through the static factory methods. The class is final and marked immutable; the row map is an unmodifiable copy. Caveat: the forest passed to `rearrangeItemForest`, `copySubtree` and `of(StructureRow)` is stored as given, not copied or frozen, so immutability of `getForest()` is only guaranteed for instances made by `of(Forest, Map)` and `copy`. Safe to share between threads when built from immutable inputs.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest EMPTY` | Shared empty item forest: an immutable empty forest and no rows. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ImmutableItemForest of(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, java.util.Map<Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow>)` | Creates an item forest from a raw forest and a map from row id to row. Every row id in the forest must have a non-null entry in the map, otherwise `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown listing the missing ids. The forest is copied into a new immutable forest and the map is copied into an unmodifiable map (extra map entries are kept but unused). Neither argument may be null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ImmutableItemForest of(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | Creates an item forest with a single root row: the forest contains just `row.getRowId()` at depth 0 and the row map contains that row. The row must not be null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ImmutableItemForest copy(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest)` | Returns an immutable snapshot of the given item forest. If the argument already is an `ImmutableItemForest` it is returned unchanged. Otherwise the forest is copied and frozen, and every row in it is fetched from the source with normal access; if the source cannot supply a row, `MissingRowException` propagates. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ImmutableItemForest copySubtree(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, long)` | Returns an item forest holding the subtree rooted at `rootId` in the source (the row and all its descendants, re-based so the row is at depth 0), with row data fetched from the source. If `rootId` is not in the source forest the result is empty. `MissingRowException` propagates if the source lacks data for a row. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ImmutableItemForest rearrangeItemForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.MissingRowException` | Builds an item forest whose structure is `newForest` and whose row data comes from `source`. Every row id in `newForest` is looked up in `source` with normal access; a missing row raises `MissingRowException`. `newForest` is used as is (not copied), so callers should pass an immutable forest if they need a truly immutable result. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest getForest()` | Returns the raw forest (row ids and depths). Never null. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow getRow(long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.ItemAccessMode) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.MissingRowException` | Returns the stored row for `rowId`. Throws `MissingRowException` if the row id is not in this item forest. With `ItemAccessMode.SKIP_ACCESS_CHECK` the returned row is a variant whose item access is not checked against the current user; with any other mode the stored row is returned as is. |


A raw `Forest` together with a `RowRetriever` that can supply the `StructureRow` for each of its rows. This is the unit of data that generators produce and that action handlers receive as fragments. Implemented by `ImmutableItemForest`, `ManagerBackedItemForest` and by the plugin internally.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest getForest()` | Returns the structure of this item forest: the row ids and their depths. Never null. |
| `public default java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity> collectItemIds(com.almworks.integers.LongIterable)` | Returns the set of distinct item identities referenced by the given row ids, resolved through this item forest without loading the items themselves. Row ids that this forest cannot resolve are skipped silently. A null argument yields an empty set (it does not mean all rows). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilder`

```java
public interface ItemForestBuilder<B extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilder<B>> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemListBuilder<B>
```

Builder for a small item forest, passed by the plugin to inserters (`StructureGenerator.Inserter.createFragment`) and extenders (`StructureGenerator.Extender.ExtenderFunction.extend`). Rows are added in display order; `nextLevel`/`prevLevel` move the insertion point down and up the hierarchy. All methods return the builder itself for chaining. Generators only call it; they do not implement it.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract B nextLevel()` | Moves the insertion point one level down: rows added afterwards become children of the row added most recently. Requires that a row was added at the current level since the last level change, otherwise `IllegalStateException` (in the provided implementation). |
| `public abstract B prevLevel()` | Moves the insertion point one level up: the parent of the current level becomes the current row, so the next added row becomes its next sibling. Throws `IllegalStateException` (in the provided implementation) if already at the top level or if no row has been added at the current level yet. |
| `public abstract B nextFragment(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest)` | Appends a whole item forest at the current insertion point: its roots become siblings following the current row (at the current level) and its hierarchy is kept. Only each row's item identity and semantics are copied; new row ids are assigned. An empty fragment is ignored. After the call the current row is the last root of the fragment. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilderImpl`

```java
public final class ItemForestBuilderImpl implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilder<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilderImpl>
```

The standard `ItemForestBuilder` implementation, also used by the plugin when it calls generators. Each added row gets a fresh temporary negative row id (starting at -100 and decreasing) and a simple row record holding the item identity and semantics. The constructor looks up the plugin's item resolver as an OSGi service, so the class only works inside a running Jira with the plugin enabled. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ItemForestBuilderImpl()` | Creates an empty builder positioned at the top level with no current row. Obtains the item resolver service from the OSGi container at construction time. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilderImpl nextRow(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Same as `nextRow(itemId, 0)`: adds a row with default (zero) semantics. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilderImpl nextRow(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, long)` | Adds a row for `itemId` with the given row semantics at the current level, immediately after the current row (or as the first row of the level if none), and makes it the current row. Semantics 0 means default; when the plugin consumes the result it replaces 0 with the default semantics for the generator kind. `itemId` must not be null. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilderImpl nextLevel()` | Makes the current row the parent for subsequent rows and clears the current row. Throws `IllegalStateException` if there is no current row. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilderImpl prevLevel()` | Returns to the parent level: the current row becomes the parent of the row just added and the level goes up by one. Throws `IllegalStateException` if there is no current row (for example right after `nextLevel()`) or if already at the top level. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilderImpl nextFragment(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest)` | Copies the fragment's rows (item id and semantics, with new temporary ids) and appends them after the current row at the current level, preserving the fragment's hierarchy. Rows are read from the fragment with normal access, so `MissingRowException` may propagate. Empty fragments are ignored. Afterwards the current row is the last row at the current level. Not determined: behaviour when the current row already has children is flagged as wrong in the original (only an assertion guards it). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest build()` | Returns an `ImmutableItemForest` with everything added so far. The builder stays usable; a later `build()` includes later additions. |
| `public long getCurrentRowId()` | Returns the temporary id of the current row (the row most recently added at the current level, or the parent after `prevLevel()`). Throws `IllegalStateException` if there is no current row. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemListBuilder`


Builder for a flat list of rows; the base of `ItemForestBuilder`. Passed by the plugin to groupers (`GrouperFunction.createGroupRows`) to create group rows. Methods return the builder for chaining.

| member | meaning |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ManagerBackedItemForest`

```java
public class ManagerBackedItemForest implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest
```

An `ItemForest` that keeps only a raw forest and asks a `RowManager` for row data on demand. It does not copy the forest; it is as mutable and thread-safe as the forest and row manager given to it. Row access mode can be overridden with a default mode fixed at construction.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ManagerBackedItemForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.RowManager)` | Creates an item forest over `forest` using `rowManager` for rows, with `ItemAccessMode.NORMAL_ACCESS` as the default access mode. Neither argument may be null. |
| `public ManagerBackedItemForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.RowManager, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.ItemAccessMode)` | Creates an item forest with an explicit default access mode. Whenever a caller asks for `NORMAL_ACCESS`, this default is used instead; other modes pass through unchanged. If the default is null, a null mode is passed to the row manager for normal-access requests (behaviour then depends on the row manager; not determined). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest getForest()` | Returns the forest given to the constructor (same instance, not a copy). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow getRow(long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.ItemAccessMode) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.MissingRowException` | Delegates to the row manager's `getRow`, with the access mode substituted as described for the constructor. Throws `MissingRowException` if the row manager does not know the row. The row does not have to be in the forest. |
| `public void scanRows(com.almworks.integers.LongIterable, boolean, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.ItemAccessMode, com.almworks.integers.LongCollector, java.util.function.Predicate<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.MissingRowException` | Delegates to the row manager's `scanRows` with the same arguments, except the access mode substituted as described for the constructor. |
| `public String toString()` | Returns the full text form of the forest (`Forest.toFullString()`), without row data. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw`

The raw forest model: an ordered list of row ids, each with a depth, which together encode a set of trees. Contains the `Forest` interface, its array-backed implementation `ArrayForest` with all editing operations, and the callback and control interfaces used to walk a forest top-down or bottom-up.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest`

```java
public class ArrayForest implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest
```

The standard `Forest` implementation, backed by a list of row ids and a parallel list of depths. It is mutable until `makeImmutable()` is called and provides editing operations (merge, move, remove, reorder, replace) that keep the forest invariants as long as inputs are valid. Row ids 0 and -1 are rejected; the other invariants are checked only when JVM assertions are enabled, and `getDiagnostics` can be used to validate explicitly. Clients create it with constructors; it is not thread-safe, and read methods return live views where noted.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ArrayForest()` | Creates an empty mutable forest. |
| `public ArrayForest(long)` | Creates a mutable forest with the single root `row` at depth 0. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `row` is 0 or -1. |
| `public ArrayForest(com.almworks.integers.WritableLongList, com.almworks.integers.WritableIntList, boolean)` | Creates a mutable forest from parallel lists of row ids and depths. If `reuseLists` is true the given lists become the backing storage (later changes through either side are shared); if false they are copied. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if any row id is 0 or -1. Other invariants (equal sizes, depth rules, uniqueness) are only checked when JVM assertions are enabled; otherwise invalid input is accepted silently and later behaviour is undefined. |
| `public ArrayForest(com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.IntList)` | Creates a mutable forest from copies of the given row and depth lists. Same validation as the three-argument constructor. |
| `public ArrayForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Creates a mutable forest with copies of another forest's rows and depths. The immutability of the source is not carried over. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest set(com.almworks.integers.WritableLongList, com.almworks.integers.WritableIntList, boolean)` | Replaces the whole content with the given rows and depths, either adopting the lists (`reuseLists` true) or copying them. Returns this. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for row id 0 or -1 (message includes the offending position). Structural invariants are checked only with JVM assertions on. Oddity: this method does not check immutability, so it also changes forests marked immutable. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest set(com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.IntList)` | Replaces the content with copies of the given lists; otherwise as the three-argument `set` (including the missing immutability check). Returns this. |
| `public String getDiagnostics()` | Checks this forest's invariants and returns null if they hold, or a short English description of the first problem found. See the static `getDiagnostics(Forest)`. |
| `public static String getDiagnostics(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Checks the invariants of any forest and returns null if valid, otherwise a description of the first problem: row and depth lists of different size, first row not at depth 0, a duplicate row id, a negative depth, or a depth more than one greater than the previous row's. Row ids 0 and -1 are not checked here. Never throws for a well-formed `Forest` object. |
| `public boolean containsRow(long)` | True if `row` occurs in the forest. |
| `public void mergeForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, long, long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Same as `mergeForest(forest, under, after, null)`. |
| `public void addForest(long, long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Same as `mergeForest(forest, under, after)` but any `StructureException` is swallowed silently, leaving the forest unchanged in that case. Note the argument order differs from `mergeForest`. |
| `public void clear()` | Removes all rows. Throws `UnsupportedOperationException` if the forest is immutable. |
| `public void mergeForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, long, long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestChangeEventHandler) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Inserts `forest` under row `under` (0 for the top level), right after the sibling `after` (0 to insert as the first child). If the two forests share no rows the whole forest is inserted in one step. Otherwise rows already present here are moved (with their existing subtrees) to the position they have in `forest`, and new rows are inserted; in each parent the merged children come first, in `forest` order, followed by children that were there before. Null or empty `forest` does nothing. `after` that is not found or is not a child of `under` (after resolving it to its ancestor at the target level) is ignored with an info log, giving first-child position. Throws `ForestMergeStructureException` if `under` or one of its ancestors occurs in `forest` (the merge would create a cycle), `StructureException` with code `INVALID_FOREST_OPERATION` if `under` is not in this forest, `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable. The event handler, if not null, is told about every removal and insertion. |
| `public boolean addRow(long, long, long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Places a single row under `under` after `after` (same position rules as `mergeForest`). If the row already exists it is moved there with its subtree; otherwise it is inserted as a leaf. Returns false (doing nothing) if `row` is 0, true otherwise. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for row -1, `StructureException` if `under` is not found or is the row itself or one of its descendants, `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable. |
| `public void addForestMutuallyExclusive(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, long, long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Inserts `forest` as is under `under` after `after`, without checking for rows that already exist here; the caller guarantees the forests share no rows (otherwise the result has duplicates and is invalid). Depths are shifted to fit below `under`. Null or empty forest does nothing. Throws `StructureException` if `under` is not found, `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable. Invalid `after` is ignored as in `mergeForest`. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest removeSubtree(long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestChangeEventHandler)` | Removes `row` and all its descendants and returns them as a new forest re-based to depth 0. If the row is not found returns an empty forest and changes nothing (no immutability check in that case). Throws `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable and the row exists. The handler, if not null, gets `beforeSubtreeRemoved` before the rows go. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest removeSubtreeAtIndex(int, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestChangeEventHandler)` | Removes the row at `index` and its descendants and returns them as a new forest re-based to depth 0. The handler, if not null, is called before removal. Throws `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable; an invalid index causes an index-out-of-bounds error. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest subtree(long)` | New mutable forest with `row` as the single root followed by all its descendants, depths re-based so the row has depth 0. Empty forest if the row is not found. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest subtreeAtIndex(int)` | Same as `subtree` for the row at `index`; empty forest for a negative index. |
| `public int getSubtreeEnd(int)` | Returns the index just past the subtree of the row at `index`, that is the index of the first following row whose depth is not greater (or `size()`). The subtree occupies `[index, result)`. A negative index returns 0; an index greater than `size()` returns `size()`. In `ArrayForest` an index exactly equal to `size()` throws index-out-of-bounds (apparent off-by-one in the original). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest copySubforest(long)` | New mutable forest with the descendants of `row` (the row itself excluded), re-based so its children become roots. With `row` 0 returns a copy of the whole forest. Returns an empty forest if the row has no children and null if the row is not in the forest. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest copySubforestAtIndex(int)` | Same as `copySubforest` for the row at index `k`: null for a negative index, empty for a leaf, otherwise the descendants with its children as roots. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongList getRows()` | The row ids in forest order (pre-order: each row is followed by its whole subtree). In `ArrayForest` this is the live backing list, not a copy: it reflects later changes and must not be modified by the caller. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.IntList getDepths()` | The depth of each row, index-aligned with `getRows()`. Roots have depth 0; a row's depth is at most one more than the previous row's depth. In `ArrayForest` this is the live backing list. |

| `public int getDepth(int)` | Depth of the row at position `index`. Out-of-range indexes cause an index-out-of-bounds exception. |
| `public long getParent(long)` | Row id of the parent of `row`; 0 if the row is a root, is not in the forest, or `row` is 0. |
| `public int getParentIndex(int)` | Index of the parent of the row at `index`, or -1 if that row is a root or `index` is negative. Index past the end throws index-out-of-bounds. |
| `public int getPathIndexAtDepth(int, int)` | Index of the ancestor of the row at `index` that sits at `depth` (the row itself if its depth equals `depth`). Returns -1 if `index` or `depth` is negative or if `depth` is greater than the row's depth. |
| `public int getPrecedingSiblingIndex(int)` | Index of the closest earlier sibling of the row at `index`, or -1 if none or if `index` is 0 or negative. |
| `public long getPrecedingSiblingForIndex(int)` | Row id of the closest earlier sibling of the row at `index`, or 0 if there is none. |
| `public long getPrecedingSibling(long)` | Row id of the closest earlier sibling of `row` (same parent), or 0 if it is the first child, is not found, or `row` is 0. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongArray getPrecedingSiblings(long)` | All earlier siblings of `row`, in forest order (the nearest one last). Empty if the row is the first child or is not found. Returns a new list. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongArray getPrecedingSiblingsForIndex(int)` | All earlier siblings of the row at `index`, in forest order (nearest last). Empty for index 0 or negative. Returns a new list. |
| `public int getNextSiblingIndex(int)` | Index of the next sibling of the row at `index` (first later row at the same depth before any shallower row), or -1 if none or if `index` is negative or is the last index. |
| `public long getNextSiblingForIndex(int)` | Row id of the next sibling of the row at `index`, or 0 if none. |
| `public long getNextSibling(long)` | Row id of the next sibling of `row`, or 0 if none, not found, or `row` is 0. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongArray getChildren(long)` | Direct children of `row` in order; with `row` 0, the roots. Empty if the row is not found or has no children. Returns a new list. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongArray getChildrenAtIndex(int)` | Direct children of the row at `index`, in order. Empty for a negative index. Returns a new list. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.IntIterator getChildrenIndicesIterator(int)` | Iterator over the indexes of the direct children of the row at `index`, in order. Index -1 iterates over the roots; any other negative index gives an iterator that throws when first advanced. The iterator reads the forest lazily, so the forest must not change while it is used. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongArray getRoots()` | All rows of depth 0, in order. Returns a new list. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest filter(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<Long, ?>)` | Returns a forest containing only rows accepted by `filter`. A rejected row is dropped but its descendants are still tested; accepted descendants move up and take the place of the dropped row (they attach to the nearest accepted ancestor, or become roots). Order is preserved. A null filter, or one that accepts every row, returns this same instance rather than a copy; otherwise a new mutable forest is returned. The filter is called once per row at most. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest filterSoft(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<Long, ?>)` | Returns a forest with every row accepted by `filter` plus all ancestors of accepted rows, so the hierarchy of matching rows is preserved. Rejected rows with no accepted descendant are dropped. A null filter, or one accepting every row, returns this same instance; otherwise a new mutable forest. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest filterHardest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<Long, ?>)` | Returns a forest from which every rejected row is removed together with its whole subtree; descendants of rejected rows are not tested. Depths of kept rows are unchanged. A null filter, or one accepting every row, returns this same instance; otherwise a new mutable forest. |

| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest copy()` | Returns a new mutable `ArrayForest` with its own copies of the row and depth lists. The copy is never immutable. |

| `public <T, C> C foldUpwards(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestParentChildrenClosure<T, C>)` | Bottom-up fold. For each row, once all its children have been processed, calls `closure.visitRow(control, row, children, carry)` where `carry` is the accumulation of its children's results (null for leaves). Each result is then folded into its siblings' accumulation with `closure.combine(control, result, carry)`; siblings are combined from the last to the first. Returns the accumulation of the roots' results, or null if the forest is empty or the walk was cancelled through `control.cancel()`. |
| `public void scanDownwards(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestScanner)` | Top-down scan: calls `scanner.acceptRow(control, row)` for each row in forest order. Through the `ForestScanControl` the scanner can read the position, skip the current subtree or the rest of an ancestor's subtree, or cancel the scan. Does nothing on an empty forest. |
| `public void visitParentChildrenUpwards(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestParentChildrenVisitor)` | Walks the forest bottom-up and calls the visitor once for every row, after all of that row's descendants have been visited, passing the forest, the row id and the ids of its direct children (in order; empty for leaves). Rows are processed from the end of the forest towards the start. The visitor is not called for the invisible top level (the list of roots). If the visitor returns false the walk stops. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongArray getPath(long)` | Path from the root down to `row`, inclusive (root first). Empty if the row is not found. Returns a new list. |

| `public com.almworks.integers.LongArray getParentPathForIndex(int)` | Path from the root down to the parent of the row at `index` (the row itself excluded). Empty for roots and for a negative index. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest removeSubtree(long)` | Same as `removeSubtree(row, null)`. |
| `public void reorder(long, com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Rearranges the direct children of `parent` (0 for the roots) into the order given by `children`, each moving with its subtree. If `parent` is not found or has no children nothing happens. `children` must list exactly the current children: a row that is not a child throws a plain `RuntimeException`; omitting children or listing one twice is only caught by an assertion and otherwise corrupts the forest. Throws `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable. |
| `public void append(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Adds the rows of `forest` at the end, unchanged in depth, so its roots become new last roots. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the two forests share any row, `UnsupportedOperationException` if immutable. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongIntIterator iterator()` | Iterator over (row id, depth) pairs in forest order, reading the live lists. |
| `public void replaceSubtrees(long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Replaces all descendants of `rowId` with `forest`, whose roots become the row's children; with `rowId` 0 the whole content is replaced. If some rows of `forest` already exist elsewhere in this forest, the replacement is done by merging (those rows are moved, and any merge error is swallowed). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `rowId` is not found. Does not check immutability when no merge is needed; when merging is needed on an immutable forest, the old descendants are already removed when the merge throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, which propagates and leaves the forest half changed (as the original does). |
| `public void replaceSubtreesMutuallyExclusive(long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Like `replaceSubtrees`, but the caller guarantees that `forest` has no rows in common with the part of this forest that stays; no check is made and duplicates would corrupt the forest. Faster. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `rowId` (non-zero) is not found. Does not check immutability. |
| `public void replaceSubtreesMutuallyExclusiveAtIndex(int, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Like `replaceSubtreesMutuallyExclusive` for the row at `index`; index -1 replaces the whole content. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `index` is below -1 or not less than `size()`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest`

```java
public interface Forest extends com.almworks.integers.LongIntIterable
```

Read-only view of a forest: a sequence of row ids with a depth for each, in pre-order, that encodes an ordered set of trees. Invariants: row ids are unique and non-zero (and not -1, which is reserved for the super-root); the first row has depth 0; each depth is at most one more than the previous one. Positions are 0-based indexes; row id 0 is used in arguments and results to mean no row or the top level. `ArrayForest` is the standard implementation; implementations may be mutable unless `isImmutable()` is true.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest EMPTY` | Shared empty forest that has been made immutable. Note: in the original it is an `ArrayForest` whose `set` methods do not check immutability, so it could in principle be altered; callers must never do so. |
| `public abstract int size()` | Number of rows in the forest. |
| `public abstract boolean isEmpty()` | True if the forest has no rows. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongList getRows()` | The row ids in forest order (pre-order: each row is followed by its whole subtree). In `ArrayForest` this is the live backing list, not a copy: it reflects later changes and must not be modified by the caller. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.IntList getDepths()` | The depth of each row, index-aligned with `getRows()`. Roots have depth 0; a row's depth is at most one more than the previous row's depth. In `ArrayForest` this is the live backing list. |
| `public abstract long getRow(int)` | Row id at position `index` (0-based). An index outside 0..size-1 causes an index-out-of-bounds exception from the underlying list. |
| `public abstract int getDepth(int)` | Depth of the row at position `index`. Out-of-range indexes cause an index-out-of-bounds exception. |
| `public abstract boolean isImmutable()` | True if the forest has been made read-only; mutating operations then throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. |
| `public abstract int indexOf(long)` | Position of `row` in the forest, or -1 if the row is not present. Row id 0 always gives -1. Linear search. |
| `public abstract boolean containsRow(long)` | True if `row` occurs in the forest. |
| `public abstract int getSubtreeEnd(int)` | Returns the index just past the subtree of the row at `index`, that is the index of the first following row whose depth is not greater (or `size()`). The subtree occupies `[index, result)`. A negative index returns 0; an index greater than `size()` returns `size()`. In `ArrayForest` an index exactly equal to `size()` throws index-out-of-bounds (apparent off-by-one in the original). |
| `public abstract int getParentIndex(int)` | Index of the parent of the row at `index`, or -1 if that row is a root or `index` is negative. Index past the end throws index-out-of-bounds. |
| `public abstract long getParent(long)` | Row id of the parent of `row`; 0 if the row is a root, is not in the forest, or `row` is 0. |
| `public abstract long getPrecedingSibling(long)` | Row id of the closest earlier sibling of `row` (same parent), or 0 if it is the first child, is not found, or `row` is 0. |
| `public abstract int getPrecedingSiblingIndex(int)` | Index of the closest earlier sibling of the row at `index`, or -1 if none or if `index` is 0 or negative. |
| `public abstract long getPrecedingSiblingForIndex(int)` | Row id of the closest earlier sibling of the row at `index`, or 0 if there is none. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray getPrecedingSiblings(long)` | All earlier siblings of `row`, in forest order (the nearest one last). Empty if the row is the first child or is not found. Returns a new list. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray getPrecedingSiblingsForIndex(int)` | All earlier siblings of the row at `index`, in forest order (nearest last). Empty for index 0 or negative. Returns a new list. |
| `public abstract int getNextSiblingIndex(int)` | Index of the next sibling of the row at `index` (first later row at the same depth before any shallower row), or -1 if none or if `index` is negative or is the last index. |
| `public abstract long getNextSiblingForIndex(int)` | Row id of the next sibling of the row at `index`, or 0 if none. |
| `public abstract long getNextSibling(long)` | Row id of the next sibling of `row`, or 0 if none, not found, or `row` is 0. |
| `public abstract int getPathIndexAtDepth(int, int)` | Index of the ancestor of the row at `index` that sits at `depth` (the row itself if its depth equals `depth`). Returns -1 if `index` or `depth` is negative or if `depth` is greater than the row's depth. |
| `public abstract long getLastChild(long)` | Row id of the last direct child of `parent`; with `parent` 0, the last root. Returns 0 if the parent has no children or is not in the forest. |
| `public abstract long getLastChildByIndex(int)` | Row id of the last direct child of the row at `parentIndex`; a negative index means the last root. Returns 0 if there are no children or if `parentIndex` is not less than `size()`. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.IntIterator getChildrenIndicesIterator(int)` | Iterator over the indexes of the direct children of the row at `index`, in order. A negative index iterates over the roots. The iterator reads the forest lazily, so the forest must not change while it is used. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray getChildren(long)` | Direct children of `row` in order; with `row` 0, the roots. Empty if the row is not found or has no children. Returns a new list. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray getChildrenAtIndex(int)` | Direct children of the row at `index`, in order. Empty for a negative index. Returns a new list. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray getRoots()` | All rows of depth 0, in order. Returns a new list. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray getPath(long)` | Path from the root down to `row`, inclusive (root first). Empty if the row is not found. Returns a new list. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray getPathForIndex(int)` | Path from the root down to the row at `index`, inclusive. Empty for a negative index. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray getParentPathForIndex(int)` | Path from the root down to the parent of the row at `index` (the row itself excluded). Empty for roots and for a negative index. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest filter(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<Long, ?>)` | Returns a forest containing only rows accepted by `filter`. A rejected row is dropped but its descendants are still tested; accepted descendants move up and take the place of the dropped row (they attach to the nearest accepted ancestor, or become roots). Order is preserved. A null filter, or one that accepts every row, returns this same instance rather than a copy; otherwise a new mutable forest is returned. The filter is called once per row at most. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest filterSoft(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<Long, ?>)` | Returns a forest with every row accepted by `filter` plus all ancestors of accepted rows, so the hierarchy of matching rows is preserved. Rejected rows with no accepted descendant are dropped. A null filter, or one accepting every row, returns this same instance; otherwise a new mutable forest. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest filterHardest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<Long, ?>)` | Returns a forest from which every rejected row is removed together with its whole subtree; descendants of rejected rows are not tested. Depths of kept rows are unchanged. A null filter, or one accepting every row, returns this same instance; otherwise a new mutable forest. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest subtree(long)` | New mutable forest with `row` as the single root followed by all its descendants, depths re-based so the row has depth 0. Empty forest if the row is not found. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest subtreeAtIndex(int)` | Same as `subtree` for the row at `index`; empty forest for a negative index. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest copySubforest(long)` | New mutable forest with the descendants of `row` (the row itself excluded), re-based so its children become roots. With `row` 0 returns a copy of the whole forest. Returns an empty forest if the row has no children and null if the row is not in the forest. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest copySubforestAtIndex(int)` | Same as `copySubforest` for the row at index `k`: null for a negative index, empty for a leaf, otherwise the descendants with its children as roots. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest copy()` | Returns an independent mutable `ArrayForest` with the same rows and depths. The copy is not immutable even if this forest is. |
| `public abstract void visitParentChildrenUpwards(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestParentChildrenVisitor)` | Walks the forest bottom-up and calls the visitor once for every row, after all of that row's descendants have been visited, passing the forest, the row id and the ids of its direct children (in order; empty for leaves). Rows are processed from the end of the forest towards the start. The visitor is not called for the invisible top level (the list of roots). If the visitor returns false the walk stops. |
| `public abstract <T, C> C foldUpwards(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestParentChildrenClosure<T, C>)` | Bottom-up fold. For each row, once all its children have been processed, calls `closure.visitRow(control, row, children, carry)` where `carry` is the accumulation of its children's results (null for leaves). Each result is then folded into its siblings' accumulation with `closure.combine(control, result, carry)`; siblings are combined from the last to the first. Returns the accumulation of the roots' results, or null if the forest is empty or the walk was cancelled through `control.cancel()`. |
| `public abstract void scanDownwards(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestScanner)` | Top-down scan: calls `scanner.acceptRow(control, row)` for each row in forest order. Through the `ForestScanControl` the scanner can read the position, skip the current subtree or the rest of an ancestor's subtree, or cancel the scan. Does nothing on an empty forest. |
| `public abstract String toFullString()` | Text form listing every row as `row:depth`, without truncation. In `ArrayForest` the format is `forest(` then `ro,` if immutable, then comma-separated `row:depth` pairs, then `)`. |

Arguments: the forest being changed, the start index (inclusive) and end index (exclusive) of the rows about to be removed, and a copy of the removed subtree re-based to depth 0. |

Arguments: the forest being changed, the start index (inclusive) and end index (exclusive) of the inserted rows in it, and the inserted forest as passed in (with its own depths, before shifting). |
