### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestMergeStructureException`

```java
public class ForestMergeStructureException extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException
```

Thrown by `ArrayForest.mergeForest` when the merge point (`under`) or one of its ancestors also appears in the forest being merged, so merging would make a row its own ancestor. A `StructureException` with error code `INVALID_FOREST_OPERATION` reported for the merge point row.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ForestMergeStructureException(long, long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Creates the exception. Arguments: the merge point row, the row on the merge point's path that also occurs in the source forest, the source forest (being merged), and the target forest. The second row must be present in the source forest (otherwise an index error occurs while computing its root). The full text of both forests is captured only when trace logging is enabled for this class; otherwise placeholders are stored. |
| `public long getMergePoint()` | Row id under which the merge was attempted. |
| `public long getMergePointFatherFromForest()` | Row id from the merge point's ancestor path (possibly the merge point itself) that was found in the source forest. |
| `public long getMergePointFatherRoot()` | Root row of the source forest under which that conflicting row sits. |
| `public String getSourceForestString()` | Full text form of the source forest, or the placeholder `(n/a)` when trace logging was off. |
| `public String getTargetForestString()` | Full text form of the target forest, or `(n/a)` when trace logging was off. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestParentChildrenClosure`

```java
public interface ForestParentChildrenClosure<T, C>
```

Callback for `Forest.foldUpwards`, a bottom-up fold where each row is visited after its children. Type `T` is the per-row result, `C` the accumulation of sibling results. Implemented by callers.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract C combine(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestIterationControl, T, C)` | Folds one child's result into the accumulation for its siblings and returns the new accumulation. Arguments: the control (positioned at that child), the child's result, and the accumulation so far (null for the first call at a level). Siblings are combined from the last one to the first. |
| `public abstract T visitRow(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestIterationControl, long, com.almworks.integers.LongList, C)` | Visits one row after all its children and returns its result (may be null). Arguments: the control (positioned at the row), the row id, the ids of its direct children in forest order (empty for leaves; the list is reused and valid only during the call), and the accumulation of the children's results (null for leaves). Call `control.cancel()` to abort the fold. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestParentChildrenListClosure`

```java
public abstract class ForestParentChildrenListClosure<T> implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestParentChildrenClosure<T, java.util.List<T>>
```

Convenience base for `ForestParentChildrenClosure` whose accumulation is simply a list of the children's results. Subclasses implement only `visitRow`. Not thread-safe; one instance per fold.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ForestParentChildrenListClosure()` | Creates the closure with an empty internal pool of lists. |
| `public java.util.List<T> combine(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestIterationControl, T, java.util.List<T>)` | Adds `value` to the list for the current level and returns it, starting a fresh (cleared) list when `carry` is null. Because children are combined from last to first, the list holds the children's results in reverse forest order. The list objects are reused per depth, so a `visitRow` implementation must not keep a reference to the list it receives after it returns. |


Callback for `Forest.visitParentChildrenUpwards`: receives each row with its direct children, bottom-up. Implemented by callers.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|

Arguments: the forest, the row id, and its direct children in order (empty for leaves; valid only during the call). Return true to continue, false to stop the walk. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestScanControl`


Control object for `Forest.scanDownwards`. Besides the position given by `ForestIterationControl`, it exposes the current row's ancestry and lets the scanner skip parts of the forest. Valid only during the `acceptRow` call.

| `public abstract int getParentIndex()` | Index of the current row's parent, -1 for a root. |
| `public abstract int skipSubtree()` | Requests that the scan skip the descendants of the current row and continue with the next row after its subtree. Returns that index (which equals `size()` if nothing follows). |
| `public abstract int skipParentSubtree(int)` | Requests that the scan skip all following rows deeper than `depth`, continuing at the next row whose depth is `depth` or less. With `depth` equal to the current depth this is the same as `skipSubtree`; with a smaller depth it also skips the rest of the ancestor's subtree; -1 ends the scan. Returns the index where the scan will continue. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `depth` is below -1 or greater than the current depth. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator`

The generator extension point. Generators are plugin modules (inserters, extenders, groupers, sorters, filters) that build or transform part of a forest automatically, and may optionally react to user edits of the generated rows. The package holds the service provider interfaces that generator authors implement, the context objects the plugin passes to them, the `GeneratorManager` service that stores generator instances, and constants naming built-in generators and common parameters.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionEffect`

```java
public interface ActionEffect
```

A deferred change produced by a generator's action handler, registered through `HandlingContext.effect(effect, inverse)`. Implemented by generator authors. The plugin calls `apply` while it evaluates a user's edit; `apply` checks feasibility and either blocks or registers the actual work through `EffectContext.effect`. The inverse effect, if given, is kept so the change can be undone later.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void apply(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.EffectContext)` | Prepares the change. Should call `context.effect(explanation, runnable)` to register the code that really performs it (run later when the action is carried out), or `context.block`/`context.yield` to refuse. If it neither blocks nor registers anything, the action counts as handled with no work to do. Exceptions thrown here are caught by the plugin, logged, and turn into a block with a generic error message. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionHandler`

```java
public interface ActionHandler
```

Marker base for the objects through which a generator reacts to user edits (add, move, reorder, remove) of rows it produced or controls. A generator that wants to handle edits implements one of the `ActionHandlingGenerator` sub-interfaces and returns a handler of the matching nested type from `createActionHandler`. Handler methods do not change data directly: they inspect the request and call `block`, `yield` or `effect` on the `HandlingContext`. Any exception from a handler method is caught by the plugin, logged, and the action is blocked with a generic error message.

Arguments: the row (or new row) concerned; the old position, null when the row is being added; the new position, null when the row is being removed; the context for blocking or registering effects. Also called once per row when a fragment is added (each with `from` null). In positions, absent neighbours are the zero row, not null. |
| `public abstract void reorderExtension(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructurePosition, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructurePosition, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.HandlingContext)` | Requests a change of order of `row` among siblings produced by this extender, under the same parent. Arguments: the row, its old position, its new position (both non-null; `after`/`before` are adjusted to neighbours produced by this extender, or the zero row), and the context. |
| `public abstract String getAddOptionDescription()` | Short user-facing text describing what an add will do, shown when the user chooses how the edit should be applied. Must not be null. |
| `public abstract String getMoveOptionDescription()` | Short user-facing text describing what a move will do. Must not be null. |
| `public abstract String getReorderOptionDescription()` | Short user-facing text describing what a reorder will do. Must not be null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionHandlingAlwaysAllowed`

Runtime annotation placed on a generator class. It means the generator's action handling cannot be switched off by the user: the plugin does not offer the allow-updates option in its configuration form and ignores the `disableActions` parameter for it.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionHandlingGenerator`

```java
public interface ActionHandlingGenerator<T extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionHandler> extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator
```

A generator that can react to user edits of the rows it affects. Type `T` is the handler type matching the generator kind. Implemented by generator authors (usually via the `AbstractGenerator` subclasses). The plugin asks for a handler when it evaluates an edit; if the handler is null, edits that need this generator are blocked with a message.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract T createActionHandler(java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Returns a handler for edits, given the generator instance's stored parameters, or null if this configuration cannot handle edits. Called whenever the plugin evaluates an edit, so it should be cheap. Exceptions are caught, logged, and treated as null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.CoreGeneratorParameters`

```java
public class CoreGeneratorParameters
```

Names of generator parameters that the plugin itself interprets for all generators of a kind, in addition to each generator's own parameters. Parameters are stored in the generator's parameter map under these keys. Only constants; the class is not meant to be instantiated.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final String DISABLE_ACTIONS = "disableActions"` | Key `disableActions`, boolean. When true, the generator does not handle user edits (they are blocked or left to other generators), unless the generator class carries `ActionHandlingAlwaysAllowed`. |
| `public static final String LEVEL_FROM = "from"` | Key `from`, positive integer: first level (1 = the level right below the generator's position) at which an extender or sorter applies. Absent means from the first level. |
| `public static final String LEVEL_TO = "to"` | Key `to`, positive integer: last level at which an extender or sorter applies. Absent means no limit. The configuration form defaults extenders to 10. |
| `public static final String LEVEL = "level"` | Key `level`, positive integer: the single level at which a grouper groups (default 1) or a filter tests rows (when set, the filter keeps shallower rows, tests rows at that level and keeps or drops each with its whole subtree). |
| `public static final String FILTER_HARD = "hard"` | Key `hard`, boolean. When true, a filter drops non-matching rows even if they have matching descendants (those descendants move up); when false, ancestors of matching rows are kept so the hierarchy stays. |
| `public static final String FILTER_SHOW_SUBITEMS = "showSubItems"` | Key `showSubItems`, boolean. When true, a row that matches the filter is kept with its whole subtree, without testing the descendants. |
| `public static final String GROUPER_LEVEL_INCLUDE_GROUPS = "includeGroups"` | Key `includeGroups`, boolean. When false (default), group rows made by other groupers do not count as a level and the grouper looks through them; when true they count as ordinary rows. |
| `public static final String SORT_DESCENDING = "desc"` | Key `desc`, boolean. When true, a sorter reverses the order given by its compare function. |
| `public static final String INSERTER_LIMIT = "limit"` | Key `limit`: maximum number of items an inserter adds (used by the query-based inserters). |
| `public static final String JQL = "jql"` | Key `jql`: a JQL query string, used by the JQL inserter and the JQL filter. |
| `public static final String FIELD_ID = "fieldId"` | Key `fieldId`: the Jira field id used by the field grouper. |
| `public CoreGeneratorParameters()` | Default constructor; the class has only constants and there is no reason to instantiate it. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.GeneratorManager`

```java
public interface GeneratorManager
```

Service that stores generator instances: a generator module key plus a parameter map, identified by a long id. Rows that show a generator refer to these ids. Obtained as a public OSGi component (inject `GeneratorManager`). Persistent generators are kept in the database; transient ones live in memory on the current node only. Persistent ids are positive even numbers, transient ids positive odd numbers. Note: the implementation performs no permission checks of its own and does not verify that the module key names an installed generator; callers are responsible for both.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long createGenerator(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>, Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Stores a new persistent generator and returns its id. Arguments: the complete module key (must not be blank; it is trimmed), the parameters (null means none; the map is copied, and nested maps and lists are copied too), and the id of the structure that owns the generator, or null. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a blank module key; database errors propagate as runtime exceptions. |
| `public abstract long createTransientGenerator(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Creates a generator that lives only in memory on this node until restart or deletion, with no owning structure, and returns its id. Arguments as for `createGenerator`. Ids start over after a restart. |
| `public abstract void updateGenerator(long, String, java.util.Map<String, Object>, Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Replaces the module key, parameters and owning structure of a persistent generator (all three; a null owner clears it) and notifies change tracking so forests using it are regenerated. Throws `StructureException` with `INVALID_PARAMETER` if the id is not a persistent id (transient generators cannot be edited), or with `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` if no such generator exists. `IllegalArgumentException` for a blank module key. |
| `public abstract void deleteGenerator(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Deletes the generator with this id, persistent or transient. Deleting a missing id does nothing and raises no error. Deleting a persistent generator notifies change tracking. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.GeneratorSpec getGenerator(long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Returns the stored definition of the generator with this id. Although declared non-null and to throw `StructureException`, the implementation returns null when no generator has this id. Non-positive ids are not valid; the result for them is not determined (only internal assertions guard it). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.GeneratorSpec`

```java
public final class GeneratorSpec
```

Immutable definition of a stored generator: module key, parameters and owning structure. Returned by `GeneratorManager.getGenerator`. Thread-safe.

The parameters are deep-copied into an unmodifiable map with insertion order kept; null or empty gives an empty map. The owning structure id may be null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.GeneratorUnavailableException`

```java
public class GeneratorUnavailableException extends Exception
```

Checked exception a generator throws from its configuration-form methods when it cannot work at the moment (for example a required application is missing). The plugin logs it and shows the localized message to the user instead of the form.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public GeneratorUnavailableException(String)` | Creates the exception with one message used both as the technical and the user-facing message. |
| `public GeneratorUnavailableException(String, String)` | Creates the exception with a technical message and a separate user-facing, localized message. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ItemChangeFilter`

```java
public interface ItemChangeFilter
```

Registered by a generator during generation (`GenerationContext.addItemChangeFilter`) to say which item changes should make the forest regenerate. Implemented by generator authors or taken from the `generator.util` helpers. The plugin keeps the filters from the latest generation and, when items change, asks them whether the generated result may be stale. Exceptions are logged and treated as false.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean accept(java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.ItemChangeFilterContext)` | Returns true if any of the changed items in `itemIds` affects this generator's output, so the forest should be regenerated. Arguments: the identities of items that changed since the last check (non-null), and a context that can resolve items. Should be fast. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.NotConfigurable`

```java
public @interface NotConfigurable
```

Runtime annotation placed on a generator class that has no configuration. The plugin then offers no edit form for it and reports it as not configurable to the UI.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator
```

Base service provider interface for generators: plugin modules that create or transform part of a forest automatically. A generator is declared as a module of one of the generator kinds in an app's plugin descriptor and implements one of the nested kind interfaces (`Inserter`, `Extender`, `Grouper`, `Sorter`, `Filter`). The plugin holds one module instance and calls it with the parameters of each stored generator instance, possibly from several threads at once, so implementations should be stateless. The methods here support the configuration form and summary; any exception other than `GeneratorUnavailableException` is caught and logged by the plugin.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void addDefaultFormParameters(java.util.Map<String, Object>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.GeneratorUnavailableException` | Fills the form map with default values for creating a new generator instance; the map is passed to the generator's form template. The plugin has already put its own entries in the map. Throws `GeneratorUnavailableException` if the generator cannot be configured now. |
| `public abstract void addParametersToForm(java.util.Map<String, Object>, java.util.Map<String, Object>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.GeneratorUnavailableException` | Converts stored parameters (first argument) into form values (second argument, to be filled) when an existing instance is edited. Throws `GeneratorUnavailableException` if the generator cannot be configured now. |
| `public abstract java.util.Map<String, Object> buildParametersFromForm(java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.atlassian.jira.util.ErrorCollection) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.GeneratorUnavailableException` | Converts submitted form values into the parameters to store and returns them (never null). Validation problems are reported by adding errors to the given collection, keyed by form field where possible. The plugin merges the result over its own kind-specific parameters (for example level settings and `disableActions`). Throws `GeneratorUnavailableException` if the generator cannot be configured now. |
| `public abstract void addParametersForSummary(java.util.Map<String, Object>, java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Fills the second map with values for the generator's summary template, based on the stored parameters (first argument). |
| `public abstract boolean isAvailable()` | False if the generator cannot be used in this installation (for example a required application is absent). Unavailable generators are not offered to users in the list of generators. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.ApplicabilityChecker`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator.ApplicabilityChecker
```

Tells whether a generator function applies to a given row. Used as the base of `Extender.ExtenderFunction` and returned by `Sorter.getApplicabilityChecker`. Implemented by generator authors; `IssueApplicabilityChecker` is a ready one.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean isApplicableTo(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | True if the generator should process this row. For extenders, false means the row is not extended. For sorters, rows that are not applicable are placed after all applicable siblings, keeping their relative order. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Context`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator.Context
```

Marker base type for the context objects the plugin passes to generators (`GenerationContext`, `HandlingContext`, `EffectContext`, `ItemChangeFilterContext`). Implemented by the plugin only.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.EffectContext`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator.EffectContext extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Context
```

Context passed to `ActionEffect.apply`. Implemented by the plugin. Lets the effect refuse the action or register the code that will perform it.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void block(String)` | Refuses the action. The argument is a user-facing explanation (may be null). Blocking prevents the whole edit. |
| `public abstract void yield(String)` | Refuses softly: this generator steps aside if another generator can handle the action, otherwise it acts like a block. The argument is a user-facing explanation. |
| `public abstract void effect(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RunnableE<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException>)` | Registers the code that actually performs the change, with a short user-facing description of it. The code runs later, when the edit is carried out; a `StructureException` it throws makes that part of the action fail with that error, and other exceptions are wrapped as an action failure. A later call replaces an earlier one within the same `apply`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Extender`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator.Extender extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator
```

Generator kind that adds child rows under existing rows (for example sub-tasks under issues). The plugin applies it repeatedly: each pass adds children to the rows at the current level, and the new rows are extended in the next pass, within the level range set by the `from`/`to` parameters. Loops are detected by the plugin and shown as loop markers. Implemented by generator authors.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Extender.ExtenderFunction getExtenderFunction(java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.GenerationContext)` | Returns the function to apply in the current pass, given the instance's parameters and the generation context, or null to add nothing. Called once per pass; exceptions are logged and the pass adds nothing. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Extender.ExtenderFunction`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator.Extender.ExtenderFunction extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.ApplicabilityChecker
```

Function that produces the children for one row. Implemented by generator authors and returned from `Extender.getExtenderFunction`. Its `isApplicableTo` decides which rows are extended.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void extend(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForestBuilder)` | Adds the children of `row` to `builder` with `nextRow`. Only applicable rows are passed; automation rows and loop markers never are. The produced rows are added as direct children after any existing children; any nesting built with `nextLevel` is flattened. Rows with semantics 0 get the plugin's default extender semantics. Exceptions are logged and stop this pass. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Filter`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator.Filter extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator
```

Generator kind that removes rows that do not match from the part of the forest below the generator. How non-matching rows are handled is controlled by the `hard`, `showSubItems` and `level` parameters (see `CoreGeneratorParameters`). Automation rows are always treated as matching. Implemented by generator authors.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Filter.FilterFunction getFilterFunction(java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.GenerationContext)` | Returns the predicate for this generation, given the instance's parameters and the generation context, or null to leave the forest unchanged. Exceptions are logged and leave the forest unchanged. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Filter.FilterFunction`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator.Filter.FilterFunction
```

Row predicate returned from `Filter.getFilterFunction`. Implemented by generator authors.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean matches(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | True if the row should stay. An exception aborts the filter for this generation, leaving the forest unfiltered. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.GenerationContext`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator.GenerationContext extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Context
```

Context passed to generators while they produce their functions or fragments. Implemented by the plugin; valid only during the generation call it was given to. Gives access to the forest being worked on, to change information, to per-generator storage, and lets the generator register what should trigger the next regeneration.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void addItemChangeFilter(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ItemChangeFilter)` | Registers a filter that decides which item changes make this generator's result stale. Filters are kept until the next generation replaces them. |
| `public abstract void addUpdateChecker(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.UpdateChecker)` | Registers a checker that is polled to find out whether the result has become stale for reasons other than item changes (for example time). Kept until the next generation. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest previewForest()` | The rows the generator is applied to, as an immutable item forest. For most kinds this is the part of the forest below the generator's position at this point of generation. While a grouper's function is being created, it is the flat list of rows that are about to be grouped. Never null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.item.ItemForest inputForest()` | The whole forest the generator works on, or null. In the original only groupers get a non-null value (during `createGrouperFunction`); for other kinds it is null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec getForestSpecBeingTransformed()` | If the forest being generated is a transformed forest (its spec has transformations), the spec of the forest before the last transformation; otherwise null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemVersionUpdate itemsUpdate()` | Description of item changes since the previous generation of this forest. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemVersionUpdate itemsUpdate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion)` | Description of item changes since the given data version, from the plugin's change tracker. |
| `public abstract void putObject(Object, Object)` | Stores a value under a key for this generator instance, kept across later generations of the same forest. Null value removes the entry. The plugin may keep it through a soft reference, so it can disappear under memory pressure; use it only as a cache. |
| `public abstract <T> T getObject(Object)` | Reads a value stored with `putObject` by the same generator instance, or null if absent or cleared. |
| `public abstract void putTempObject(Object, Object)` | Stores a value for this generator instance for the current generation only. |
| `public abstract <T> T getTempObject(Object)` | Reads a value stored with `putTempObject` during the current generation, or null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSpec getForestSpec()` | The spec of the forest being generated. Never null. |
| `public abstract boolean isStopped()` | True if the generation has been cancelled; long-running generators should check it and return early. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.HandlingContext`

```java
public interface StructureGenerator.HandlingContext extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.Context
```

Context passed to action handler methods while the plugin evaluates a user edit. Implemented by the plugin. The handler must answer by calling `block`, `yield` or `effect`; calling none means the generator does not take part. The plugin may call handler methods while it evaluates alternative ways to apply an edit, before anything is carried out, so they must not change data directly; real changes go through effects.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void block(String)` | Refuses the edit with a user-facing explanation (may be null); the whole edit is prevented. |
| `public abstract void yield(String)` | Refuses softly: if another generator handles the edit, this refusal is dropped; if not, it acts as a block. The argument is a user-facing explanation. |
| `public abstract void effect(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionEffect, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ActionEffect)` | Accepts the edit and supplies the change to perform (`effect`, non-null) and optionally its undo (`inverse`, may be null). The plugin calls `effect.apply` right away; if it does not block, the edit counts as handled by this generator. |
| `public abstract java.util.Map<String, Object> parameters()` | The extra action parameters addressed to this generator by the client, with the generator prefix removed. Read-only; empty if none. |
| `public abstract void putObject(Object, Object)` | Stores a value for this generator instance for the duration of handling this edit. |
| `public abstract <T> T getObject(Object)` | Reads a value stored with `putObject` during this edit, or null. A request with key `AuthContext.class` returns the security context the generator should use. |

The hierarchy built is kept. Rows with semantics 0 get the plugin's default inserter semantics. If it throws, the error is logged and nothing is inserted. |

If it throws, the sorter does nothing in this generation. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.util`

Helpers for generator authors: abstract base classes with sensible defaults for each generator kind, ready-made item change filters and update checkers, an issue-only applicability checker, and a helper that loads attribute values for the rows a generator is working on while arranging re-generation when those values change.

| `public boolean isAvailable()` | Returns true: always available. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.util.BasicItemChangeFilter`

```java
public class BasicItemChangeFilter implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.util.RecordingItemChangeFilter
```

An `ItemChangeFilter` that accepts a change when it touches any item from a known set, held as a set of issue ids plus a set of other item identities. Created through the static factories: fixed filters (`forIssues`, `forItems`) or recording filters (`createRecording`) to which items are added while generating. Not thread-safe while recording; reading is safe once recording is finished.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected BasicItemChangeFilter(com.almworks.integers.WritableLongSet, java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Protected constructor for subclasses: creates a recording filter that adds issues to the given issue id set and other items to the given identity set (both used directly, not copied). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ItemChangeFilter forIssues(com.almworks.integers.LongSet)` | Returns a fixed (non-recording) filter that accepts a change if any changed item is an issue whose id is in `issues`. The set is used directly, not copied. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.ItemChangeFilter forItems(com.almworks.integers.LongSet, java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Returns a fixed filter that accepts a change if any changed issue id is in `issues` or any changed non-issue item is in `nonIssues`. Sets are used directly. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.util.RecordingItemChangeFilter createRecording()` | Returns a new empty recording filter backed by its own sets. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.util.RecordingItemChangeFilter createRecording(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity...)` | Returns a new recording filter with the given items already recorded. |
| `public final void recordItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | Records the item shown by `row`, so changes to it will be accepted. Throws `UnsupportedOperationException` on a fixed filter. |
| `public final void recordItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Records an item: issues go to the issue id set, others to the identity set. Throws `UnsupportedOperationException` on a fixed filter. |
| `public boolean accept(java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.ItemChangeFilterContext)` | True if any identity in `itemIds` is a recorded or given item (issues are matched by issue id). The context is not used. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.util.GenerationUtil`

```java
public class GenerationUtil
```

Static helper for generators that need attribute values of the rows they process (for example sorters and groupers by attribute). Not instantiable.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.util.lang.Pair<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.util.RecordingAttributeUpdateChecker> getValuesFromSubjectForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.GenerationContext, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.StructureAttributeService)` | Same as the collection variant with a single attribute spec. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.util.lang.Pair<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.RowValues, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.util.RecordingAttributeUpdateChecker> getValuesFromSubjectForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.generator.StructureGenerator.GenerationContext, java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>>, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.StructureAttributeService)` | Loads the given attributes for the given rows through the attribute service and returns the values together with a `RecordingAttributeUpdateChecker`. If the forest being generated is a transformation, values are computed in the forest before that transformation; otherwise they are computed in the context's input forest (or preview forest if there is no input) under the current forest spec. The checker is registered with the context automatically; the generator should call `record` for each row whose value it actually used, so that a change in those values triggers regeneration. Errors from the attribute service propagate. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.i18n`

A minimal localisation abstraction: an `I18n` object resolves message keys to text in one locale, and an `I18nProvider` gives one for the current user. The Jira-backed implementations delegate to Jira's own i18n helper.

```java
public interface I18n
```

| `public abstract String getText(String, Object...)` | Returns the message for `key` in this object's locale, with the given arguments substituted into its placeholders. Behaviour for unknown keys follows the underlying implementation (the Jira-backed one typically returns the key itself). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.i18n.JiraI18n`

```java
public class JiraI18n implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.i18n.I18n
```

`I18n` backed by a Jira `I18nHelper`. Internal-use. Instances wrap a helper given to the constructor, or are made by the static factories, which use Jira's i18n helper factory and fall back to a stand-in when Jira services are not available (for example in unit tests). Thread safety follows the wrapped helper.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public JiraI18n(com.atlassian.jira.util.I18nHelper)` | Wraps the given Jira helper; all calls are delegated to it. |
| `public String getText(String, Object...)` | Returns the helper's text for `key` with the given arguments. |
| `public java.util.Locale getLocale()` | Returns the helper's locale. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.i18n.I18n forCurrentUser()` | Static. Same as `create(null, user)` where `user` is the user the plugin considers current for this thread (may be null for anonymous). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.i18n.I18n create(java.util.Locale, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Static. Returns an `I18n` for `locale` if it is not null; otherwise for the preferred locale of `user` if not null; otherwise for Jira's default locale (or the root locale if that cannot be read). If Jira's i18n helper factory is unavailable, returns a stand-in whose `getText` returns the key followed by a space and the argument array in bracketed list form, and whose locale is English. Never null. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item`

Item identities and item types. Every row of a forest points to an item (an issue, a project, a folder, a memo, a user and so on); an item is named by an `ItemIdentity` (an item type key plus a numeric or textual ID) whose string form is persisted. The package also holds the constants for the built-in type keys, helper factories, the bulk identity set, the resolver that turns identities into Jira objects, the change tracker, and the extension interfaces an item type module may implement.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.AuxiliaryIdentities`

```java
public class AuxiliaryIdentities
```

Holder of type keys and identity factories for item types that come from integrations with other apps (remote issue links, Tempo work attributes and teams, Jira global/project permissions, Xray test runs). Marked internal. All members are static; the class is never instantiated in practice. The values are persisted, so the exact strings, including a misspelling in three of them, must be kept.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final String REMOTE_ISSUE_LINK_TYPE = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-remote-issue-link"` | Item type key for remote issue links coming from the integration: exactly `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-remote-issue-link`. Not the same key as `CoreItemTypes.REMOTE_LINK`. |
| `public static final String TEMPO_WORK_ATTRIBUTE = "com.almworks.jira.stucture:type-tempo-work-attribute"` | Item type key for Tempo work attributes: exactly `com.almworks.jira.stucture:type-tempo-work-attribute` (note the misspelled plugin prefix `stucture`; it is the persisted value and must not be corrected). Used with string IDs. |
| `public static final String TEMPO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP = "com.almworks.jira.stucture:type-tempo-team-membership"` | Item type key for Tempo team memberships: exactly `com.almworks.jira.stucture:type-tempo-team-membership` (misspelled prefix kept on purpose). Used with string IDs. |
| `public static final String TEMPO_TEAM_PERMISSIONS = "com.almworks.jira.stucture:type-tempo-team-permissions"` | Item type key for Tempo team permissions: exactly `com.almworks.jira.stucture:type-tempo-team-permissions` (misspelled prefix kept on purpose). Used with string IDs. |
| `public static final String GLOBAL_PERMISSION_TYPE = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-global-permission"` | Item type key for a Jira global permission: exactly `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-global-permission`. Used with string IDs (the permission key). |
| `public static final String PROJECT_PERMISSION_TYPE = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project-permission"` | Item type key for a Jira project permission: exactly `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project-permission`. Used with string IDs (the permission key). |
| `public static final String XRAY_TEST_RUN = "com.almworks.jira.structure:xray-test-run"` | Item type key for an Xray test run: exactly `com.almworks.jira.structure:xray-test-run` (note: no `type-` prefix). Used with long IDs. |

Null, blank or over-long keys give `IllegalArgumentException`. |

Null, blank or over-long keys give `IllegalArgumentException`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.BulkAccessCheckingItemType`

```java
public interface BulkAccessCheckingItemType
```

Optional extension interface that an item type module (a `StructureItemType` implementation) may also implement to check visibility of many items at once instead of one by one. When the plugin works out which rows of a forest a user may see, it groups the items by type and, for a type implementing this interface, makes one call per type; for other types it falls back to `accessItem` plus `isVisible` per item. If the call throws, the plugin treats every item of that batch as inaccessible.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void filterInaccessible(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, boolean, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet)` | Examines the items in the first argument (the plugin passes only items of this module's type) and adds to the fourth argument (a mutable collector) every item that does not exist or that the user in the second argument (null means anonymous) may not see. When the third argument is true, security is overridden: only items that do not exist should be collected. Must not modify the first argument and must not remove anything from the collector; items not added are treated as accessible. This is the rule for other plugins' types; the built-in item types follow their own module claims, where several collect fewer items (some none at all). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.BulkAccessibleItemType`

```java
public interface BulkAccessibleItemType<T>
```

Optional extension interface for item type modules (public SPI) that can load many item objects in one go. Type parameter `T` is the item object class, the same as the module's `StructureItemType<T>`. The plugin uses it when resolving several identities of one type at once (`ItemResolver.resolveItems`, bulk attribute loading); the plugin still applies `isVisible` to each returned object afterwards.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void accessItems(java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, java.util.function.BiConsumer<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, T>)` | Loads the items named by the identities in the first argument (all of this module's type; the collection may be unmodifiable) and reports each one found by calling the second argument with the identity and the loaded object. Items that do not exist are simply not reported (the caller treats them as null). No permission filtering is expected here. Each identity should be reported at most once; order is free. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.CoreIdentities`

```java
public class CoreIdentities
```

Static factory and test methods for the identities of the built-in item types (issues, projects, versions, users, folders, memos, links and so on). Each factory builds an `ItemIdentity` with the matching `CoreItemTypes` key and does not check that the item exists; each `isX` method checks both the type key and the ID kind (long or string). Public API; the class cannot be instantiated. Results are immutable and safe to share. The string forms shown in examples follow `ItemIdentity.toString`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final String ANONYMOUS_USER_ID = "-"` | The string ID `-` used for the anonymous (not logged-in) user: `user((String) null)` returns `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-user//-`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.CoreItemTypes`

```java
public interface CoreItemTypes
```

Constants for the item type keys of the built-in item types. A type key is the complete key of the item type module (`<plugin key>:<module key>`) and is the first part of every persisted item identity, so these exact strings are part of the stored data format. Public API; an interface used only for its constants and one static helper.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final String ISSUE = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`: Jira issues; long ID = issue ID. |
| `public static final String PROJECT = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project`: Jira projects; long ID = project ID. |
| `public static final String VERSION = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-version"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-version`: a single Jira project version; long ID = version ID. |
| `public static final String VERSION_NAME = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-version-name"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-version-name`: all versions sharing a (canonical) name across projects; string ID = canonical name. |
| `public static final String COMPONENT = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project-component"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project-component`: Jira project components; long ID. |
| `public static final String ISSUETYPE = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issuetype"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issuetype`: Jira issue types; string ID = issue type ID. |
| `public static final String STATUS = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-status"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-status`: Jira statuses; string ID = status ID. |
| `public static final String RESOLUTION = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-resolution"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-resolution`: Jira resolutions; string ID = resolution ID. |

| `public static final String LABEL = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-label"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-label`: labels; string ID = the label text. |
| `public static final String USER = "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-user"` | Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-user`: Jira users; string ID = user key, `-` for anonymous. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.CoreSemantics`

```java
public interface CoreSemantics
```

Constants for the semantics code of a forest row (a long stored with each row next to its item). The code tells how the row got into a generated forest. Marked internal. When a generator creates a row with semantics 0, the plugin replaces it with the code of that generator's kind.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final int NONE = 0` | 0: an ordinary row with no special meaning (also the value for rows added by hand). |
| `public static final int TITLE = 1` | 1: a title row, a heading row placed at the top of a forest (for example the name of a sub-structure or query); several features skip such rows. |
| `public static final int GROUP = 2` | 2: a group row created by a grouper generator to collect rows sharing a value. |
| `public static final int INSERTED = 3` | 3: a row added by an inserter generator. |
| `public static final int EXTENSION = 4` | 4: a row added by an extender generator under an existing row. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.CreatableItemType`

```java
public interface CreatableItemType
```

Optional extension interface for an item type module whose items can be created from the plugin's UI or REST API ("create new item" in a structure). The plugin first asks for a dummy row to preview where the new item would go (running generators in a dry run), then calls `createItem`. Both receive the raw value map sent by the client (for generic items the keys are `summary`, `description` and `params`).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow createDummyRow(long, long, java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.atlassian.jira.util.ErrorCollection) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Builds a temporary, not persisted row standing for the item that would be created. Arguments: the row ID to give the row, the row semantics code, the client's values, and an error collection to fill with field-level validation errors. Returns the row, or null when validation failed (errors must then be added; a null result with no errors is reported by the plugin as a creation failure). Throws `StructureException` for non-field errors. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity createItem(java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.atlassian.jira.util.ErrorCollection) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Creates and persists the item from the client's values (first argument) and returns its new identity. Field-level problems are added to the error collection (second argument) and null is returned; other failures are thrown as `StructureException`. A null result without errors is treated by the plugin as a failure. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.DeadItemsCheckingItemType`

```java
public interface DeadItemsCheckingItemType
```

Optional extension interface for an item type module that can tell which of its items no longer exist. The plugin's periodic forest cleanup collects the items used in stored forests, groups them by type and calls this once per type that implements it; rows of dead items may then be removed. Errors are logged and the type is skipped.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void filterDead(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet)` | Looks at the items in the first argument (a copy containing only this module's type) and adds to the second argument (a mutable collector) every item that has been permanently deleted. Items whose existence cannot be decided should not be added. Must not remove anything from the collector. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity`

```java
public abstract class ItemIdentity implements java.io.Serializable
```

Immutable, serializable identity of an item: an item type key (see `CoreItemTypes`) plus either a long ID or a string ID. There are exactly two concrete forms, `ItemIdentity.LongIdentity` and `ItemIdentity.StringIdentity`; the constructors are private, so instances come only from `longId`, `stringId`, `parse` or the helpers in `CoreIdentities`. Equality is by kind, type key and ID. Safe to share between threads. The canonical string form, used in REST, persistence and backups, is `<type>/<long id>` for long identities and `<type>//<string id>` for string identities, e.g. `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue/10001` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-user//jsmith`. The type key must be non-empty and at most 190 characters; for round-tripping through `parse` it must not contain `/`. Java serialization version UID is 201611180000.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity ITEM_ZERO` | A special long identity with type key `0` and ID 0 (string form `0/0`), used as a neutral "no item" placeholder (for example for a row record that has no item). |
| `public String getItemType()` | Returns the item type key, never null or empty, e.g. `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`. |
| `public boolean isStringId()` | True for a string identity, false for a long identity. |
| `public String getStringId()` | Returns the string ID of a string identity (never null or blank). On a long identity it throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. |
| `public boolean isLongId()` | True for a long identity, false for a string identity. |
| `public long getLongId()` | Returns the long ID of a long identity. On a string identity it throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity stringId(String, String)` | Creates a string identity from a type key (first argument) and string ID (second). The type is checked as for `longId` (`AssertionError` for a null or whitespace-only type when assertions are enabled). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` when the type is empty or longer than 190 characters, or when the ID is null, blank (empty or whitespace only) or longer than 190 characters. The ID may contain any characters, including `/`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity longId(String, long)` | Creates a long identity from a type key and a long ID (any value, including 0 and negatives). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` when the type is empty or longer than 190 characters. A null or whitespace-only type is checked only by a Java assertion: with assertions enabled it throws `AssertionError`; with assertions disabled a null type gives `IllegalArgumentException` and a whitespace-only type is accepted. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity parse(String) throws java.text.ParseException` | Parses the canonical string form back into an identity. Rules, in order: null or empty input fails; text without any `/` must be a decimal long and is read as an issue ID (legacy form: `10001` becomes `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue/10001`); otherwise the type is everything before the first `/`, which must not be empty. If the first `/` is followed by a second `/`, the rest is the string ID (`type//abc`, `type//a/b` gives ID `a/b`); otherwise the rest must be a decimal long (`type/42`, `type/-1`). Failures (empty type, nothing after the separator, a non-numeric long part, an invalid ID such as an over-long or blank one) throw `java.text.ParseException`. The simplified form from `toSimplifiedString` is not understood: `issue/10001` parses as type `issue`, not as an issue. |
| `public abstract String toSimplifiedString()` | Returns a shorter human-readable form: the same as `toString` but with the type key passed through `CoreItemTypes.simplifyType`, e.g. `issue/10001` or `user//jsmith`; keys without the standard prefix stay in full. For display and logs only; it is not meant to be parsed back. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet`

```java
public class ItemIdentitySet extends java.util.AbstractSet<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>
```

A `java.util.Set` of `ItemIdentity` optimised for many identities: IDs are kept per type key, long IDs in primitive long sets and string IDs in string sets. Marked internal but widely used in signatures. Not thread-safe for concurrent modification; can be frozen with `makeImmutable`, after which every mutating call throws `IllegalStateException`. Copies share storage with an immutable source until either side writes (copy on write). Iteration returns all long identities first (grouped by type) and then all string identities; order inside a group is not defined. Iterators are fail-fast (`ConcurrentModificationException` if the set changes) and do not support `remove`. `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString` follow the usual `AbstractSet` rules. Null elements are not allowed.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ItemIdentitySet()` | Creates an empty, mutable set. |
| `public ItemIdentitySet(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity...)` | Creates a mutable set holding the given identities (duplicates collapse). A null array gives an empty set; a null element gives `IllegalArgumentException`. |
| `public ItemIdentitySet(java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Creates a mutable set holding all identities of the collection. A null collection gives an empty set; a null element gives `IllegalArgumentException`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet of(String, long[])` | Creates a mutable set with one long identity of the given type (first argument) for every value in the array (second). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet of(String, com.almworks.integers.LongIterable)` | Creates a mutable set with one long identity of the given type for every value of the iterable. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet of(String, Iterable<String>)` | Creates a mutable set with one string identity of the given type for every string of the iterable; each string must be a valid string ID (non-blank, at most 190 characters) or `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown. |
| `public java.util.Iterator<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity> iterator()` | Returns a fail-fast iterator over all identities: long identities first, grouped by type, then string identities. Each returned identity is a new object equal to the one added. `remove()` is not supported. |
| `public int size()` | Number of identities in the set (sum over all types and both ID kinds). |
| `public boolean contains(Object)` | True if the argument is an `ItemIdentity` held by the set (same kind, type and ID). Any other object, including null, gives false. |
| `public boolean containsAll(java.util.Collection<?>)` | True if every element of the argument is in this set. Returns false at once if the argument has more elements than this set. Fast per-type comparison when the argument is also an `ItemIdentitySet`. |
| `public boolean add(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Adds an identity; returns true if it was not already present. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for null and `IllegalStateException` if the set is immutable. |
| `public boolean addAll(java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Adds every identity of the argument; returns true if the set changed. Adding the set to itself does nothing and returns false. Throws `IllegalStateException` if this set is immutable, `IllegalArgumentException` on a null element. |
| `public void addAll(String, Iterable<String>)` | Adds one string identity of the given type (first argument) for every string in the second argument. No return value. Invalid IDs give `IllegalArgumentException`; an immutable set gives `IllegalStateException`. |
| `public void addAll(String, com.almworks.integers.LongIterable)` | Adds one long identity of the given type for every value in the second argument. No return value. An immutable set gives `IllegalStateException`. |
| `public boolean remove(Object)` | Removes the identity if present and returns true; returns false if absent or if the argument is not an `ItemIdentity`. When the last ID of a type is removed the type disappears from `getItemTypes`. Throws `IllegalStateException` on an immutable set, even if nothing would be removed. |
| `public boolean removeAll(java.util.Collection<?>)` | Removes every element of the argument that is present; returns true if anything was removed. On an immutable set it throws `IllegalStateException` as soon as it tries to remove one element (an empty argument does not throw). |
| `public boolean retainAll(java.util.Collection<?>)` | Removes every identity that the argument does not contain; returns true if anything was removed. On an immutable set it throws `IllegalStateException` when the first removal is attempted. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet makeImmutable()` | Freezes this set permanently (there is no way back) and returns this same set for chaining. Afterwards all mutating methods throw `IllegalStateException`; reading and copying stay allowed. Use `copy()` to get a mutable set again. |
| `public boolean isImmutable()` | True once `makeImmutable` has been called. |
| `public void clear()` | Removes all identities. Throws `IllegalStateException` on an immutable set. Invalidates open iterators even if the set was already empty. |
| `public Iterable<String> getItemTypes()` | Returns a live, read-only iterable over the distinct type keys that currently have at least one identity in the set (each type once, even if it has both long and string IDs). Order is not defined. Iterating after the set changes throws `ConcurrentModificationException`. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet copyAllOfType(String)` | Returns a new mutable set holding only the identities (long and string) of the given type key; empty if there are none. The source is not changed. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet copy()` | Returns a new mutable set with the same identities. Cheap when this set is immutable (storage is shared until the copy is changed). |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongSizedIterable longIds(String)` | Returns the long IDs held for the given type as a sized long iterable; an empty list when there are none. Not determined whether callers may rely on it being a snapshot: the original returns the internal storage, so it reflects later changes of the set; callers must treat it as read-only and must not keep it across modifications. |
| `public java.util.Set<String> stringIds(String)` | Returns an unmodifiable view of the string IDs held for the given type (reflects later changes of the set); an empty set when there are none. |
| `public static java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity> collectItemIds(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.RowRetriever, com.almworks.integers.LongIterable)` | Static helper: looks up each row ID of the second argument through the given `RowRetriever` (first argument) and returns the set of their item identities. Missing rows are skipped silently; item objects are not loaded. A null row list gives an empty, unmodifiable set; otherwise the result is a new mutable `ItemIdentitySet`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemResolver`

```java
public interface ItemResolver
```

Turns item identities into the Jira or plugin objects they stand for (an `Issue`, a `Project`, a `GenericItem` and so on), applying the current user's visibility. Public API; the plugin provides the single implementation as an OSGi component (also available from `StructureComponents`). For each identity it finds the item type module for the type key, loads the object through `StructureItemType.accessItem` (or `BulkAccessibleItemType.accessItems` for bulk calls) and checks `isVisible` for the current user unless security is overridden in the current auth context. Errors thrown by item type modules are logged and turn into null results; these methods do not throw for missing, unknown or hidden items. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract <T> T resolveItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, Class<T>)` | Returns the object for the identity (first argument) if it exists, the current user may see it, and it is an instance of the class in the second argument (cast to it); otherwise null. A null identity gives null; a null class gives `NullPointerException`. Example: `resolveItem(CoreIdentities.issue(10001), Issue.class)`. |
| `public abstract Object resolveUnchecked(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Marked internal. Returns the raw object for the identity with no class check and no visibility check, or null if it does not exist, its type is unknown, the identity is null, or loading fails. Callers are responsible for permission checks. |
| `public abstract <T> void resolveItems(java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, Class<T>, java.util.function.BiConsumer<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, T>)` | Bulk form of `resolveItem`: for each identity of the first argument calls the third argument with the identity and either the visible object of the requested class (second argument) or null. Identities are grouped by type and loaded in bulk where the type supports it. Each identity is reported once; order is not defined. A collection of two or more that holds the same identity twice (a list, say) throws `IllegalStateException`, and a null element among two or more throws `NullPointerException`. Identities whose type module is unknown, or whose type fails while loading, are skipped and not reported at all (except when the collection holds a single identity, which is always reported). An empty collection does nothing; a null class or consumer gives `NullPointerException`. |
| `public abstract void resolveItemsUnchecked(java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, java.util.function.BiConsumer<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, Object>)` | Bulk form of `resolveUnchecked`: reports every identity with its raw object or null, with no class or visibility checks. Same grouping, ordering and skipping rules as `resolveItems`. A null consumer gives `NullPointerException`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemTracker`

```java
public interface ItemTracker extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.VersionedDataSource<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemVersionUpdate>
```

Records that items changed and lets clients ask which items changed since a version they saw. It is a `VersionedDataSource` of `ItemVersionUpdate`: each recorded change increments the current `DataVersion`. Provided by the plugin as an OSGi component; the plugin itself records changes of issues and of its own items, and other plugins may record changes of their items so that caches and attributes depending on them are refreshed. Only a bounded history is kept: when a client is too far behind, or the version is from another signature (another plugin start or a reset), it gets a full update. In a cluster, changes are written to the database and become visible on other nodes asynchronously. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemVersionUpdate getUpdate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion)` | Returns the changes since the given version; a null version gives a full update. Result kinds: an empty update (`isEmpty()` true) when nothing changed; an incremental update listing the affected items; or a full update (`isFull()` true, no item list) when the version has a different signature, is newer than the current one, or is too far behind: by default only the last 20,000 recorded changes are kept, and an incremental answer is given only when at most 500 changes were recorded since the given version; otherwise a full update is returned. The returned update's version is the current version; pass it to the next call. |
| `public abstract void recordChange(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Records that the given item changed (created, updated or deleted) and advances the version. A null identity is ignored. Must not be called inside a database transaction. |
| `public abstract void recordChanges(Iterable<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Records several changed items at once; null elements are ignored. Same effect as calling `recordChange` for each. |
| `public abstract void reset()` | Forgets the change history and advances the version, so every client's next `getUpdate` call returns a full update. Used when changes cannot be tracked item by item (for example after a full reindex). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.StructureItemType`

```java
public interface StructureItemType<T>
```

The main extension interface (public SPI) of an item type: implemented by the class of a `structure-item-type` plugin module, in the plugin itself for the built-in types and in other plugins for their own types. The module's complete key (`<plugin key>:<module key>`) is the item type key used in identities. Type parameter `T` is the class of the item objects. The plugin calls it whenever it needs an item object or a visibility decision for one item: resolving items, checking which rows a user may see (unless the type implements `BulkAccessCheckingItemType`), loading attributes. The same instance is called from many threads, so it must be thread-safe. Optional capabilities are added by also implementing `BulkAccessibleItemType`, `BulkAccessCheckingItemType`, `CreatableItemType`, `UpdatableItemType`, `StructureOwnedItemType` or `DeadItemsCheckingItemType`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract T accessItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Returns the object for the given identity (always of this module's type, never null), or null when the item does not exist or the identity is not valid for this type. Must not check permissions; may be called without a user context. |
| `public abstract boolean isVisible(T, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Says whether the user (second argument; null means anonymous) may see the item object (first argument, previously returned by `accessItem`, never null). Hidden items are shown as inaccessible rows or left out. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.StructureOwnedItemType`

```java
public interface StructureOwnedItemType
```

Optional extension interface for item types whose items belong to one structure (for example memos and other generic items). When rows are added to a structure (by hand, by a generator's fragment, during restore or migration), the plugin calls it for each long-ID item of the type so that the item is owned by, or copied into, the target structure; the row then points to the returned identity.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity getOwnedItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, long, boolean) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Returns the identity to use for the item (first argument) inside the structure whose ID is the second argument. The reference behaviour for generic items: an item with no owner is assigned to the structure in place and the same identity is returned; an item already owned by this structure keeps its identity unless the third argument (copy even if same owner, used when the item already occurs in the same operation) is true, in which case a new copy owned by the structure is created; an item owned by another structure is always copied, and the copy's new identity is returned. Unknown or non-matching identities are returned unchanged. Throws `StructureException` if the change cannot be stored. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.UpdatableItemType`

```java
public interface UpdatableItemType
```

Optional extension interface for item types whose items can be edited through the plugin's REST API (inline editing in the grid). When a client sends new values for an item, the plugin first applies any item property editors and then, if values remain, calls this method; if the type does not implement it, the update is rejected.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void updateItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.atlassian.jira.util.ErrorCollection) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Applies the values (second argument, raw client values keyed by field name; only keys present are changed) to the item (first argument) as the current user. Field-level problems go into the error collection (third argument); other failures, such as a missing or inaccessible item or a wrong item type, are thrown as `StructureException`. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic`

Generic items: plugin-stored items that consist only of a name, an optional owning structure, an optional description and a map of JSON-like parameters (memos, planning tasks and items of third-party generic types are stored this way). Contains the immutable value class, the low-level storage manager, the permission-checking service and a reusable item type implementation that other plugins can register as their own item type module.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem`

Immutable value object holding the stored data of a generic item: a name, an optional owning structure ID, an optional description and a map of parameters. Public API, final. A null argument gives `NullPointerException`. |

| `public Long getOwningStructure()` | The ID of the structure that owns the item, or null if it has no owner. Visibility of an owned item follows the user's permission on that structure; an unowned item is visible to everyone who can use the app. |
| `public String getDescription()` | The free-text description, or null if none. Stored as given (no trimming). |
| `public java.util.Map<String, Object> getParameters()` | The parameters as an unmodifiable, insertion-ordered map from name to value; empty (never null) when there are none. Values are deep-copied, immutable JSON-like data (strings, numbers, booleans, nested lists and maps). Item types keep their own fields here; memos, for example, keep their field values under a `fields` entry. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True for another `GenericItem` with equal name, owning structure, description and parameters. |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash over name, owning structure, description and parameters, consistent with `equals`. |
| `public String toString()` | Debug text listing all four fields; the exact format is not part of the contract. |
