### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemManager`

```java
public interface GenericItemManager
```

Low-level storage of generic items in the plugin's database, without permission checks. Public API; the plugin provides it as an OSGi component. Each generic item has a numeric ID that is unique across all generic item types (and must fit in a 32-bit int) and is addressed by a long `ItemIdentity` whose type key is the key of a registered generic item type module. Reads are cached. Every create, update and delete notifies `ItemTracker`; create and update also add a record to the item change history with the current user as author. Thread-safe. Methods throw `StructureStoppedException` when the plugin is not running.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity createItem(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Stores a new item of the given type key (first argument) with the given data (second) and returns its new long identity `<type>/<new id>`. Throws `StructureException` (create-item-failed) when the type key does not belong to an installed item type module built on `GenericItemType`. No license, app-access or permission checks are made at this level; use `GenericItemService` for checked access. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem getItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Returns the stored item, or null when the identity is a string identity, no item has that ID, or the stored item's type differs from the identity's type key. No license, app-access or permission checks are made at this level; use `GenericItemService` for checked access. |
| `public abstract void loadItems(java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, java.util.function.BiConsumer<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem>)` | Loads many items at once: for each identity of the set (first argument) that exists with the same type, calls the second argument with the identity and the item; missing items are skipped. Order is not defined. All identities must be long identities (a string identity gives `UnsupportedOperationException`). Loading is done in chunks (1,000 IDs by default). No license, app-access or permission checks are made at this level; use `GenericItemService` for checked access. |
| `public abstract void updateItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Replaces all stored fields of the item (first argument) with the given data (second). Throws `StructureException`: invalid-parameter for a string identity, item-not-exists-or-not-accessible when no item of that ID and type exists. No license, app-access or permission checks are made at this level; use `GenericItemService` for checked access. |
| `public abstract void deleteItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Deletes the item. A string identity gives `StructureException` (invalid parameter); a missing item or a type mismatch is silently ignored. Rows that point to the item are not removed (they later show as missing). No history record is written for a deletion. No license, app-access or permission checks are made at this level; use `GenericItemService` for checked access. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity getOwnedItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, long, boolean) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Implements the `StructureOwnedItemType` rule for generic items. Arguments: the item, the target structure ID, and whether to copy even when the item is already owned by that structure. If the item has no owner it is assigned to the structure in place (without a history record) and the same identity is returned; if it is owned by another structure, or by the same one and the flag is true, a copy owned by the target structure is created and the copy's identity returned; otherwise the identity is returned unchanged. String identities and missing items are returned unchanged. Throws `StructureException` if storing fails. |
| `public abstract boolean isVisible(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Decides whether the user (second argument; null = anonymous) may see the item: true when the item has no owning structure, otherwise true only if the user has at least `PermissionLevel.VIEW` on the owning structure. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService`

```java
public interface GenericItemService
```

Permission-checking service for generic items, following the Jira validate-then-execute pattern: each change is first validated (returning a result object) and then executed by passing that result to the matching method. Public API; the plugin provides it as an OSGi component. Acts as the current user of the plugin's auth context. Never throws for business failures: problems are reported through the result's error collection and `getException()`. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.GenericItemResult getItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Reads an item as the current user. Fails (exception in the result) when the user may not use the app, when the item does not exist, or when the user may not see it. On success the result carries the item; its `getItemId()` is null. Note: when the item exists but is not visible, the failed result still carries the item data in `getGenericItem()`; callers must check `isValid()` first. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.CreateValidationResult validateCreate(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem)` | Validates creating an item of the given type key (first argument) with the given data (second). Fails when the app is not fully licensed, when the current user may not use the app, or when there is no logged-in user. The type key and the item's owning structure are not checked here (the owning structure needs no permission). |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.GenericItemResult create(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.CreateValidationResult)` | Creates the item if the validation result is valid and returns a result whose `getItemId()` is the new identity. If the validation is invalid, its errors and exception are passed on and nothing is created. Storage failures (for example an unsupported type key) come back as the result's exception. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.UpdateValidationResult validateUpdate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem)` | Validates replacing the item (first argument) with new data (second). Fails when the app is not licensed, the user may not use the app, the identity is not a long identity, or the item does not exist. If the item currently has an owning structure, the user must also see it and have `PermissionLevel.EDIT` on that structure. An item with no owner can be updated by any user with app access. The new data's owning structure is not checked. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.GenericItemResult update(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.UpdateValidationResult)` | Stores the new data if the validation is valid. On success the result carries neither item nor identity. An invalid validation is passed on unchanged; storage failures come back as the result's exception. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.DeleteValidationResult validateDelete(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Validates deleting the item. Fails when the app is not licensed, the user may not use the app, the identity is not a long identity, the item does not exist or is not visible, or the user lacks `PermissionLevel.EDIT` on the owning structure. Because an item with no owner has no structure to grant EDIT, deleting an unowned item through this service always fails with an edit-denied error. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.GenericItemResult delete(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService.DeleteValidationResult)` | Deletes the item if the validation is valid. On success the result carries neither item nor identity. An invalid validation is passed on unchanged. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemType`

```java
public class GenericItemType implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.StructureItemType<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.CreatableItemType, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.UpdatableItemType, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.StructureOwnedItemType, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.DeadItemsCheckingItemType, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.BulkAccessCheckingItemType
```

Ready-made item type implementation for generic items (public API). Another plugin declares a `structure-item-type` module whose class is this class or a subclass; the module's complete key becomes the item type key, and the plugin then stores, shows, creates, edits, copies and cleans up such items through `GenericItemService` and `GenericItemManager`. It implements `StructureItemType` with `GenericItem` objects, `CreatableItemType`, `UpdatableItemType`, `StructureOwnedItemType`, `DeadItemsCheckingItemType` and `BulkAccessCheckingItemType`. Item identities are long identities of the module's type. Client values used for creation and update: `summary` (the name, required and non-blank on create), `description`, and `params` (an object whose entries are merged into the parameters). Subclasses can override `readItemValues` to read more values. Instances are created by the plugin system with constructor injection; thread-safe after `init`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final long NEW_ITEM_ID = 9223372036854775807` | The long ID `Long.MAX_VALUE` (9223372036854775807) used for the not-yet-created item of a dummy row; such identities are never loaded and are treated as accessible. |
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService myGenericItemService` | Protected field: the `GenericItemService` passed to the constructor, used for checked create and update. |
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemManager myGenericItemManager` | Protected field: the `GenericItemManager` passed to the constructor, used for loading items, visibility and ownership. |
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.StructurePluginHelper myHelper` | Protected field: the `StructurePluginHelper` passed to the constructor, used for translated error messages. |
| `public GenericItemType(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemService, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItemManager, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.StructurePluginHelper)` | Creates the item type from the three plugin services (normally injected). The item type key is not known until `init` is called. |
| `public void init(com.atlassian.plugin.ModuleDescriptor)` | Marked internal; called by the plugin system when the module is set up. Takes the module descriptor and, the first time only, remembers its complete key as this type's item type key. Every other method requires this to have happened (otherwise they fail with `NullPointerException`). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem accessItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Returns the stored `GenericItem` when the identity has this type key, is a long identity and is not `NEW_ITEM_ID`; null otherwise or when the item does not exist. No permission check. |
| `public boolean isVisible(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Same as `GenericItemManager.isVisible`: visible if the item has no owning structure, or if the user has at least VIEW on it. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow createDummyRow(long, long, java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.atlassian.jira.util.ErrorCollection) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Builds the item from the client values (blank or missing `summary` adds an error under the field `summary` and returns null), validates creation with `GenericItemService.validateCreate`, and on success returns a temporary row with the given row ID and semantics whose identity is `<type>/NEW_ITEM_ID` and whose item object is the built `GenericItem`. If validation fails with an exception it is thrown as `StructureException`; plain errors are copied into the error collection and null is returned. Nothing is stored. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity createItem(java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.atlassian.jira.util.ErrorCollection) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Builds the item from the client values like `createDummyRow` and creates it through `GenericItemService`. Returns the new identity, or null with errors added. A service failure carrying an exception (license, access, anonymous user, unsupported type) is thrown as `StructureException`. |
| `public void updateItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.atlassian.jira.util.ErrorCollection) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Updates an item as the current user. Throws `StructureException`: invalid parameter when the identity's type is not this type; item-not-exists-or-not-accessible when the item cannot be loaded or the current user cannot see it. Starts from the stored data; if `summary` is present it must be non-blank (else an error is added and nothing changes); `description` and `params` are applied when present (see `readItemValues`). Then validates and stores through `GenericItemService`; a failure with an exception is thrown, plain errors are added to the collection. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity getOwnedItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, long, boolean) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | For long identities of this type, delegates to `GenericItemManager.getOwnedItem` (assign unowned item to the structure, or copy it); other identities are returned unchanged. |
| `public void filterDead(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet)` | For every long ID of this type in the first set, adds the identity to the second set when no item can be loaded for it (including `NEW_ITEM_ID`). String identities and other types are ignored. |
| `public void filterInaccessible(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, boolean, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentitySet)` | Loads all identities of the first set except `NEW_ITEM_ID` in bulk and adds to the fourth set those that do not exist and, unless the third argument (override security) is true, those the user (second argument) cannot see. Expects only long identities of this type, as the plugin passes them; a string identity makes it fail with `UnsupportedOperationException`. |
| `protected void readItemValues(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem.Builder, java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem, com.atlassian.jira.util.ErrorCollection)` | Protected hook that copies client values into the builder (first argument). Arguments: the builder, the client values (may be null: then nothing happens), the existing item when updating or null when creating, and the error collection for problems. Default behaviour: if the key `description` is present, the description is set to its single value (null clears it); if the key `params` is present, its value is converted to a map: when that is not possible (or the value is null) all parameters are removed, otherwise each entry is set on the builder, a null entry value removing that parameter and other parameters being kept. Subclasses may override to read more keys; adding errors stops creation or update. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job`

Background job execution. A job manager runs `StructureJob` instances on a single background queue thread, on named thread pools, or periodically, and a scheduled-job manager runs cluster-wide periodic tasks whose last run time is persisted.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.AbstractStructureJob`

```java
public abstract class AbstractStructureJob implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob
```

Convenient base class for `StructureJob` implementations that tracks the job state: PENDING initially, RUNNING while `job()` runs, FINISHED after it returns or throws. Subclasses put the work in `doJob()` and supply `getUser()`. State access is synchronized on `myLock`, so the state can be read from any thread.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected final Object myLock` | Protected monitor object guarding the state; subclasses may synchronize on it for their own state too. |
| `public AbstractStructureJob()` | Creates a job in the PENDING state. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob.State getState()` | Returns the current state (final; thread-safe). |
| `public String toString()` | Returns the job class's fully qualified name followed by the state in parentheses, e.g. `com.example.MyJob(PENDING)`. |
| `public void reset()` | Puts the job back into PENDING so it can be submitted again (the job manager does this before each run of a periodic job). Allowed in any state; resetting a RUNNING job only logs a warning. |
| `public final void job() throws Exception` | Final. Moves the state from PENDING to RUNNING, runs `doJob()`, and always moves the state to FINISHED afterwards, passing on any exception thrown by `doJob()`. If the job was not PENDING when called, a warning is logged, the state is left as it was and the work still runs. |
| `protected abstract void doJob() throws Exception` | Protected, abstract: the job's work. May throw any exception; the job manager logs it. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.ScheduledJob`

```java
public interface ScheduledJob
```

A periodic task registered with `ScheduledJobManager`. The manager asks it about once a minute whether it is due, giving it the time of its last run across the whole cluster, and runs it on the system thread pool when it is.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean shouldRun(long)` | Decides whether the task is due. The argument is the wall-clock time in milliseconds since the epoch when the task was last started (on any cluster node), or 0 if it never ran or was forced. Should be fast and side-effect free; an exception is logged and treated as false. |
| `public abstract void run() throws Exception` | Performs the task. Runs in a background thread without a logged-in user; exceptions are logged by the job manager. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.ScheduledJobManager`

```java
public interface ScheduledJobManager
```

Runs `ScheduledJob` tasks periodically under string keys, coordinated across a cluster. Provided by the plugin as an OSGi component. About every 60 seconds (by default) it checks each registered task, skipping the check while the plugin is locked (for example during a restore). For each task not already running it calls `shouldRun` with the stored last run time, and if due it takes a cluster lock for the key, re-checks, records the start time persistently and submits the task to the job manager's `system` executor. Registrations live in memory on each node; the last run time is stored in the plugin's settings under `sjm.<key>`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void addJob(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.ScheduledJob)` | Registers the task (second argument) under the key (first argument). A task already registered under the same key is replaced (a warning is logged; a running instance is not stopped). The first run happens on a later periodic check. |
| `public abstract void forceRun(String)` | Clears the stored last run time of the task with this key and checks it immediately: the task runs now if `shouldRun(0)` returns true and it is not already running. Does nothing for an unknown key. |
| `public abstract void removeJob(String)` | Unregisters the task with this key and cancels it if it is currently running. Does nothing for an unknown key or when the manager is stopped. The stored last run time is kept. |
| `public abstract long getLastRunTime(String)` | Returns the time (milliseconds since the epoch) when the task with this key was last started on any node, or 0 if it never ran or was forced since. Works for keys that are not (or no longer) registered. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob`

```java
public interface StructureJob
```

A unit of background work for `StructureJobManager`. Implementations usually extend `AbstractStructureJob` (or `SystemStructureJob`). The manager runs `job()` with Jira's logged-in user set to `getUser()`, and requires the job to be PENDING when submitted.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void job() throws Exception` | Performs the work. Called by the job manager in a background thread; may throw, the manager logs the exception. |
| `public abstract void reset()` | Returns the job to the PENDING state so that it can run again; called by the manager before each repetition of a scheduled job. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob.State getState()` | Returns the job's current state (PENDING, RUNNING or FINISHED). |
| `public abstract com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser getUser()` | Returns the user the job runs as (set as Jira's logged-in user during the run), or null to run with no user (anonymous/system). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob.State`

```java
public enum StructureJob.State
```

Lifecycle state of a `StructureJob`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `PENDING (enum constant)` | Not started yet (or reset); the only state in which a job can be submitted to the job manager. |
| `RUNNING (enum constant)` | The job's work is executing. |
| `FINISHED (enum constant)` | The work has completed, normally or with an exception. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob.State[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob.State valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |


| member | meaning |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJobManager`

```java
public interface StructureJobManager
```

Runs `StructureJob` instances in the background. Provided by the plugin as an OSGi component. Three ways to run: `enqueue` puts the job on a single background queue processed one at a time in FIFO order (capacity 1,000 by default); `execute` hands it to a named thread pool (executor) right away; `schedule` runs it on the queue thread after a delay and then repeatedly. Every accepted job gets a new positive ID, unique while the plugin runs. Finished jobs stay registered (for `getJob`/`getFuture`) for about 12 hours by default (3 minutes for callables). During a run Jira's logged-in user is set to the job's user. Exceptions from jobs are logged, never rethrown. When the plugin stops, queued and scheduled jobs are dropped and running pool jobs are interrupted. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final String USER_EXECUTOR_ID = "user"` | Executor ID `user`: the pool for user-initiated work (3 threads in the reference). Default of `execute(StructureJob)`. |
| `public static final String SYSTEM_EXECUTOR_ID = "system"` | Executor ID `system`: the pool for internal maintenance work (1 thread in the reference); used for scheduled-job runs. |
| `public static final String GENERATOR_EXECUTOR_ID = "generator"` | Executor ID `generator`: the pool for running generators (by default the larger of 4 and CPU count + 1 threads). |
| `public static final String ATTRIBUTE_EXECUTOR_ID = "attribute"` | Executor ID `attribute`: the pool for attribute loading (by default the larger of 4 and CPU count + 1 threads). |
| `public static final String EFFECTOR_EXECUTOR_ID = "effector"` | Executor ID `effector`: the pool for effector work (by default the larger of 4 and CPU count + 1 threads). |
| `public abstract long enqueue(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJobException` | Adds the job to the end of the single background queue and returns its ID. Throws `NullPointerException` for null; `StructureJobException` when the job is not PENDING, the manager is stopped, or the queue is full. |
| `public abstract long execute(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJobException` | Same as `execute(job, USER_EXECUTOR_ID)`. |
| `public abstract long execute(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob, String) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJobException` | Submits the job to the thread pool with the given executor ID (one of the `*_EXECUTOR_ID` constants; the reference also has an `indexing` pool) and returns its ID. Throws `NullPointerException` for a null job; `StructureJobException` when the job is not PENDING, the manager is not started, or the pool rejects it. An unknown executor ID throws `StructureJobException` with the message `illegal executor id ` followed by the ID, and no job is registered. |
| `public abstract long schedule(long, long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJobException` | Schedules the job (third argument) to run on the queue thread first after the initial delay (first argument, milliseconds) and then repeatedly, each next run starting the given interval (second argument, milliseconds) after the previous run finished; an interval of 0 or less means run once. The job is reset to PENDING before each repetition. Returns the job ID, which `cancel` takes to stop repetitions. Timing is approximate (the queue thread checks the schedule when idle, about every 3 seconds). Throws as `enqueue`. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJob getJob(Long)` | Returns the job registered under the ID, or null if unknown, cancelled or already cleaned up. Any caller can look up any job. |
| `public abstract void cancel(Long)` | Unregisters the job with this ID: removes it from the queue and schedule (no further repetitions) and, if it is running on a pool, interrupts it. Unknown IDs are ignored. There is no ownership check: any caller can cancel any job. |
| `public abstract long execute(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.CallableE<?, ?>, String) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.job.StructureJobException` | Runs a callable on the given executor as a job, under the auth context (user and security override) of the calling thread, and returns the job ID; the callable's result or exception is available through `getFuture`. Throws `StructureJobException` when the manager is not started, the pool rejects it, or the executor ID is unknown (as for `execute(job, executorId)`). |
| `public abstract <T> java.util.concurrent.Future<T> getFuture(Long)` | Returns the `Future` of a job started with one of the `execute` methods (for a callable it yields the callable's result), or null when the ID is null or unknown, the job was not started on a pool, or the job's user differs from the current user. Cancelling the future interrupts the job. |

Base class for jobs that run without a user: an `AbstractStructureJob` whose `getUser()` returns null.

| `public com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser getUser()` | Always null, so the job runs with no logged-in user. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.lifecycle`

Lifecycle helpers: the cache-clearing callback that plugin components implement, and the exception thrown when a plugin service is called while the plugin is not started or is being restarted.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.lifecycle.CachingComponent`

```java
public interface CachingComponent
```

Callback for components that hold caches. Marked internal. The plugin looks up every enabled plugin module implementing this interface and calls `clearCaches()` when all caches must be dropped (for example when extension modules are enabled or disabled, or when another cluster node requests a cache reset), and the per-user method when data of one user changed. Exceptions are logged and ignored. Implementations must be thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void clearCaches()` | Drops all cached data so that it is reloaded on next use. |
| `public abstract void clearUserCaches(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Deprecated. Drops cached data that belongs to the given user (not null). This is the variant the plugin itself calls. |
| `public default void clearUserCaches(String)` | Default method: looks up the user with the given user key and, if such a user exists, calls `clearUserCaches(ApplicationUser)`; does nothing for an unknown key. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.lifecycle.StructureStoppedException`

```java
public class StructureStoppedException extends IllegalStateException
```

Unchecked exception (an `IllegalStateException`) thrown by plugin services when they are called before the plugin has started, after it stopped, or while it is being restarted (for example during a restore from backup). Callers may retry later. Public API.

|---|---|
| `public StructureStoppedException(Object)` | Creates the exception; the argument names the component that refused the call and is included in the message (converted with `toString`), together with a hint that the app may be restarting or restoring and that the caller should wait. |

Collects field changes for one memo and applies them with `update()`. Obtained from `MemoManager.getUpdateBuilder`. Each setter records a change for one field (a null value clears the field) and returns this builder; fields not set keep their values. Not thread-safe.

Throws `StructureException` when the memo does not exist or is not visible, when the app is not licensed or not available to the user, when the user lacks EDIT permission on the structure owning the memo, or when a value fails the memo's field validation. ## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions`

Structure-level and app-level permissions: the ordered permission levels, the app permission keys, permission subjects (anyone, a user, a group, a project role) and permission rules, together with their compact string encodings and JSON forms that are persisted in structure definitions.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.CoreAppPermissions`

```java
public interface CoreAppPermissions
```

Constants for the app-wide permissions an administrator grants in the plugin's global settings (each to anyone or to a list of permission subjects). The key of each constant is persisted in settings and used by `byKey`. Public API; an interface used only for constants. Some permissions are combined by the plugin with Jira global permissions, as noted.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission USE` | Key `use`: may use the app at all (see structures, open the app pages). Most other checks require it as well. |
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission CREATE_STRUCTURE` | Key `createStructure`: may create new structures. |
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission SYNCHRONIZATION` | Key `synchronization`: may set up and control synchronizers. |
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission AUTOMATION` | Key `automation`: may add and change automation (generators) in structures they can control. |
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission CONFIGURE_GENERATORS` | Key `configureGenerators`: may configure generators (also requires AUTOMATE on the structure). |
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission CONFIGURE_EFFECTORS` | Key `configureEffectors`: may configure effectors (also requires AUTOMATE on the structure). |
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission EXECUTE_EFFECTORS` | Key `executeEffectors`: may run effectors; the plugin additionally requires Jira's bulk change global permission. |
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission EXECUTE_EFFECTORS_ON_QUERIES` | Key `executeEffectorsOnQueries`: may run effectors on query-based (unsaved) forests; also requires the configure and execute effector permissions. |
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission MANAGE_GLOBAL_SAVED_COLUMNS` | Key `manageGlobalSavedColumns`: may manage saved column sets shared globally; the plugin additionally requires Jira's create-shared-objects global permission. |
| `public static final java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission> ALL` | Unmodifiable set of all nine permissions above, iterating in the order they are declared (USE, CREATE_STRUCTURE, SYNCHRONIZATION, AUTOMATION, CONFIGURE_GENERATORS, CONFIGURE_EFFECTORS, EXECUTE_EFFECTORS, EXECUTE_EFFECTORS_ON_QUERIES, MANAGE_GLOBAL_SAVED_COLUMNS). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.StructureAppPermission byKey(String)` | Returns the permission from `ALL` whose key equals the argument exactly (case-sensitive), or null for an unknown key or null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel`

```java
public enum PermissionLevel
```

Ordered access levels a user can have on a structure (or view). Each level has a numeric serial that is persisted (in encoded rules and storage); a higher serial includes all lower ones. Note that two constants share serial 25.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `NONE (enum constant)` | Serial 0: no access; the structure is not visible. |
| `VIEW (enum constant)` | Serial 10: may see the structure and its content. |
| `EDIT (enum constant)` | Serial 20: may also change the structure's forest (add, move, remove rows) and its owned items. |
| `EDIT_GENERATORS (enum constant)` | Deprecated, serial 25: old name of the automation level; equivalent to `AUTOMATE` in every comparison. Decoding serial 25 always gives `AUTOMATE`. |
| `AUTOMATE (enum constant)` | Serial 25: may also add and configure automation (generators, effectors) in the structure. |
| `ADMIN (enum constant)` | Serial 30: full control, including the structure's details and permissions and deleting it. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |
| `public int getSerial()` | Returns the numeric serial (0, 10, 20, 25, 25, 30 for NONE, VIEW, EDIT, EDIT_GENERATORS, AUTOMATE, ADMIN). |
| `public boolean includes(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel)` | True if this level is at least the required one (compares serials, so `EDIT_GENERATORS` and `AUTOMATE` include each other). A null argument means nothing is required and gives true. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel fromSerial(int)` | Returns the highest level whose serial is not greater than the argument: values below 10 (including negatives) give `NONE`, 10 to 19 give `VIEW`, 20 to 24 `EDIT`, 25 to 29 `AUTOMATE`, 30 and above `ADMIN`. Never null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule`

```java
public abstract class PermissionRule implements Cloneable
```

One entry of a structure's permission list. The list is evaluated in order starting from a given level, each rule receiving the level produced by the rules before it, so later matching rules override earlier ones. Two kinds exist: `SetLevel` (if a subject matches the user, set a level) and `ApplyStructure` (evaluate another structure's rules at this point). Rules are mutable Java beans and cloneable; not thread-safe while being changed. String encoding (persisted): `set:<serial>:<encoded subject>` and `apply:<structure id>`, e.g. `set:10:anyone`, `set:20:group:jira-developers`, `apply:12`; lists are comma-separated. JSON form (Jackson): an object with a `type` property `set` or `apply`; `set` rules carry `subject` and `level`, `apply` rules carry `structure`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public PermissionRule()` | Constructor for subclasses. |
| `public abstract String toEncodedString()` | Returns the compact string encoding of the rule (see the type summary and the subclasses). |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel apply(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel, java.util.List<Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<Long, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule>>)` | Evaluates the rule. Arguments: the user (null = anonymous), the level produced so far (`pass`, not null), a mutable list of structure IDs being evaluated (used to detect cycles; may be null), and a function returning the permission rule list of a structure ID (may be null). Returns the resulting level. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule fromEncodedString(String) throws java.text.ParseException` | Same as `fromEncodedString(s, false)`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule fromEncodedString(String, boolean) throws java.text.ParseException` | Decodes one rule. Null or empty input gives null. `apply:<id>` gives an `ApplyStructure` (the ID must be a decimal long). `set:<level>:<subject>` gives a `SetLevel`; the level is a serial decoded with `PermissionLevel.fromSerial` or, if not numeric, a level constant name such as `VIEW`; the subject is decoded with `PermissionSubject.fromEncodedString`, passing on the second argument (true when user subjects hold user names from an old version that must be turned into user keys). Anything else, a missing `:` after the level, an unknown level, a non-numeric ID or an undecodable or empty subject throws `java.text.ParseException`. |
| `public static String encodePermissions(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule>)` | Deprecated. Joins the encodings of the non-null rules of the list with commas, e.g. `set:10:anyone,apply:12`. A null or empty list gives the empty string. |
| `public static java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule> decodePermissions(String) throws java.text.ParseException` | Deprecated. Splits the text at every comma and decodes each part with `fromEncodedString`, returning a new mutable list without null entries; null or empty text gives an empty list. Throws `java.text.ParseException` for a bad part. Because group names and user keys may contain commas, this list format is not safe for every value. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule clone()` | Returns a copy of the rule (`SetLevel` also copies its subject). |
| `public String toString()` | Same as `toEncodedString()`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule.ApplyStructure`

```java
public static class PermissionRule.ApplyStructure extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule
```

Rule that inserts the permission rules of another structure at its position ("apply the permissions of structure N"). Encoded as `apply:<structure id>`; JSON `{"type":"apply","structure":<id>}`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ApplyStructure()` | Creates a rule with no structure ID (bean constructor for deserialization). |
| `public ApplyStructure(Long)` | Creates a rule referring to the structure with the given ID (may be null). |
| `public Long getStructureId()` | The referenced structure ID, or null if not set. JSON property `structure`. |

| `public String toEncodedString()` | Returns `apply:<id>`, e.g. `apply:12`. When the ID is null this yields `apply:null`, which cannot be decoded again. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel apply(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel, java.util.List<Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<Long, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule>>)` | Returns the second argument (`pass`) unchanged when the structure ID is null, when the resolver (fourth argument) is null, or when the ID is already in the call stack (a cycle, which is also logged as an error). Otherwise asks the resolver for that structure's rules, adds the ID to the stack while evaluating them in order starting from `pass`, removes it again and returns the result. A null rule list from the resolver gives `pass`. A null stack disables cycle detection. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True for another `ApplyStructure` with an equal structure ID (both null counts as equal). |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash of the structure ID, 0 when null. |

The other arguments are ignored. Caution: a matching rule with no level returns null. |

| `public void setSubject(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionSubject)` | Sets the subject (null allowed). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel getLevel()` | The level given to matching users, or null. |
| `public void setLevel(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel)` | Sets the level (null allowed). |
| `public String toEncodedString()` | Returns `set:<serial>:<subject encoding>`; a null level is written as `0` and a null subject as nothing (`set:20:`, which cannot be decoded again). `EDIT_GENERATORS` is written as 25 and so reads back as `AUTOMATE`. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True for another `SetLevel` with the same level and an equal subject (nulls equal to nulls). |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash over subject and level, consistent with `equals`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionSubject`

```java
public abstract class PermissionSubject implements Cloneable
```

Who a permission rule (or an app permission) applies to: anyone, one Jira user, the members of a Jira group, or the members of a project role. Mutable, cloneable Java beans; supports the visitor pattern. String encodings (persisted): `anyone`, `user:<user key>`, `group:<group name>`, `role:<project id>:<role id>` (project ID 0 means any project enabled for the app). JSON form (Jackson): an object with a `type` property `anyone`, `user`, `group` or `project.role`; users and groups carry `name` (for users this is the user key), project roles carry `project` and `role`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public PermissionSubject()` | Constructor for subclasses. |
| `public abstract boolean matches(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | True if the user (null = anonymous) belongs to this subject. |
| `public abstract String toEncodedString()` | Returns the compact string encoding (see the type summary). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionSubject fromEncodedString(String) throws java.text.ParseException` | Same as `fromEncodedString(s, false)`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionSubject fromEncodedString(String, boolean) throws java.text.ParseException` | Decodes a subject. Null or empty input gives null. Input starting with `anyone` gives `Anyone` (anything after that word is ignored). `user:<x>` gives a `JiraUser` with key `x`; when the second argument is true, `x` is treated as an old-style user name and converted to a user key by lower-casing it. `group:<name>` gives a `JiraGroup`. `role:<project>:<role>` gives a `ProjectRole` (both decimal longs; non-numeric parts throw `java.text.ParseException`); `role:` without a second colon gives null. Any other input throws `java.text.ParseException`. No existence checks are made. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionSubject clone()` | Returns a shallow copy of the subject. |
| `public String toString()` | Same as `toEncodedString()`. |
| `public abstract <T> T visit(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionSubject.Visitor<T>, T)` | Calls the visitor method matching the concrete kind (`onAnyone`, `onUser`, `onGroup` or `onProjectRole`) with this subject and the carry value (second argument) and returns what the visitor returns. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionSubject clone(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionSubject)` | Static null-safe clone: returns null for null, otherwise `clone()` of the argument. |

Subject matching one Jira user, identified by user key (not user name). Encoded `user:<key>`, e.g. `user:jsmith` or `user:JIRAUSER10100`; JSON `{"type":"user","name":"<key>"}` (the JSON property is called `name` but holds the key). A subject with a null key stands for the anonymous user.

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pinger`

Internal scheduling helper that calls registered callbacks periodically on one shared, low-priority daemon thread. Meant for the plugin's own components; it is exported as a service but is not a supported extension point.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pinger.Pinger`

```java
public interface Pinger
```

Service that repeatedly calls registered `Pinger.Pingable` callbacks at a requested period. Implemented by the plugin and available as an OSGi component; internal. All callbacks run on a single daemon thread of below-normal priority, which wakes up roughly every 166 ms, so periods are honoured only approximately and a slow callback delays all others. The thread is started on demand and exits after about two minutes with nothing registered. After the plugin stops, registrations are dropped and new ones are ignored.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final int MIN_PING_TIME = 500` | Smallest allowed ping period, 500 (milliseconds). `ping` rejects shorter periods. |
| `public abstract void ping(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pinger.Pinger.Pingable, long)` | Registers the callback (arg 1) to be called about every `period` milliseconds (arg 2). The first call happens roughly one period after registration. Returns immediately. Throws `NullPointerException` if the callback is null and `IllegalArgumentException` if the period is below `MIN_PING_TIME`. Registering the same callback twice creates two independent registrations. Silently ignored when the service has been stopped. |
| `public abstract void stopPinging(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pinger.Pinger.Pingable)` | Removes every registration of the given callback (compared by identity). A call that is already running is not interrupted. Unknown callbacks and calls after shutdown are ignored; errors are logged, never thrown. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pinger.Pinger.Pingable`

```java
public interface Pinger.Pingable
```

Callback registered with `Pinger`. Implemented by the caller. It is invoked on the pinger's shared background thread, never concurrently with itself for one registration.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean ping(long) throws Exception` | Called once per period. The argument is the current value of `System.nanoTime()` at the start of the ping round (useful only for measuring elapsed time). Return `true` to keep being called, `false` to be unregistered. Throwing any exception (or linkage error) also unregisters the callback; the error is logged as a warning. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.planningtask`

Read and update access to planning tasks: issue-like items that exist only inside the plugin (item type `CoreItemTypes.PLANNING_TASK`) and carry a subset of the standard issue fields plus values of supported custom fields. Marked internal; the contract may change between versions.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.planningtask.PlanningTask`

```java

```

Read-only snapshot of one planning task's field values. Instances are created by `PlanningTaskManager`; they reflect the stored data at the moment they were obtained and do not change afterwards. Reading does not check the current user's permissions. Internal API.

|---|---|
| `public abstract String getSummary()` | Returns the summary (title) of the planning task, or null when it is not set. The stored value is checked against the field configuration that applies to the task (its project and issue type); a value that is not valid there is reported as null. |
