## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process`

Tracking and reporting of long-running background operations (backup, restore, maintenance, import/export, resynchronisation, automation runs). Contains a persistent process registry with status, progress, cancel flag and display parameters for a progress page, and lightweight in-memory progress reporting interfaces.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessButtonParameters`

```java
public class ProcessButtonParameters
```

Description of one button shown on the progress page of a background process: a localizable caption and a target URL. Mutable bean, also serialized to JSON when process parameters are stored, so it needs a no-argument constructor and getters/setters. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ProcessButtonParameters(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText, String)` | Creates a button with the given caption (arg 1) and URL (arg 2). Either may be null. |
| `public ProcessButtonParameters()` | Creates a button with null caption and null URL (for deserialization). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText getCaption()` | The localizable caption text (i18n key plus arguments), or null. |
| `public void setCaption(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText)` | Sets the caption; null allowed. |
| `public String getUrl()` | The URL the button leads to, or null. Not determined: whether relative URLs are resolved against the Jira base URL; the plugin's own callers pass page paths. |
| `public void setUrl(String)` | Sets the URL; null allowed. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True when the other object is of exactly the same class and has equal caption and URL (nulls compare equal to nulls). |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash consistent with `equals`, computed from caption and URL. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters`

```java
public class ProcessDisplayParameters
```

What the progress page of a background process shows: a localizable process name and a list of buttons. Mutable bean (also stored as JSON with the process record). Build one with `ProcessDisplayParameters.Builder` or the setters. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ProcessDisplayParameters()` | Creates parameters with no name and an empty, modifiable button list. |
| `public ProcessDisplayParameters(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters)` | Copy constructor: same name and a new list holding the same button objects (the buttons themselves are shared, not copied). Throws `NullPointerException` if the argument is null. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText getName()` | The localizable name of the process, or null. |
| `public void setName(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText)` | Sets the process name; null allowed. |
| `public java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessButtonParameters> getButtons()` | The live, modifiable list of buttons (never copied). Null only if `setButtons(null)` was called. |
| `public void setButtons(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessButtonParameters>)` | Replaces the button list with the given list object (stored as is, not copied); null allowed. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True when the other object is of exactly the same class with equal name and equal button lists (order matters). |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash consistent with `equals`, from name and buttons. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters.Builder`

```java
public static class ProcessDisplayParameters.Builder
```

Fluent builder for `ProcessDisplayParameters`. It wraps one instance and `build()` returns that same instance, so the builder must not be used after `build()` if the result is to stay unchanged.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public Builder()` | Starts from empty parameters. |
| `public Builder(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters)` | Starts from a copy of the given parameters (see the copy constructor). Throws `NullPointerException` for null. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters.Builder withProcessName(String, Object...)` | Sets the process name to the i18n key (arg 1) with the given message arguments (arg 2). Returns this builder. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters.Builder addButton(String, String, Object...)` | Appends a button with URL (arg 1) and a caption made of the i18n key (arg 2) and message arguments (arg 3). Returns this builder. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters build()` | Returns the parameters built so far (the builder's own instance, not a copy). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessFeedback`

```java
public interface ProcessFeedback
```

The side of a background process that the worker uses: report status and poll for cancellation. Obtained from `ProcessHandleManager.getFeedback(Long)` or as part of a `ProcessHandle`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void setStatus(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessStatus)` | Stores a new status for the process and refreshes its timestamp (the timestamp drives automatic cleanup, see `ProcessHandleManager`). A null status is ignored. If the process record no longer exists the call does nothing (an error is logged). |
| `public abstract boolean isCancelled()` | True if someone has requested cancellation of the process (see `ProcessInfo.cancel()`). False if not, or if the process record no longer exists. The worker is expected to poll this and stop; nothing is interrupted automatically. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessHandle`

```java
public interface ProcessHandle extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessInfo, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessFeedback, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessUIController
```

Full handle to one background process, combining read access (`ProcessInfo`), worker feedback (`ProcessFeedback`) and display control (`ProcessUIController`). Returned by `ProcessHandleManager.createNew`. Handles are cheap views over the persistent process record: every call reads or writes the stored state (through a cache), so several handles for the same ID see the same data and the handle may be used from any thread or cluster node.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long getId()` | The process ID, a positive number assigned when the record was created. Use it to find the process again through `ProcessHandleManager`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessHandleManager`

```java
public interface ProcessHandleManager
```

Registry of background processes, kept in the plugin's database so that progress is visible across requests and cluster nodes. Implemented by the plugin and exported as a public OSGi component. No permission checks are made by this service; callers decide who may see a process with `ProcessInfo.isVisibleTo`. Process records whose timestamp (creation or last status change) is older than 30 days are deleted by the plugin's periodic maintenance, except those still referenced by automation.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessHandle createNew(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters)` | Creates and stores a new process record with status `PENDING`, no activity, percent complete -1 (unknown) and not cancelled, and returns a handle to it. Arg 1 is the managing user (the only user who may see it; null means visible to everyone). Arg 2 is the display parameters, may be null. Throws `StructureRuntimeException` if the parameters cannot be serialized. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessInfo getInfo(Long)` | Returns a read view of the process with the given ID, or null if the ID is null or no such process exists (also null, with an error logged, if the record cannot be loaded). |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessFeedback getFeedback(Long)` | Returns the worker-side view of the process with the given ID, or null under the same conditions as `getInfo`. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessUIController getUIController(Long)` | Returns the display-control view of the process with the given ID, or null under the same conditions as `getInfo`. |
| `public abstract void delete(long)` | Deletes the process record with the given ID. Existing handles then behave as for a missing process (status null, percent -1, not cancelled; updates are ignored). Not determined: behaviour for an ID that does not exist (passed to the database layer as is). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessInfo`

```java
public interface ProcessInfo
```

Read view of a background process, plus the ability to request cancellation. Obtained from `ProcessHandleManager.getInfo(Long)` or a `ProcessHandle`. Values are read from the stored record at call time.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessStatus getStatus()` | The current status, or null if the process record no longer exists. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters getParameters()` | The display parameters (name and buttons) last stored, or null if none were set or the record no longer exists. |
| `public abstract boolean isVisibleTo(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | True if the given user may see this process: when the process has no managing user, or the managing user equals the argument. A null argument matches only processes without a managing user. False if the record no longer exists. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText getActivity()` | Localizable description of what the process is doing right now, or null if never set or the record is gone. |
| `public abstract int getPercentComplete()` | Progress in percent, 0 to 100, or -1 when unknown (not set yet, or the record is gone). |
| `public abstract void cancel()` | Requests cancellation by setting the stored cancel flag (once set it cannot be cleared). Does nothing if already cancelled. It only signals the worker, which must poll `ProcessFeedback.isCancelled()`. If the record is gone the call is ignored. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessStatus`

```java
public enum ProcessStatus
```

Life-cycle state of a background process. Each constant has a stable integer code used for storage.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `PENDING (enum constant)` | Created but not started yet. Code 0. Initial status of new processes. |
| `RUNNING (enum constant)` | Work in progress. Code 1. |
| `FINISHED (enum constant)` | Work has ended (successfully or not). Code 2. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessStatus[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessStatus valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |
| `public int getValue()` | The integer storage code: 0, 1 or 2 as listed on the constants. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessStatus valueOf(int)` | Maps a storage code back to a status: 0 gives `PENDING`, 1 gives `RUNNING`, and any other number (including negatives) gives `FINISHED`. Never throws, never returns null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessUIController`

```java
public interface ProcessUIController
```

The side of a background process that controls what the progress page shows. Obtained from `ProcessHandleManager.getUIController(Long)` or a `ProcessHandle`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void setParameters(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProcessDisplayParameters)` | Replaces the stored display parameters. Null, or parameters equal to the stored ones, are ignored. If the record is gone, nothing happens (an error is logged). |
| `public abstract void setProgress(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText, Integer)` | Updates the current activity text (arg 1) and/or percent complete (arg 2). A null argument leaves that value unchanged; a value equal to the stored one is not rewritten. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the percentage is outside -1..100 (-1 means unknown). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProgressGauge`

```java
public interface ProgressGauge
```

Read side of an in-memory progress tracker: lets an observer see what a task is doing, how far it is, and ask it to stop. The plugin's own tracker implements both this and `ProgressSink`; it is thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText getActivity()` | The localizable description of the current activity, or null if none was set. |
| `public abstract int getPercentComplete()` | Progress in percent, 0 to 100, rounded, including the scaled progress of delegated sub-sinks; -1 if the tracker has not been initialized with a positive total. |
| `public abstract void cancel()` | Sets the cancelled flag. The worker sees it through `ProgressSink.isCancelled()`. Cancelling a delegate cancels the whole tracker. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProgressSink`

```java
public interface ProgressSink
```

Write side of an in-memory progress tracker, used by code doing the work. Work is measured in abstract units: call `initialize` once with the total, then report units done. A part of the units can be handed to a sub-task with `delegate`, which gets its own sink with its own unit scale. In the plugin's implementation all methods are thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void setActivity(String, Object...)` | Sets the current activity as an i18n key (arg 1) with message arguments (arg 2). On a delegate this sets the activity of the root tracker. |
| `public abstract void initialize(int)` | Sets the total number of units to the argument and resets progress to 0. Throws `IllegalStateException` if already initialized with a positive total, and `IllegalArgumentException` if the total is negative. Initializing with 0 is allowed but leaves the tracker unusable for `increment`, `setDone` and `delegate` (they then fail as not initialized). |
| `public abstract void increment(int)` | Marks the given number of additional units as done. Throws `IllegalStateException` if not initialized, and `IllegalArgumentException` if the count is negative or larger than the units still left (units already delegated count as used). |
| `public default void increment()` | Same as `increment(1)`. |
| `public abstract void setDone(int)` | Sets the absolute number of units done. Throws `IllegalStateException` if not initialized, and `IllegalArgumentException` if the value is lower than the current done count or higher than the total. |
| `public abstract void complete()` | Marks all remaining units of this sink as done (nothing to do if no units are left, including an uninitialized sink) and then completes every delegate created from it, recursively. Does not throw. |
| `public abstract boolean isCancelled()` | True if `cancel()` was called on the tracker (or on any of its delegates, which share the flag). Also returns true, and sets the flag, when the calling thread has been interrupted; the thread's interrupt status is cleared in that case. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.process.ProgressSink delegate(int)` | Reserves the given number of this sink's units for a sub-task and returns a new sink for it. The sub-sink must be initialized with its own total; its progress is scaled into the reserved units when computing percent complete. Activity, cancellation and the lock are shared with the parent. Throws `IllegalStateException` if this sink is not initialized and `IllegalArgumentException` if the count is negative or exceeds the units left. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.property`

Small key/value property stores kept in the plugin's own database tables: one global store and one store scoped to individual structures. Values are strings; numeric and boolean helpers convert on the fly.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.property.PropertyService`

```java
public interface PropertyService
```

Global string key/value store persisted in the plugin's database, with a non-expiring in-memory cache of values. Implemented by the plugin and exported as a public OSGi component. Internal API: no permission checks are made. Writing an empty or null value deletes the key. Values are read as strings; boolean and long helpers parse them.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract String getString(String, String)` | Returns the stored value for the key (arg 1), or the default (arg 2) when there is none. Never null when the default is not null. If loading fails, the default is returned and a warning logged. |
| `public abstract boolean getBoolean(String, boolean)` | Returns true if the stored value is exactly `true` (case-sensitive), false for any other stored value, and the default (arg 2) when no value is stored. |
| `public abstract long getLong(String, long)` | Returns the stored value parsed as a decimal long, or the default (arg 2) when no value is stored or it cannot be parsed. |
| `public abstract void set(String, String)` | Stores the value (arg 2) under the key (arg 1); a null or empty value deletes the key. The key is trimmed before storing and must not be null or blank (`IllegalArgumentException`). The local cache entry is refreshed. Note: the getters do not trim the key, so keys with surrounding spaces are written and read under different names. |
| `public abstract void set(String, boolean)` | Stores `true` or `false` as text under the key. Same key rules as `set(String, String)`. |
| `public abstract void set(String, long)` | Stores the decimal text of the number under the key. Same key rules as `set(String, String)`. |
| `public abstract void remove(String)` | Deletes the key; same as setting a null value. Same key rules as `set(String, String)`. |
| `public abstract void invalidate(String)` | Drops the cached value for the key on this node so that the next read goes to the database (for example after the table was changed by other means). Does not change stored data. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.property.StructurePropertyService`

```java
public interface StructurePropertyService
```

Key/value store for properties attached to individual structures, persisted in the plugin's database and cached with a moderate expiry. Implemented by the plugin and exported as a public OSGi component; also returned by `StructureComponents`. No permission checks. Keys should be at most 170 characters (checked only when assertions are enabled). Properties of deleted structures are removed by maintenance.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract String getString(long, String, String)` | Returns the property value for the structure ID (arg 1) and key (arg 2), or the default (arg 3) if there is none. A load failure returns the default (warning logged). |
| `public default long getLong(long, String, long)` | Returns the property value parsed as a decimal long, or the default (arg 3) if absent or unparsable. |
| `public abstract void setValue(long, String, String)` | Stores the value (arg 3) for the structure ID and key. A null, empty or whitespace-only value deletes the property. Not checked: that the structure exists. |
| `public default void setValue(long, String, long)` | Stores the decimal text of the number. Same rules as the string variant. |
| `public abstract java.util.Set<String> getAllKeys(long)` | Returns the set of keys that have a stored value for the given structure ID (a new modifiable set; empty if none). Read directly from the database. |
| `public abstract void removeAllProperties(long)` | Deletes every property of the given structure ID. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull`

Versioning primitives for incremental (pull-based) data delivery. A data source has a current `DataVersion`; a client that knows an older version asks for an update and receives either the changes since that version or a full replacement when the versions are not comparable.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion`

```java
public class DataVersion
```

Immutable version stamp of a versioned data source: a signature identifying the data source instance (it changes, for example, after a restart or reset, making older stamps meaningless) and a version counter that grows with every change. Two stamps are comparable only when their signatures are equal. String form is `xxxxxxxx:n` (signature as 8 lower-case hex digits, then the decimal version).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion ZERO` | The stamp with signature 0 and version 0, used as the starting point by clients that have no data yet; it is normally not comparable with any real source and therefore yields a full update. |
| `public DataVersion(int, int)` | Creates a stamp with the given signature (arg 1) and version (arg 2). No checks. |
| `public boolean isComparable(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion)` | True if the argument is not null and has the same signature as this stamp. |
| `public boolean isBefore(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion)` | True if both stamps are comparable and this version number is strictly smaller. For a null or incomparable argument it returns false (and throws `AssertionError` when Java assertions are enabled), so callers should check `isComparable` first. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion increment()` | Returns a stamp with the same signature and version plus one. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion increment(int)` | Returns a stamp with the same signature and version plus the count; returns this same instance for 0. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative count. |
| `public int getSignature()` | The signature identifying the data source instance. |
| `public int getVersion()` | The version counter. |
| `public String toString()` | `String.format("%08x:%d", signature, version)`, e.g. `0000002a:17`. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True for another object of exactly this class with equal signature and version. |
| `public int hashCode()` | `31 * signature + version`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.VersionedDataSource`

```java
public interface VersionedDataSource<T extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.VersionedDataUpdate>
```

Contract for a data source that supports incremental retrieval. Implemented by the plugin's sources (forests, item changes, attribute subscriptions and similar); clients keep the version of the last update they received and pass it back to get what changed.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract T getUpdate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion)` | Returns the changes since the given version, stamped with the version the client will have after applying them. If the argument equals the current version the update is empty; if it is incomparable (other signature) or too old to compute a delta, the update is full. Never null; the argument must not be null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion getCurrentVersion()` | The current version stamp of the source. Never null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.VersionedDataUpdate`

```java
public abstract class VersionedDataUpdate
```

Base class of updates returned by a `VersionedDataSource`. Subclasses carry the actual data and override `isFull` / `isEmpty`. An update is either full (replace everything the client has), incremental (apply on top of the client's data), and possibly empty (nothing changed).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected VersionedDataUpdate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion)` | Creates an update stamped with the given version, which is the version the client will be at after applying it. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the version is null. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.pull.DataVersion getVersion()` | The version stamp of this update; never null. Final. |
| `public boolean isFull()` | True if the update replaces the client's data entirely. The base implementation returns false. |
| `public boolean isEmpty()` | True if the update contains no changes. The base implementation returns false. |
| `public boolean isIncremental()` | True if the update must be applied on top of the client's earlier data; always the negation of `isFull()`. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query`

The structure query language: a query evaluated against a `Forest` that selects rows by their position in the hierarchy, by the issues they show (issue keys, issue IDs, embedded JQL) and by pluggable named constraints. Queries are obtained by parsing text (`StructureQueryParser`) or with a fluent builder (`StructureQueryBuilder`). Other plugins can add named constraints through the `structure-query-constraint` module type by implementing `StructureQueryConstraint`. The text syntax is described on `StructureQueryParser.parse(String)`.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.QueryContext`

```java
public interface QueryContext
```

Evaluation context handed to a `StructureQueryConstraint` while a query runs. It describes the forest being searched, addressed by row index (0-based position in the forest, in forest order), and offers issue lookups performed as the searching user. Created by the plugin per query execution; valid only during that execution and not thread-safe. Index arguments must be within 0..size()-1 unless stated otherwise.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long rowId(int)` | The row ID at the given index. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow row(int)` | The full row at the given index, loaded from the row manager with normal item access. Throws `MissingRowException` if the row no longer exists. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongIterator rows(com.almworks.integers.IntIterator)` | Lazily converts an iterator of indices into an iterator of the corresponding row IDs, in the same order. |
| `public abstract boolean isIssue(int)` | True if the row at the index shows a Jira issue. |
| `public abstract long issueId(int)` | The issue ID shown by the row at the index, or 0 if the row is not an issue row. Results are cached per context. |
| `public abstract int depth(int)` | The depth of the row at the index; 0 for top-level rows. |
| `public abstract int size()` | Number of rows in the forest. |
| `public abstract int parent(int)` | Index of the parent row of the row at the index, or -1 for top-level rows (also -1 for a negative argument). |
| `public abstract int subtreeEnd(int)` | Index just past the last descendant of the row at the index (exclusive end of its subtree); so the subtree occupies indices idx..subtreeEnd(idx)-1. For a negative index it returns `size()`. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest getForest()` | The forest the query is evaluated against. |
| `public abstract void resolveRowIdsToIssues(com.almworks.integers.LongIterator, boolean, com.almworks.integers.func.LongLongProcedure)` | For each row ID from the iterator (arg 1) that is an issue row, calls the procedure (arg 3) with (row ID, issue ID). Non-issue rows and missing rows are skipped. Arg 2 tells whether the row IDs are sorted ascending (a performance hint). Callback order is not guaranteed to match input order. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray filterIssues(com.atlassian.query.Query, com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Returns, as a new sorted array without duplicates, those issue IDs from the list (arg 2, which must be sorted ascending; duplicates allowed) that match the JQL query (arg 1) and are visible to the searching user (unless security is overridden for the current thread). A null query keeps every visible issue. A search failure is thrown as an unchecked exception and makes the whole query return no rows. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongIterable resolveIssueIdToRows(long)` | Returns the IDs of all rows, anywhere in the instance and not only in this forest, that show the given issue. No permission check. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongIterable resolveIssueKeyToRows(String)` | Looks up the issue by key (case-insensitive) and returns all rows that show it, as for `resolveIssueIdToRows`. Returns an empty iterable if the issue does not exist or the searching user cannot browse it (unless security is overridden). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQuery`

```java
public abstract class StructureQuery
```

A parsed or built query that selects rows of a `Forest`. Obtained from `StructureQueryParser.parse(String)` or `StructureQueryBuilder`. Execution and validation run as the current user (the thread's authentication context); if security is overridden for the thread, validation is skipped and issue visibility is not checked. A query that fails validation for the current user returns no rows from every execute/check method. Instances cache the last validation and the last evaluation context, so they are not thread-safe; equality compares the query logic (after simplification), not the text. Results are row indices or row IDs in forest order. `toString()` of the plugin's implementation returns the original text, or for built queries a generated text in the same syntax (where all-rows prints as `!EMPTY` and constraint arguments are double-quoted without escaping).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public StructureQuery()` | Protected constructor for implementations; clients obtain queries from the parser or builder. |
| `public abstract com.atlassian.jira.util.MessageSet validate()` | Checks the query for the current user and returns the messages (never null; errors make the query unusable for execution). Checks: embedded JQL is valid for the user; every referenced issue key/ID exists and is visible (`BROWSE_PROJECTS`) to the user, and belongs to a project where the plugin is enabled; each named constraint accepts its arguments; no saved-filter references form a cycle. Search failures during the check become warnings. |
| `public abstract String getSanitizedQueryString()` | Returns the query text with details the current user must not see removed: issue keys the user cannot see are replaced by their numeric ID when known, otherwise by `?`, and embedded JQL is replaced by Jira's sanitized form of that JQL for the user. Validates first if not yet validated for this user. Never null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongArray execute(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Runs the query on the forest and returns the matching row IDs in forest order as a new array. Empty if validation fails. A search error is logged and yields an empty or partial result. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongIterator executeUnbuffered(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Same as `execute` but returns a lazy iterator; results are computed while iterating, so the forest must not change meanwhile. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.IntArray executeIndices(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Runs the query and returns the indices (positions) of matching rows in ascending order as a new array. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.IntIterator executeIndicesUnbuffered(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Lazy variant of `executeIndices`. |
| `public abstract boolean checkRow(Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | True if the row with the given ID (arg 1) is in the forest (arg 2) and matches the query. False for a null ID, a row not in the forest, or a query that fails validation. Relations are still evaluated against the whole forest. |
| `public abstract boolean checkIndex(int, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | True if the row at the given index matches; false for an index out of range. |
| `public abstract String getQueryString()` | The text this query was parsed from, or null for queries made with the builder. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder`

```java
public class StructureQueryBuilder<B extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder<B>>
```

Fluent, type-safe builder for `StructureQuery`, equivalent to the text syntax. Start with `begin()` (or `StructureQueryBuilderFactory.builder()`), add constraints, combine them through the `and` / `or` fields, and finish with `Head.end()`. The type parameter B is the type returned after each completed constraint, so nested groups (`sub()` ... `endsub()`) return to the right level. Precedence matches the text syntax: constraints joined by `and` form a group, and `or` starts a new group; the result is the union of the groups. Builders are mutable, single-use and not thread-safe. Example: `StructureQueryBuilder.begin().child.in.issueKey("A-1").and.not().leaf().end()`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.StartStep<B> and` | Step for adding the next constraint joined with AND to the current group. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.StartStep<B> or` | Step for adding the next constraint as the start of a new OR group (if the current group is empty, it is added to it instead). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.StartStep<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.Head> begin()` | Creates a new builder using the plugin's `StructureQueryBuilderFactory` OSGi component and returns its first step. Throws `IllegalStateException` if the factory is not available (plugin not running or not visible to the caller). |
| `protected StructureQueryBuilder(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.StartStep<B>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.StartStep<B>)` | For implementations: creates a builder whose `and` and `or` fields are the given steps. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.BasicConstraintStep`

```java
public interface StructureQueryBuilder.BasicConstraintStep<B extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder<B>>
```

Step at which a basic constraint is added. Each method adds one constraint (combined with any pending negation or relation from the preceding steps) and returns the builder of type B to continue. When reached after a relation and operator (e.g. `child.in`), the constraint is the operand of that relation.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract B jql(com.atlassian.query.Query)` | Adds a constraint matching issue rows whose issue matches the JQL query (as the searching user). A null query, or a query without a condition, matches every issue row visible to the user. |
| `public abstract B issueKey(String)` | Adds a constraint matching rows that show the issue with this key. Equivalent to `issues(List.of(key), null)`. |
| `public abstract B issueKeys(Iterable<String>)` | Adds a constraint matching rows that show any of the issues with these keys. The keys are copied. |
| `public abstract B issueKeys(String...)` | Varargs form of `issueKeys(Iterable)`; a null array means no keys. |
| `public abstract B issueId(long)` | Adds a constraint matching rows that show the issue with this ID. |
| `public abstract B issueIds(com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Adds a constraint matching rows that show any of these issue IDs. The list is copied. |
| `public abstract B issueIds(long...)` | Varargs form of `issueIds(LongList)`; a null array means no IDs. |
| `public abstract B issues(Iterable<String>, com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Adds one constraint matching rows that show any of the listed issues, given by keys (arg 1) and/or IDs (arg 2); either may be null. Both are copied. Keys are resolved case-insensitively when the query is validated and executed. |
| `public abstract B leaf()` | Adds a constraint matching rows that have no children (text form `leaf`). |
| `public abstract B root()` | Adds a constraint matching top-level rows (text form `root`). |
| `public abstract B empty()` | Adds a constraint matching no rows (text form `empty`). As the operand of a relation it has the special meaning described on `StructureQueryParser.parse`. |
| `public abstract B all()` | Adds a constraint matching every row. No text keyword exists; it prints as `!EMPTY`. |
| `public abstract B constraint(String, String...)` | Adds a named constraint (arg 1, as registered by a `structure-query-constraint` module, matched case-insensitively) with the given arguments (arg 2). Throws `NullPointerException` if any argument is null. An unknown name is not an error here: at execution it matches nothing (warning logged); a constraint that throws during execution also matches nothing. |
| `public abstract B constraint(String, Iterable<String>)` | Same as the varargs form, taking the arguments from an iterable (copied). |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.StartStep<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.Sub<B>> sub()` | Opens a parenthesized group and returns its first step. Finish the group with `Sub.endsub()`, which adds the whole group as one constraint here and returns the builder of type B. |
| `public abstract B query(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQuery)` | Embeds an existing query as one constraint. Only queries created by this plugin's parser or builder can be embedded; any other implementation (or null) is ignored with a warning and the builder is returned unchanged. |

```java
public static class StructureQueryBuilder.OpStep<B extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder<B>>
```

Step after a relation has been chosen (e.g. after `child`): pick the operator by field, then give the operand constraint. Fields that share a meaning are the same object.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.BasicConstraintStep<B> in` | Rows having at least one relative of the chosen kind that matches the operand (text `in`). Same object as `equals` and `is`. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.BasicConstraintStep<B> notIn` | Complement of `in` (text `not in`). Same object as `notEquals` and `isNot`. |

Returns a step on which the next relation is picked; the operator and operand then apply to the combined relation. |
| `public OpStep(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryBuilder.RelationStepHelper<B>)` | For implementations: wires the operator fields from the helper (`in`, `equals`, `is` from its inverse-composition step; `notIn`, `notEquals`, `isNot` from its negated step; `of` from its composition step). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryConstraint`

```java
public interface StructureQueryConstraint
```

Extension point for named constraints in the query language. Other plugins implement it and declare it with a `structure-query-constraint` module whose `fname` attribute gives the name used in queries (matched case-insensitively; if two modules use the same name, one replaces the other and a warning is logged). The plugin calls `validate` when a query is validated and `filter` when it is executed, possibly concurrently for different queries, so implementations should be stateless or thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.atlassian.jira.util.MessageSet validate(java.util.List<String>)` | Called with the constraint's arguments (never null, may be empty) during query validation. Return a message set (never null; a null return breaks validation with an exception): each error is reported prefixed with the constraint name and makes the query invalid, warnings are passed on. Return an empty set when the arguments are acceptable. `StructureQueryConstraints.validateArgumentCount` helps with arity checks. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryConstraint.Sequence filter(com.almworks.integers.IntIterator, java.util.List<String>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.QueryContext)` | Called at execution. Arg 1 iterates the candidate row indices in ascending order; arg 2 is the argument list; arg 3 gives access to the forest. Return a `Sequence` that passes on the matching indices, which must be a subset of the input in ascending order. Return `Sequence.EMPTY` to match nothing. Exceptions (here or while the sequence advances) are caught by the plugin, logged, and treated as matching nothing further. |

Receiver of matching row indices, given to `Sequence.advance`. Implemented by the plugin. Indices must be pushed in ascending order and must come from the input of the constraint.

| `public abstract void accept(com.almworks.integers.IntIterable)` | Reports several matching row indices, in ascending order. |
| `public abstract void willAccept(int)` | Optional hint that about the given number of indices will follow, so storage can be pre-allocated. It does not oblige the caller to push them. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQueryParser`

```java
public interface StructureQueryParser
```

Parser for the text form of the query language. Implemented by the plugin and exported as a public OSGi component; also available from `StructureComponents`. Thread-safe; each call returns a new query.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.query.StructureQuery parse(String) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Parses query text into a `StructureQuery`. The returned query remembers the original text (`getQueryString`). The text is not validated against the instance here (unknown issues, invalid JQL field names and constraint argument errors are found by `validate`). Throws `NullPointerException` for null and `StructureException` (the plugin's own error 6005 `INVALID_SJQL`, category `INVALID_INPUT`, carrying the position and a localized message with up to 40 characters of context and line/column) for a syntax error. Syntax (keywords are case-insensitive; multi-word keywords may be written with underscores or in camelCase, e.g. `prev_sibling` or `prevSibling`; whitespace between tokens is free): - `A or B` (also `\|\|`, `\|`), `A and B` (also `&&`, `&`), `not A` (also `!`). `not` binds tightest, then `and`, then `or`. Parentheses group: `( ... )`. - Basic constraints: `empty` or `null` (matches nothing); `leaf`/`leaves` (rows without children); `root`/`roots` (top-level rows); a comma-separated list of issue keys and/or numeric issue IDs, e.g. `PROJ-1, proj-2, 10001` (an issue key is letters/digits, a hyphen and digits, accepted in any letter case; a key or ID must be followed by end of text, whitespace or punctuation); embedded JQL in square brackets, e.g. `[status = Open ORDER BY key]` (the closing bracket is found while skipping single- and double-quoted strings, where backslash escapes the next character, and custom field references such as `cf[10010]`; an ORDER BY part is ignored; `[]` with an empty condition matches every issue row the user can see); or a named constraint (see below). - Relational constraints: `RELATION OPERATOR C`, where C is a single clause (possibly negated, possibly itself relational; use parentheses for `and`/`or`). Relations: `self`; `issue`/`issues`; `child`/`children`/`sub_issue`/`sub_issues`; `parent`/`parents`; `descendant(s)`; `ancestor(s)`; `preceding_sibling`/`prev_sibling`/`previous_sibling` (plural forms too); `following_sibling`/`next_sibling` (plural too); `sibling(s)`. Combined forms `issue_or_R`, `issues_or_R`, `R_or_issue(s)`, `self_or_R`, `R_or_self` exist for R = child, parent, descendant, ancestor and the sibling relations, and relations can also be joined explicitly: `self or child in C`. - Operators: `in`, `=`, `is` select rows having at least one relative of the given kind that matches C (e.g. `child in C` = rows with a child matching C; `ancestor in C` = rows below a row matching C). `of` selects the relatives themselves (e.g. `child of C` = children of rows matching C; `descendant of C` = everything below rows matching C). `not in`, `!=`, `is not` are the complement of `in`. When C is `empty`: `R in empty` / `R is empty` = rows having no such relative (`child is empty` = leaves); `R of empty` = rows that are not such a relative of any row (`child of empty` = roots). `self` is identity; `issue` is identity restricted to issue rows. - Named constraints: `name(arg1, arg2, ...)`, `name()`, `name arg` (one argument, up to whitespace) or bare `name` when followed by `and`, `or`, `)` or the end. Names come from installed `structure-query-constraint` modules and are matched case-insensitively; the plugin itself defines `folder`, `memo`, `item`, `rowId` and `planningtask`. An unquoted argument runs up to the next `,` or `)` and is trimmed. A quoted argument uses `"..."` or `'...'`; inside it `\"`, `\'` and `\\` stand for the escaped character and any other backslash is kept literally. An empty argument between commas is a syntax error. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row`

Rows, the building blocks of forests. A row is an immutable triple of a row ID (unique across the instance), an item identity and a semantics code; the same item can appear in many rows. The package holds the row manager service, the `StructureRow` contract with its standard implementations, and static helpers for special row IDs (super-root, temporary rows).

Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the row ID is 0 or -1 (see `StructureRows.validateForestRowId`). |
| `public long getRowId()` | The row ID given at construction. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity getItemId()` | The item identity given at construction. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.RowManager`

```java
public interface RowManager extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.RowRetriever
```

Service that creates rows and looks them up. Implemented by the plugin and exported as a public OSGi component; also available from `StructureComponents`. Thread-safe. Rows are either persistent (stored in the database, created with `createRow`) or transient (created by generators at forest-build time, kept in memory and lost on restart). Row IDs are positive; 0, -1 and values up to -100 have special meanings (see `StructureRows`). No permission checks are made on lookups.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long createRow(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, long)` | Creates a new persistent row for the item (arg 1) with the semantics code (arg 2; see `CoreSemantics`, 0 for none) and returns its new, never reused ID. Each call creates a new row even for the same item. The item is not checked for existence. |
| `public default com.almworks.integers.LongIterator findRows(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | Returns an iterator over the IDs of all rows (persistent first, then transient) that show the item. Empty for null or an unknown item. The result is a snapshot. |
| `public default void findRows(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, java.util.function.LongConsumer)` | Passes the ID of every row showing the item to the consumer. Nothing happens for null. |
| `public abstract void findRows(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, java.util.function.LongPredicate)` | Passes row IDs showing the item to the predicate until it returns false. Persistent rows come first, then transient rows. Nothing happens for null; a database error is logged and skips the persistent rows only (the empty answer may be cached); transient rows are still passed. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.RowMapper createMapper(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Internal: returns a `RowMapper` that maps row IDs a client may hold (for example from an older build of a generated forest) to the matching rows of the given forest. |
| `public default java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity> collectItemIds(com.almworks.integers.LongIterable)` | Returns the set of item identities shown by the given rows, ignoring rows that do not exist. Null gives an empty set. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.RowMapper`

```java
public interface RowMapper
```

Internal helper that translates row IDs into rows of a specific forest. In generated forests the transient rows are recreated on every rebuild under new IDs; each new row remembers the row it replaces (its original) and the generator that created it, and the mapper follows that chain. Created by `RowManager.createMapper`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long mapRow(long)` | Returns the ID to use in the mapper's forest for the requested row ID: the ID itself if the row is in the forest (or is the super-root -1); otherwise, for a transient row, follows the chain of original rows until it reaches a row in the forest or a row whose creating generator is in the forest; returns 0 when no match exists (persistent row not in forest, missing row, row without creator, a cycle, or more than about 100 steps). |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.RowMapper.Mapping map(com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Maps a list of row IDs with `mapRow` and returns the result as a `Mapping`. When every row maps to itself, the mapping is marked as identical and no new lists are created. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.SimpleRow`

```java
public class SimpleRow implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow
```

Standard row implementation that resolves its item lazily through an `ItemResolver` the first time `getItem` is called, then caches the result (thread-safe, resolved at most once). Created through the static `create` methods (the constructor is private). A variant that skips the user's access check exists for trusted code; it is obtained through the `create` methods with the skip flag, `tryMakeUnchecked` or `StructureRows.makeUnchecked`. Internal.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected final long myRowId` | The row ID (for subclasses). |
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity myItemId` | The item identity (for subclasses). |
| `protected final long mySemantics` | The semantics code (for subclasses). |
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemResolver myResolver` | The resolver used to load the item (for subclasses). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow create(long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemResolver)` | Creates a row from row ID, item identity, semantics and resolver that checks the current user's access when loading the item. With a null resolver a `ShallowRow` is returned instead. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for row ID 0 or -1. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow create(long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemResolver, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.ItemAccessMode)` | Creates a row according to the access mode (arg 5): a `ShallowRow` for `ITEM_NOT_NEEDED` or a null resolver, a row without access check for `SKIP_ACCESS_CHECK`, otherwise a checking row. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for row ID 0 or -1. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow create(long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemResolver, boolean)` | Creates a row that loads its item without access check if arg 5 is true, with the check otherwise. A null resolver gives a `ShallowRow`. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for row ID 0 or -1. |
| `public long getRowId()` | The row ID given at construction. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity getItemId()` | The item identity given at construction. |
| `public long getSemantics()` | The semantics code given at construction. |
| `protected String getQualifier()` | Label used by `toString`: `SimpleRow`, or `SimpleRow(unchecked)` for the variant without access check. |
| `public String toString()` | `<qualifier>[<rowId>:<itemId>:<semantics>]`. |
| `public <I> I getItem(Class<I>)` | Loads the item on first call (through the resolver, with or without the user's access check depending on the variant). If loading throws, the exception propagates from that first call and the row is nevertheless marked as loaded, so later calls return null. Otherwise returns the item cast to the requested class, or null if it was not found, is invisible to the user, or is not an instance of that class. |
| `protected Object resolve()` | Loads the item object: through the resolver with access check, or without it in the unchecked variant. Called at most once per row. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow tryMakeUnchecked(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | If the argument is a checking `SimpleRow`, returns a new row with the same data and resolver that loads its item without access check; otherwise returns the argument unchanged (already unchecked, or another row class). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow`

```java
public interface StructureRow
```

A row of a forest: row ID, item identity, semantics and, on demand, the item object. Implementations are immutable apart from lazy item loading and safe to share between threads. Obtained from `RowManager` / `RowRetriever`; also implemented by the plugin's helper classes in this package.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow ROW_ZERO` | Placeholder row with row ID 0 and item `ItemIdentity.ITEM_ZERO`, used where a non-null row is needed but there is none. |
| `public abstract long getRowId()` | The row ID: positive for real rows, -1 for the super-root, -100 and below for temporary rows in forest actions, 0 only for `ROW_ZERO`. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity getItemId()` | Identity of the item shown in the row. Never null. |
| `public abstract long getSemantics()` | Code describing how the row came to be in the forest (see `CoreSemantics`: 0 none, 1 title, 2 group, 3 inserted, 4 extension); 0 for ordinary rows. |
| `public abstract <I> I getItem(Class<I>)` | The item object (for example a Jira `Issue` for issue rows) if it can be loaded and is an instance of the requested class, otherwise null. Depending on how the row was obtained, the item is null when the current user may not see it, and it is always null for rows retrieved with `ITEM_NOT_NEEDED`. Request `Object.class` to get the item regardless of class. |

```java
public class StructureRows
```

Static helpers for row IDs and rows. Not instantiable. Special row IDs: 0 is never a valid row; -1 is the super-root (the invisible parent of all top-level rows); -100 and lower are temporary IDs used in forest actions to refer to rows that do not exist yet.

|---|---|
| `public static final long STARTING_TEMPORARY_ROW_ID = -100` | -100, the first (highest) temporary row ID; temporary IDs count down from it. |
| `public static void validateForestRowId(long)` | Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the ID is 0 (message says the row ID must be non-zero) or -1 (message says -1 is reserved for the super-root). Any other value passes. |
| `public static void validateForestRowIds(com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Validates each ID as `validateForestRowId`; the exception message is prefixed with the offending position as `[index] `. A null list passes. |

| `public static com.almworks.integers.LongIterable withoutSuperRoot(com.almworks.integers.LongIterable)` | Returns a lazy iterable that applies `withoutSuperRoot` to each new iterator of the argument. |
| `public static boolean isSuperRoot(long)` | True if the ID is -1. |
| `public static boolean isSuperRoot(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | True if the row is not null and its ID is -1. |
| `public static boolean isGenerator(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | True if the row's item type is `CoreItemTypes.GENERATOR`. False for null. |
| `public static boolean isEffector(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | True if the row's item type is `CoreItemTypes.EFFECTOR`. False for null. |
| `public static boolean isAutomation(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | True if the row is a generator or an effector row. |
| `public static boolean isLoopMarker(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | True if the row's item type is `CoreItemTypes.LOOP_MARKER` (a marker row inserted where a generated hierarchy would repeat itself). False for null. |
| `public static boolean isItemType(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow, String)` | True if both arguments are non-null and the row's item type equals the given type key exactly. |
| `public static boolean isTemporary(long)` | True if the ID is -100 or lower. |
| `public static long temporaryRow(int)` | Returns the temporary row ID for the given sequence number: `-100 - sequence`. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative number. |
| `public static boolean isItemVisibleForSure(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | True if the row (after unwrapping `TransientRow` wrappers) is a `SimpleRow` that loads its item without access check, meaning visibility has already been established by the caller. False otherwise, which does not mean the item is invisible. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow makeShallow(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | Returns a row with the same ID, item and semantics that never loads the item (a `ShallowRow`); a `TransientRow` wrapper is kept with the shallow row inside. Returns the argument if it is already shallow. For `StructureRow.ROW_ZERO` or the super-root row it throws `IllegalArgumentException`, because a shallow row cannot have ID 0 or -1. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow makeUnchecked(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | Returns an equivalent row that loads its item without access check (see `SimpleRow.tryMakeUnchecked`), keeping any `TransientRow` wrapper. Rows of other classes are returned unchanged. |

| `public long getCreatorId()` | Row ID of the generator that created this row, or 0. |
| `public long getOriginalId()` | Row ID of the row this one was derived from (for example the row it replaces from an earlier build of the forest), or 0. |

| `public static long getCreatorId(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | The creator ID if the row is a `TransientRow`, otherwise 0 (also for null). |
| `public static long getOriginalId(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow)` | The original ID if the row is a `TransientRow`, otherwise 0 (also for null). |

| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow replaceDelegate(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow, java.util.function.Function<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.StructureRow>)` | Applies the function (arg 2) to the innermost row. For a plain row returns the function's result, or the row itself if the result is null. For a wrapper returns a new single `TransientRow` around the result with the outer wrapper's creator and original IDs, or the original wrapper if the function returned null or the same row. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings`

Global and per-user configuration of the plugin: which projects it is enabled for, application-level permissions and who holds them, default structures, preferences for the panel shown on issue and project pages, and the attribute sensitivity settings that control which computed values may be shown when they depend on items a user cannot see.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.AttributeSensitivityMode`

```java
public enum AttributeSensitivityMode
```

Global policy for "sensitive" attributes: computed values (typically aggregates) that could reveal information about items the viewing user cannot see. The plugin withholds sensitive values in such cases. Each mode has a stable integer code used for storage.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `STANDARD (enum constant)` | Default mode (code 0). Attributes are sensitive unless their value format is one the plugin considers harmless by default or its value class is annotated with `NonSensitiveInStandardMode`; attributes listed as non-sensitive in the settings are exempt. |
| `STRICT (enum constant)` | Every attribute is treated as sensitive (code 1), except those explicitly listed as non-sensitive in the settings. |
| `PERMISSIVE (enum constant)` | No attribute is treated as sensitive (code 2); the non-sensitive list is ignored. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.AttributeSensitivityMode[] values()` | All constants, in declaration order (a new array on every call). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.AttributeSensitivityMode valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |
| `public int getCode()` | The integer storage code: 0, 1 or 2. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.AttributeSensitivityMode valueOf(int)` | Returns the mode with the given code. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` for any other number (message says the code is not a valid sensitivity mode). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.AttributeSensitivitySettings`

```java
public interface AttributeSensitivitySettings
```

The attribute sensitivity configuration: a mode and a list of attributes explicitly declared non-sensitive. Read and written through `StructureConfiguration`; `ImmutableAttributeSensitivitySettingsBean` is the standard implementation.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.AttributeSensitivityMode getSensitivityMode()` | The global mode. Never null. |
| `public abstract java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<?>> getNonSensitiveAttributes()` | Attributes declared non-sensitive (used by `STANDARD` and `STRICT` modes). An entry also covers more specific variants of the same attribute (a generalization match), and an entry with format `ValueFormat.ANY` matches the attribute in any format. Never null. |

What the plugin's panel on an issue or project page does with the selected structure when the user opens the page. Each constant has a string code used for storage.

| `STRUCTURE_WITH_ISSUE (enum constant)` | Switch to a structure that contains the current issue. Code `withIssue`. This is the plugin's default. |
| `DEFAULT_STRUCTURE (enum constant)` | Switch to the default structure (for the project, else the global one). Code `default`. |

| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.AutoSwitchStrategy valueOf(String)` | The constant with exactly this name; `IllegalArgumentException` when there is none, `NullPointerException` for null. |
| `public String getStringCode()` | The storage code: `off`, `withIssue` or `default`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.AutoSwitchStrategy fromStringCode(String)` | Returns the strategy whose code equals the argument exactly (case-sensitive), or null for null or an unknown code. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.StructureConfiguration`

```java
public interface StructureConfiguration
```

Global configuration of the plugin, stored in Jira application properties (and, for UI preferences, in user properties) and cached. Implemented by the plugin and exported as a public OSGi component; also available from `StructureComponents` and `StructurePluginHelper`. Covers: the projects the plugin is enabled for; application permissions (who may use the plugin, create structures, configure synchronization and automation, and further permissions from `CoreAppPermissions`); default structures; panel UI settings; attribute sensitivity. Setters perform no permission check on the caller; protect them yourself. Defaults when nothing is stored: enabled for all projects, and every application permission granted to anyone.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean isEnabledForAllProjects()` | True if the plugin is enabled in all projects (default true). If the setting cannot be loaded, false. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.integers.LongList getPickedProjectIds()` | IDs of the projects explicitly selected for the plugin (used when not enabled for all projects), sorted ascending without duplicates. Never null. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.atlassian.jira.project.Project> getPickedProjects()` | The selected projects that still exist, in the order Jira lists projects. Never null. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.atlassian.jira.project.Project> getCurrentlyEnabledProjects()` | All projects when enabled for all projects, otherwise the selected ones. Never null. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.statistics`

Internal hooks for counting feature usage inside the plugin. The original aggregates these counters locally and could upload them to the vendor; the replacement must keep the API callable but never upload usage statistics or contact the vendor (SPEC.md §1.8).

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.statistics.StatisticSource`

```java
public interface StatisticSource
```

Callback that contributes named numeric values to the plugin's usage-statistics report. Implemented by plugin components (and potentially other plugins) and registered with `StructureStatisticsRecorder.addStatisticSource`. Marked internal. In the replacement the report is never sent anywhere (SPEC.md §1.8), so sources may be registered but their values are at most kept locally.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract java.util.Map<String, Double> getStatistics()` | Returns a map from statistic name to its current value, computed at the time of the call (for example a count of structures). Called whenever a statistics report is assembled; an exception thrown here is logged and the source is skipped for that report. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.statistics.StructureStatisticsRecorder`

```java
public interface StructureStatisticsRecorder
```

Service (OSGi component, internal) for recording usage counters. Recording calls are cheap and asynchronous: values are accumulated in memory and periodically (every 10 minutes by default) written to the plugin's local statistics store; data older than 40 days is purged. The original could upload a daily report to the vendor when an administrator opted in; the replacement never uploads usage statistics or contacts the vendor (SPEC.md §1.8). Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void addUniqueUserCountAsync(String)` | Records that the current user (as known to `StructureAuth`) used the feature named by the argument; the statistic counts distinct users. Does nothing when there is no current user (anonymous) or when the name is null or blank (a warning is logged). Throws the plugin's stopped exception if the plugin is not running. |
| `public abstract void addTotalCountAsync(String)` | Increments the total counter named by the argument by 1. Same as `addTotalCountAsync(name, 1.0)`. |
| `public abstract void addTotalCountAsync(String, double)` | Adds the second argument to the running total of the counter named by the first argument. A null or blank name is ignored with a logged warning. Throws the plugin's stopped exception if the plugin is not running. |
| `public abstract void addToIntValueDistrAsync(String, int, int...)` | Records one observation of an integer value into a histogram. Arguments: statistic prefix, the value, and ascending bin upper bounds. The value falls into the first bin whose bound is greater than or equal to it, or into an overflow bin named `inf` when it exceeds all bounds; the counter `<prefix>.<bound>` (or `<prefix>.inf`) is then incremented by 1. With no bins nothing is recorded. |
| `public abstract void addStatisticSource(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.statistics.StatisticSource)` | Registers a source whose values are added to every statistics report assembled afterwards. The same object may be added more than once (it is then queried more than once). Not persisted across restarts. |
| `public abstract void removeStatisticSource(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.statistics.StatisticSource)` | Unregisters one registration of the given source; does nothing if it was not registered. |
| `public abstract void addTotalCountAndActiveUserAsync(String)` | Convenience: increments the total counter named by the argument by 1 and also records the current user under the distinct-user statistic `activeUser.<name>`. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure`

The structure entity itself: reading and editing a structure's metadata (name, description, owner, permission rules, archive flag), looking structures up and checking access, creating, copying and deleting them, and listening for content changes.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure`

```java
public interface Structure
```

A structure's metadata as a mutable, unsaved working copy. Instances are obtained from `StructureManager` (`getStructure`, `getAllStructures`, `createStructure`, copies) and are snapshots: they do not reflect later changes by others. Setters only change the local copy and return the same object for chaining; nothing is persisted until `saveChanges()`. The forest (the rows) is not part of this object; it is accessed via the forest service. Not thread-safe; use one instance per thread.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long getId()` | The structure's numeric ID (positive). For a new structure that has not been saved yet, returns 0. |
| `public abstract String getName()` | The structure's name; never null (empty string when unset). |
| `public abstract String getDescription()` | The structure's description; never null (empty string when unset). |
| `public default com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser getOwner()` | The owner resolved to a Jira user from `getOwnerUserKey()`; null when there is no owner or the user key no longer resolves to a user. |
| `public abstract String getOwnerUserKey()` | The Jira user key of the structure's owner, or null when the structure has no owner. The owner can always administer the structure. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule> getPermissions()` | A copy of the structure's own permission rules, in evaluation order (later rules override earlier ones for the same user). Never null; changing the returned list does not affect the structure. These rules complement the owner and global administrators, who always have full access. |
| `public abstract boolean isEditRequiresParentIssuePermission()` | True when editing the structure additionally requires that the user can edit the parent issue of any issue being added, moved or removed under it (the parent-issue edit check is applied on every forest change). |
| `public abstract boolean isArchived()` | True when the structure is archived. Archived structures are read-only (forest changes are refused) and are excluded from most listings by default. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure setName(String)` | Sets the name in the working copy. Null becomes the empty string; names longer than 190 characters are shortened with a trailing ellipsis. A blank name makes `saveChanges()` fail. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure setDescription(String)` | Sets the description in the working copy (null clears it). Returns this. |
| `public default com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure setOwner(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Sets the owner in the working copy from a Jira user (null clears the owner); equivalent to `setOwnerUserKey` with the user's key. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure setOwnerUserKey(String)` | Sets the owner by Jira user key in the working copy; null clears the owner. The key is not validated here; ownership-change permission is checked by `saveChanges()`. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure setPermissions(java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule>)` | Replaces the permission rules in the working copy with the given rules (null means no rules). Rules are validated on `saveChanges()`. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure setEditRequiresParentIssuePermission(boolean)` | Sets the parent-issue edit check flag (see `isEditRequiresParentIssuePermission`) in the working copy. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure setArchived(boolean)` | Sets the archived flag in the working copy. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure saveChanges() throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Persists the working copy and returns this. If nothing was changed since the copy was obtained or last saved, does nothing. For a new structure, creates it (the ID becomes available from `getId()`), gives it an empty forest and, when no owner was set, makes the current user the owner. Throws `IllegalStateException` when the name is blank. Unless security is overridden (`StructureAuth.sudo`), creation requires the global right to create structures (`StructureException` with `NOT_ALLOWED_TO_CREATE_STRUCTURE`), and updating requires ADMIN level on the structure (`STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` when the user has no access at all, `STRUCTURE_ADMIN_DENIED` otherwise). Changed permission rules are validated (`StructureException` on invalid rules). Assigning the owner to another user requires being a Jira administrator, or holding the Jira user-picker permission together with ADMIN on the structure or being the previous owner; otherwise `STRUCTURE_OWNER_EDIT_DENIED`. Also fails when the plugin license does not allow writes. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel getEffectivePermission()` | The access level the current user has to this structure, computed now from the stored (not the unsaved) settings. `ADMIN` when security is overridden; `NONE` for a structure that has not been saved yet. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.StructureListener`

```java
public interface StructureListener
```

Extension point notified after structure forests change. Register with `StructureManager.addListener`. Called synchronously on the thread that finished writing history, once per batch of recorded changes; exceptions are logged and do not affect other listeners. Implementations should be fast and must not assume a particular user context.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void onStructuresChanged(com.almworks.integers.LongObjMap<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry>)` | Called with a map from structure ID to the history entry that was just recorded for that structure (one entry per changed structure in the batch). The map should be treated as read-only. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.StructureManager`

```java
public interface StructureManager
```

Main service (OSGi component) for structure metadata: lookup, access checks, creation, copying, deletion and change listeners. Implemented by the plugin. Unless stated otherwise, calls act as the current user from `StructureAuth`, and permission checks are skipped when security is overridden. Methods taking a `PermissionLevel` treat null as "no minimum level", so a null level returns structures even when the user's level is NONE. If the plugin is not available to the current user (license or global access restriction), listings are empty. Lists of structures are sorted by name with the current user's locale collation unless noted. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure getStructure(Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Returns the structure with the given ID (first argument) if the current user has at least the given level (second argument; null means any). Throws `StructureException` with `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` when the ID is null, the structure does not exist or the level is insufficient (the two cases are deliberately indistinguishable). Archived structures are returned too. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure> getAllStructures(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel)` | All non-archived structures on which the current user has at least the given level (null means any). Same as `getAllStructures(level, false)`. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure> getAllStructures(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel, boolean)` | All structures on which the current user has at least the given level (null means any); the second argument includes archived structures when true. Sorted by name. Never null. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure> getArchivedStructures(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel)` | Only the archived structures on which the current user has at least the given level (null means any), sorted by name. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure> getStructuresOwnedBy(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Non-archived structures whose owner is the given user and which the current user can at least view, sorted by name. Null user yields an empty list. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure> getStructuresByName(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel)` | Non-archived structures with the given name that the current user can access at the given level. Same as the three-argument form with `false`. |
