## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history`

Read access to the change history of structure forests: each saved forest modification produces a numbered history entry made of add, copy, move and remove changes. Includes a filterable activity query across structures and reconstruction of a forest as it was at an earlier version.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.ForestVersion`

```java
public class ForestVersion
```

Immutable value: the complete forest of a structure at one version together with the history entry that produced that version. Returned by `HistoryService.getForestVersion`. Public fields only.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest fullForest` | The entire forest of the structure as it was right after the version was recorded. |
| `public final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry entry` | The history entry for this version. For version 0 (the initial empty state) a synthetic entry with no changes, timestamp 0 and no user. |
| `public final int weight` | Estimated memory size of this object, used by caches. Computed in the constructor from the sizes of the full forest and of every change's forest and row lists; a rough approximation, not a byte count. |
| `public ForestVersion(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry)` | Creates the value from the full forest (first argument) and its entry (second, must not be null) and computes `weight`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry`

```java
public final class HistoryEntry
```

Immutable record of one saved modification of a structure's forest, identified by structure ID and version number. Versions of one structure increase by one with every recorded change; each entry lists the elementary changes in the order applied. Created by the plugin when recording history; can be constructed by callers (for example in tests). Equality is by value of all fields.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public HistoryEntry(long, int, int, long, String, Long, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry.Change>)` | Arguments in order: structure ID, version, previous version, timestamp (milliseconds since epoch), author user key (null or empty string are stored as null), synchronizer instance ID that made the change (null if none), and the list of changes (not copied; must not be null). |
| `public long getStructure()` | ID of the structure the entry belongs to. |
| `public int getVersion()` | Forest version produced by this entry (1 for the first recorded change). |
| `public int getPrevVersion()` | Forest version that this entry was applied to. Normally `getVersion() - 1`. |
| `public long getTimestamp()` | When the change was recorded, in milliseconds since the epoch. |
| `public String getUserKey()` | Jira user key of the user who made the change; null when unknown or anonymous. |
| `public Long getSynchronizer()` | ID of the synchronizer instance that made the change, or null if it was not made by a synchronizer. |
| `public java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry.Change> getChanges()` | The changes in this entry, in the order applied. Never null. Entries returned by `getHistoryEntriesWithoutChanges` have an empty list. In activity queries the list may be shortened (changes involving rows the user cannot see are filtered out) or truncated by a change limit. |
| `public String toString()` | Debug text listing all fields; format not part of the contract. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True for another `HistoryEntry` with equal structure, versions, timestamp, user key, synchronizer and change list. |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash consistent with `equals`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry.Change`

```java
public static final class HistoryEntry.Change
```

Immutable description of one elementary forest change inside a `HistoryEntry`: which rows were added, copied, moved or removed, and where. Positions are given as a parent path (list of row IDs from a root down to the parent, empty or null for top level) plus the preceding sibling. Equality is by value.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public Change(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry.Operation, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.LongList, int, com.almworks.integers.LongList)` | Arguments in order: operation; the forest fragment affected; path from (old parent path); after from (old preceding sibling); path to (new parent path); after to (new preceding sibling); direction; original rows. Values are stored as given (not copied). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry.Operation getOperation()` | The kind of change. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest getForest()` | The forest fragment that was added, copied (the new rows), moved or removed, with its subtrees. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongList getPathFrom()` | For MOVE and REMOVE: the row IDs from the top level down to the former parent of the fragment (empty when it was at top level). Null for ADD and COPY. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongList getAfterFrom()` | For MOVE and REMOVE: the former preceding sibling, as a list of at most one row ID (empty when the fragment was first among its siblings). Null for ADD and COPY. During forest reconstruction the plugin may prepend further preceding siblings to this list. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongList getPathTo()` | For ADD, COPY and MOVE: the row IDs from the top level down to the new parent, including the parent itself (empty for top level). Null for REMOVE. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongList getAfterTo()` | For ADD, COPY and MOVE: the new preceding sibling as a list of at most one row ID (empty when inserted first). Null for REMOVE. |
| `public int getDirection()` | For MOVE: 1 if the fragment moved further down the forest, -1 if it moved up, 0 if its position index did not change. 0 for other operations. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongList getOriginalRows()` | For COPY: for each row of `getForest()` in the same order, the ID of the row it was copied from, or 0 when that source row was not (or no longer) in this structure. Null for other operations. |
| `public String toString()` | Debug text listing all fields; format not part of the contract. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True for another `Change` with equal operation, forest, paths, preceding siblings, direction and original rows. |
| `public int hashCode()` | Hash consistent with `equals`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryQuery`

```java
public final class HistoryQuery
```

Immutable filter for `HistoryService.queryActivity`. All conditions are combined with AND. Each dimension has an inclusion (`is...`) and an exclusion (`not...`) list; for structures, authors, issues and projects only the inclusion list is applied when it is non-empty, otherwise the exclusion list. ID lists must be sorted ascending. Created by its constructors; all collections are copied or defaulted to empty, never null (except `operations`).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry.Operation> ALL_OPERATIONS` | Unmodifiable list of all `Operation` constants in declaration order. |
| `public final java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry.Operation> operations` | Operations to match: an entry matches when it contains at least one change of these kinds. Null means all operations (no restriction); the constructor stores null when all four were given. |
| `public final com.almworks.integers.LongList isIssuesSorted` | Issue IDs (sorted): match entries that touched at least one of these issues. Never null. |
| `public final com.almworks.integers.LongList notIssuesSorted` | Issue IDs (sorted): when there is no inclusion list, match entries that touched some issue other than these. Never null. |
| `public final com.almworks.integers.LongList isStructuresSorted` | Structure IDs (sorted): match entries of any of these structures. Never null. |
| `public final com.almworks.integers.LongList notStructuresSorted` | Structure IDs (sorted): when there is no inclusion list, exclude entries of these structures. Never null. |
| `public final java.util.Set<String> isAuthors` | User keys: match entries made by one of these users. A null element in the authors argument makes the constructor throw `NullPointerException`. Never null. |
| `public final java.util.Set<String> notAuthors` | User keys: when there is no inclusion set, exclude entries made by these users. Never null. |
| `public final com.almworks.integers.LongList isProjectsSorted` | Project IDs (sorted): match entries that touched issues of at least one of these projects. Never null. |
| `public final com.almworks.integers.LongList notProjectsSorted` | Project IDs (sorted): when there is no inclusion list, match entries touching issues of some other project. Never null. |
| `public final com.almworks.integers.LongList isSynchronizersSorted` | Synchronizer instance IDs (sorted) to include. Special values: -2 means "made without a synchronizer", -1 means "made by any synchronizer". Never null. |
| `public final com.almworks.integers.LongList notSynchronizersSorted` | Synchronizer instance IDs (sorted) to exclude, with the same special values -2 and -1. Applied together with the inclusion list. Never null. |
| `public final java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity> isAncestors` | Item identities: keep only entries having a change located under one of these items (an item on the from or to parent path), or, when an issue or project filter is set, a change whose fragment contains such an item with a matching issue below it. Never null. |
| `public final java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity> notAncestors` | Item identities: drop entries whose every change is located under one of these items, in the same sense as `isAncestors`. Never null. |
| `public final Long minDate` | Earliest timestamp to include (inclusive), milliseconds since epoch; null for no lower bound. |
| `public final Long maxDate` | Latest timestamp to include (inclusive), milliseconds since epoch; null for no upper bound. |
| `public final Long startId` | Paging cursor: only entries whose internal history key is strictly less than this value are returned. The key of an entry is `(structureId << 32) \| version`. Null to start from the newest. |
| `public HistoryQuery(Iterable<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry.Operation>, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.LongList, Iterable<String>, Iterable<String>, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.LongList, com.almworks.integers.LongList, java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, java.util.Set<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, java.util.Date, java.util.Date, Long)` | Arguments in field order: operations, issues in, issues out, structures in, structures out, authors in, authors out, projects in, projects out, synchronizers in, synchronizers out, ancestors in, ancestors out, min date, max date, start key. Any argument may be null (meaning no restriction). For operations pass `ALL_OPERATIONS` (or any collection containing all four) for no restriction. Not determined: what a null or empty operations argument does in a query; the original stores an empty set and then builds no operation condition for it, so behaviour is undefined; a replacement should treat it as no restriction or reject it. Long lists are kept as given (not copied) and must already be sorted; dates are converted to milliseconds. |
| `public HistoryQuery(long, Long)` | Query for all activity of one structure (first argument), all operations, starting below the given paging key (second argument, nullable). |
| `public String toString()` | Compact debug text listing the non-empty conditions; computed once and cached. Format not part of the contract. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryService`

```java
public interface HistoryService
```

Service (OSGi component) for reading recorded forest history. Implemented by the plugin. Only `queryActivity` and `getForestVersion` apply the current user's permissions; the per-structure methods read history without access checks, so callers must check access themselves. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void queryActivity(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryQuery, int, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryConsumer)` | Streams entries matching the query (first argument) to the consumer (third), newest first (by timestamp, then key, descending), with all their changes. Second argument: maximum number of entries delivered (0 or less for no limit). Unless security is overridden, entries of structures the current user cannot view are skipped, and changes are filtered by row visibility only loosely: a change is removed when the user can see none of its rows, but rows the user cannot see may still appear in a kept change (as ancestors in its path, or in its after-lists). An entry with no changes is never delivered, whether or not anything was filtered. Stops when the consumer returns false. |
| `public abstract void queryActivity(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryQuery, int, int, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.LimitedHistoryConsumer)` | Same as the three-argument form, but the third argument limits how many changes are loaded per entry (0 or less loads all); the consumer receives each entry together with its total number of changes, which may exceed the size of the truncated change list; this total is counted before visibility filtering. |
| `public abstract void getHistoryEntries(long, int, int, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryConsumer)` | Streams the entries of the structure (first argument) with versions greater than the second argument and up to and including the third, oldest first, with changes. A negative "from" version means from the very beginning. Returns nothing when both versions are equal. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` when "to" is less than "from" or negative. No access check. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry> getHistoryEntries(long, int, int)` | Same range and rules as the streaming form, collected into a list (oldest first). |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.HistoryEntry> getHistoryEntriesWithoutChanges(long, int, int)` | Same as `getHistoryEntries(long, int, int)` but each entry's change list is empty (cheaper when only metadata is needed). |
| `public abstract int getLatestHistoryEntryVersion(long)` | Highest recorded history version of the structure, or 0 when it has no history. No access check. |
| `public abstract int getEarliestHistoryEntryVersionGtEqDate(long, long)` | Lowest version of the structure (first argument) whose entry was recorded at or after the timestamp (second argument, epoch milliseconds); 0 when there is none. |
| `public abstract int getEntryCount(long)` | Number of history entries stored for the structure. |
| `public abstract int getEntryCountGtEqDate(long, long)` | Number of history entries of the structure (first argument) recorded at or after the timestamp (second argument, epoch milliseconds). |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.history.ForestVersion getForestVersion(long, int) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Reconstructs the full forest of the structure (first argument) as of the given version (second argument) and returns it with that version's entry. Version 0 gives the initial state with a synthetic empty entry. Requires VIEW access for the current user; otherwise `StructureException` `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. A version above the current version, or missing from history, gives `StructureException` `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. A version below 0 is checked only by an assertion: with assertions enabled (as tests run) it throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled the result is not specified. Results are cached; the forest is not filtered by row visibility. |

Callback for `HistoryService.queryActivity` with a per-entry change limit. Implemented by callers.

Return true to continue, false to stop. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync`

Synchronizers: extension modules that keep a structure's forest consistent with some Jira data (links, epics, sprints, filters, and so on). Contains the extension-point interface and a convenience base class, the manager that installs and runs synchronizer instances, the event data handed to incremental runs, and the audit log of actions synchronizers performed.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.AbstractSynchronizer`

```java
public abstract class AbstractSynchronizer implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizer
```

Recommended base class for synchronizer extension modules (`structure-synchronizer` module type in a plugin descriptor). Supplies JSON-map parameter storage, issue lookup helpers, descriptor access, and audit logging: subclasses implement `doSync` and `doResync`, returning a result whose actions are written to the `SyncAuditLog`. Instances are created by the plugin framework (one per module) and shared by all sync instances of that module, so they must be thread-safe and keep per-instance state in `SyncInstance.transientData`. Subclasses still implement `isAvailable`, `isAutosyncSupported`, the description and form methods.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.StructureComponents myStructureComponents` | The service bundle passed to the constructor, for subclass use. |
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.StructureManager myStructureManager` | The structure manager taken from the service bundle. |
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.row.RowManager myRowManager` | The row manager taken from the service bundle. |
| `protected final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncAuditLog myAuditLog` | The synchronizer audit log taken from the service bundle; used by `sync` and `resync` to record actions. |
| `protected AbstractSynchronizer(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.StructureComponents)` | Creates the synchronizer, taking the audit log, structure manager and row manager from the given service bundle (normally injected). |
| `public void init(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SynchronizerDescriptor)` | Stores the module descriptor returned later by `getDescriptor()`. Expected to be called once, before use, with this module's descriptor by the module-descriptor framework. Not determined: the plugin's own code never calls it; the call comes from the platform's module initialisation. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SynchronizerDescriptor getDescriptor()` | The descriptor set by `init`. Null if `init` was not called (despite the not-null contract). |
| `protected String getText(String, Object...)` | Localized text for the given i18n key (first argument) with message parameters (rest), resolved through the descriptor's i18n helper, which uses the current user's locale. Fails if `init` was not called. |
| `public void addDefaultFormParameters(java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Does nothing by default; override to put default values for a new instance's configuration form into the given map. |
| `public String storeParameters(Object) throws java.io.IOException` | Serializes the parameters to a JSON string. Null gives null. Parameters must be a `Map` (of JSON-compatible values); any other type throws `IOException`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSyncManager`

```java
public interface StructureSyncManager
```

Service (OSGi component) that manages synchronizer instances: installing a synchronizer module on a structure with parameters and an owner, enabling or disabling automatic (incremental) synchronization, requesting full resyncs, editing and uninstalling. Instances run in background jobs as their owner. Note: this service performs no permission checks of its own; callers (UI, REST) are responsible for checking that the user may manage synchronizers on the structure. Every state change is also written to the `SyncAuditLog`. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncInstance getInstalledSynchronizer(Long)` | The installed instance with the given ID, or null when the ID is null or no such instance exists. If the synchronizer module is currently not installed or enabled, an instance is still returned but its `getSynchronizer()` is null. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncInstance> getInstalledSynchronizersForStructure(Long)` | All instances installed on the given structure, or an empty list for a null ID or none. Order not specified (storage order). |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncInstance installSynchronizer(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizer, Long, Object, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizerException` | Installs a new instance of the synchronizer (first argument) on the structure (second) with the given parameters (third, stored via the synchronizer's `storeParameters`) and owner (fourth); runs will execute as that owner. The instance starts with autosync disabled. Returns the new instance. Throws `StructureSynchronizerException` when the synchronizer or user is null, the synchronizer is not available, the structure ID is null or not positive, the synchronizer is not a registered module, or the parameters cannot be stored. The structure's existence is not checked. |
| `public abstract long installSynchronizerOffline(String, String, Long, String, boolean) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizerException` | Installs an instance from stored data without loading the module (used for import/restore). Arguments: complete module key, already-serialized parameters, structure ID, owner user key, and whether autosync starts enabled. Returns the new instance ID. Throws `StructureSynchronizerException` when the structure ID is null or not positive, or the owner key is blank or not an existing user. A null or blank module key throws `IllegalArgumentException`; otherwise the module key is not checked (an unknown module is accepted). |
| `public abstract void uninstallSynchronizer(Long)` | Deletes the instance with the given ID (stopping its autosync). Null or unknown ID does nothing. |
| `public abstract void uninstallAllSynchronizers()` | Deletes every synchronizer instance on all structures. |
| `public abstract void uninstallSynchronizersForStructure(Long)` | Deletes all instances on the given structure. Null does nothing. |
| `public abstract boolean isAutosyncEnabled(Long)` | True when the instance exists and its automatic incremental synchronization is enabled. False for null. |
| `public abstract void setAutosyncEnabled(Long, boolean) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizerException` | Enables (second argument true) or disables automatic synchronization of the instance. Enabling makes the instance react to changes from that moment on. Null ID does nothing. Throws `StructureSynchronizerException` when the instance does not exist, its module is unavailable, the synchronizer reports it is not available, or it does not support autosync (also when disabling). |
| `public abstract void resync(Long, boolean, Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizerException` | Requests a full resynchronization of the instance (first argument); it is queued and runs asynchronously as the owner. Second argument: also enable autosync. Third: optional ID of a background process (see the process manager) whose status is updated by the run. Throws `StructureSynchronizerException` when the ID is null or unknown, the synchronizer is unavailable, enabling is requested but autosync is not supported, or the owner user no longer exists. |
| `public abstract void resyncOnce(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizer, Object, Long, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser, Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizerException` | Queues a one-time full synchronization without installing an instance. Arguments: synchronizer, parameters, structure ID, user to run as, optional process ID. During the run the instance ID is 0. Throws `StructureSynchronizerException` when the structure ID is null or not positive, the user is null, the synchronizer is unavailable or not registered, or parameters cannot be stored. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncInstance updateSynchronizer(Long, Object, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizerException` | Changes the parameters (second argument, null keeps them) and/or owner (third, null keeps it) of the instance (first) and returns the updated instance. Throws `StructureSynchronizerException` when the ID is null or unknown, autosync is currently enabled (disable it first), no synchronizer module is registered under the instance's module key (whether it is available is not checked), or parameters cannot be stored or restored. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.StructureSynchronizer`

```java
public interface StructureSynchronizer
```

Extension point for synchronizers, declared in a plugin descriptor as a `structure-synchronizer` module (with label, description, rules text and a `form` template). One object per module serves all instances, so implementations must be thread-safe. The plugin calls `sync` for incremental runs (when autosync is enabled and there are new events) and `resync` for full runs, on a background thread with the instance owner as current user and a `SyncLogger` installed. Most implementations extend `AbstractSynchronizer`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean isAvailable()` | Whether the synchronizer can currently be used (for example its required Jira feature is present). Unavailable synchronizers cannot be installed or run. |
| `public abstract boolean isAutosyncSupported()` | Whether the synchronizer supports incremental automatic synchronization (`sync`). If false only full resyncs are possible. |
| `public abstract String getConfigDescription(Object)` | Short human-readable summary of the given parameters, shown in the synchronizer list; null if none. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<String> getConfigDescriptionDetails(Object)` | Additional lines describing the given parameters; null if none. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<String> getPossibleResyncEffects(Object)` | Human-readable warnings about what a full resync with these parameters may change, shown before the user confirms; null or empty if none. |
| `public abstract String storeParameters(Object) throws java.io.IOException` | Serializes parameters to a string for storage (null allowed both ways). Throw `IOException` (or `ClassCastException`) when the object is not a valid parameters object. |
| `public abstract Object restoreParameters(String) throws java.io.IOException` | Recreates the parameters object from a stored string; null gives null. Throws `IOException` on bad data. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SynchronizerDescriptor getDescriptor()` | The module descriptor of this synchronizer (label, rules, i18n, complete module key, form rendering). |
| `public abstract Object buildParametersFromForm(java.util.Map<String, ?>, com.atlassian.jira.web.action.JiraWebActionSupport)` | Builds a parameters object from submitted form fields (first argument, field name to values). Report validation problems as errors on the web action (second argument) and return null when invalid. |
| `public abstract void addDefaultFormParameters(java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Puts the defaults for a new instance's form into the given map (template variables). |
| `public abstract void addFormParameters(Object, java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Puts template variables representing the given existing parameters (first argument, may be null) into the map (second) so the edit form shows them. |
| `public abstract void resync(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncInstance, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSource) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Performs a full synchronization for the instance (first argument) on the structure's forest source (second). Throw `StructureException` on failure; the plugin logs it and records the failure. |
| `public abstract void sync(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncInstance, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.IncrementalSyncData, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.ForestSource) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Performs an incremental synchronization for the instance (first) in response to the changes (second), using the forest source (third). Only called when autosync is supported and enabled. Throw `StructureException` on failure. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncAuditLog`

```java
public interface SyncAuditLog
```

Service (OSGi component) storing a log of what synchronizers did, grouped per run or per management action. Entries are queued in memory and written to the database in the background (about every 30 seconds), so a just-recorded group may not be visible to `getActions` immediately; if more than a million groups are pending the oldest are dropped. Groups without actions are normally not stored. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void recordActions(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncInstance, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.MapObject, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.MapObject>)` | Records a group for the given instance (its ID, module key and structure) with an optional description (second argument) and actions (third, null means none). Timestamp is the current time. |
| `public abstract void recordActions(long, String, long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.MapObject, java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.MapObject>)` | Records a group with explicit sync instance ID (0 if none), module key (empty if none), structure ID (0 if none), optional description and actions. |
| `public abstract boolean isActionGroupRecorded(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.MapObject>)` | Whether a group with these actions would be stored: true when the list is non-empty, or when storing of empty groups has been turned on by a system setting. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.SyncAuditLog.ActionGroup> getActions(long, long, long, long)` | Recorded groups matching all given filters, newest first. Arguments: sync instance ID (0 or less for any), structure ID (0 or less for any), earliest timestamp inclusive (`Long.MIN_VALUE` for none), latest timestamp inclusive (`Long.MAX_VALUE` for none). The number of stored records read is capped (10,000 by default, header and action records counted together, in no defined order), so long ranges may be truncated, the records dropped are not necessarily the oldest, and a group may come back with only part of its actions. With a structure filter (positive structure ID) the groups come back with empty action lists (as the original does). |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.util`

Helpers for writing synchronizers: a per-run logger with formatting helpers for issues, rows and forests, a parent lookup that accounts for pending moves, and a change-callback interface.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.util.HierarchyHelper`

```java
public class HierarchyHelper
```

Answers parent and ancestor questions about a forest while a synchronizer plans moves that have not been applied yet: recorded moves override the forest's real parents. Created by the caller over an indexed forest and its row index; not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public HierarchyHelper(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.LongListHashIndex, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.IndexedForest)` | Creates the helper from a row-ID-to-position index (first argument) and the indexed forest (second) it describes. |
| `public void recordMove(long, long)` | Records that the row (first argument) is to be placed under the new parent row (second). Later queries treat this as the row's parent. Not determined: behaviour when either row is not in the forest (the position becomes -1, which later makes the row appear top-level or fails). |
| `public long getParent(long)` | The parent row ID of the row, taking recorded moves into account; 0 for top level. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` when the row is not in the forest. |
| `public boolean isInSubtree(long, long)` | True when the row (first argument) is a proper descendant of the subtree root (second), taking recorded moves into account. False when the row is 0; true for any non-zero row when the root is 0. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` when either row is not in the forest. |

The prefix starts empty. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template`

Extension point for the "create structure" wizard: a template is a module (`new-structure-template` in a plugin descriptor) that contributes a sequence of form steps and then configures the newly created structure (name, permissions, initial content, automation).

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.EmptyTemplate`

```java
public class EmptyTemplate implements com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.NewStructureTemplate
```

The built-in template that creates an empty structure. It has no steps of its own: the wizard goes straight to the plugin's general final step (name, description, sharing) and the template adds nothing to the structure. Registered by the plugin as a template module; may also be subclassed.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public EmptyTemplate()` | Creates the template; it has no state. |
| `public boolean isEnabled()` | Always true. |
| `public String getInitialStep()` | Always `__end` (`NewStructureTemplateStep.END_STEP`), so the first page shown is the general final step. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.NewStructureTemplateStep createStep(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.NewStructureTemplateContext) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.StructureTemplateException` | Always throws `StructureTemplateException` with a localized "unknown step" message naming the (HTML-encoded) step, because this template defines no steps. |
| `public void configureNewStructure(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure, java.util.Map<String, Object>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.StructureTemplateException` | Does nothing. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.NewStructureTemplate`

```java
public interface NewStructureTemplate
```

Extension point for structure templates offered by the create-structure wizard. Declared as a `new-structure-template` module, with one velocity resource per step (resource name = step key) that renders the step's form fields. The wizard keeps all submitted values in a parameters map: for each step key, a map of that step's form field names to their submitted values (string arrays as received from the request), plus wizard-level keys starting with `__`. One object serves all users; implementations must be thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract boolean isEnabled()` | Whether the template is offered and usable now (for example only if a required Jira feature is installed). Exceptions are treated as false. |
| `public abstract String getInitialStep()` | Key of the first step to show. Return `NewStructureTemplateStep.END_STEP` to go straight to the general final step. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.NewStructureTemplateStep createStep(String, java.util.Map<String, Object>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.NewStructureTemplateContext) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.StructureTemplateException` | Returns the step object for the given step key (first argument), given the parameters collected so far (second) and the wizard context (third). Not called for `__end` unless `hasCustomFinalStep()` is true. Throw `StructureTemplateException` for an unknown key; its message is shown to the user as an error. |
| `public abstract void configureNewStructure(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure, java.util.Map<String, Object>) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template.StructureTemplateException` | Called when the user finishes the wizard, as that user. First argument: the new structure; unless the template has a custom final step it has already been saved with the name, description and permissions from the general step, otherwise it is unsaved and the template should set it up (the wizard saves it afterwards if its ID is still 0). Second argument: all collected parameters. Typical work: add generators or content. A `StructureTemplateException` aborts with its message shown to the user (a structure already saved stays created). |
| `public default String getCreateButtonTextKey()` | i18n key of the label of the final button. Default: the plugin's standard "finish" key. |
| `public default String prepareNewStructureUrl(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure)` | Relative URL to open after creation. Default: the structure board page for the new structure (`/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`). |
| `public default boolean shouldRedirectForNewStructure()` | Whether to always redirect to `prepareNewStructureUrl` after creation, even when the wizard was opened from the structure board (where it otherwise just reports the new structure's ID). Default false. |
| `public default boolean hasCustomFinalStep()` | Whether the template supplies its own `__end` step instead of the plugin's general step (name, description, sharing). Default false. If true, the template is responsible for naming the structure and setting permissions. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util`

General-purpose helpers shipped with the API and used throughout the plugin and by client plugins: small functional-programming primitives (`La`, `La2`, `La3`), value and ordering helpers (`ComparableTuple`, `TotalOrder`), JSON and map access (`MapObject`, `JsonMapUtil`, `SpecParams`), forest/row-tree indexing (`IndexedForest`, `RowTree`), null-safe numeric and type helpers, Jira component and user lookup shortcuts, and debug/logging helpers. Most classes are static utility holders or small mutable value objects with no thread-safety guarantees unless stated.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.CallableE`

```java
public interface CallableE<V, E extends Exception> extends java.util.concurrent.Callable<V>
```

A `java.util.concurrent.Callable` whose `call()` is declared to throw one specific checked exception type `E` instead of the general `Exception`. Clients implement it (usually as a lambda) to pass code that returns a value of type `V` and may fail with `E`, for example to `JiraComponents.withThreadContextClassLoaderOf`. It has no state of its own.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract V call() throws E` | Runs the computation and returns its result (may be null if the implementation chooses). May throw the declared checked exception type `E` or any unchecked exception. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple`

```java
public final class ComparableTuple implements Comparable<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple>
```

An immutable, totally ordered tuple of strings and numbers, used as a sort key (for example as a comparable attribute value). Instances are created only through the static `of(...)` factories; the constructor is private. Elements are compared position by position; numbers always sort before strings at the same position, and a shorter tuple that is a prefix of a longer one sorts first. Instances are immutable and safe to share between threads.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple NIL` | The empty tuple (zero elements). It sorts before every non-empty tuple, equals only other empty tuples, has hash code 0 and prints as `()`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(long)` | Returns a one-element tuple holding the given integer number. Never throws. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(double)` | Returns a one-element tuple holding the given floating-point number. `NaN` and infinities are accepted; see `compareTo` for how they order. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(String)` | Returns a one-element tuple holding the given string. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` (no message) if the string is null. The empty string is allowed. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(String, String)` | Returns a two-element tuple (a, b). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if either argument is null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(long, long)` | Returns a two-element tuple of the two integer numbers, in argument order. Never throws. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(String[])` | Returns a tuple whose elements are the strings of the array, in order. The array is copied, so later changes to it do not affect the tuple. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the array itself is null. Null elements inside the array are not rejected here, but such a tuple throws `NullPointerException` when hashed or compared with a number; printed, it shows `null`, and compared with a string it sorts first; callers must not pass null elements. An empty array yields an empty tuple equal to `NIL`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(Long[])` | Returns a tuple whose elements are the given `Long` values, in order; the array is copied. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the array is null. Null elements are not checked and will cause `NullPointerException` on comparison or hashing. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(String, long)` | Returns the two-element tuple (a, b) with a string first and a number second. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `a` is null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(String, long, String)` | Returns the three-element tuple (a, b, c). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `a` or `c` is null. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple of(java.util.List<?>)` | Builds a tuple from a list of mixed values, in list order. Each element must be a `String`, a `java.lang.Number` (any subclass) or another `ComparableTuple`; a nested tuple is flattened, that is, its elements are inserted in place rather than as a single element (so `of([of(1,2), "x"])` equals the tuple (1, 2, "x")). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the list is null, if any element is null, or if any element has another type. An empty list yields an empty tuple. |
| `public int compareTo(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ComparableTuple)` | Compares lexicographically. For each position up to the shorter length: two strings compare with `String.compareTo` (case-sensitive, UTF-16 code unit order); a string is greater than a number (returns 1 when this side holds the string, -1 when the other side does); two numbers are compared first by their `longValue()` (truncated toward zero) and, only if those are equal, by their `doubleValue()`. The first non-zero element result is returned, normalized to -1 or 1 for numbers (strings return the raw `String.compareTo` difference). If all shared positions are equal, the shorter tuple is smaller (-1/1), equal lengths give 0. Consequences: integer 1 and double 1.0 are equal; double 1.5 is greater than integer 1; `NaN` has long value 0, so against any number whose long value is 0 (including another NaN) the double step returns 1 in both directions; NaN is therefore not consistently ordered and should not be used. Throws `NullPointerException` if `other` is null. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True if the other object is also a `ComparableTuple` (exact class) and `compareTo` returns 0. So a tuple holding integer 2 equals a tuple holding double 2.0. |
| `public int hashCode()` | Start with 0; for each element in order, multiply the running value by 31 and add the element's hash: for a string its `String.hashCode()`, for a number the `java.lang.Double.hashCode()` of its `doubleValue()`. Integer overflow wraps silently. This keeps equal tuples (e.g. 2 and 2.0) with equal hash codes. |
| `public String toString()` | Returns the elements in parentheses separated by commas with no spaces; strings are wrapped in single quotes (no escaping), numbers use their own `toString()`. Examples: `()` for `NIL`, `('abc',5)` for of("abc", 5), `(1.5)` for of(1.5). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ConsiderateLogger`

```java
public class ConsiderateLogger
```

A wrapper over an SLF4J `org.slf4j.Logger` that rate-limits repeated messages per caller-chosen source key, so a recurring problem does not flood the log. For each source key, the first message is written; further messages for that key arriving within the configured interval after the last written one are dropped and counted; the next message after the interval has passed is written, preceded by a summary line saying how many were dropped. Created directly by clients with `new`. Safe for concurrent use (state is kept in a concurrent map with atomic counters; under a race two first messages for a new key may both pass).

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ConsiderateLogger(org.slf4j.Logger)` | Creates a throttling logger writing to the given logger, with the default interval of 5 minutes. The logger must not be null (not checked; a null logger fails with `NullPointerException` when the first message is written). |
| `public ConsiderateLogger(org.slf4j.Logger, long)` | Creates a throttling logger with an explicit suppression interval, given in nanoseconds (as measured by `System.nanoTime()`). An interval of 0 or less effectively disables suppression only for messages that arrive at a different nanosecond timestamp; normal values are positive. |
| `public void info(String, String)` | Logs `source + " " + message` at INFO level, unless an earlier message for the same source key was written less than or exactly one interval ago, in which case the message is dropped and counted. When a message for this key is written after drops, a summary line is first written of the form `<count> info log entries from <source> were not shown` (at INFO) or `<count> warnings from <source> were not shown` (at WARN); the level and wording of the summary are fixed by whichever method (info or warn) was first called for that source key, and both methods share one throttle per key. The source must not be null (`NullPointerException`). The INFO-enabled state of the logger is not consulted before throttling. |
| `public void info(String, String, Throwable)` | Same as `info(String, String)` but passes the throwable to the underlying logger so its stack trace is logged with the message. Throttling and summary behaviour are identical. |
| `public void warn(String, String)` | Same as `info(String, String)` but writes the message at WARN level. Shares the throttle of the same source key with `info`. |
| `public void warn(String, String, Throwable)` | Same as `warn(String, String)` with the throwable attached to the logged message. |
| `public void reset()` | Forgets the throttling state of all source keys: the next message for any key is written immediately, and any counts of dropped messages are discarded without a summary line. |
| `public void setInterval(long)` | Changes the suppression interval, in nanoseconds, for all source keys; takes effect for the next message. No validation. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18nText`

```java
public class I18nText
```

A serializable reference to a localizable message: an i18n key plus format arguments, to be resolved into text later in the viewer's locale (for example with `StructureUtil.getTextInCurrentUserLocale(I18nText)`). It is a mutable Java bean, JSON-serializable with Jackson using the properties `i18nKey` and `arguments`. Created directly by clients; not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public I18nText(String, Object...)` | Creates a message reference with the given key (null allowed but not useful) and arguments. Each argument is normalized when stored: null stays null, any `java.lang.Number` is kept as is, and every other object is replaced by its `toString()` result; the stored array is a new array. The varargs array itself must not be null (passing a null array throws `NullPointerException`); calling with no arguments gives an empty array. This is also the Jackson creator, binding JSON properties `i18nKey` and `arguments`. |
| `public I18nText()` | Creates an empty instance with null key and null arguments, intended for bean-style frameworks; fill it with the setters. |
| `public String getI18nKey()` | Returns the i18n key of the message, possibly null. |
| `public void setI18nKey(String)` | Replaces the i18n key. No validation. |
| `public Object[] getArguments()` | Returns the stored arguments array itself (not a copy); it may be null for an instance built with the no-argument constructor. Elements are strings, numbers or null when set through the main constructor; `setArguments` may have stored anything. |
| `public void setArguments(Object[])` | Replaces the arguments array with the given array as is (no copying and no string normalization, unlike the constructor). Null is allowed. |
| `public boolean equals(Object)` | True if the other object has exactly the same runtime class, an equal key (null equals null) and arguments arrays that are equal element by element (nested arrays compared deeply, null arrays equal only to null). |
| `public int hashCode()` | Computed in the style of Apache Commons Lang `HashCodeBuilder` with its defaults (initial 17, multiplier 37): start from 17, fold in the key's hash (0 if null), then fold in each argument's hash in order (0 for null elements; nested arrays element-wise); a null arguments array contributes a single 0 step. Consistent with `equals`. |
| `public String toString()` | If the arguments array is null or empty, returns the key alone (which can be null). Otherwise returns the key immediately followed, without any separator, by the arguments joined with commas, where null arguments become empty text; e.g. key `a.b` with arguments `x`, `1` gives `a.bx,1`. This is a debugging form, not the localized text. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.IndexedForest`

```java
public class IndexedForest
```

A read-only navigation index over a `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest`, answering parent, children, sibling and subtree-end questions by row index in amortized constant time. Clients create it with `new IndexedForest(forest)`. Indexes are computed lazily on first use and cached, so the wrapped forest must not change while the index is in use (changes are not detected). Not thread-safe: even read-only queries mutate internal caches. Row positions are zero-based indices into the forest; -1 is used both as the virtual parent of top-level rows and as the 'none' result.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public IndexedForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Wraps the given forest (not copied). Reads its size immediately, so a null forest throws `NullPointerException`. No other work is done until queries are made. |
| `public int subtreeEnd(int)` | Returns the index just past the last descendant of the row at `idx`, i.e. the index of the next row whose depth is less than or equal to that row's depth, or `size()` if there is none. For a leaf this is `idx + 1`. Any negative `idx` returns `size()` (the whole forest). An `idx` at or beyond `size()` fails with an index exception from the internal list. |
| `public int parent(int)` | Returns the index of the parent of the row at `idx`, or -1 if that row is top-level (depth 0) or `idx` is negative. An index beyond the forest size fails with the forest's own index exception. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.IntIterator children(int)` | Returns an iterator over the indices of the direct children of the row at `idx`, in forest order. `idx` = -1 iterates the top-level rows. For any other out-of-range index or a row without children, returns an empty iterator. The iterator is lazy and computes siblings as it goes. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.IntIterator roots()` | Returns an iterator over the indices of all top-level (depth 0) rows, in order; same as `children(-1)`. Empty for an empty forest. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongList childrenRows(int)` | Returns the row IDs (not indices) of the direct children of the row at `idx` (-1 for top-level rows), in order, as a new `LongList`. Returns the shared empty `LongList.EMPTY` when there are no children or the index is out of range. |
| `public int firstChild(int)` | Returns the index of the first child of the row at `idx`, which is always `idx + 1` when that row is exactly one level deeper; otherwise -1. For `idx` = -1 returns 0 if the forest is non-empty, else -1. Any other out-of-range index returns -1. |
| `public int nextSibling(int)` | Returns the index of the next row with the same parent as the row at `idx` (that is, `subtreeEnd(idx)` if that position exists and has the same depth), or -1 if it is the last child or `idx` is out of range (negative or at least `size()`). |
| `public int depth(int)` | Returns the depth of the row at `idx` (0 for top-level rows), straight from the forest. Out-of-range indices fail as the forest's accessor does. |
| `public long row(int)` | Returns the row ID at position `idx`, straight from the forest. Out-of-range indices fail as the forest's accessor does. |
| `public com.almworks.integers.LongIterator rows(com.almworks.integers.IntIterator)` | Returns a lazy iterator that maps each index produced by the given index iterator to the row ID at that position. The source iterator is consumed as the result is iterated. |
| `public int size()` | Returns the number of rows in the wrapped forest. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest getForest()` | Returns the forest this index was created for (the same instance). |
| `public int root(int)` | Returns the index of the top-level ancestor of the row at `idx` (the row itself if it is top-level). A negative `idx` is returned unchanged. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.IndexedRowTree`

```java
public class IndexedRowTree extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree
```

A `RowTree` that additionally keeps a lookup table from row ID to node, so nodes can be found by row ID in constant time. Row IDs must be unique within the tree. Created by clients with a constructor or with `create(Forest)`. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public IndexedRowTree(int)` | Creates an empty tree whose lookup table is pre-sized for about `size` rows (a capacity hint only). A negative size throws `IllegalArgumentException` from the underlying hash map. |
| `public IndexedRowTree()` | Creates an empty tree with a default capacity hint of 16. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.IndexedRowTree create(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Creates a new indexed tree and appends the whole forest under its super-root, preserving order and nesting. All row IDs in the forest are expected to be distinct. |
| `protected com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node createNode(long, int)` | Overrides the node factory: creates the node as the base class does and registers it in the row-ID lookup. A duplicate row ID is a broken invariant: with Java assertions enabled it raises `AssertionError`; otherwise the new node silently replaces the old one in the lookup. |
| `protected void forgetNode(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node)` | Overrides the removal hook: unregisters the node and, recursively, all of its descendants from the row-ID lookup. Called by `remove`. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node getNodeWithRowId(long)` | Returns the node for the given row ID. Row ID 0 returns the super-root. Returns null if no node with that ID is currently in the tree. |
| `public boolean hasRow(long)` | True if a node with this row ID is currently registered. The super-root (ID 0) is not registered, so `hasRow(0)` is false. |

A read-only `com.almworks.integers.LongList` view of a Java `java.util.List`, where each element is converted to a `long` by a given function on every access. Nothing is copied or cached, so changes to the source list are visible through the view. Created by clients with the constructor. Thread safety is that of the source list.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public JavaListToLongListAdapter(java.util.List<T>, java.util.function.ToLongFunction<T>)` | Creates the view over `source`, converting elements with `f`. Neither argument is checked; nulls fail later on use. |
| `public int size()` | Returns the current size of the source list. |
| `public long get(int) throws java.util.NoSuchElementException` | Returns `f` applied to the source element at `index`. An out-of-range index throws whatever the source list throws (typically `IndexOutOfBoundsException`); exceptions from `f` propagate. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.JiraComponents`

```java
public class JiraComponents implements org.springframework.beans.factory.DisposableBean, org.springframework.beans.factory.InitializingBean, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.lifecycle.CachingComponent
```

Static shortcuts for obtaining Jira platform services from inside a plugin, plus a helper to run code under a given thread context class loader. Every returned service is wrapped in a dynamic proxy implementing the requested interface which, for the duration of each call, switches the calling thread's context class loader to the class loader of the real service object and restores it afterwards; exceptions thrown by the service are rethrown unwrapped. Proxies for the named getters and for `getComponent`/`getComponentOfType` are cached per interface class in a static concurrent map until the cache is cleared. The class is also registered in the plugin as a component (Spring lifecycle and the API's caching-component contract) only so that the proxy cache is cleared on plugin start, stop and global cache resets. All static methods are safe to call from any thread.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public JiraComponents()` | Public constructor used by the plugin's component container; clients have no reason to create instances, all useful methods are static. |
| `public static <T> T getOSGiComponentInstanceOfType(Class<T>)` | Looks up an OSGi service implementing the given interface (through Jira's component accessor) and returns it wrapped in a class-loader-switching proxy, or null if no such service is available. The interface class must be an interface (checked only by a Java assertion). Unlike the other getters, this result is not cached: every call creates a new proxy around the currently registered service. |
| `public static <T> T getComponentOfType(Class<T>)` | Looks up a Jira component by interface type (Jira's `getComponentOfType`) and returns it wrapped in a class-loader-switching proxy, or null if not found. The proxy is cached per interface: later calls return the same proxy (wrapping the service found the first time) until the cache is cleared. Note that this cache is shared with `getComponent` and the named getters for the same interface. |
| `public static <T> T getComponent(Class<T>)` | Looks up a Jira component by interface (Jira's `getComponent`) and returns it as a cached class-loader-switching proxy, or null if not available. Same caching as `getComponentOfType`. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.security.JiraAuthenticationContext getJiraAuthenticationContext()` | Returns Jira's `JiraAuthenticationContext` (current user, locale, i18n helper), as a cached class-loader-switching proxy; null if Jira cannot provide it. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.project.ProjectManager getProjectManager()` | Returns Jira's `ProjectManager` as a cached class-loader-switching proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.bc.project.component.ProjectComponentManager getProjectComponentManager()` | Returns Jira's `ProjectComponentManager` (project components) as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.config.ConstantsManager getConstantsManager()` | Returns Jira's `ConstantsManager` (issue types, statuses, priorities, resolutions) as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.project.version.VersionManager getVersionManager()` | Returns Jira's `VersionManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.issue.customfields.manager.OptionsManager getOptionsManager()` | Returns Jira's `OptionsManager` (custom field options) as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.user.util.UserManager getUserManager()` | Returns Jira's `UserManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.security.groups.GroupManager getGroupManager()` | Returns Jira's `GroupManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.user.util.UserUtil getUserUtil()` | Returns Jira's `UserUtil` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.plugin.PluginAccessor getPluginAccessor()` | Returns the Atlassian plugin system's `PluginAccessor` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.security.PermissionManager getPermissionManager()` | Returns Jira's `PermissionManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.config.properties.ApplicationProperties getApplicationProperties()` | Returns Jira's `ApplicationProperties` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.issue.IssueManager getIssueManager()` | Returns Jira's `IssueManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.avatar.AvatarManager getAvatarManager()` | Returns Jira's `AvatarManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.plugin.ComponentClassManager getComponentClassManager()` | Returns Jira's `ComponentClassManager` (loads classes from plugins) as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.security.GlobalPermissionManager getGlobalPermissionManager()` | Returns Jira's `GlobalPermissionManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable. |
| `public final void afterPropertiesSet() throws Exception` | Spring initialization callback: clears the static proxy cache. Final. |
| `public final void destroy() throws Exception` | Spring shutdown callback: clears the static proxy cache. Final. |
| `public void clearCaches()` | Clears the static proxy cache, so the next lookups wrap freshly obtained services. Called by the plugin when caches are reset. |
| `public void clearUserCaches(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Does nothing; there is no per-user state. |
| `public static <T, E extends Exception> T withThreadContextClassLoaderOf(Object, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.CallableE<T, E>) throws E` | Runs `code` with the current thread's context class loader set to the class loader of `object` (if `object` is itself a `Class`, that class's loader; otherwise the loader of the object's runtime class; a bootstrap class gives a null loader), and returns the code's result. The previous context class loader is always restored, also when the code throws; the code's exception (of type `E` or unchecked) propagates unchanged. A null `object` throws `NullPointerException` before anything runs. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.JiraUsers`

```java
public class JiraUsers
```

Static helpers that call Jira's `ApplicationUsers` conversion utilities between user keys, Crowd directory users (`com.atlassian.crowd.embedded.api.User`) and `ApplicationUser`. Several of them temporarily set the thread context class loader to the one that loaded Jira's user classes, which is required when called from plugin code. Thread-safe and stateless.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public JiraUsers()` | Public constructor; the class has only static methods and no state. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser byKey(String)` | Returns the `ApplicationUser` for the given user key, as Jira resolves it, or null if the key is null (or Jira finds no such user). Runs the lookup with the context class loader switched to Jira's and restored afterwards. |
| `public static com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser from(com.atlassian.crowd.embedded.api.User)` | Converts a Crowd directory user to the corresponding `ApplicationUser` using Jira's conversion; null input gives null. Switches the context class loader during the call. |
| `public static String getKeyFor(com.atlassian.crowd.embedded.api.User)` | Returns the Jira user key for a Crowd directory user; null input gives null. Switches the context class loader during the call. |
| `public static String getKeyFor(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Returns the user key of the given `ApplicationUser`; null input gives null (as Jira's utility does). |
| `public static com.atlassian.crowd.embedded.api.User toDirectoryUser(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Returns the underlying Crowd directory user of an `ApplicationUser`; null input gives null. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.JsonMapUtil`

```java
public class JsonMapUtil
```

Static helpers for validating and deep-copying JSON-compatible parameter maps, such as the parameter maps stored in specs of generators, attributes and views. A JSON-compatible value is a `String`, `Integer`, `Long`, `Double`, `Boolean`, a `java.util.List` of such values, a `java.util.Map` with `String` keys and such values, or an `org.json` `JSONArray`/`JSONObject`, which are converted to plain lists and maps on copy. Stateless and thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public JsonMapUtil()` | Public constructor; the class has only static methods. |
| `public static java.util.Map<String, Object> copyParameters(java.util.Map<?, ?>, boolean, boolean, boolean)` | Deep-copies a parameter map. If `parameters` is null or empty: returns null when `allowNull` is true; otherwise returns an immutable empty map when `makeImmutable` is true, or a new mutable empty map when not. Otherwise returns the same as `mergeParameters(makeImmutable, verify, parameters)`. With `allowNull` false the result is never null. |
| `public static java.util.Map<String, Object> mergeParameters(boolean, boolean, java.util.Map<?, ?>...)` | Merges the given maps, in argument order, into one new insertion-ordered map: entries of later maps replace values of earlier ones for equal keys (the key keeps its original position). Null maps (and a null varargs array) are skipped. Each value is deep-copied with `copyParameter(value, makeImmutable)`. If `verify` is true, every key must be a non-null `String` (otherwise `IllegalArgumentException` with message `null key` or `non-string key: <key>`) and every value must pass `checkValidParameter`. If `makeImmutable` is true the result and all nested lists and maps are unmodifiable views; otherwise all are mutable. Never returns null. Without verification, non-string keys would be cast and fail with `ClassCastException`. |
| `public static Object copyParameter(Object, boolean)` | Deep-copies one value: `JSONArray`/`JSONObject` values are first converted with `jsonToList`/`jsonToMap`; lists become new `java.util.ArrayList`s with each element copied recursively; maps become new insertion-ordered maps whose keys are converted with `String.valueOf` and values copied recursively; any other value (including null) is returned as is. With `makeImmutable`, the new lists and maps are wrapped as unmodifiable. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if JSON conversion fails. No cycle detection (a self-containing structure overflows the stack). |
| `public static void checkValidParameter(Object) throws IllegalArgumentException` | Checks that a value is JSON-compatible, recursively, and returns normally if so. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` when: the value (or any nested element) is null (`null value`); it has another type (`invalid value type: <class name>`); a nested map has a non-`String` key (`invalid map: non-string key <key>`). Errors inside containers are wrapped with context, `invalid list: invalid value at index <i>: <inner message>` or `invalid map: invalid value for key <key>: <inner message>`, with the inner exception as cause. `JSONArray`/`JSONObject` are converted and checked (so JSON nulls inside them are rejected). Excessive nesting or a cyclic structure gives `IllegalArgumentException` with message `stack overflow`. Note that `Float`, `Short`, `BigDecimal` and similar numeric types are rejected. |
| `public static Object unwrapJsonCollection(Object)` | Converts a `JSONArray` with `jsonToList` or a `JSONObject` with `jsonToMap`; any other value (including null) is returned unchanged. A JSON parsing error is reported as `IllegalArgumentException` with message `failed to convert json object: <reason>`. |
| `public static java.util.List<Object> jsonToList(org.json.JSONArray) throws org.json.JSONException` | Marked internal. Converts a `JSONArray` to a new `java.util.ArrayList`, recursively converting nested arrays and objects; JSON null elements become Java null; other elements are kept as `org.json` returns them. Throws `org.json.JSONException` on access errors and `NullPointerException` for a null argument. |
| `public static java.util.Map<String, Object> jsonToMap(org.json.JSONObject) throws org.json.JSONException` | Marked internal. Converts a `JSONObject` to a new `java.util.HashMap` (key order is not preserved), recursively converting nested objects and arrays; JSON null values become Java null. Throws `org.json.JSONException` on access errors and `NullPointerException` for a null argument. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La`

```java
public abstract class La<T, R> implements java.util.function.Function<T, R>, java.util.function.Predicate<T>
```

An abstract one-argument function (`T` to `R`) that also acts as a predicate, with many helpers to map, filter, collect and compare collections. It implements both `java.util.function.Function` and `java.util.function.Predicate`. Clients subclass it (usually anonymously) implementing `la`, or use the static factories. As a predicate, a result is 'truthy' when it is non-null and not equal to `Boolean.FALSE`, `Integer` 0 or `Long` 0 (so `Double` 0.0, `Short` 0 and empty strings count as true). A `La` may optionally declare its result class, needed only by `array`. Thread safety depends on the implementation; the shared constants are stateless. Helpers that build collections never modify their input.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected La()` | Protected constructor for subclasses that do not declare a result class (`array` will then fail). |
| `protected La(Class<R>)` | Protected constructor for subclasses that declare the class of their results, which `array` uses to create correctly typed arrays. Null is allowed and means 'no result class'. |
| `public abstract R la(T)` | The function itself, implemented by subclasses: computes the result for the argument. Whether null arguments or results are allowed is up to the implementation. |
| `public static <T, R> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<T, R> adapt(java.util.function.Function<T, R>)` | Wraps a standard `java.util.function.Function` as a `La` that calls it. The result has no result class. Throws `NullPointerException` if `f` is null. |
| `public static <T, R> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<T, R> constant(R)` | Returns a function that ignores its argument and always returns `result`. For the canonical `Boolean.TRUE`/`Boolean.FALSE` instances it returns the shared constants of `constantTrue()`/`constantFalse()`; otherwise a new function without result class. Null is allowed (the function always returns null). |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<T, Boolean> constantFalse()` | Returns the shared function that always returns `Boolean.FALSE` (rejects everything as a predicate). |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<T, Boolean> constantTrue()` | Returns the shared function that always returns `Boolean.TRUE` (accepts everything). |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<T, Boolean> isEqual(T)` | Returns a predicate that is `TRUE` for arguments equal to `value` (using `value.equals(argument)`); if `value` is null, it is `TRUE` exactly for null arguments. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<T, Boolean> inCollection(java.util.Collection<T>)` | Returns a predicate that is `TRUE` when the collection contains the argument (`Collection.contains`, live: later changes to the collection are seen). A null collection gives the constant-false function. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<T, Boolean> instanceOf(Class<? extends T>)` | Returns a predicate that is `TRUE` when the argument is a non-null instance of the class. A null class gives the constant-false function. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<Object, T> cast(Class<T>)` | Returns a function that returns the argument cast to the class if it is an instance of it, and null otherwise (including for null). A null class gives a function that always returns null. |
| `public static <A, B, C> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<A, C> compose(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<B, C>, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<A, ? extends B>)` | Returns the composition g after f: the result for x is `g.la(f.la(x))`. Null results of `f` are passed to `g` as is. The composed function takes the result class of `g`. Throws `NullPointerException` if either argument is null. |
| `public static <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<T, T> self()` | Returns the shared identity function (returns its argument). As a predicate it accepts truthy values. No result class. |
| `public static <T, R> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<T, R> fromMap(java.util.Map<? super T, ? extends R>, Class<R>)` | Returns a function that looks the argument up in the map (`map.get`, live view) and returns the value, or null if absent. `rClass` becomes the declared result class (may be null). Throws `NullPointerException` if the map is null. |
| `public final R apply(T)` | Implementation of `java.util.function.Function`: same as `la(from)`. Final. |
| `public boolean test(T)` | Implementation of `java.util.function.Predicate`: same as `accepts(input)`, i.e. whether the result is truthy. |

If `acceptFalsy` is false, results that are not truthy (null, `FALSE`, integer or long zero) are left out. Null input gives a new empty list. |
| `public java.util.List<R> arrayList(java.util.Iterator<? extends T>)` | Same as `arrayList(from, true)` for an iterator: consumes it and returns all results in a new list. Null gives a new empty list. |
| `public java.util.List<R> arrayList(java.util.Iterator<? extends T>, boolean)` | Consumes the iterator and returns a new list of the results, leaving out non-truthy results when `acceptFalsy` is false. Null gives a new empty list. |

| `public <D extends T> Iterable<R> transformIterable(Iterable<D>)` | Returns a lazy `Iterable` whose iterators map a fresh iterator of the source through this function. A null source fails with `NullPointerException` when iterated. |

| `public R[] array(java.util.Collection<? extends T>, boolean)` | Returns a new array whose component type is this function's declared result class, holding the results for the elements in iteration order; when `acceptFalsy` is false non-truthy results are dropped and the array is shortened to fit.
