### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La.ComparableComparator`

```java
public static class La.ComparableComparator<B extends Comparable<B>> implements java.util.Comparator<B>
```

A `java.util.Comparator` for `Comparable` values using their natural order, with null treated as smaller than any non-null value. Stateless; create with `new`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public ComparableComparator()` | Creates the comparator. |
| `public int compare(B, B)` | Returns 0 if both are null, -1 if only the first is null, 1 if only the second is null, otherwise `b1.compareTo(b2)`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La.FilterIterator`

```java
public class La.FilterIterator<D extends T> implements java.util.Iterator<D>
```

A lazy iterator that returns only those elements of an underlying iterator that the enclosing `La` accepts (truthy result). It is an inner class bound to its `La` instance (create with `la.new FilterIterator(it)` or via `La.filter(Iterator)`). It reads ahead one element: `hasNext()` advances the underlying iterator until it finds an accepted element. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public FilterIterator(java.util.Iterator<D>)` | Creates a filtering iterator over the given iterator for the enclosing `La` (the first, implicit parameter). Nothing is read until `hasNext()` or `next()` is called. |
| `public boolean hasNext()` | Returns whether another accepted element exists, consuming underlying elements (and evaluating the function) up to and including that element. Repeated calls without `next()` do not advance further. |
| `public D next()` | Returns the next accepted element. Throws `java.util.NoSuchElementException` if there is none. |
| `public void remove()` | Not supported; always throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La.LaComparator`

```java
public static class La.LaComparator<A, B> implements java.util.Comparator<A>
```

A `java.util.Comparator` that compares two objects by first mapping each through a `La` function and then comparing the results with another comparator. The function is evaluated on every comparison (no caching). Immutable; thread safety follows the function and comparator.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public LaComparator(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<A, B>, java.util.Comparator<? super B>)` | Creates the comparator. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `function is null` or `comparator is null` when the respective argument is null. |
| `public int compare(A, A)` | Applies the function to both arguments and returns the comparator's result for the two images. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La.TransformIterator`

```java
public class La.TransformIterator<D extends T> implements java.util.Iterator<R>
```

A lazy iterator that returns the enclosing `La`'s result for each element of an underlying iterator. Inner class bound to its `La` instance (created by `La.transform` or `la.new TransformIterator(it)`). Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public TransformIterator(java.util.Iterator<D>)` | Creates the mapping iterator for the enclosing `La` (the implicit first parameter) over the given iterator, which is not checked for null. |
| `public boolean hasNext()` | Returns whether the underlying iterator has more elements. |
| `public R next()` | Takes the next underlying element and returns the function's result for it (which may be null). Throws whatever the underlying iterator throws when exhausted. |
| `public void remove()` | Removes the last element from the underlying iterator, if it supports removal. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La2`

An abstract two-argument function, the binary counterpart of `La`, also implementing `java.util.function.BiFunction`. Clients subclass it implementing `la(A1, A2)` or use the static helpers for currying and constant functions. Thread safety depends on the implementation.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La2<Integer, Integer, Integer> sum` | A shared function adding two `Integer`s with `int` arithmetic (overflow wraps). Null arguments throw `NullPointerException`. |

| `public abstract R la(A1, A2)` | The function itself, implemented by subclasses: computes the result for the two arguments. |
| `public R apply(A1, A2)` | Implementation of `java.util.function.BiFunction`; same as `la(a1, a2)`. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<A2, R> la(A1)` | Partial application: returns a one-argument `La` that, given `a2`, returns `la(a1, a2)` with the first argument fixed to `a1`. The returned function has no result class. |
| `public static <A1, A2, R> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La2<A1, A2, R> uncurry(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<A1, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<A2, R>>)` | Turns a curried function (one that, given the first argument, returns a function of the second) into a two-argument function: `la(a1, a2)` computes `curried.la(a1)` and applies it to `a2`; if that intermediate function is null, the result is null. |
| `public static <R> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La2.Const<R> const2(R)` | Returns a holder that produces two-argument functions always returning `ret` (call `f()` on it). The holder exists only so that the argument types can be inferred at the use site. |
| `public static <A2, R> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La2.Binder2<A2, R> bind2(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La<A2, R>)` | Returns a holder that produces two-argument functions which ignore their first argument and apply `f` to their second (call `create()` on it). |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Limits`

```java

```

Constants for the maximum lengths, in characters, of string identifiers and names the plugin stores, all equal to 190. For example, the canonical version name used in item identities (`com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.CoreIdentities.canonicalVersionName`) is cut to this length. Not determined: the exact use sites of each constant, because compile-time constants are inlined in the compiled plugin; the meanings below follow the constant names. Not instantiable.

| member | meaning |

Otherwise, if `t` is non-null, logs at WARN the text `message`, a space, then `getMessageWithCauseChain(t)`, without a stack trace; if `t` is null, logs just `message`. It is backed by a `JSONObject` that is either the one passed in (shared, not copied) or built from a Java map. Typed getters follow the coercion rules of the `org.json` library's `opt...` methods. Subclassed by `SpecParams`. Not thread-safe; the lazily built map view is cached.

| `protected final org.json.JSONObject myObject` | Protected: the backing JSON object; never null. |
| `protected java.util.Map<String, Object> myMapView` | Protected: cache of the immutable map view built by `asImmutableMap`; null until first requested. |
| `public MapObject(org.json.JSONObject)` | Wraps the given JSON object without copying it (later changes to it are visible through the getters). Null is treated as a new empty object. |
| `public MapObject(java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Creates a new backing JSON object from the map's entries, using `org.json`'s map constructor. Not determined: handling of a null map and whether nested maps and collections are converted eagerly depends on the `org.json` version provided by the host. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.MapObject from(Object)` | Returns a `MapObject` for a `JSONObject` (wrapped, shared) or a `java.util.Map` (converted), and null for anything else, including null. |
| `public static <T> java.util.List<T> transform(org.json.JSONArray, java.util.function.BiFunction<org.json.JSONArray, Integer, T>)` | Applies `extractor(array, index)` to every index of the array in order and returns a new list of the non-null results. A null or empty array gives an immutable empty list. |
| `public boolean isEmpty()` | True if the object has no keys. |
| `public boolean has(String)` | True if the key is present (even if its value is JSON null). |

| `public Iterable<String> keys()` | Returns an `Iterable` over the keys of the object; each iteration reads the current keys of the backing object. Order is the backing object's (not guaranteed). |
| `public Object get(String)` | Returns the raw value under the key, or null if absent. A JSON null may be returned as the `org.json` null sentinel object rather than Java null. |
| `public String getString(String)` | Returns the value under the key as a string, or null if absent or JSON null. Non-string values are converted with their `toString()` (so a number 5 gives `5`). |
| `public long getLong(String)` | Returns the value as a `long`, or 0 if absent or not convertible. Numbers are converted with `longValue()`; numeric strings are parsed per `org.json`'s `optLong`. |
| `public long getLong(String, long)` | Like `getLong(String)` but returns `defaultValue` when the key is absent or the value is not convertible. |
| `public int getInt(String)` | Returns the value as an `int` (numbers narrowed with `intValue()`, numeric strings parsed per `org.json`'s `optInt`), or 0 if absent or not convertible. |
| `public int getInt(String, int)` | Like `getInt(String)` but returns `defaultValue` when absent or not convertible. |
| `public boolean getBoolean(String)` | Returns true if the value is `Boolean.TRUE` or the string `true` (any letter case); false otherwise, including when absent. |
| `public boolean getBoolean(String, boolean)` | Returns the boolean value (a `Boolean`, or the string `true`/`false` in any letter case), or `defaultValue` if absent or not convertible. |

A Java collection value is treated like an array. If the key is null, absent, not an array, or the array is empty, returns an immutable empty list; otherwise a new mutable list (possibly empty). |
| `public java.util.List<Integer> getIntList(String)` | Like `getLongList` but converts numeric elements with `intValue()` (narrowing, may overflow). |
| `public java.util.List<String> getStringList(String)` | Returns the elements of the array under the key converted to strings with `toString()` (numbers included), in order, skipping missing elements. Not determined: whether JSON null elements are skipped or yield the text `null` depends on the host's `org.json` version. Empty-list rules as in `getLongList`. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.NumericFunctions`

```java
public final class NumericFunctions
```

Null-tolerant static helpers for converting and combining `java.lang.Number` values, mainly used when aggregating attribute values. Thread-safe and stateless. Conversions use `Number.longValue()`/`doubleValue()`, so fractional values are truncated toward zero and out-of-range values follow Java's narrowing rules.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public NumericFunctions()` | Public constructor; the class has only static methods. |
| `public static long longOrZero(Number)` | Returns the number's `longValue()`, or 0 if it is null. |
| `public static <T> long longOrZero(T, java.util.function.Function<? super T, ? extends Number>)` | Applies `function` to `argument` and returns `longOrZero` of the result. Returns 0 without calling anything if `argument` or `function` is null. |
| `public static Long longOrNull(Number)` | Returns the number as a `Long`: the same object if it already is a `Long`, otherwise a boxed `longValue()`; null for null. |
| `public static <T> Long longOrNull(T, java.util.function.Function<? super T, ? extends Number>)` | Applies `function` to `argument` and returns `longOrNull` of the result; null if `argument` or `function` is null. |
| `public static long nonNegativeLong(Number)` | Returns `longOrZero(number)`, or 0 if that is negative. |
| `public static <T> long nonNegativeLong(T, java.util.function.Function<? super T, ? extends Number>)` | Returns `longOrZero(argument, function)`, or 0 if that is negative. |
| `public static double doubleOrZero(Number)` | Returns the number's `doubleValue()`, or 0.0 if it is null. |
| `public static <T> double doubleOrZero(T, java.util.function.Function<? super T, ? extends Number>)` | Applies `function` to `argument` and returns `doubleOrZero` of the result; 0.0 if `argument` or `function` is null. |
| `public static Double doubleOrNull(Number)` | Returns the number as a `Double`: the same object if it already is a `Double`, otherwise a boxed `doubleValue()`; null for null. |
| `public static <T> Double doubleOrNull(T, java.util.function.Function<? super T, ? extends Number>)` | Applies `function` to `argument` and returns `doubleOrNull` of the result; null if `argument` or `function` is null. |
| `public static double nonNegativeDouble(Number)` | Returns the larger of 0.0 and `doubleOrZero(number)` (per `Math.max`, so negative values and -0.0 give 0.0, while NaN stays NaN). |
| `public static <T> double nonNegativeDouble(T, java.util.function.Function<? super T, ? extends Number>)` | Returns the larger of 0.0 and `doubleOrZero(argument, function)` per `Math.max`. |
| `public static Double nonNegativeDoubleAddOrNull(Number, Number)` | Returns null if both arguments are null; otherwise the sum of `nonNegativeDouble(a)` and `nonNegativeDouble(b)` (a null side counts as 0, negative sides are clamped to 0 before adding). |
| `public static Long longAddOrNull(Number, Number)` | Returns null if both are null; the `longValue()` of the non-null one if only one is null; otherwise the sum of both `longValue()`s. Overflow wraps around silently; negative values are not clamped. |
| `public static long longAddOrNull(long, Long)` | Returns `a` if `b` is null, otherwise `a + b` (overflow wraps). Despite the name it never returns null. |
| `public static boolean equals(Number, Number)` | Null-safe equality: true if both are null, false if exactly one is null, otherwise `a.equals(b)`. Note that this uses the boxed types' `equals`, so values of different classes (e.g. `Long` 1 and `Integer` 1) are not equal. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree`

```java
public class RowTree
```

A mutable, pointer-based tree of row IDs used to build or edit a forest incrementally and then convert it to an `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest`. The tree has an invisible super-root node (row ID 0) whose children are the top-level rows. Nodes (`RowTree.Node`) carry a row ID and an integer bit set of caller-defined flags. Clients create it with `new RowTree()`; subclasses (such as `IndexedRowTree`) may hook node creation and removal. Not thread-safe; structural invariants (row ID uniqueness, no cycles, `afterNode` being a child of the given parent) are only checked by Java assertions, if at all.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public RowTree()` | Creates an empty tree consisting only of the super-root. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node getSuperRoot()` | Returns the invisible root node (row ID 0, flags 0). Its children are the top-level rows. It is never null and is never part of `toForest()` output. |
| `public String toString()` | Returns the compact nested text of the whole tree, as produced by `RowTree.Node.toFullString()` on the super-root, e.g. `(1(2,3),4)`; an empty tree gives an empty string. Flags are not shown. |
| `public void appendForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest)` | Adds a copy of the whole forest as new top-level nodes placed after the current last top-level node, keeping the forest's order and nesting. New nodes get flags 0. Uses the node-creation hook for every row. |
| `public void appendForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node)` | Adds a copy of the whole forest under `underNode`: the forest's top-level rows become children of `underNode`, placed right after `afterNode` (which must be a child of `underNode`) or, if `afterNode` is null, at the beginning, before any existing children. New nodes get flags 0. |
| `public int appendForest(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node, int, int, java.util.function.LongPredicate)` | General form. Copies part of `forest` into the tree: if `parentIndex` is negative, the whole forest; otherwise only the subtree below forest position `parentIndex` (its descendants, not the row itself). The copied top-level rows become children of `parentNode`, inserted right after `afterNode` (must be a child of `parentNode`) or first among its children if `afterNode` is null; deeper rows keep their relative nesting. Every created node gets `flags`. If `rowFilter` is non-null, a row for which it returns false is skipped together with its entire subtree. Returns the forest index just past the copied range (the first index after `parentIndex` whose depth is not deeper than the parent, or the forest size). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node insertNode(long, int, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node)` | Creates a new leaf node with the given row ID and flags (through the node-creation hook) and inserts it as a child of `parentNode`: right after `afterNode` if given (it must be a child of `parentNode`), or as the first child if `afterNode` is null. Returns the new node. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node moveNode(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node)` | Detaches `node` (with its whole subtree) from its current place and inserts it under `parentNode`, after `afterNode` or first if `afterNode` is null. Returns `node`. Moving a node under its own descendant is not detected and corrupts the tree. Moving the super-root or a detached node throws `NullPointerException`. |
| `public void remove(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node)` | Detaches `node` and its subtree from the tree and then calls the removal hook (`forgetNode`) for it. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `node` is the super-root. A node that is already detached causes `NullPointerException`. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest toForest()` | Returns a new `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ArrayForest` with all nodes except the super-root in depth-first pre-order, top-level nodes at depth 0. Flags are not included. Later changes to the tree do not affect the returned forest. |
| `protected com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node createNode(long, int)` | Protected factory hook used for every node this tree creates (by `appendForest` and `insertNode`). The base version returns a new unattached node with the given row ID and flags; subclasses may override to track nodes but must return a fresh unattached node. |
| `protected void forgetNode(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node)` | Protected hook called by `remove` after a node has been detached. Does nothing in the base class. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node`

```java
public static class RowTree.Node
```

One node of a `RowTree`: a row ID, a mutable integer bit set of flags and links to parent, children and siblings. Nodes are created only by the tree; clients navigate and read them and change them only through the tree's methods and `addFlags`. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public String toString()` | Returns the row ID in decimal if the node has no flags, otherwise the row ID, a `#` and the flag value in decimal, e.g. `42` or `42#3`. |

Example: `5(6,7(8))`. Flags are not shown. |
| `public StringBuilder append(StringBuilder)` | Appends the same text as `toFullString()` to the given builder and returns that builder. |
| `public long getRowId()` | Returns the row ID this node stands for; 0 for the super-root. |
| `public boolean hasFlags(int)` | True if every bit set in `flagMask` is also set in this node's flags. `hasFlags(0)` is always true. |
| `public void addFlags(int)` | Sets the bits of `flagMask` in this node's flags (bitwise OR); existing bits are kept. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node getParent()` | Returns the parent node; for top-level rows this is the super-root. For the super-root or a detached node the result is null, but with Java assertions enabled the call raises `AssertionError` instead. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node getFirstChild()` | Returns the first child, or null if the node has no children. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node getLastChild()` | Returns the last child, or null if the node has no children. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node getNextSibling()` | Returns the next node with the same parent, or null if this is the last child. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node getPrevSibling()` | Returns the previous node with the same parent, or null if this is the first child. |
| `public void writeTo(com.almworks.integers.LongCollector, com.almworks.integers.IntCollector, int)` | Writes this node's subtree in depth-first pre-order: if `depth` is 0 or more, first adds this node's row ID to `rows` and `depth` to `depths`; then does the same for each child, in order, with `depth + 1`. Passing -1 writes only the descendants, with the children at depth 0 (this is how the super-root is serialized). |
| `public void collectDirectChildren(com.almworks.integers.LongCollector)` | Adds the row IDs of this node's direct children, in order, to the collector. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.RowTree.Node findFirstWithFlags(int)` | Searches this node and then its descendants in depth-first pre-order and returns the first node for which `hasFlags(flags)` is true, or null if none matches. With `flags` = 0 it returns this node. |

```java
public class SpecParams extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.MapObject
```

A `MapObject` over the parameter map of a spec (for example an attribute spec's parameters), adding typed access to nested parameter objects and to nested attribute specs. Created by clients from a parameter map. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public SpecParams(java.util.Map<String, Object>)` | Creates the accessor over a new JSON object built from the given parameter map (see `MapObject(Map)`). |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.SpecParams getObject(String)` | Returns the value under `name` as a `SpecParams` if it is a JSON object or a `java.util.Map` (a JSON object is first converted into a plain map); returns null if absent or of another type. Overrides the `MapObject` version with a narrower return type. |
| `public <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T> getAttributeParameter(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValueFormat<T>)` | Same as `getAttributeParameter("attribute", expectedFormat)`: reads a nested attribute spec stored under the key `attribute`. |
| `public <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec<T> getAttributeParameter(String, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.ValueFormat<T>)` | Reads a nested attribute spec stored under `name` as an object with keys `id` (string), optional `format` (format ID string) and optional `params` (object). Returns null if there is no such object. If both `format` and `expectedFormat` are given and the stored format is neither `expectedFormat`'s ID nor the ID of `ValueFormat.ANY`, returns null. The format of the result is `expectedFormat` when given (even if the stored one is `any`); if `expectedFormat` is null, the standard format named by the stored `format` is used, and if there is none, returns null. Builds a `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribute.AttributeSpec` from the ID, the format and the `params` map (null if `params` is absent or not an object). If the spec cannot be built because the values are invalid (`IllegalArgumentException`, e.g. a missing ID), returns null and logs at DEBUG level. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.StructureUtil`

```java
public class StructureUtil
```

A grab-bag of static helpers used across the plugin: lenient reading of request-style parameter maps, chunked storage of long strings in Jira application properties, debug strings for issues, structures and rows, i18n text lookup, user lookups, Jackson JSON conversion, URL encoding and small null/number helpers (several of which simply delegate to `TypeUtils`, `LoggingUtils`, `IntegersUtil` and `MapUtils`). Marked as internal: available to clients but not covered by compatibility guarantees. Stateless apart from logging; thread-safe unless noted. Some helpers query Jira services through `JiraComponents` and therefore only work inside a running Jira.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder`

```java
public class TotalOrder
```

Defines a total order over values of arbitrary, mixed types, for sorting heterogeneous data such as attribute values. Values are first normalized: all integer-like boxed numbers (`Long`, `Integer`, `Short`, `Byte`) and floating numbers (`Double`, `Float`) become `ComparableTuple` numbers so they compare numerically with each other; strings are kept as is (strict), lower-cased (case-insensitive) or turned into `java.text.CollationKey`s (collator mode) depending on how the order was created; other objects are kept unchanged. Normalized values are wrapped (`wrap`) and compared with `COMPARATOR`. Instances are created only by the static factories and are immutable; a collator-based instance shares its collator, so thread safety then follows `java.text.Collator`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public static final java.util.Comparator<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder.ValueWrapper> COMPARATOR` | A shared comparator of `TotalOrder.ValueWrapper`s. Order: a wrapper is equal to itself; wrappers holding null sort after all others (two nulls are equal). Values of the same runtime class compare by `compareTo` if they are `Comparable`, otherwise by comparing their `toString()` texts. Values of different classes are ordered by class: `ComparableTuple` (i.e. all numbers) first, then `String`, then all other classes ordered by their simple class names (`Class.getSimpleName`, case-sensitive); classes with the same simple name compare equal. Note that collation keys produced by the JDK are instances of a subclass of `java.text.CollationKey`, so in practice they fall into the 'other classes by simple name' group rather than a group of their own. Wrappers from different `TotalOrder` instances must not be mixed (checked only by Java assertions). Null wrappers are not allowed. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder withStrictStringComparison()` | Returns an order that compares strings with `String.compareTo` (case-sensitive, UTF-16 code unit order). |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder withCaseInsensitiveStringComparison()` | Returns an order that compares strings after lower-casing them with the root locale. Strings differing only in case are equal. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder withCaseInsensitiveStringComparison(java.util.Locale)` | Returns an order that compares strings after lower-casing them with the given locale (`String.toLowerCase(Locale)`); null means the root locale. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder withCollatorStringComparison(java.util.Locale)` | Returns an order that compares strings with a new `java.text.Collator` for the locale (default strength and decomposition). A null locale throws `NullPointerException`; if no collator can be obtained, throws `IllegalArgumentException`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder withCollatorStringComparison(java.util.Locale, int)` | Like the one-argument form but sets the collator strength (one of the `Collator` strength constants, e.g. `Collator.PRIMARY`). An invalid strength throws `IllegalArgumentException` from the JDK. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder withCollatorStringComparison(java.util.Locale, int, int)` | Like the two-argument form but also sets the collator decomposition mode (one of the `Collator` decomposition constants). Invalid values throw `IllegalArgumentException`. |
| `public static com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder withCollator(java.text.Collator)` | Returns an order that compares strings with the given collator, which is used as is (not copied). A null collator gives strict string comparison. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder.ValueWrapper wrap(Object)` | Normalizes the value as described for the class and returns it in a new `ValueWrapper` bound to this order. Null is allowed and sorts last. |
| `public <T> com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TotalOrder.PayloadWrapper<T> wrap(Object, T)` | Like `wrap(Object)` but returns a `PayloadWrapper` that also carries an arbitrary payload (ignored for ordering), e.g. the row the value belongs to. |
| `public int compare(Object, Object)` | Wraps both values with this order and compares them with `COMPARATOR`: negative, zero or positive as `o1` sorts before, equal to or after `o2`. For repeated comparisons, wrap once and sort the wrappers instead, since normalization (e.g. building collation keys) happens on every call. |


A `TotalOrder.ValueWrapper` that also carries a payload object, so that items can be sorted by a value while keeping a reference to the item. Created by `TotalOrder.wrap(Object, Object)`. Immutable.

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.TypeUtils`

```java
public class TypeUtils
```

Static helpers for generic class literals, null defaults and lenient number parsing. Stateless and thread-safe. Several methods are also re-exported by `StructureUtil`.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public TypeUtils()` | Public constructor; the class has only static methods. |
| `public static <T> Class<java.util.Set<T>> setType()` | Returns `java.util.Set.class` typed as `Class<Set<T>>`, for generic-safe casts such as `setType().cast(obj)`. |
| `public static <T, V> Class<java.util.Map<T, V>> mapType()` | Returns `java.util.Map.class` typed as `Class<Map<K, V>>`. |
| `public static <T> Class<java.util.List<T>> listType()` | Returns `java.util.List.class` typed as `Class<List<T>>`. |
| `public static long nn(Long, long)` | Returns the unboxed value, or `defaultValue` if it is null. |
| `public static int nn(Integer, int)` | Returns the unboxed value, or `defaultValue` if it is null. |
| `public static <T> T nnv(T, T)` | Returns `value` if non-null, otherwise `defaultValue` (which is expected to be non-null but is not checked). |
| `public static long lv(String, long)` | Parses the string as a decimal `long` with `Long.parseLong` (no trimming, optional leading sign); returns `defaultValue` if the string is null or not a valid number (including out-of-range values and surrounding spaces). |
| `public static int iv(String, int)` | Parses the string as a decimal `int` with `Integer.parseInt`; returns `defaultValue` if null or invalid (spaces, decimals, overflow). |
| `public static Long lvn(String)` | Like `lv` but returns null instead of a default when the string is null or invalid. |
| `public static Integer ivn(String)` | Like `iv` but returns null when the string is null or invalid. |
| `public static String nn(String)` | Returns the string, or the empty string if it is null. |
| `public static long nnl(Long)` | Returns the unboxed value, or 0 if null. |
| `public static int nni(Integer)` | Returns the unboxed value, or 0 if null. |
| `public static boolean fitsIntoInt(long)` | True if the value lies within the `int` range (from -2147483648 to 2147483647 inclusive), i.e. converting it to `int` loses nothing. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view`

Views: named, shareable grid configurations (columns, display modes, pinned columns) for displaying structures, plus per-structure and global settings saying which views appear in the view menu and which is the default on each page.

| `public static final int SCROLLABLE = 2` | Value 2: columns keep their widths and the grid scrolls horizontally. |
| `public static boolean isValid(int)` | True only for 1 or 2. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView`

```java
public interface StructureView
```

A view as a working copy with change tracking, obtained from `StructureViewManager` (`getView`, `getViews`, `createView`, menu items). Getters return pending changes if set, otherwise the loaded values. Setters only record changes in memory and return this; `saveChanges()` persists them. Not thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract long getId()` | The view ID; 0 for a new view that has not been saved. |
| `public abstract String getName()` | The view name; never null. |
| `public abstract String getDescription()` | The view description; never null (empty when unset). |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSpecification getSpecification()` | The view's columns and display settings. Columns that refer to shared saved column definitions are returned resolved to their current definition. |
| `public abstract com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser getOwner()` | The owner as a Jira user, or null when there is no owner or the user cannot be found. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule> getPermissions()` | A copy of the view's sharing rules, in evaluation order; never null. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel getEffectivePermission(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | The access level the given user (null for anonymous) has to the stored view: Jira administrators get ADMIN (unless disabled by a system setting), users without access to the plugin get NONE, the owner gets ADMIN, otherwise the result of the sharing rules. Pending unsaved changes are not considered; NONE for an unsaved view. |
| `public abstract boolean isShared()` | True when the sharing rules grant something to someone, that is, there is at least one rule other than a "set level to none" rule. |
| `public abstract boolean isPublic()` | True when the rules give everyone (the "anyone" subject) at least VIEW and no later rule takes it away. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView setName(String)` | Records a new name. A null leaves the name unchanged. A blank name makes `saveChanges` fail. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView setDescription(String)` | Records a new description; null leaves it unchanged. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView setOwner(com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | Records a new owner; null leaves the owner unchanged. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView setPermissions(java.util.Collection<? extends com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionRule>)` | Records new sharing rules (copied). Null leaves the rules unchanged; an empty collection makes the view private. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView setSpecification(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSpecification)` | Records a new specification (null means an empty one). Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView setSpecification(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSpecification.Builder)` | Records a new specification from a builder (kept by reference, not copied); null leaves it unchanged. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView update(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureViewBean.Builder)` | Copies every property that is set (non-null) in the given builder into the pending changes, including the ID if set. Null does nothing. Returns this. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView makePublic()` | Replaces the sharing rules with: everyone may VIEW, followed by copies of the existing rules that grant more than VIEW (EDIT, ADMIN...). Rules granting VIEW or less and non-level rules are dropped. Returns this; save to persist. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView saveChanges() throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Persists the view and returns this. For a new view: requires the global right to create views (`StructureException` `VIEW_CREATION_DENIED`), makes the current user the owner (unless security is overridden), requires a non-blank name (`INVALID_PARAMETER`), and if rules are set and non-empty requires the right to share views. For an existing view with no changes, does nothing. Otherwise: changing only the specification requires EDIT on the view; changing name, description, owner or rules requires ADMIN (`VIEW_EDIT_DENIED` / `VIEW_ADMIN_DENIED`, or `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` when the user has no access); changed rules are validated and require the sharing right. Fails when the license does not allow writes. Note: an ADMIN of a view can assign any user as owner; no further check is made. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureViewManager`

```java
public interface StructureViewManager
```

Service (OSGi component) for views: lookup with access checks, creation and deletion, and view settings that associate views with structures and pages (per structure and global default). Acts as the current user; checks are skipped when security is overridden. A null `PermissionLevel` argument means "no minimum". Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView getView(Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | The view with the given ID if the current user has at least the given level (null: any) and may use the plugin. Throws `StructureException` `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` otherwise, including for a null or unknown ID. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView> getViews(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel)` | All views the current user can access at the given level (null: any), sorted by name using the user's locale collation. Empty on storage errors. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel getViewPermission(Long, com.atlassian.jira.user.ApplicationUser)` | The access level of the given user (second argument, null for anonymous) to the view (first argument); NONE when the view does not exist. See `StructureView.getEffectivePermission` for the rules. |
| `public abstract boolean isAccessible(Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.permissions.PermissionLevel)` | True when the current user has at least the given level to the view. For a nonexistent view, true only when the level is null or NONE and the user may use the plugin. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureView createView()` | A new, unsaved view with empty properties. Set at least a name and call `saveChanges()`. |
| `public abstract void deleteView(Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Deletes the view and its associations with structures. Requires ADMIN on the view (`VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, `VIEW_ADMIN_DENIED` otherwise). Fails when the license does not allow writes. Structure view settings that mention the view are not rewritten. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSettings getViewSettings(Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | The view settings of the structure. Requires VIEW on the structure, otherwise `StructureException` `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. Returns settings for which `isDefined()` is false when the structure has none of its own (the global default then applies). On storage errors returns `ViewSettings.EMPTY_SETTINGS`. |
| `public abstract void setViewSettings(Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSettings) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Replaces the structure's view settings; null (or undefined settings) removes them so the global default applies. Requires ADMIN on the structure (`STRUCTURE_ADMIN_DENIED`, or `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` without VIEW); with security overridden the structure must still exist. Fails when the license does not allow writes. The referenced views are not checked. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSettings getDefaultViewSettings()` | The global default view settings used for structures without their own. No access check. `ViewSettings.EMPTY_SETTINGS` on storage errors. |
| `public abstract void setDefaultViewSettings(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSettings) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Replaces the global default view settings (null clears them). Only Jira administrators may do this (`StructureException` `JIRA_ADMIN_DENIED`), unless security is overridden. Fails when the license does not allow writes. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.StructureViewMenuItem> getMenuItems(Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.StructurePage)` | The views to show in the view menu for the structure (first argument; null uses only the global default) on the page (second). Uses the structure's settings if defined, otherwise the global default. Includes, in settings order, each associated view listed for that page that the current user can view; the first view marked default for the page is moved to the front and flagged as preferred. Empty when the user cannot view the structure. Component and version tabs count as the project tab; other pages count as the structure board. |
| `public abstract java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structure.Structure> getAssociatedStructures(Long) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Structures whose view settings mention the given view and which the current user can view, sorted by name. Requires VIEW on the view (`StructureException` otherwise). |
| `public abstract void makeDefaultForStructure(Long, Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.settings.StructurePage) throws com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error.StructureException` | Makes the view (first argument) the default view of the structure (second) on the page (third), also putting it on that page's menu; starts from the global default settings if the structure has none. Other views lose their default flag for that page; a view not yet associated is added at the front. Does nothing when it is already the default. Requires ADMIN on the structure and VIEW on the view. |

```java
public static class ViewSpecification.Builder implements Cloneable
```

Mutable builder of `ViewSpecification` with shortcuts for common columns; also its JSON form. New columns get a column ID (`csid`) one greater than the largest numeric ID already present. Defaults: no columns, `AUTO_FIT`, `ONE_LINE`, no pins. Not thread-safe.

| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSpecification.Builder removeColumn(String)` | Removes every column whose csid equals the argument (null removes columns without a csid). Returns this. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view.ViewSpecification.Column.Builder addColumn(String, String)` | Appends a new column with the given column type key (first argument) and csid (second) and returns its builder for further setup. |

## Package `com.almworks.jira.structure.generic`

Not part of the public API jar: a service exported by the plugin itself (public OSGi component) that stores the change history of generic items (items managed by the generic item service: each create or update of such an item is recorded with old and new values).

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.generic.GenericItemHistoryManager`

```java
public interface GenericItemHistoryManager
```

Plugin-internal service, exported as a public OSGi component, that stores and reads change-history records of generic items. The plugin's generic item service adds a record whenever an item is created or updated, and history records are themselves exposed as items of the memo-change-history-group type (`CoreIdentities.memoChangeHistoryGroup(recordId)`). No permission checks are made. Thread-safe.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public abstract void addRecords(java.util.List<com.almworks.jira.structure.generic.GenericItemHistoryRecord>)` | Stores the given records (their own IDs are ignored; new IDs are assigned) and notifies the item change tracker about both the changed items and the new record items. Storage errors are logged and remaining records are skipped, not thrown. |
| `public abstract com.almworks.jira.structure.generic.GenericItemHistoryRecord getRecord(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity)` | The record identified by a history-record item identity (memo-change-history-group type, long ID = record ID); null when the identity is of another type or no such record exists. Cached. Throws the plugin's storage exception on database errors. |
| `public abstract void loadRecords(java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, java.util.function.Consumer<com.almworks.jira.structure.generic.GenericItemHistoryRecord>)` | Passes to the consumer each existing record named by the given history-record identities (others are ignored). Records already cached are delivered first; the rest are read in chunks ordered by timestamp. |
| `public abstract void loadRecordsForItems(java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>, java.util.function.Consumer<com.almworks.jira.structure.generic.GenericItemHistoryRecord>)` | Passes to the consumer all history records of the given generic items (by item identity), grouped by item type and ordered by timestamp within each chunk. |
| `public abstract void removeRecordsForItems(java.util.Collection<com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity>)` | Deletes all history records of the given generic items and clears the record cache. |

### `com.almworks.jira.structure.generic.GenericItemHistoryRecord`

```java
public class GenericItemHistoryRecord
```

Immutable record of one create or update of a generic item: which item, its new and previous state, who and when.

| member | meaning |
|---|---|
| `public GenericItemHistoryRecord(Long, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem, com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem, String, long, boolean)` | Arguments in order: record ID (null for a record not yet stored), changed item identity, new item state, previous state (null on create), author user key (nullable), timestamp in epoch milliseconds, and whether this was a creation. |
| `public Long getId()` | The record ID, or null when not stored yet. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.ItemIdentity getItemId()` | Identity of the generic item that changed. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem getNewItem()` | The item's state after the change. |
| `public com.almworks.jira.structure.api.item.generic.GenericItem getOldItem()` | The item's state before the change; null for a creation. Records read back from storage also return null when the previous name was blank. |
| `public String getAuthorKey()` | User key of the user who made the change, or null. |
| `public long getTimestamp()` | When the change happened, epoch milliseconds. |
| `public boolean isCreate()` | True when the record describes the creation of the item. |
